cards.title: Anchor knobs (closed list)
cards.body:
**T-00-20 Anchor knobs (closed list).** `dc` (source or tier) · `attribute` · `action_cost` ·
`reach_unit` · `stakes` · `duration` · `condition` (inflicted) · `harm_severity` · `harm_tags` ·
`targets` (count or selection over relationship-state) · `time_cost` · `focus_cost`.
Counting [revision: I-062]: a change is counted per knob, not per word changed. `duration` is a feature's
whole **behavior over time**: how long it lasts and how it changes while it lasts (grows, spreads, fades,
burns out, stays put); changing both its length and its growth is one knob. Where a created feature sits
(the doorway instead of the thatch) is the beat's target, not a knob.

cards.title: Banned words
cards.body:
**T-00-22 Banned words.** In rules text and data: *level* (of a character), *class*, *XP*, *HP / hit
points*, *mana*, *stamina*, *saving throw*, *skill check*, *advantage / disadvantage*, *injury /
injured / hurt*, *minor / major / severe* as severity names, *exploration turn*, *the System*, *focus*
(for an item), bare *gate* for the generator. In narration: any mechanical number, any rules term
voiced by an in-world character.

---

cards.title: A boundary crossing: two days on the Salt Road
cards.body:
### WE-00-1 A boundary crossing: two days on the Salt Road

*Situation.* Spring, week 3, day 7, start of the morning watch, at Ashford. Wren travels to Grey Keep:
5 travel watches along the Salt Road *(illustrative; ch.10 owns travel)*. Plan: travel morning and
afternoon, camp in the evening, sleep through the night. The DM calls
`advance_time(until: arrival, mode: travel)`. The engine lists every boundary crossed and runs them in
order (PR-00-2). Encounter checks use an illustrative d6 per watch (1 encounter, 2 omen, 3–6 nothing;
ch.10 owns the real procedure); the region carries a hidden danger clock `clk.cinder_hunting_ground`
(6 segments; ticks 1 on each omen result; an encounter result here rolls on the road's encounter table).

| # | Boundary | Handlers that fired (phase) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | watch end, D7 morning | `h.10.travel_progress` (4); `h.10.watch_check` (7) | progress 1/5; d6 = 4, nothing |
| 2 | watch end, D7 afternoon | same | progress 2/5; d6 = 2, omen → `tick_clock(cinder_hunting_ground)` 0→1, stage *stirring*, omen: "a hare burned black lies by the road, with no fire anywhere near it" |
| 3 | watch end, D7 evening (camp) | `h.10.watch_check` (7) | d6 = 5, nothing |
| 4 | **dawn, D1**: `rest_long` completes (event boundaries first, 00.7.6) | `h.07.rest_recovery`, `h.05.focus_recover` (3); `h.00.reflection` (8) | Vitality and Focus already full; `reflection` fires |
| 5 | `reflection` | `h.03.recency_update`, `h.04.recognition_pass`, `h.04.standing_offers` (8) | recognition pass: **abstain** (no calling eligible); nothing is voiced |
| 6 | watch end, D7 night | `h.10.watch_check` (7) | d6 = 3, nothing |
| 7 | day end, D7 | `h.05.day_recharge` (3); `h.07.natural_recovery` (3); `h.10.supply` (4); `h.11.situation_timelines` (6); `h.10.weather` (7) | supply 3 → 2; weather for D1: cold rain |
| 8 | **week end, W3** | `h.08.upkeep`, `h.16.retinue_upkeep` (4); `h.11.world_turn` (6); `h.15.downtime_week` (6); `h.00.reflection_if_downtime` (8) | World Turn *(illustrative; 11)*: the Salt Guild's hidden goal clock "Corner the Salt Road" ticks 4 → 5 of 8; its perceivable trace is written as a rumor, "tolls doubled at the Grey Keep bridge", heard at the next settlement |
| 9 | watch end, D1 morning | travel, check | progress 3/5; d6 = 6 |
| 10 | watch end, D1 afternoon | travel (4), check (7) | progress 4/5; d6 = 1 → encounter table → "a cinder hound on the hunt"; the handler is **interrupting** |

The afternoon boundary finishes its phases 8–9, then `advance_time` halts at dusk on D1 and returns
`remainder: 1 travel watch`. The DM narrates the journey from the returned list only: the burned hare,
the cold rain at dawn, then a shape pacing the verge in the rain, steam rising where the drops hit its
back. It invents no second omen and no weather that was not rolled. After the encounter, Wren may
resume; the remaining watch is not lost.

cards.title: The gate→fill generator produces an item
cards.body:
### WE-00-2 The gate→fill generator produces an item

*Situation.* The hound fight resolves *(illustrative; 06)*. Wren's last beat is a shortbow shot:
Agility +3, competence +2 (`deed.martial.archery`), total +5 vs the hound's Guard 13. The d20 shows 19:
total 24, margin +11, **critical success**. The hound (`adv.cinder_hound_07`; tags
`creature.beast.predator`, `creature.elemental.fire`; threat band T2) is killed.

The DM classifies `[J:enum]` circumstance = **decisive** (killed in a fair fight by a resolved success;
not costly, not merciful, not scavenged) and calls
`generate(gen.loot, adv.cinder_hound_07, decisive, critical_success)`.

1. **Pool gate** *(pool content illustrative; 08 owns)*. The archetype's trophy base is
   `item.jewelry.charm`. Entries gated on the source's tags:

   | Entry | Gate | mod_group | Weight | Kept? |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `prop.ember_ward` (the archetype's **signature**): reduce `harm.fire` by the tier value | `creature.elemental.fire` | resist_fire | 3 | yes |
   | `prop.warm_blood`: cold-weather hazards count one severity rung lower | `creature.elemental.fire` | env_cold | 2 | yes |
   | `prop.hounds_nose`: a Precision lever on Observe when tracking by scent | `creature.beast.predator` | senses | 2 | yes |
   | `prop.snarl`: edge +1 on Talk to intimidate `creature.beast` | `creature.beast.predator` | intimidate | 1 | yes |
   | `prop.searing_bite`: Strikes add fire harm | `creature.elemental.fire` | weapon_fire | 2 | **no**: `base_kinds: item.weapon` excludes a charm |

2. **Tier gate.** T2 → `tier_cap` 2. All entries start at tier 1: all kept.
3. **Quality rung.** (decisive, critical_success) → `fine`: 1 signature slot + 1 magnitude slot
   *(illustrative; 08)*. Fill method for `decisive`: **signature**.
4. **Degree effect.** Critical success → **Greater**: the signature property gains +1 tier (may reach
   `tier_cap` + 1 = 3).
5. **Signature slot.** `prop.ember_ward` at tier 2 + 1 = **3**: reduce fire harm by 3. Its mod_group
   `resist_fire` is removed from the pool.
6. **Magnitude slot.** Weights: warm_blood 4 × ½ (recency: generated three loot draws ago from a fire
   beetle; weights are doubled first, 00.11.3 step 7) = 2; hounds_nose 4; snarl 2. Total 8 → 25% / 50% / 25%. [verification: V1-002] The engine draws d100 = 63 → bands
   1–25 warm_blood, 26–75 hounds_nose, 76–100 snarl → **`prop.hounds_nose`**, tier `tier_cap − 1` = 1.
7. **Caps.** Charm slot cap 2 and the item budget (reduction 3, inside ch.07's cap of 4): pass.
8. **Output.** `item.i0107`, base `bi.fang_charm`, quality fine, signature `[ember_ward T3]`,
   magnitude `[hounds_nose T1]`, provenance {cinder_hound_07, decisive, critical_success}, log {pool 4 →
   4 → 3; weights 2/4/2; d100 63}.

The DM names it ("a fang on a thong, still warm") and narrates only what it holds. *Non-example:* "the
charm keeps the chill of the rain off you" is forbidden: warm_blood was not generated (INV-2, SG-15).

cards.title: An unlicensed attempt, redirected by the license's fallback
cards.body:
### WE-00-3 An unlicensed attempt, redirected by the license's fallback

*Situation.* Night at Grey Keep. The archive door is established as locked with a guild-made lock
(`door_archive.locked = true`; `door_archive.lock_make = guild`). Player: "I pick the lock with my
knife. It's just a cheap archive lock."

- **Assertion.** "It's just a cheap lock" contradicts an established fact and creates nothing (SG-06).
- **GATE** `[J:enum]`. Picking a lock is not within any basic verb's coverage (T-00-11 lists
  lockpicking as licensed). The license that would cover it is `lic.training.lockwork` *(illustrative;
  05 owns)*: scope "Open mechanical locks and simple traps with picks or improvised tools; at grade
  `common`, locks up to Hard tier." Wren does not hold it → **G3**.
- **Redirect (a lookup, not an invention).** The license's `crude_fallback`: `{verb: force, method:
  "break the lock, hasp or hinges", dc_shift: 0, reach_cap: standard, consequence: "trait.sense.loud"}`;
  `acquisition_paths`: mentor (a locksmith or a thief teaches; a 6-segment project clock ticked by one
  practice roll per week), origin (urban origins at creation), recognition (`deed.guile.thievery`,
  04). No time or action is spent.
- **The DM says:** "The wards are guild-cut; nothing in your hands knows how to read them. You can break
  it: the hasp is iron and the oak around it is old, but it will be loud. Picking locks like this is
  something a locksmith or a thief could teach you." The ruling is logged (`kind: g3_redirect`).
- The player chooses to break it (WE-00-4). *Boundary pair:* had the door carried a plain latch-bar,
  lifting it is `verb.handle` (G1) with no license at all; had the lock been sealed by a ward spell,
  breaking the hasp would open the wood but leave the ward: the beat splits by scope (00.12.2).

cards.title: Assembling a check through the evaluation pass
cards.body:
### WE-00-4 Assembling a check through the evaluation pass

*Beat.* Break the hasp. Anchor `verb.force` (no deltas). Primary deed tag `deed.martial.athletics`.
Two scenes ago the DM narrated "a length of iron bar lies among the gate's wreckage" and, by
write-on-mention, recorded it (`obj.iron_bar_03`, now carried: fact `pc.wren.holds obj.iron_bar_03`).

PR-00-1:
1. Attribute: Force allows Might only → **+1**.
2. Competence: entries on `deed.martial.athletics`, `deed.martial`, `deed`: only the floor → **+1**.
3. Edge: none → **0**.
4. Circumstance: lever `obj.iron_bar_03` typed **Precision** (a tool that lets the method be done
   better) → **+2**. The player also proposes "the rain has rusted it". There is no such fact; the
   question is G0: the Oracle, rung Unlikely (hasps in covered doorways rarely rust through), d100 = 41
   → **no**; `set_fact(door_archive.hasp.condition = sound)`. No snag, no lever.
5. Status: none → **0**. Total **+4** (clamp not reached).
6. DC: no stored DC for the hasp; not opposed; tier `[J:rung]` **Moderate** (an iron hasp in old oak:
   a strong, competent person usually manages) → **15** (reference; ch.01 owns), written as
   `door_archive.hasp.dc = 15`.
7. Odds: needs 11+ → success-or-better 50%, critical success 5%, critical failure 5%, near miss 15%.
8. Stakes `[J:rung]` **Risky** (guards in the keep; failure means being heard: an S2 Exposure cost).
   Reach **Standard**. Method consequence regardless of degree: loud.

OFFER: "Breaking the hasp: you need 11 or better (50%). It will be loud whatever happens; if it fails,
someone hears you properly." The player commits. `roll_check`: d20 = 9 → total 13, margin −2 →
**failure, near miss**. The player takes success-at-cost: one cost at S2 → the DM picks the menu type
whose trigger fits the method (`cost.exposure`: noise). State writes: `door_archive.hasp = broken`,
`door_archive.locked = false`; the alarm clock ticks for the loud consequence and for the exposure cost
(WE-00-5).

cards.title: A hidden clock ticks with omens, and two clocks race
cards.body:
### WE-00-5 A hidden clock ticks with omens, and two clocks race

`clk.alarm_grey_keep` *(template content illustrative; 10, or a region's seed, 12.16)*: kind danger, 6 segments, **hidden**;
tick sources: a `trait.sense.loud` beat inside the keep → 1; `cost.exposure` → U(severity);
auto_ticks: +1 at each `hour` boundary while the PC is inside after dusk; omens — stirring: "a dog
barks twice somewhere below", "a door closes across the yard"; building: "lantern light moves along the
wall walk", "boots on the stair, unhurried"; imminent: "a voice calls a name and no one answers", "in
the gatehouse, someone is untying the bell rope". On complete: guards converge on the PC's location
(`create` encounter), **interrupting**; defeat disposition capture (so not lethal).

| Event | Tick | Fill | Stage → omen the narrator must render |
|---|---|---|---|
| hasp broken (loud) | +1 | 1/6 | stirring: a dog barks twice somewhere below |
| exposure cost S2 (U = 1) | +1 | 2/6 | stirring: a door closes across the yard |
| search beat 1 (Observe, success, Standard) | — | 2/6 | `clk.find_ledger` (public, 4) +2 → 2/4 |
| `hour` boundary (auto) | +1 | 3/6 | building (3 ≥ half): lantern light on the wall walk |
| search beat 2 (failure; Risky → S2 `cost.time`) | +1 | 4/6 | building: boots on the stair, unhurried |
| search beat 3 (success; Amplifying lever = the clerk's index card found earlier → Great) | — | 4/6 | `clk.find_ledger` +3 → complete; its link creates `clk.get_out` (public, 4) with `races_with: clk.alarm_grey_keep` |
| escape beat 1 (Sneak, success, Standard) | — | 4/6 | `clk.get_out` 2/4 |
| `hour` boundary (auto) | +1 | 5/6 | **imminent** (remaining 1 ≤ max(1, 6÷4)): someone is untying the bell rope. Completion is capture, not lethal: no lethal warning |
| escape beat 2 (Sneak, near miss; the player takes success-at-cost: `cost.exposure` S2) | would be +1 | — | the same event completes both clocks; the acting side's delivered reach completes first (00.8.5): `clk.get_out` 4/4 **completes**, `clk.alarm_grey_keep` is **voided** before its tick lands |

Wren drops over the outer wall as the bell starts, too late to matter. Narration mentions each omen
once, in the turn its tick happened, and never states the alarm's number (hidden clock).

cards.title: An effect composing through the substrate
cards.body:
### WE-00-6 An effect composing through the substrate

*Situation.* Next morning Captain Hesk (T3; Agility +2, competence `deed.martial` +4 → Guard 16;
Vitality 16; armor reduction 2 against `harm.physical` *(illustrative; 06/08/09)*) rides Wren down on
the Salt Road. On her previous turn Wren feinted (Setup, success), recording `cond.off_balance` on Hesk.
Earlier this conflict she activated Cinder Stride (Focus 4 → 3) and then coated her spear in Rime Oil.

1. **Priority-exclusive.** Both claim `slot.strike_delivery`. Rime Oil (rank 20) owns the slot. Cinder
   Stride (rank 10) is **fully suppressed**: no fire conversion and no +1 harm_edge. (`use_ability`
   warned at activation, since Rime Oil was already applied: the Focus was spent knowingly.)
2. **Frame.** Strike, a quick thrust → Agility +3; primary tag `deed.martial.polearm` → competence:
   floor +1 (her archery +2 does not cover polearms); lever: `cond.off_balance` on Hesk, typed
   **Amplifying** by the player (an opening to exploit) → reach Standard → Great. Total +4 vs Guard 16:
   needs 12 (45%). Stakes Risky (failure: Hesk's counter, S2 harm).
3. **Roll.** d20 = 20 → total 24, margin +8 = success; natural 20 → **critical success**. Delivered
   reach: Great + 1 = **Exceptional (4)**.
4. **Harm, dealer side** (00.10.5): E1 base S2 pierce; the slot owner replaces the harm type with
   `harm.frost`. E2 steps: delivered reach 4 → +2 → **S4**. E3 → **8**. E4 harm_edge: Rime Oil +1
   (Cinder Stride suppressed) → **9**.
5. **Harm, receiver side.** E4 reduction: Hesk's armor reduces `harm.physical` only; the harm is now
   `harm.frost` → 0. E5: no resistance or vulnerability to frost. **9** harm. Hesk 16 → **7** (at or
   below half → **bloodied**, a shown descriptor via `on_vitality_threshold`).
6. **Hooks** on the depth-0 event `on_attack_hit`: target's prevent/redirect first: Hesk's shield block
   is his reaction, already used this round, so none. Then Wren's: Quarry's Mark fires (Focus 3 → 2) →
   `apply_condition(cond.exposed)` on Hesk. That application is a **depth-1** event, so
   Pressing Advantage (`on_condition_applied by self`) does **not** fire (INV-12). Core rules still
   run: the harm counted, the threshold was crossed.
7. **Narration obligations:** name the exposed condition (visible) and the frost (rime crackling in the
   wound); never fire.

*Boundary pair.* Without the Rime Oil, Cinder Stride would own the slot: fire, +1 → 9 again but typed
`harm.fire`. *Non-example:* "the fire and the frost together shatter his mail": no composite exists for
this pair, and a suppressed claimant never counts as present for a composite's keys.

cards.title: Conditions stacking and neutralizing
cards.body:
### WE-00-7 Conditions stacking and neutralizing

Hesk's squire throws a lamp at Wren: `cond.burning` *(illustrative; 06)*: intensify, max 3; periodic
at `turn_end`: harm S1 (`harm.fire.flame`) per stack.
- Applied: 1 stack. At Wren's turn end: harm 1 → receiver side: reduction from the Ember-Fang Charm
  (`harm.fire`, 3; cascade covers `harm.fire.flame`) → **0**.
- Applied again: intensify → 2 stacks, duration refreshed; at turn end: harm 2 → **0**.
- A hedge-witch's frost bolt then applies `cond.chilled`, which `neutralizes: [cond.burning]`: burning
  is removed and chilled is **not** applied (PR-00-5 step 1). The narrator shows steam and nothing else.
- *Boundary:* without the charm, 2 stacks would deal 2 harm per turn end, and a third stack 3.

cards.title: Tags, competence and evidence
cards.body:
### WE-00-8 Tags, competence and evidence

Wren shoots a fleeing bandit's horse from the treeline. The DM classifies the primary deed tag
branch → child → deeper: `deed.martial` → `deed.martial.archery` → `deed.martial.archery.bow` (if 03
has added level 3). Competence lookup over ancestors: `.bow` none, `.archery` **+2**, `.martial` none,
`deed` +1 → **+2**. Evidence after the resolved success: `record_evidence {deed: "shot a fleeing
rider's horse from cover at dusk", tags: [deed.martial.archery.bow], challenge_band: 2, stakes: risky,
lethal_context: false, witnesses: [npc.bandit_03]}`; the engine cascades it to `.archery`, `.martial`,
`deed` with ch.03's weights, and returns nothing about tallies. Wren then lets the unhorsed bandit run:
a second event, `tags: [conduct.mercy]`, `conduct_sign: +1`.

cards.title: A precedent reused
cards.body:
### WE-00-9 A precedent reused

During the escape Wren swung on the gatehouse chain to drop onto the outer bank. There was no rule for
it; the DM anchored to `verb.exert` (jump) with two knob changes: `dc` (re-derived tier: Hard, because
the chain turns a Beyond drop into a controlled swing) and `stakes` (Dire: a 20-ft fall). The ruling was
logged: signature `verb.exert+dc:tier_rederived+stakes`. A week later, at a mill, the player says "I
swing across the millrace on the hoist rope." `find_rulings(verb.exert)` returns it; the facts match
(a rope swing replacing an unjumpable gap), so the DM reuses **Hard** and **Dire**. The rope is wet: that
is a new fact, handled as a snag (Precision −2), not as a departure from the precedent.

---

cards.title: The pipeline and its record
cards.body: ### 01.1 The pipeline and its record

cards.title: One pipeline for every action
cards.body:
**01.1.1 One pipeline for every action.** `[D]` Every declaration by the player, and every attempt by a
non-player entity that the engine resolves with a d20, passes through the eleven steps below, in order,
producing one frame (00.13) per beat. No chapter may add a judgment step outside the pipeline
(00.13.1); a chapter's own rule plugs into the pipeline as an **anchor** (01.5), a **license** (01.3),
a **clock** (01.14.6), a **cost form** (01.13) or a **delivery table** (01.10).

| # | Step | Kind | Question it answers | Output (frame fields) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | PARSE | `[J:enum]` | What is wanted, what is done, how many beats? | `beat.{intent, method, assertion, shape, parent_beat}` |
| 2 | GATE | `[J:enum]` + `[D]` | May this be attempted at all? | `gate.{class, verb, license, mode}` |
| 3 | NECESSITY | `[J:flag]` | Does it need a roll? | `necessity.{roll, reason}` |
| 4 | ANCHOR | `[J:enum]` + `[D]` | Which rule is it most like? | `anchor.{rule_id, deltas, precedent}` |
| 5 | FRAME | `[J:enum]` `[J:flag]` `[J:rung]` + `[D]` | How hard, how dangerous, how much? | attribute, deed_tag, traits, obstacle, levers, snags, stakes, reach, threatened cost, modifier, odds |
| 6 | OFFER | `[N]` + `[D]` | Does the player commit? | `offer.{shown_at, choice}` |
| 7 | ROLL | `[D]` | What did the die say? | `roll`, `degree`, `near_miss` |
| 8 | READ | `[D]` | How much was achieved, what is due? | `success_at_cost_taken`, `delivered.reach`, cost severities |
| 9 | DELIVER | `[D]` + `[J:enum]` | Which parts of a compound intent landed? | `delivered.{units, items}` |
| 10 | CONSEQUENCE | `[J:enum]` + `[D]` | Which cost form, which method consequences, what next? | `costs`, `method_consequences` |
| 11 | RECORD | `[D]` | Is everything in state before narration? | `state_writes`, `evidence`, `ruling` |

Steps 1–6 cost nothing and may be repeated freely: a player who changes method at OFFER re-enters at
PARSE with the new method. From ROLL on, the frame is immutable except for READ, DELIVER, CONSEQUENCE and
RECORD fields (00.13.2). Narration happens after RECORD and restates only what the store holds (INV-2).
[C:VII; C:P8; C:P17; R7 §4.0; R4 §7.1; R: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.19519]

cards.title: The beat
cards.body:
**01.1.2 The beat.** `[D]` [DL-00A-19; DL-01-20; revision: I-065] A **beat** is one method, aimed at one target (an entity, an obstacle, or a
question), intending one change. A turn (06) may hold several beats; a declaration may hold several beats;
one beat is never split across two frames except by the partial-license split of 01.3.4. The beat's
`actor` is the entity whose method it is; the beat's `target` must be resolved to an id before GATE
(01.2.5).

cards.title: No roll without a committed frame
cards.body:
**01.1.3 No roll without a committed frame.** `[D]` [DL-00A-23; C:P13; revision: I-065] `roll_check(frame_id)` refuses unless the frame
passes every validation of 00.13.2 and of PR-01-2 step 12: gate class G1 or G2 (or an accepted G3
fallback) with the verb or license id present; every lever and snag citing an established fact that
existed before the declaration; stakes set; `lethal` legal; a threatened cost declared when stakes are
Risky or Dire; offer choice `commit` (or `auto` under 01.7.4). *Invariant INV-5* [SG-08].

cards.title: What the DM supplies to the pipeline
cards.body:
**01.1.4 What the DM supplies to the pipeline.** `[D]` [DL-00A-02; C:I; revision: I-065] Ids, enum values, rungs, flags, the player's own
stated quantities, and short text (intent, method, reasons, fictional forms). Never a DC, modifier,
odds, harm amount, tick count, duration or price (INV-3; 00.14.3). Where this chapter says "the DM
picks", the pick is always from a closed list defined here or in data.

cards.title: PARSE
cards.body: ### 01.2 PARSE

cards.title: Intent, method, assertion
cards.trigger: the player (or the DM, for an NPC's attempt) declares an action
cards.license_check: none (PARSE precedes GATE)
decisions: 1. Split the declaration into three fields [J:enum over sentence parts]: INTENT — what the player wants to be true afterward. True only when the words state or clearly imply a change in the world. False for how it is done. METHOD — what the character physically, verbally or magically does. True only for observable acts. False for thoughts, feelings, reasons and results. ASSERTION — anything stated as fact or outcome ("it's a cheap lock", "and he falls", "since he's half asleep"). True for every clause that claims a fact, a probability, or a result. Default for an ambiguous clause: ASSERTION.

2. If INTENT is unstated [J:flag] "Does exactly one intent follow from the method in this scene?" True only when a single change is the obvious purpose. If true, state it ("Taking that as: you want him to let you in"). If false, ask (01.2.4).
cards.computation: none
narration_may_not_imply: that an asserted fact or outcome is true
cards.worst_case: a result-clause read as method (e.g. "I kill it" treated as done). Bounded because method never produces outcomes by itself — every outcome passes GATE→READ; the assertion field is audited against state (class iv).
examples: inside: "I pick the lock with my knife" → method: pick with knife; intent: door open. outside: "It's just a cheap lock" → assertion (creates nothing). non-example: "I quickly hop the wall and succeed" — "and succeed" is an assertion; the hop is the method; nothing about success is decided (CoC-Seduce "omission" framing, 6.99% false-pass rate in the literature).
cards.body:
**01.2.1 Intent, method, assertion.** `[J:enum]`

```
Trigger [T]:        the player (or the DM, for an NPC's attempt) declares an action
Loads in:           core
License check:      none (PARSE precedes GATE)
Decisions (J):      1. Split the declaration into three fields [J:enum over sentence parts]:
                       INTENT — what the player wants to be true afterward. True only when the words
                         state or clearly imply a change in the world. False for how it is done.
                       METHOD — what the character physically, verbally or magically does. True only
                         for observable acts. False for thoughts, feelings, reasons and results.
                       ASSERTION — anything stated as fact or outcome ("it's a cheap lock", "and he
                         falls", "since he's half asleep"). True for every clause that claims a fact,
                         a probability, or a result. Default for an ambiguous clause: ASSERTION.
                    2. If INTENT is unstated [J:flag] "Does exactly one intent follow from the method in
                       this scene?" True only when a single change is the obvious purpose. If true,
                       state it ("Taking that as: you want him to let you in"). If false, ask (01.2.4).
Computation [D]:    none
Stakes:             none (no roll)
State writes:       frame.beat.intent, .method, .assertion (assertion is context only: INV-9),
                    .change {kind, slots} (01.2.7) [revision: R2-H]
Narration may not imply: that an asserted fact or outcome is true
Worst case (J):     a result-clause read as method (e.g. "I kill it" treated as done). Bounded because
                    method never produces outcomes by itself — every outcome passes GATE→READ; the
                    assertion field is audited against state (class iv).
Examples:           inside: "I pick the lock with my knife" → method: pick with knife; intent: door
                    open. outside: "It's just a cheap lock" → assertion (creates nothing).
                    non-example: "I quickly hop the wall and succeed" — "and succeed" is an assertion;
                    the hop is the method; nothing about success is decided (CoC-Seduce "omission"
                    framing, 6.99% false-pass rate in the literature).
Anchor:             no
Basis:              [C:VII] [R4 SG-06; R4 §3.3 W2] [R7 §4.0 step 1] [R3 01.8] [R: https://thealexandrian.net/wordpress/37960/roleplaying-games/art-of-rulings-part-2-intention-and-method]
```

A player's *reason* why something should work ("the guard owes me", "fire beats ice") is an assertion
unless it names an established fact id; if it proposes a new fact, it is a World-Fact Oracle question
(01.15) that PARSE queues ahead of the beat (00.6.7, SG-06). A player's *internal monologue* ("I feel
the old anger rise") creates no beat.

cards.title: Splitting beats
cards.worst_case: a wrong shape changes how many rolls resolve the intent, not whether it is possible; the OFFER shows the structure before any commitment (class ii). [R7 §4.0 step 1, §3.3 F7; R3 01.7; R4 §9 01 #7]
cards.body:
**01.2.2 Splitting beats.** `[J:enum]` A declaration becomes one beat per distinct (method, target,
intended change). Test: *"If one part failed, could the other part still be attempted as described?"*
Yes → separate beats. No → one beat. Each beat carries one typed intended change (01.2.7): a message with two
changes is two beats, so no part is lost ("grab the purse and punch her" is `take` and `harm`) [revision: R2-H;
DL-01-34]. A step or gesture that only accompanies another act is part of that act's
beat (00.12.6) [revision: R2-G; I-171]. Each beat is then classified by **shape**:

| Shape | True only when | False for | Resolved by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `single` | one method, one target, one change | — | the pipeline once |
| `sequential` | a later beat depends on an earlier beat's result ("throw sand, *then* slide under") | beats that merely happen in the same turn | 01.14.1 |
| `repeated` | the same method against the same kind of target, N times ("shoot it ten times", "stab again and again") | one sustained effort toward a single result (that is `extended`) | 01.14.3 |
| `bundled` | one act seeks several distinct pieces of information or several distinct results ("is it a demon, does it have a weakness, is it intelligent?"; "disarm him and knock him down") | several acts (split them instead) | 01.10 (DELIVER) |
| `conditional` | "if X, then Y", where X is a fact or an earlier result | a plain sequence | 01.14.4 |
| `extended` | the intent cannot honestly be achieved by one attempt in one time unit of the current mode (search a library, learn a tongue, dig a tunnel, calm a riot) | a hard single attempt (that is a high tier) | 01.14.6 (clock) |

Default when uncertain between `single` and `extended`: `single` if the result could plausibly be known
within the mode's time per beat (00.7.3), else `extended`. Default between `bundled` and several beats:
several beats (each with its own roll; this never grants more than the bundle would). *Worst case (J):* a
wrong shape changes how many rolls resolve the intent, not whether it is possible; the OFFER shows the
structure before any commitment (class ii). [R7 §4.0 step 1, §3.3 F7; R3 01.7; R4 §9 01 #7]

cards.title: At most three beats resolve per declaration
cards.body:
**01.2.3 At most three beats resolve per declaration.** `[D]` A declaration yielding more than three
beats resolves the first three in the player's order; the DM restates the rest as queued ("Then, if
that works: the seal") and confirms them at the next declaration. In conflict mode, ch.06's action
economy also limits beats per turn; a beat that would exceed the actions left is queued to the next
turn, never compressed. Reason: one declaration must not become many effects without a decision point
(WoW's global cooldown; Story-Engine's action-unit cap) [R3 01.7; R4 §9 01 #7].

cards.title: At most one clarifying question
cards.worst_case: a wrong assumed reading reaches OFFER, where the player sees it and can change it for free (class ii).
cards.body:
**01.2.4 At most one clarifying question.** `[J:flag]` The DM asks one clarifying question only when
*"Would the answer change the gate class, the anchor, or the stakes?"* is true. Otherwise the DM states
the reading it is assuming, in one sentence, and continues; the player may correct it at OFFER at no
cost. Reason: models that assume silently "do not recover", while a stated assumption is correctable
[R: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06120; R7 §4.0 step 1]. *Worst case (J):* a wrong assumed reading reaches
OFFER, where the player sees it and can change it for free (class ii).

cards.title: The target is resolved before GATE
cards.worst_case: the default picks the wrong one of several candidates; the OFFER names the target before commitment, so the player corrects it at no cost (class ii). [integration: 00.2.3 audit] [R3 01.9; R: ChatRPG v1 "self-inflicted trip" failure, R3 FP6]
cards.body:
**01.2.5 The target is resolved before GATE.** `[J:enum]` + `[D]` A beat's target must be one id, or one unnamed description of people or things present (01.2.7)
[revision: R2-I; DL-12-97]. If
the player's words plus relationship-state (06) leave exactly one legal candidate, it is that one; if
several, the stated default applies (in conflict: the nearest engaged foe; otherwise: the most recently
mentioned addressable element of the right kind); if none fits, ask (this counts as the one clarifying
question). A beat never resolves against an unresolved target, and self-harm is never narrated unless a
resolved result licenses it (a critical-failure cost). *Worst case (J):* the default picks the wrong one of
several candidates; the OFFER names the target before commitment, so the player corrects it at no cost
(class ii). [integration: 00.2.3 audit] [R3 01.9; R: ChatRPG v1 "self-inflicted trip" failure, R3 FP6]

cards.title: Neutral restatement
cards.body:
**01.2.6 Neutral restatement.** `[D]` Before GATE the DM writes the beat as a neutral one-line
restatement ("Wren tries to open the guild lock with a knife tip") into `beat.method`. GATE, NECESSITY
and FRAME read the restatement, never the player's dramatic phrasing: framing measurably moves model
decisions [R1 01.B; R: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18566], and the neutral line is what the ruling ledger
stores. The restatement ends with the beat's typed change in plain words ("…, to take the purse from Murzak"), and the
OFFER shows it, so a wrong kind or slot is fixed for free before anything is spent (01.2.7) [revision: R2-H; DL-01-34].

cards.title: The typed intended change
cards.worst_case: a wrong kind or slot — the OFFER and the restatement show it in plain words ("Taking: the purse, from Murzak") and the player fixes it for free before anything is spent (class ii); after commit, a misread beat is taken back by 12.5.8 (class ii). *Evidence:* ROUND3-ANALYSIS S4: "take the purse" succeeded (18 vs 10) and nothing moved the purse; a punch in a two-part message vanished.
cards.body:
**01.2.7 The typed intended change.** `[J:enum]` + `[D]` [DL-01-34; revision: R2-H] Each beat carries one **typed
intended change**: what the player wants to be different afterward (01.2.1's INTENT), as one kind from a closed list
with typed slots (`resolution.yaml#intended_change`). Slots take ids from scope (the Reader's view: the scene's and
the spotlight's entities) or a place the PC knows. A person or thing slot (`whom`, `what`) may instead hold an
**unnamed description** ("the refugees", "the other carters", "the queue") [revision: R2-I; DL-12-97]: a change on it
applies as a scene fact about the description ("the refugees are willing to talk"), and the narrator voices whoever
speaks for it. There is no group entity and no spokesperson; only when the description becomes consequential (it
holds a clue) do the case and casting pick an individual (12.14.13).

| Kind | Slots | On success, resolution applies |
|---|---|---|
| `take` | item; from (a person, place or container) | the item's holder becomes the actor |
| `give` | item; to (a person) | the item's holder becomes the recipient (one who refuses it is a Talk) |
| `move_to` | place or band, or a person or thing present; who (default the actor) | the position: the place, or beside the person or thing in one beat (an approach, 01.4.1); in a conflict, bands toward or away (PR-06-4) [revision: R2-I] |
| `open` / `close` | thing (a door, lock, container or way) | the thing's state |
| `learn` | topic or entity | delivered items (01.10; PR-12-10; 15.9) |
| `persuade_to` | person; act | the agreement (15.3; `npc.<id>.agreed`) |
| `restrain` / `free` | person | held, restrained or pinned (T-12-18's Grapple rows) / the hold ends |
| `harm` | person or thing | harm and conditions (ch.06, ch.07) |
| `hide` | who or item; from whom | hidden (Sneak, 01.18.13) |
| `make` | item kind; from | a made or mended thing (Handle; ch.08 crafting) |
| `none` | — | a beat that seeks no change in the world (a look around, Ready, Help: their own rules write) |

1. **Choose** `[J:enum]` at PARSE (12.2.2 decision 3): the kind and its slots, from the restatement, the verb and the
   ids in scope. A message with two changes is two beats (01.2.2). **Before framing** `[D]` [revision: R2-I;
   DL-01-36]: a change **already true** in the store (the actor already holds the item; `npc.<id>.agreed` already
   holds the same act; the door is already open; the actor is already beside the target) is certain: no roll and no
   OFFER, the beat narrated as already so (01.4.1). A change with **no valid target** is settled before anything is
   framed: by a description (above), else by asking "who?" (01.2.5's clarifying question). A roll is never offered
   whose success would have nothing to deliver.
2. **Apply on success** `[D]` at RECORD (PR-01-3 step 5); **reach scales it** (`intended_change.reach`): delivered
   reach 1 gives the partial form (`take`: a hand on it, still contested; `move_to`: part of the way, one band in a conflict;
   `persuade_to`: a smaller act; `restrain`: a grip; `learn`: 01.10's count), reach 2 or more the whole change, and
   the kind's extra where it has one (`restrain`: restrained at 3, pinned at 4, T-12-18). A failure applies nothing;
   a success at a cost applies the change and its cost, and the cost never undoes it (01.9.3). A change code cannot
   apply (the slot is not in scope; the item is not where the slot says) is not applied, and the RESULT says why
   ("the purse is not on her"), so 12.3.6 can explain it.
3. **Cite** `[D]`: the applied change is a must-name record line (12.14.12); narration that omits it fails coverage
   (12.3.1a), and narration of a different change fails the outcome check (12.3.1b, blocking item 1).
4. **One table among them**: T-12-18's per-verb scene writes (a Grapple's hold, a Force's knock-down, a Move's
   bands) are the scene-state face of `restrain`, `harm` and `move_to`, and stay the table for the slots they write.

**Design note (Laya-ready).** Choosing the kind and slots is a short-input decision with at most 20 options (the
beat's restatement, its verb and the ids in scope in; one kind and its slot ids out), logged with its inputs
(`intended_change.log`), so a small trained classifier can replace the model call later without changing this rule.
*Worst case (J):* a wrong kind or slot — the OFFER and the restatement show it in plain words ("Taking: the purse,
from Murzak") and the player fixes it for free before anything is spent (class ii); after commit, a misread beat is
taken back by 12.5.8 (class ii). *Evidence:* ROUND3-ANALYSIS S4: "take the purse" succeeded (18 vs 10) and nothing
moved the purse; a punch in a two-part message vanished.

cards.title: GATE — may this be attempted at all?
cards.body: ### 01.3 GATE — may this be attempted at all?

cards.title: Gate classification
cards.trigger: a beat leaves PARSE with a resolved target
cards.license_check: this rule IS the license check
decisions: 1. Gate class [J:enum], first match wins (the test order is itself the tie-break): G0 Question — true only when the player asks about the world or the character's knowledge and describes no act (out-of-fiction questions included). False when any observable act is described (then the act is gated and any embedded unknown fact is queued to the Oracle). G4 Impossible — true only when one of the four G4 tests (01.3.7) holds. G1 Basic — true only when the method is within the `covers` list of one of the fifteen verbs in data/basic_verbs.yaml AND not within that verb's `excludes` AND the sensitive-upgrade test (01.3.3) is false. False for anything the admission test fails ("could any able-bodied adult in the setting attempt this with no training and a real chance?"). G2 Licensed — true only when the actor HOLDS a license (00.6.1 license state) whose literal `scope`, at the held grade, covers this method on this target. The DM must cite its id. A license not in the actor's state is not held. G3 Unlicensed — everything else: beyond the basic verbs, not covered by any held license, but possible for someone in the setting. Default when uncertain between G1 and G3, or between G2 and G3: G3 (SG-05).

2. For G2 only, mode [J:enum]: normal (inside scope) | stretch | emulate (01.3.5). Default: normal if the scope text covers it word for word; otherwise the license must declare stretch/emulate and pass 01.3.5's tests; if neither passes → G3.
cards.computation: the engine validates that the cited verb or license id exists, is held (lifecycle not retired, not expired, not forbidden by an active `restrict` effect) and belongs to the actor. A cited license the actor lacks → refusal → G3.
state_writes: on G3/G4 a ruling record (g3_redirect / g4)
narration_may_not_imply: that a G3 or G4 method was attempted, partly worked, or "almost" worked
cards.worst_case: a licensed attempt redirected as G3 — the redirect names the license id it checked, so the player can point to the license (class iv); an unlicensed attempt framed as G2 — the frame records the cited license id, which the claim-vs-state audit (ch.12) checks against held licenses (class iv). A basic-verb over-reach (G1 claimed for a licensed method) is caught by the verb's `excludes` list.
examples: inside G1: "I shove the cart into the doorway" (Force: shove). outside G1: "I pick the lock" (Force excludes lockpicking → G2 if held, else G3). inside G2: Wren (native Common) haggles in Common. outside G2: haggling in Ogrish with no Ogrish license → G3; crude fallback: gesture. non-example (persuasive but unlicensed): "I'm a hunter, so obviously I can read these old elven runes — hunters see signs everywhere." The reason is an assertion; reading an unknown script is excluded from Observe; no language license is held → G3, however well argued (WE-01-16).

**Computed, not proposed** [revision: R2-C] [DL-01-30]. The engine runs the tests above as a pure function of the
beat's verb, method facets and target (12.2.2), the actor's held licenses, the verb's `excludes`, active
conditions and any cited G4 fact (00.12.3). No role proposes the gate class or the license; a sheet knack is an
edge, never a gate. The judgment left is PARSE's verb and facets, whose worst case is the wrong card,
named in the OFFER and changed for free (class ii).

cards.title: What counts as a license
cards.body:
**01.3.2 What counts as a license.** `[D]` [DL-00A-19; C:V; revision: I-065] A license is any held entry of the 00.12.1 schema: an
ability (`ab.*`), a spell, a calling capability, a training license (`lic.training.*`), a language
(`lic.lang.*` at a grade), an item property granting a license while equipped, a rank, a
condition-granted license, or a **fact license** (`kind: fact`) — an established narrative fact that
permits a method ("the smith gave you the forge key": `lic.fact.forge_key`). A fact license exists only
if it was written to state *before* the declaration (by narration under write-on-mention, by the Oracle,
or by a ruling); a player's claim that such a fact exists is an Oracle question, never a license (00.6.7,
INV-9). Rolls never create licenses (INV-7). An entity holds at most one instance of a license id
(INV-13).

cards.title: The literal-reading rule and the sensitive-upgrade test
cards.worst_case: an ordinary act (listening at a door) sent to G3 — the redirect's fallback is the basic verb itself, so the player loses one sentence (class ii).
cards.body:
**01.3.3 The literal-reading rule and the sensitive-upgrade test.** `[J:flag]` A license covers exactly
its `scope`, read literally at the held grade, and nothing more (INV-8). Before classifying a beat G1 or
G2, the DM asks: *"Would this beat give the actor more perception, memory, mobility, control, access,
awareness or freedom than an ordinary person has in this situation?"* These are the seven dimensions in
which generous narration produces impossible outcomes [R1 01.B; R1 #4; NCP-Bench auditor rule]. True
only when success would let the actor sense what cannot be sensed, know what was never learned, move
where bodies cannot, compel a mind or body, enter what is sealed, detect what magic hides, or escape
what physically binds — beyond what a basic verb's `covers` list states. If true, the beat is **not
G1**: it needs a license whose scope names that upgrade, else G3 or G4. False for ordinary uses of the
senses, memory and movement listed under Observe, Recall and Move. Uncertain → true. *Worst case (J):* an
ordinary act (listening at a door) sent to G3 — the redirect's fallback is the basic verb itself, so the
player loses one sentence (class ii).

cards.title: Splitting a beat that a license covers only partly
cards.worst_case: a clause wrongly held covered grants one beat's worth of the license's own literal effect — never more than the license can ever do (class i). [R7 §4.0 step 2, §5 Ex.3, Ex.12; 00.12.2]
cards.body:
**01.3.4 Splitting a beat that a license covers only partly.** `[D]` + `[J:enum]` When a held license's
scope covers part of a beat (the fire harm, but not the smoke; the lock, but not the ward on it), the
beat is split before framing:
1. The covered part is G2 under that license and is framed or applied exactly as its effects state.
2. Each uncovered part is re-gated alone: G1 if a basic verb covers it (its own frame, or a separate cost
   source inside the same frame), else G3 or G4.
3. If an uncovered part is G3/G4 and the intent cannot be reached without it, the whole intent is
   redirected (01.3.6); the covered part is still offered as what the license *does* allow ("your
   resistance will let you reach into the coals; it will not cool them").
4. Narration describes each part by its own gate: the license doing exactly its text, the basic-verb part
   succeeding or failing on its own roll, nothing more. "The flames part around you" from a harm
   reduction is an embellishment and is forbidden (INV-8; the probe's invented cold vulnerability).
Which parts exist is `[J:enum]` over the license's scope clauses (each clause is covered or not); default
for a clause that "sort of" applies: not covered. *Worst case (J):* a clause wrongly held covered grants one
beat's worth of the license's own literal effect — never more than the license can ever do (class i).
[R7 §4.0 step 2, §5 Ex.3, Ex.12; 00.12.2]

cards.title: Stretch, emulate and crude fallback
cards.worst_case: a wrongly allowed stretch gives one beat at a raised DC and capped reach — worse than a licensed use by construction, and logged with the principle sentence it relied on (class i/iv). [R2 #4 (Mother of Learning structured vs unstructured); R7 §4.4; R: https://www.d20srd.org/srd/skills/useMagicDevice.htm; R7 §2.14 (Beginner's Luck); 00.12.4]
cards.body:
**01.3.5 Stretch, emulate and crude fallback.** `[J:flag]` + `[D]` These are the only three priced ways
past a license's literal scope. Each is looked up in the license entry (00.12.1), never invented, and
each is shown in the OFFER with its price.

| Mode | Who may use it | Legal only when (all true) | Price (from the entry; applied by the engine) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **stretch** | a holder of license L | (a) L's `stretch` is not null; (b) `[J:flag]` *"Does the new use perform the same operation that L's `principle` sentence names, only on a different target, scale or form?"* — true only when the principle's verb and its object category both still apply (a principle "push metal away from you" stretches to pushing a metal door; not to pulling, not to pushing wood); (c) the stretched use grants none of the seven sensitive upgrades (01.3.3) that L's scope does not already grant | DC + `stretch.dc_shift` (shown as its own line); Focus + `stretch.cost_add`; reach capped at `stretch.reach_cap` |
| **emulate** | a holder of a *domain* license D | (a) D's `emulate` is not null; (b) the technique is in `emulate.allowed_for`; (c) a fact records that the actor *witnessed* the technique (00.12.4); (d) the actor does not already hold it | DC + `emulate.dc_shift`; Focus × `emulate.cost_mult`; reach capped at `emulate.reach_cap`; on a critical failure `emulate.crit_fail` applies in place of the READ cost when it is worse; success ticks `emulate.learn_clock` by delivered reach and grants nothing else (INV-7) |
| **crude fallback** | anyone, on a G3 beat | the license that would cover the beat has `crude_fallback` not `none`, and the player accepts it at OFFER | a new frame on the fallback verb; DC = that verb's DC for this obstacle (01.6.4) + `dc_shift` (0, 5 or 10, shown as "improvised +N"); reach capped at `reach_cap`; the listed `consequence` (e.g. `trait.sense.loud`) becomes a method consequence |

Tie-break for stretch (b) and emulate (c): false (SG-05, "does this grant something? → no"). A license
entry missing one of these fields reads as `stretch: null`, `emulate: null`, `crude_fallback: none`, and
the gap is logged as a `rule_conflict` ruling for ch.05. When **no license entry in data** covers a G3
method at all, the redirect names the deed branch that would hold such a license (`deed.arcane`,
`deed.guile.thievery`…) and the generic acquisition types `mentor` and `recognition`, offers the nearest
basic verb, and logs a `rule_conflict` ruling so ch.05/13 can author the license. *Worst case (J):* a wrongly
allowed stretch gives one beat at a raised DC and capped reach — worse than a licensed use by
construction, and logged with the principle sentence it relied on (class i/iv). [R2 #4 (Mother of
Learning structured vs unstructured); R7 §4.4; R: https://www.d20srd.org/srd/skills/useMagicDevice.htm;
R7 §2.14 (Beginner's Luck); 00.12.4]

cards.title: The redirect: every refusal is a lookup that leaves a path
cards.body:
**01.3.6 The redirect: every refusal is a lookup that leaves a path.** `[D]` + `[N]` A G3 or G4 result is
spoken in this fixed four-part shape, fiction first, with the out-of-fiction line in the codex layer
(00.1.7):
1. **Acknowledge the intent** in the player's own terms ("You want the door open without waking the
   keep").
2. **Why, in one sentence of fiction**, naming what is missing: the license (G3: "the wards are guild-cut;
   nothing in your hands knows how to read them") or the fact (G4: "he has no sister, and he'd know it on
   sight") [integration: I-024]. The out-of-fiction line names the id checked (`lic.training.guile_thievery`; `npc.tam_harlan.siblings`).
3. **What is possible now**: the crude fallback if there is one (with its odds on request, through a free
   OFFER), else the nearest basic verb that serves the same intent, else the nearest achievable intent. At
   least one concrete option is always given (P16).
4. **How the capability could be gained** (G3 only): at least one `acquisition_path` of the license,
   stated as a fact of the world ("a locksmith or a thief could teach you"), plus the recognition path if
   the entry lists one.
A redirected or declined beat spends **no time, no action and no Focus** unless the player accepts an
alternative (00.12.3). The redirect is logged (`kind: g3_redirect` or `g4`). *Acceptance test*
(NCP-Bench's player-input rule): the response acknowledges the intent, offers concrete follow-through,
never substitutes a different action for the player, and never silently resets a state the player's
action implied [R1 01.B; R1 T-2]. Forbidden redirect forms: a bare "you can't"; "nothing happens" with no
option; an alternative the player did not ask for narrated as already taken. [C:VII; C:P16; R7 §2.4
(Dungeon World Ritual: "yes, if…"); R1 T-6]

cards.title: G4 — impossible
cards.trigger: GATE tests G4 for a beat
decisions: 1. CONTRADICTS A FACT [J:flag]: "Does success require an established fact to be false?" True only when a fact id in state is contradicted (the guard has no sister; the door is bricked) [integration: I-024]. Cite the fact id.

2. CONTRADICTS CANON [J:flag]: "Is this impossible for anyone in the setting, per the region's canon_impossible list (the world seed's, 12.16.5, or a pre-made setting's) or an established world law?" True only when the list or a fact says so (no mortal flies unaided). Never true merely because it is unusual.

3. ZERO REACH [J:flag]: "Do two or more effect factors stand against this method reaching this intent, with nothing offsetting them?" Factors (closed list): POTENCY — the method cannot affect this kind of target (playing dead to hungry wolves; words to a thing with no mind); QUALITY — the means is categorically inadequate (a knife against a stone wall); SCALE — the target outsizes or outnumbers the method by a whole category (one voice against a rioting square). An offset is an established fact or license that cancels one factor (a crowd on your side offsets scale). Exactly one uncancelled factor → not G4: reach is capped at Limited instead (01.6.10 test 2) [verification: V2c-001]. Counting [D] [revision: I-073]: POTENCY is **total** when the target cannot be affected by this kind of method at all (no mind for Talk or Handle, no body for Grapple or Strike: a shadow, a voice); a total POTENCY counts as **two** factors, so alone it is G4 unless an offset cancels one of them (a license that lets words move a thing, 05). Partial POTENCY (the wolves can be swayed, just not by this) is one factor. **One reason supplies one factor**: the fact that makes POTENCY (words; a gate has no mind) cannot be cited again as QUALITY or SCALE. A listener behind the gate is a different target: re-PARSE with that target.

4. FORBIDDEN BY CONDITION [D]: an active condition or `restrict` effect forbids the verb, method, sense or license (00.9.3b). The engine answers from state. Default when uncertain on 1–3: false — fall through to G1/G2/G3 and roll. This is the one gate test whose tie-break favors the attempt: wrongly calling something impossible builds the wall goal 1 forbids, while wrongly allowing an attempt still has to beat an honest DC on the dice.
cards.computation: no roll; ruling logged (kind g4)
state_writes: any Oracle answer that established the contradicting fact
narration_may_not_imply: that the attempt was made, partly worked, or could work with more effort
cards.worst_case: a possible attempt declared impossible — the redirect still offers the nearest achievable intent and the ruling is reviewable (class iv); an impossible attempt allowed — it is framed at its tier (usually Very hard or Legendary) and must beat the dice (class i).
examples: inside: "I leap the 30-ft chasm" (canon: tier Beyond). outside: "I leap the 12-ft gap from a running start" (Hard; roll). inside: calm a river the Oracle said has no spirit (fact). outside: calm the river spirit the Oracle said exists (Talk, G1; reach capped Limited by scale). inside: "I shout the barred gate open" — words to a thing with no mind: total POTENCY, two factors → G4; the redirect offers the bar (Exert) or whoever is behind the gate (Talk) [revision: I-073]. outside: "I shout at the guard to open the gate" — a mind; G1, roll. non-example: "Nobody could climb that sheer ice, so I anchor my rope-dart and haul myself up" — not a G4 request; a new method (Exert with a tool lever).

cards.title: G0 — questions about the world
cards.worst_case: a free answer that should have needed a Recall roll — one item of common knowledge (class i).
cards.body:
**01.3.8 G0 — questions about the world.** `[D]` + `[J:flag]` [DL-00A-19; DL-01-13; C:VII; revision: I-065] A G0 beat is answered by the first match:
(1) from state, through the character's permitted slice (sealed content is never returned, INV-10);
(2) from the character's own established knowledge — free (00.12.6); (3) if the answer requires
*finding out* (looking, searching, recalling specialist lore, reading a person), it is not G0 but an
Observe or Recall beat (re-enter PARSE with that method); (4) if the fact is **unestablished** and **not
settled by canon or scene logic**, the World-Fact Oracle (01.15). An out-of-fiction question ("what are
my odds if I climb?", "how was that ruled?") is answered from the codex and a free OFFER and takes no
fictional time. The test between (2) and (3) is `[J:flag]` *"Would the character already know this
without doing anything?"* True only for common knowledge of the character's origin, culture or trade
(Recall's `covers`) and facts the character has learned. Uncertain → false (a Recall beat, which may
roll). *Worst case (J):* a free answer that should have needed a Recall roll — one item of common knowledge
(class i).

cards.title: "Yes, and" and default-deny work at different layers
cards.body:
**01.3.9 "Yes, and" and default-deny work at different layers.** `[N]` The DM says yes to *premises and
approaches* — any method a basic verb or held license covers is attempted, however strange — and says no
only to *capabilities* the character does not hold, and then only through the 01.3.6 redirect ("yes,
but"). These are not competing instructions: an unlicensed capability is exactly the "breaks the rules"
case in which improv craft itself reserves a no, and "yes, but — here is what you can do" is Principle
VII's required redirect [R1 T-6; R1 M-10].

cards.title: NECESSITY — does it need a roll?
cards.body: ### 01.4 NECESSITY — does it need a roll?

cards.title: The roll test
cards.trigger: a beat is gated G1 or G2 (or an accepted G3 fallback)
cards.license_check: as gated
decisions: 1. UNCERTAIN [J:flag]: "Given the established facts, could this method, done by this actor now, realistically fail?" True unless the obstacle is Trivial: its obstacle class's base is `trivial` (01.6.5; no class fits: anyone, in these conditions, succeeds every time, T-01-2 rung 0); a nudge never crosses this line [revision: R2-C]. The actor's competence never makes an obstacle Trivial — that is what the modifier is for.

2. COSTLY [J:flag]: "Would failure cost something, change the situation, or use up a chance that cannot be retaken freely?" True when any running clock listens to this beat or to time, when an aware party would ACT on a failure (hostile, or the act is against their wishes; mere presence is not enough) [revision: R2-C], when a hazard is present, when failure would alert, break, spend, or close a door, or when the intent is contested by anyone. False only when failure leaves the situation exactly as it was and the attempt can be repeated at leisure.

3. RIDING [J:flag] (01.4.2): "Is this the same obstacle, same anchor and same approach as a resolved beat whose ride is still active?" ROLL = UNCERTAIN and COSTLY and not RIDING. Tie-break for 1 and 2: TRUE (roll). Tie-break for 3: FALSE (roll).
cards.computation: necessity.{roll, reason}; reason ∈ uncertain_and_costly | riding | trivial | good_idea | impossible | take_the_time | certain_with_cost; a Talk beat whose computed social DC is certain (15.3.10) does not roll [revision: R2-C]
narration_may_not_imply: success that the pipeline did not produce
cards.worst_case: a needless roll (a false check — the rarer error, ~0.08% in the literature, and it costs one die); a skipped roll that should have been made grants one beat's success at Standard reach — bounded because the no-roll paths never grant Great reach, never apply to Dire or lethal frames, never create licenses, and never unseal (class i).
examples: inside (roll): climbing a rough wall while a patrol clock runs (costly: time). outside (no roll): climbing the same wall at noon with nobody about and nothing pressing (take the time, 01.4.4). inside (roll): recalling a rival house's crest under a herald's gaze (a herald who would mark the error). outside: slipping through a market crowd that would not care if you stumbled, with nothing pressing (no roll). outside: recalling your own village's saint's day (free knowledge, 01.3.8). non-example: "This is easy for someone like me, no need to roll" — an assertion; ease is the tier's business, and competence enters as modifier only.
basis: R7 §2.19 Dogs in the Vineyard; §2.14 Burning Wheel

The no-roll classes are closed: **trivial** (01.4.1 decision 1 false), **free activity** (00.12.6),
**riding** (01.4.2), **good idea** (01.4.3), **take the time** (01.4.4), **certain with cost** (01.4.5),
**question** (G0) and **impossible** (G4). Every other gated beat rolls.

**Already true, and approaching** [revision: R2-I; DL-01-36; DL-12-98]: two everyday readings of decision 1, not new
classes. A beat whose typed change (01.2.7) is **already true** in the store cannot fail: it is `trivial`, with no
roll and no OFFER (persuading someone whose `agreed` fact already holds the same request). **Approaching** someone or
something present in the scene, outside a conflict, is Move / open ground: one beat, no roll, no band-by-band steps,
ending beside it (T-12-18), unless something obstructs it (an obstacle on the way, or a hostile watcher who would act
on it, decision 2); then it is framed like any Move. Range bands are tracked step by step only in a conflict (ch.06).

cards.title: Let it ride
cards.worst_case: a legitimately new approach treated as riding — the player names the difference at OFFER and the engine re-checks (class ii). [R: https://thealexandrian.net/wordpress/38313/roleplaying-games/the-art-of-rulings-part-8-let-it-ride; R7 §2.13 (Year Zero no-retry); C:P17]
cards.body:
**01.4.2 Let it ride.** `[J:flag]` + `[D]` One resolved beat settles one obstacle for one approach. The
engine stores a **ride** record `{actor, obstacle_id, anchor_id, method_class, degree, facts_at: [fact
ids], until}` at RECORD. A new beat against the same obstacle with the same anchor and approach does
**not** roll; the stored result stands — a success keeps covering the whole effort (one Sneak covers the
common room and the kitchen), a failure stays a failure. The ride ends, and a new roll becomes legal, when
the first of these holds (checked by the engine against state):
1. the **approach changes** — a different anchor, or a different attribute-bearing method on the same
   anchor (climb by strength → climb with a grapnel);
2. a **new fact** that is a lever for this beat (00.3.9) was established after the ride began;
3. the **circumstances change** — a fact the ride's frame cited is superseded, or the obstacle's stored DC,
   stakes source or threatened cost changes;
4. the ride's **interval passes** — for extended beats, the clock's tick interval (01.14.6); otherwise the
   end of the scene;
5. the player **pays the re-attempt cost**: one `cost.time` or `cost.exposure` (player's choice where both
   fit) at the frame's stakes severity (S1 when Safe), paid up front whatever the new roll shows.
"Is this the same obstacle and approach?" is `[J:flag]` — true only when the target id, anchor id and
method class all match; uncertain → true (the failure stands). *Worst case (J):* a legitimately new approach
treated as riding — the player names the difference at OFFER and the engine re-checks (class ii).
[R: https://thealexandrian.net/wordpress/38313/roleplaying-games/the-art-of-rulings-part-8-let-it-ride;
R7 §2.13 (Year Zero no-retry); C:P17]

cards.title: The Good Idea rule
cards.trigger: a player claims (or the DM notices) that the method makes the roll unnecessary
cards.license_check: as gated (G1/G2 only)
decisions: 1. REMOVES THE SOURCE [J:flag]: "Does the method use one or more established facts (cited by id) to remove the obstacle's source of uncertainty entirely, rather than to make overcoming it easier?" True only when, after the cited facts, there is no longer anything to overcome (waiting for the established patrol schedule's gap removes being seen; a lantern at the right angle removes having to search a dark floor). False when the facts only help (a tool, a distraction, a good angle — those are levers).
2. UNOPPOSED [J:flag]: "Is no aware entity actively opposing this beat and no hazard acting on it right now?" True only when state holds no aware opponent, observer or active hazard for the target.

3. BOUNDED [D]: the beat's stakes would be Safe or Risky (not Dire), not lethal, and success would not grant or stretch a license, unseal a sealed fact, generate content (00.11), move standing, or tick a progress clock by more than
2. Good Idea = all three true. Default for 1 and 2 when uncertain: FALSE (roll).
cards.computation: success at Standard reach, no roll, no cost; the beat consumes its normal time; ruling logged (kind good_idea) with the cited fact ids.
narration_may_not_imply: that a rolled-for result (Great reach, a critical) happened
cards.worst_case: one Safe-or-Risky beat succeeds at Standard reach without a roll it should have had — bounded by decision 3 (class i), logged and reusable as precedent (class iv).
examples: inside: the patrol's round is established as "lantern passes every half hour"; Wren waits for it to pass and crosses the empty yard — no one watches (fact: yard empty between rounds) → no roll. outside: same yard, but a sentry on the wall is established (decision 2 false) → Sneak roll; the patrol schedule becomes a Precision lever instead. inside: the ledger's shelf mark was read on the clerk's index card (established); Wren goes straight to shelf 14 → the find needs no search roll. outside: "it's probably filed under the family name" — a guess, not a fact → Observe roll (or an Oracle question about the filing system). non-example (persuasive): "Guards never look up, everyone knows that, so I just walk along the rafters" — a claimed generality is an assertion; if the player wants it as a fact, it is an Oracle question about THESE guards; until answered, Sneak rolls.

cards.title: Take the time
cards.body:
**01.4.4 Take the time.** `[D]` When a beat is UNCERTAIN but not COSTLY (no clock, observer, hazard or
contest), the character succeeds given time: success at Standard reach, no roll, and the beat consumes
**twice** the current mode's time per beat (site: 2 intervals; free: twice the activity's listed
duration; travel: 2 watches; downtime: twice the listed days; conflict: never applies, because a
conflict is always costly). Time passes through `advance_time`, so every boundary runs (INV-15) — which
is exactly how "taking the time" can become costly (an encounter check fires). An obstacle whose tier is
Very hard or Legendary cannot be taken with time: those rungs require a roll whenever attempted, because
"experts often fail" is not a function of patience. [R: 5e "take 20" and PF2e "take your time"
lineage via R7 §2.8; DL-01-09]

cards.title: Certain with cost
cards.body:
**01.4.5 Certain with cost.** `[D]` When the outcome is certain but a known, fixed cost attaches to the
method (reaching bare-handed into coals; swimming through water established as freezing; crossing a
hazard the character cannot avoid), there is no roll: the success applies and the cost applies as a
**method consequence** at the severity its source declares (a hazard's data severity; the fire's stated
harm). This is not a READ cost and cannot be reduced by success-at-cost choices; licenses that reduce the
harm apply literally (01.3.4). [R7 §5 Ex.12]

cards.title: Passive noticing
cards.body:
**01.4.6 Passive noticing.** `[D]` Looking around casually is a free activity (00.12.6); it succeeds
automatically against anything whose **concealment DC** is at or below the character's **notice**:
`notice = 10 + Wits + competence (on the deed tag of the Observe method that would find it) + edge +
status`, computed by the engine (the defense formula of 00.3.8 with Wits). Concealment DCs are stored
on the hidden thing: its tier (a trap's `detect.dc_tier`, a secret door's tier), or, when an entity hides
actively, that entity's Sneak total (rolled by the engine when it hid; stored). The engine compares at
`scene_start`, on entering a new place, and at each `interval` boundary in site mode while the character
is not `cond.distracted`; a pass unseals the thing into the narrator's slice (INV-10) and narration must
mention it that turn. No die is rolled, nothing is shown, and nothing is lost when it fails — an active
Observe beat is always still available. Symmetrically, an NPC's notice is the DC for the PC's Sneak
(00.3.8 opposed defense). [R5 RS-12; R: PF2e secret checks via R5 §1.3; 00.12.6]

cards.title: Secret frames
cards.trigger: an Observe, Recall, or Talk-to-read beat whose target's existence, truth or nature is sealed or undetermined
cards.license_check: as gated
decisions: 1. [J:flag] "Would seeing the die, the DC or the odds tell the player something the character could not know?" True only when the target is sealed (a hidden door, a lie, a forged seal) or undetermined (whether anything is there at all). False for a known obstacle (a visible lock, a wall, a known question with a known answer). Uncertain → true.
cards.computation: frame.secret = true. If the target's existence is undetermined, the engine first asks the Oracle SEALED (01.15.6). The OFFER shows method, attribute, modifier breakdown, stakes, reach and threatened cost, but not the DC, the odds or the d20. The engine rolls; READ and DELIVER run normally; the narrator receives only what the character perceives. Fate cannot be spent on a secret frame (01.16.3). The whole frame becomes `available` in the codex once its target unseals.
cards.stakes: declared as usual (a secret frame still has a threatened cost if Risky or Dire)
narration_may_not_imply: whether a failure was "close"
whether anything was there to find
cards.worst_case: an unnecessary secret frame hides the odds of an ordinary check (the player can still see modifier, stakes and cost; class ii); a needed one skipped leaks one sealed existence-fact through the displayed DC (class iv — the leak is logged and the fact's gate records it).
examples: inside: searching a study for a hidden compartment nobody has established → sealed Oracle (Unlikely) then a secret Observe. outside: searching the same study for the letter the steward said is in the desk (known to exist) → ordinary frame. inside: reading whether the merchant is lying (truth sealed). outside: reading whether the merchant is afraid, when he has been shaking all scene (established). non-example: the player asks to see the DC "to decide whether to bother" on a secret frame — the stakes and cost are the decision information; the DC stays hidden, and asking costs nothing.

cards.title: ANCHOR — which rule is this most like?
cards.body: ### 01.5 ANCHOR — which rule is this most like?

cards.title: Choosing the anchor
cards.trigger: a beat will roll (NECESSITY roll = true) or needs a no-roll ruling
cards.license_check: as gated
decisions: 1. [D] `load_cards(anchors for the beat's verb, deed tags, situation)` returns at most eight candidate anchors from data/anchors.yaml (00.15.3), always including the gated basic verb's own card (01.18) or the license's own rule (G2).

2. [J:enum] pick one: the candidate whose intent verbs name what the beat tries to change AND whose "Covers" includes the method. True only when both match. False when only the surface matches (a shove and a grapple both touch the target: the distinguishing test is "does the actor keep hold? → grapple; target moved away → shove", 01.18). Default when two fit: the more specific one (a chapter sub-rule over a verb card; a license's own rule over a verb card); when none fits: the gated verb's own card with deltas.
cards.computation: frame.anchor.rule_id
narration_may_not_imply: rules the anchor does not contain
cards.worst_case: a near-but-wrong anchor: its degree table and knobs apply instead of the right one's; bounded by the two-change limit and logged for precedent review (class iv).
