cards.title: One character from the first name to a consolidation and beyond
cards.body:
### WE-04-1 One character from the first name to a consolidation and beyond

**Session 2, a long rest at the Ashwood waystation (reflection). The first recognition: a grant.**
03's digest marks `deed.martial.archery` dirty. PR-04-1 step 4 evaluates `call.archer` (`req.narrow.1`):

| Requirement | Needs | Wren | |
|---|---|---|---|
| weighted | ≥ 80 | 84 | ✓ |
| counted | ≥ 8 | 12 (`cnt.defeat` and `cnt.focus`) | ✓ |
| quality events | ≥ 6 | 11 (2 challenging, 9 difficult; 4 routine do not count) | ✓ |
| distinct scenes | ≥ 5 | 8 | ✓ |

Eligible. Confidence (her `recent` at the key is 84, all of it; `weighted(deed)` is 104):
K1 Current `2·84 = 168 ≥ 80` ✓ · K2 Rising `168 ≥ 84` ✓ · K3 Central `5·84 = 420 ≥ 104` ✓ · K4 Leading
(archery is her largest level-2 node) ✓ · K5 Margin `4·84 = 336 ≥ 400` ✗. **Confidence 4.** Currency floor
`4·84 ≥ 80` ✓. Policy (04.4.3): tier 1, narrow, no oath, a free seat, no lineage held, never declined, and the
field is clear (no other `martial` candidate is eligible; the martial × wilds hybrid is far from it) →
**grant**. Session 2 is early for the targets of 04.3.5 (3–5); one seed's luck, two fights at the edge of her
reach in her first ten scenes.

Vehicle (PR-04-3): the family's grant list is V8, V1, V7. Two of her shots at the ford were seen by caravan
guards who lived (`public(wren, deed.martial.archery, fac.caravaners_compact).events = 3`, one noteworthy):
V1's `requires` hold; V8's do not (no hostile scope has two events). The engine returns [V1, V7]; the DM
picks V1.

> The waystation's cook, who was not at the ford, sets down a bowl and looks at the bow propped by the door.
> "So you're the one. Two wagons through and a wyvern in the river, they're saying. *Ford-arrow*, the guards
> call you." She seems to think you knew.
>
> `[RESULT] Changed: calling — Archer, tier 1 (Called), provisional · competence: archery +3 · training
> under archery: trained · capability: The Mark of the Calling · 2 picks · you may set it aside at any rest
> (say "renounce Archer")`
> `[CHOICE] A pick for Archer — (a) Pinning Shot: <literal text> · (b) Steady Draw: <literal text> ·
> (c) Quarry's Mark: <literal text> · (d) keep the pick for later`

State: `callings: [{call.archer, tier 1, provisional, crystallized_by: ev.000052 (the wyvern shot), vehicle:
veh.V1}]`; competence `deed.martial.archery` +3 (her origin's +2 is now the lower entry); `lic.call.mark`;
`recognition_event {kind: first, policy: grant, vehicle: veh.V1, witnesses: [the cook], scope:
[fac.caravaners_compact, loc.ashwood_waystation], epithet_seed: "Shot a wyvern through the eye at the ford
while the wagons crossed"}`. Ch.11 owns what becomes of "Ford-arrow". The three pick candidates are the
eligible abilities whose first tags she has the most evidence on (04.8.4); she takes two over two prompts.

**Session 9. Tier 2 of Archer, voiced by an order's letter.** At a reflection after scene 42 the Archer's
next tier is ready (`req.narrow.2`): weighted 181 ≥ 160; counted 43 ≥ 16; **since** tier 1: quality events
11 ≥ 10, scenes 14 ≥ 8, great deeds at band 2 or higher 11 ≥ 5 (8 of them successes). The since-floor of
quality events is what came last: her weight passed 160 a session earlier. No crisis completed it, so 04.5.8
(c) applies: the next reflection. `institutions_matching(deed.martial, region.ashwood)` returns the
Caravaners' Compact at status +1, which has heard of her (public events 5): V3's requirements hold.

> A letter has been waiting at the waystation three days, sealed with a wheel in blue wax. The Compact
> wants an outrider for the Salt Road before the autumn caravans; it names a wage, and it names you.
>
> `[CHOICE] Recognition — The Order Seeks You Out: Archer, tier 2 (Proven)`
> `  (a) Accept — you gain: archery +4 · Proven (you may teach archery) · 1 pick · when your bow fells a foe
>      at or above your measure, regain 1 Focus (once per scene) · price: service to the Caravaners' Compact
>      as outrider (its duties are shown under Factions) · provisional`
> `  (b) Decline — nothing changes. Refusing the Compact's rider to his face costs one step of its regard;
>      leaving the letter unanswered costs nothing.`
> `  (c) Defer — the letter can be presented at any Compact house until the season after next`

She accepts. The **rank** of outrider and its obligations are ch.11's (`recognition_event.institution`); had
she declined the post, the tier would still be hers at the next rest by V7, at no price beyond the seat
(04.11.1). Twelve evidence-bearing scenes after a grant, a reflection confirms it (04.8.2); with Archer 2
confirmed, `power_band` is 2 [revision: I-037].

**Session 14. Tracker: eligible, and an abstain.** After scene 70, `call.tracker` (key `deed.wilds.tracking`)
is eligible: weighted 84 ≥ 80, counted 11 ≥ 8, quality events 12 (5 challenging), scenes 13. Its confidence is
**0**: recent 30 (K1 `2·30 = 60 < 80`; K2 `60 < 84`), K3 `5·84 = 420 < 618` (her deeds are mostly archery), K4
not among her three strongest level-2 nodes, K5 `4·84 = 336 < 400`. The currency floor holds (`4·30 = 120 ≥
80`), so it is not stale, only thin → **abstain** (04.4.3 row 2). Nothing is voiced; her Leanings view shows
"tracking: on the threshold". Four reflections abstain the same way.

**Session 16. An offer by a mentor, then a tier seized in a crisis.** After scene 77 tracking weighs 101
(recent 41, quality events 16, scenes 15): K1 `82 ≥ 80` ✓ and K5 `404 ≥ 400` ✓, the rest still fail →
**confidence 2**, under the grant line → **offer**. She is back at the waystation, where the old trapper Odo
Kettle (`npc.odo_kettle`, depth recurring, role `deed.wilds.tracking.trailing`, standing +1) has watched her
read sign for a week: V2's requirements hold.

> Odo turns the snare over in his hands. "You found the doe's bed from one bent stem. I've men who've trapped
> twenty winters who'd have walked past it. I could show you the rest. It'd cost you a winter pelt, and your
> patience."
>
> `[CHOICE] Recognition — The Mentor's Acknowledgement: Tracker, tier 1 (Called)`
> `  (a) Accept — tracking +3 · training in tracking: trained · The Mark of the Calling · 2 picks ·
>      price: a seat (2 of 3 deed seats used), the calling's shadow and a bond to Odo Kettle (one winter pelt
>      by the season's end) · provisional`
> `  (b) Decline · (c) Defer`

She accepts. Tracker, tier 1, provisional; a commitment of kind bond is written. Seats: 2 of 3.

Three scenes later, in scene 80, she looses at raiders on the Salt Road under a lethal frame. The scene's
shots are flagged `crisis`. `h.04.crisis_check` runs at `beat_end`: the Archer's tier 3 was
`on_the_threshold` at the last reflection, its weight already past the line; with the pending evidence
included the set is complete (at the scene's close: weighted 384 ≥ 340, counted 91 ≥ 34, and since tier 2:
quality events 35, scenes 21, great deeds at band 3 or higher 10 with 6 successes, crises 4 ≥ 2). This
scene's crisis is what completed it → `trg.04.crisis_offer` → V5.

> The string is against your cheek and the world has gone very quiet. Your hands are steady. They have
> never been this steady.
>
> `[RECOGNITION] An offer is open (see below). Nothing is lost by waiting; play continues when you answer or move on.`
> `[CHOICE] Recognition — The Awakening in Crisis: Archer, tier 3 (Tempered)`
> `  (a) Seize it — archery +5 · training: expert · Sure Hand (a Precision lever whenever you stretch or
>      emulate with the bow) · 1 pick, now, from what this shot was · price: none beyond what you already carry`
> `  (b) Refuse it · (c) Let it pass — it returns at your next rest or your next such moment`

She seizes it. The pick's candidates rank first the abilities whose first tag matches the crisis deed
(`deed.martial.archery.bow`). `power_band` 3 once confirmed; picks held: Archer 4, Tracker 2.

**Sessions 18–19. A broaden fork, and a decline.** After scene 89 `call.wayfarer` (key `deed.wilds`, broad)
is eligible: weighted 203 ≥ 120, counted 28 ≥ 12, quality events 39, scenes 33, three level-2 children at 30
or more, the largest under two-thirds of the branch; confidence 3. She holds Tracker, in its lineage, so it
comes as a **broaden fork** (04.8.3, 04.8.6: Wayfarer in place of Tracker), offered by V7; she declines it.
After scene 95, `call.shadow` (key `deed.guile.stealth`; she scouts by stealth in about a quarter of her
scenes) is eligible: weighted 115, counted 8, quality events 20, scenes 16. Only K5 holds (`4·115 = 460 ≥
400`; recent 31, `5·115 = 575 < 841`): confidence 1 → **offer**, by V7.

> `[CHOICE] Recognition — The Reflection at Rest: Shadow, tier 1 (Called) … (b) Decline …`

"I hide when I must. It is not what I am." **Decline**: recorded with `weighted_at_decline: 115`. The engine
will not raise it again until 24 more evidence-bearing scenes have passed **and** weighted reaches 155; she
may ask for it at any rest. No cost, and her stealth competence is unaffected (it has none beyond the floor).

**Session 20. The hybrid surfaces as a consolidation, and she waits.** After scene 97,
`cooccurrence(wren, deed.martial, deed.wilds)` gives weighted 565 and 227, `min` 227 ≥ 60, `balance`
227/565 (`5·227 = 1,135 ≥ 2·565 = 1,130` ✓, by five points), `joint_scenes` 11 ≥ 5, `recent_min` 54 ≥ 15,
counted 119 and 29. `call.ranger` is eligible, and she holds a calling under each of its branches: a
**consolidation** offer (04.8.5). The tier would be the highest not above 3 that `min` supports: 227 meets
tier 2's 120 and not tier 3's 255 → **Ranger, tier 2**. Ch.12's lead engine places a principal who embodies
both roads; V12.

> The warden who has shadowed the caravan since the hills steps out where you can see her, an unstrung
> longbow across her shoulders and a brace of hares at her belt. "You shoot like the Compact's best and you
> read ground like Odo's. You keep them in two hands. I keep them in one."
>
> `[CHOICE] Recognition — The Master of the Fusion: Ranger, tier 2 (consolidating Archer 3 + Tracker 1)`
> `  (a) Accept — one calling in place of two (1 of 3 seats used). You keep: archery +5 and tracking +3 as
>      specialties, every pick you hold (6), Sure Hand, your training. You gain: Hunter's Quarry (when a deed
>      of the wilds succeeds, an Amplifying lever on one later martial beat that scene). You give up: the
>      Archer's Focus trigger, and separate growth: your next 3 Ranger picks are already counted.
>      price: a bond to Sefa (a season's patrols when she calls) · provisional`
> `  (b) Decline · (c) Defer — she walks these woods until the season turns; after that it returns at your rests`

The player reads that the label would be tier 2 and defers: the wilds half is thin. Nothing is lost.
*This is the engine declining to compute a winner for a mixed history* [C:P5]: Archer and Tracker stand, the
named hybrid stands beside them, and the player chooses when.

**Session 23.** Tracker's tier 2 is ready after scene 112 (weighted 162 ≥ 160; counted 17 ≥ 16; since tier 1:
quality events 14, all challenging, scenes 11, great deeds at band 2 or higher 14 with 1 success: she tracks
what hunts at band 3 and 4 now) and Odo voices it (V2, `return_to_person`). Accepted.

**The season turns after session 26 (`h.04.season_consolidation`).** PR-04-8: (1) the provisional tests run as
at any reflection (Tracker's tier 2 has 18 evidence-bearing scenes behind it). (3) The standing Ranger offer is
re-presented; now `martial` 695, `wilds` 336, `min` 336 ≥ 255 → **Ranger, tier 3**. She accepts.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Callings (seats) | Archer 3, Tracker 2 (2 seats) | **Ranger 3** (1 seat); Archer and Tracker `retired, superseded_by: call.ranger` |
| Competence | archery +5, tracking +4 | roads archery +4, tracking +4; **specialties** archery +5 (expert), tracking +4 (trained): highest-only, so every roll is as before |
| Picks | 4 + 3 = 7 held | 7 held; `picks_total[3]` = 4, so `legacy_picks` = 3 |
| Capabilities | Mark, Proven, Sure Hand | the same (held once; the specialties keep their scope) |
| Family mechanic | martial and wilds Focus triggers, rank 1 [verification: V2a-005] | **Hunter's Quarry**, rank 2: a success on either road gives an Amplifying lever on the other, twice per scene; fused deeds +1 edge |
| `power_band` | 3 | 3 (`inherited_band` 3; a hybrid's tier 3 is also 3) |

`recognition_event {kind: consolidation, calling: call.ranger, tier: 3, vehicle: veh.V12, …}`. Two labels,
two ladders and two Focus triggers are retired; nothing she could do yesterday is gone today; her next three
Ranger picks are pre-paid; and two seats are free for whatever she becomes next (VI: structural retirement,
written as a transformation).

**Session 34. Tier 4, and the one attribute increase.** After scene 170: `min` = 486 ≥ 480 (martial 894,
wilds 486); counted 193 and 60 ≥ 48 each; since the consolidation: quality events 38 + 36, scenes 16 and 23,
great deeds at band 4 or higher 16 + 26 (9 successes), crises 7 + 6 ≥ 3, contexts 9 + 7 ≥ 5. Offered at a
rest by V11 (the old wardens' cairn, a place with `resonance: [deed.wilds, deed.martial.archery]`) and
accepted: Master's Eye; training on her roads at expert; the tier's pick cancels one legacy pick (2 remain).
The attribute increase waits for confirmation (04.8.2); twelve evidence-bearing scenes later the tier is
confirmed and she raises **Agility +3 → +4**, the one increase of her life. `power_band` 4: ch.09's advisory
now rates a T4 champion as a fair fight.

**Sessions 35–60.** Tier 5 needs `min` 900 and 90 counted on **each** branch. By session 60 every
since-field is long met (band-5 deeds 56 + 86, 14 of them successes; crises 27 + 23) and her wilds weigh 933,
but their counted units are 87: three short, because a tracker's deeds tick few clocks. She does not become a Paragon in
this campaign. Many characters never do: in the simulation 183 of 200 focused archers reach tier 5 of a single
narrow calling by session 60, a deliberate 50/50 hybrid at a median 36, and a two-road life like hers
lands near the end of a long campaign or past it. The ladder has a top, and it is far away on purpose.

cards.title: Abstain, three ways
cards.body:
### WE-04-2 Abstain, three ways

| Case | Tallies | Why abstain | What the player can learn |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Not eligible: the grinder.** Brann shoots cellar rats in every scene for 20 sessions. | archery weighted 340, counted 100, quality events **0** (all routine), scenes 60 | the quality floor (6) is unmet | Leanings: "the bow: on the threshold". A reader: "You have done it often, and seldom when it was hard." |
| **Stale: the old soldier.** Hesk fought with the sword for years and has kept an inn for the last forty scenes of play. | `martial.blade` weighted 300, recent 12 | eligible, but `4·12 = 48 < 80`: stale | A reader: "That was who you were. I am asked who you are." If he takes up the sword again, recent passes 20 within a session and the offer comes. |
| **Thin: Wren's tracking at scene 75** (WE-04-1, session 15). | weighted 95, recent 39, confidence 0 | eligible and current (`4·39 = 156 ≥ 80`), with nothing confirming it | silence; two scenes later (scene 77: weighted 101, recent 41) K1 and K5 hold, confidence 2, and it is offered [revision: I-109] |

*Other side of each boundary:* give Brann one real fight a session and his quality events pass 6 by about
session 4; give Hesk recent 20; give Wren's tracking one more recent point (K1 `2·40 ≥ 80`) and five more weighted (K5 `4·100 ≥ 400`). *Tempting non-example:* the DM feels Brann has
"earned it by persistence". There is no such input: the packet for Brann is empty, and the narrator has no
tally to be moved by.

cards.title: Grant against offer: the same tallies, two fields
cards.body:
### WE-04-3 Grant against offer: the same tallies, two fields

Two archers reach scene 10 with Wren's exact numbers at her first grant (WE-04-1: weighted 84, confidence 4) [revision: I-109]. **A** has done little else:
no other candidate is eligible → clear field → **grant**. **B** has also fought with the spear enough that
`call.spearhand` is eligible in the same pass (weighted 82) → the field is not clear → **offer**, with both
named in one block, and the branch calling Warrior beside them if its breadth requirement holds. The engine
does not rank B's identities; the player does. *Non-example:* B's player says "obviously I'm an archer first".
That is an answer to the block, and the right place for it.

cards.title: Defer, a standing offer, and an expiry that takes nothing
cards.body:
### WE-04-4 Defer, a standing offer, and an expiry that takes nothing

Wren had answered the Compact's letter (WE-04-1, session 9) with (c). The offer stands:
`{status: deferred, vehicle: veh.V3, represent_when: [arrival_at_institution, reflection_in_its_region],
expires: season boundary after next}`. It appears under "Open offers" at each session start. Two seasons
pass. At that boundary `h.04.standing_offers` expires the **staging**: the outrider's post is gone (ch.11
gives it to someone else). The tier's eligibility is untouched, so at the same reflection the engine offers
Archer tier 2 again by V7, with no obligation attached. *Boundary:* had the Compact's status toward her
fallen below 0 in the meantime, the letter would have expired then, in the same way. *Non-example:* "You
ignored the letter, so the skill fades." Nothing fades: capability never depends on an institution (04.11.1).

cards.title: A pick, with the numbers the player never sees
cards.body:
### WE-04-5 A pick, with the numbers the player never sees

Archer tier 1, first pick. Eligible by the pool gate (04.8.4) *(abilities illustrative; ch.05 owns)*:

| Ability | First tag | `min_tier` | Pool | Wren's weighted at the tag | Rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pinning Shot | `deed.martial.archery.bow` | 1 | own | 84 | 1st |
| Steady Draw | `deed.martial.archery` | 1 | own | 84 (tie: all her archery is with the bow; engine draw) | 2nd |
| Volley | `deed.martial.archery.bow` | 2 | own | — | not eligible: `min_tier 2 > 1` |
| Tumbling Escape | `deed.martial.athletics.acrobatics` | 1 | kin | 37 | 3rd (kin ranks after own) |
| Read the Field | `deed.martial.tactics.reading` | 1 | kin | 0 | 4th: not shown |

The weights are Wren's at her grant in scene 10 (`04-wren04.py` seed 7; WE-04-1) [revision: I-109].

The block shows Pinning Shot, Steady Draw and Tumbling Escape, each with its literal rank-1 text. Her second
pick shows the remaining two and Read the Field. At tier 2 Volley joins the eligible set; at tier 3 a picked
`min_tier 1` ability is restated at rank 2 (`1 + floor((3 − 1) ÷ 2)`). *Boundary:* an archer who had spent
her fights reading ground (tactics weighted 90) would see Read the Field ahead of Tumbling Escape. The table
she is offered is her own history.
*Non-example:* "Can I just take Fireball?" Its first tag is `deed.arcane.fire.blast`: not under any gate of
this calling. The redirect names the paths: an arcane calling's pick, or learning it by ch.05's own paths.

cards.title: The Fraying: a warning that clears, and a forbidden act
cards.body:
### WE-04-6 The Fraying: a warning that clears, and a forbidden act

**Corin** is a Paladin, tier 2 (roads `martial.blade` and `divine.smiting` at +3; oath axes protection and
mercy; keeper: the Shrine of the Ford; forbidden acts: "Slay a being that has yielded to you." and "Abandon
to harm one under your sworn protection."). Mercy: `pos` 14, `neg` 0, `strain` 0.

*A single contrary act warns.* In a rage he beats a bound cultist for answers (mercy −4: harm to a helpless
victim, 03.3.3). At settlement `neg` 4, `strain` 4. At the next `scene_start`, PR-04-7: stage **1, Dimmed**.

> The morning prayer comes out as only words. The warmth that has sat behind your breastbone since the ford
> is still there, but it has drawn back, as a friend does who has seen something and not yet decided what
> to say.
>
> `[RESULT] Changed: Paladin — Dimmed (stage 1 of 3). Now inactive: Sworn Strike; abilities that need your
> oath of mercy. No new tier while dimmed. Clears by: deeds of mercy, or atonement (ask at any rest).
> Next stage if: more cruelty to the helpless.`

Next session he spares two beaten foes at real cost (+2, +2, in different scenes): strain 4 − 1 − 1 = **2** →
stage 0. Sworn Strike returns; one V10 line; a RESULT line.

*A forbidden act goes to the Choice at once.* Instead, suppose the cult's captain throws down his blade and
Corin kills him. The DM cites `forb.paladin.slay_yielded` (03.3.3: the act matches the sentence word for
word). `forbidden` = 1 → stage **3** whatever the strain. The calling is suspended: roads fall to the floor,
no composite, no oath abilities, and `power_band` falls from 2 to 1.

> `[CHOICE] Paladin — The Choice (stage 3). The calling is suspended until you answer.`
> `  (a) Atone — carry the captain's body to his kin at Harl's Crossing and stand their judgment (a thread)
>      · keep a week's vigil at the Shrine and give up your sword to it (S3) · or deeds of mercy at real
>      cost (a 6-segment clock; the calling returns one tier down while it runs)`
> `  (b) Turn — become the Defiler in its place, tier 1 · price: the first time each scene that you do a
>      reverent deed, lose 1 Focus`
> `  (c) Release — let the calling go; its 3 picks return to the pool; your training stays`
> `  (d) Defer — it stays suspended; it lapses at Midwinter (the second season's turn) if nothing is done`

He chooses service. `clk.atonement.paladin` (6, public) opens; the calling is read at stage 2 (tier 1's
values), so the keeper's regard holds again and his divine spells work at tier 1's ranks (05.7.4) [revision: I-064]. Over three sessions: a +4 mercy entry (2 ticks), a +2 (1), a +4 (2), a +2 (1) → 6 of 6.
`record_evidence(op: atonement, axis: conduct.mercy, supersedes: [the killing])`: `neg` 0, `atoned` 4,
`strain` 0, the citation cleared → stage 0, tier 2 restored in full. The ledger still shows the killing,
marked superseded; the cult still calls him a murderer (ch.11).

*Tempting non-example:* Corin kills the captain **mid-fight**, before any yield. No alternative was plainly
open (03.3.3): no conduct entry, no citation, no stage. The oath forbids slaying the yielded, not winning.

cards.title: The Taking: a success, a failure, and what narration may not add
cards.body:
### WE-04-7 The Taking: a success, a failure, and what narration may not add

**Tamsin** is a Devourer, tier 1 (Resolve +1; competence `deed.lore.bestiary` +3; library 0 of 4; Focus 4).
She has just killed a cinder hound (T2; `creature.beast.predator`, `creature.elemental.fire`) with her own
spear, never below 4 Vitality, and it breathed fire at her this scene. PR-04-9:
1. Gate: license held; every trigger condition holds.
2. Circumstance: her own resolved success; never Staggered → **decisive**.
3. Frame: Endure, Resolve +1, competence +3 → +4 against the effect DC of a T2 creature, Moderate 15: needs
   11, **50%**. Stakes Risky (band 2 ≤ her band 1 + 1). The OFFER shows: "Success: its signature power at
   tier 2. Bane while slotted: double cold harm. Failure: the fire answers (harm S2)." She commits; Focus 4 → 2.
4. d20 = 14 → 18: **success**. `generate(gen.absorb, adv.cinder_hound_07, decisive, success)`: pool gate →
   Ember Heart (the archetype's signature *(ch.09)*), Predator's Nose, Thick Hide, Night Eyes, Pounce;
   fill `signature` → **Ember Heart**; tier `min(tier_cap 2, calling tier + 1 = 2)` = 2: "halve fire harm you
   take, rounded down". Library 1 of 4. At her next long rest she slots it; the elemental bane applies:
   double `harm.frost` taken.

*The other side.* d20 = 5 → 9, margin −6: **failure**. Nothing is taken; `apply_costs(cost.harm, S2)`: 3
Vitality of `harm.fire`. No second attempt on this hound; the next hound she defeats may be tried.
*Boundary (narrow survival).* Had the hound Staggered her first, the fill is `biased`: among the non-signature
entries Thick Hide (bias `ward`, weight 2 × 3 = 6) against Predator's Nose 3, Night Eyes 2, Pounce 2.
*Non-example.* "The flames part around you as you walk through the burning barn." Ember Heart halves fire
harm taken; it parts nothing (INV-8). The claim check cuts the sentence.

cards.title: A provisional grant that lapses, with its warning
cards.body:
### WE-04-8 A provisional grant that lapses, with its warning

A second archer (the simulation's seed 10) is offered tier 2 at the last rest of session 11 and accepts. From
session 12 she apprentices to a fire-sorcerer and puts the bow away (03's scenario D). The grant is
provisional; `lived` is her archery evidence since that rest.
- Session 13, a reflection: 9 evidence-bearing scenes since the grant; `lived` 0, under half of 24 →
  `trg.04.lapse_warning`:
  `[RESULT] Notice: Archer tier 2 is provisional and is not being lived; it will lapse after about fifteen
  more scenes of other deeds unless that changes. Nothing else is at risk.` and one line of fiction: the
  bowstring has gone stiff in its case.
- Session 14: 12 or more since the grant; `lived` 0 < 24 → not confirmed; not yet 24 → no lapse.
- Session 16, the first reflection at 24 since the grant: `lived` 0 → **lapse**: archery +4 → +3, the tier's
  pick returns to the pool, the Proven license and the Focus trigger go (unless another calling grants
  them). Tier 1 was confirmed long before and is untouched: she is still an Archer. Meanwhile
  `call.pyromancer` has been offered (in the simulation the new calling came a median of 4 sessions after the turn, p10–p90 2–5; T-04-8 R8).
*Other side:* had she fought one more session with the bow before turning, `lived` would have passed 24 and
the tier would have been confirmed at the first reflection twelve scenes after the grant (it confirmed in
112 of 179 such runs; T-04-8 R8) [revision: I-108]. *Non-example:* a season spent healing in a monastery adds no evidence-bearing scenes,
so the count does not advance and nothing lapses (03.6.1).

cards.title: Tempting non-examples, with the refusal each gets
cards.body:
### WE-04-9 Tempting non-examples, with the refusal each gets

| The player says, or the DM is tempted to | What happens |
|---|---|
| "The duke knights me. So now I'm a Cavalier." | A knighthood is a rank (ch.11). `call.cavalier` comes from deeds of mounted combat. The duke's act creates no packet (04.11.3). |
| "My mentor is a great wizard; she makes me one." | She can teach a first arcane license (ch.05's mentor path) and her teaching counts as `cnt.training`, for at most half a counted requirement. The calling waits on deeds. |
| The DM narrates "you feel yourself growing stronger" after a hard fight | Forbidden: implies a mechanic with no recognition packet behind it (12.14.5). Evidence was recorded; nothing is said. |
| "I renounce my oath so the Fraying can't touch me." | Releasing the calling is always possible (04.9.5 release): the calling, its picks and its boon go with the oath. There is no keeping the power without the keeper. |
| The DM wants to stage V5 because the scene is dramatic | V5 is returned only when the engine flagged a crisis event on a candidate at the threshold. Drama is not a trigger. |
| "I'll consolidate to dodge the Dimmed stage." | A calling at stage 1 or higher cannot be consolidated, forked or folded (04.8.5 step 6). |
| A fourth deed-keyed calling is eligible and the DM quietly drops the least used | The engine never evicts. The block offers consolidate, fork, release, decline or defer (04.8.1). |
| "Show me how close I am to Tracker." | The codex shows Leanings: "tracking: becoming". Numbers are sealed; a reader in the world can say what kind of deed is missing. |

---

cards.title: Foundations
cards.body: ### 05.1 Foundations

cards.title: What an ability is
cards.body:
**05.1.1 What an ability is.** `[D]` [C:VII; C:P5; DL-05-02; revision: I-065] An **ability** is a license (00.12.1) with mechanics: an entry of
`data/abilities.yaml` (id `ab.*`) that a character **holds** in a slot. A **spell** is an ability whose
first tag is under `deed.arcane`, `deed.divine` or `deed.primal`; it is the same record with `kind:
spell` and the trait `trait.nature.magical`. Everything else a character may be licensed to do
(training, languages, calling capabilities, fact licenses, rites) is a license **without** a slot
(05.2.3). The one exception is the three **branch workings** (05.7.11): `ab.*` records with `slot_class:
license`, held by every holder of a magic training license of their branch and occupying no slot
[revision: I-009]. An ability is read literally at its active rank (INV-8): it does what its `scope` and `effects`
say and nothing else, and narration may never describe it doing more [00.12.2; 01.3.3].

cards.title: Abilities in state
cards.body:
**05.1.2 Abilities in state.** `[D]` [DL-05-01; DL-05-03; DL-05-22; revision: I-065] `Character.slots` (00.6.2) holds three lists of held abilities.
Each entry is:

```yaml
HeldAbility:
  ability_id: ab.*
  partition: calling | acquired | equipped
  source: {kind: pick | learned | taught | absorbed | gift | item, ref: <calling id + tier | clock id | mentor id | library | offer id | item id>}
  rank: 1..3                 # computed, never stored by hand (05.3.9)
  uses: {remaining: int, per: boundary} | null
  sustained: bool            # true while this ability's sustained effect is running
  bound: bool                # equipped partition only: true while the item's ability occupies a slot
  lifecycle: provisional | permanent
  acquired_at: time
```

`Character.focus` gains fields owned by this chapter: `{current, max, reserve: {banked: int, capacity:
int, charging: int, vessel: item_id|null}, state: steady | spent, generated_this_scene: int,
restored_by_consumables_since_long_rest: int, breathers_since_short_rest: int, short_rests_today: int,
overdraws_since_long_rest: int}`. `Character.shelf: [ability_id]` holds acquired abilities that are known
but not slotted (05.2.6). `Character.witnessed: [ability_id]` and learning clocks are 05.8's. Visibility:
slots, ranks, uses, Focus and the shelf are **shown**; `witnessed` and learning clocks are **available**
(00.6.4).

cards.title: The words
cards.body:
**05.1.3 The words.** `[N]` [DL-05-04; DL-05-07; DL-05-08; revision: I-065] **Hold**: have an ability in a slot. **Pick**: a calling tier's right to
fill a calling slot from the pool (04.8.4). **Activation**: one use of an active ability. **Working**: an
activation that is itself the character's beat, or a Working-form rider that adds effects of its own to that
beat (05.3.2) [revision: I-110]. **Rider**: an activation that attaches to the
character's own beat. **Stretch**, **emulate**, **crude fallback**: the three priced ways past a
license's text (01.3.5). **Flare**: one optional surcharge on an activation (05.6.8). **Push**: spending
Focus on an ordinary beat (05.6.7). **Spent**: at 0 Focus. **Overdraw**: paying Focus with Vitality.
**Rite**: this chapter's short word for a ritual, a clocked magical extended task (`rit.*`).
**Miscast**: a working of magic that goes wrong in its branch's way. **Shelf**: known, unslotted acquired
abilities.

cards.title: Slots and the hard ceiling
cards.body: ### 05.2 Slots and the hard ceiling

cards.title: Twenty slots in three partitions
cards.body:
**05.2.1 Twenty slots in three partitions.** `[D]` A character holds at most **20** abilities:

| Partition | Slots | Filled by | Usable when | Changes at |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `calling` | **12** | a **pick** granted by a calling tier (04.8.4), and nothing else | always, at the rank the holding calling's tier gives | recognition, crystallization, the `season` re-pick, the Retrain activity (04.8.7) |
| `acquired` | **4** | abilities **learned** (a completed learning clock), **taught** (a mentor), **absorbed** (the Taking, 04.10), or given as a **gift** (a patron or power, 08's `gen.gift`) | always, at rank 1 (absorbed powers: at the tier the generator gave) | any completed `rest_long` (05.2.7) |
| `equipped` | **4** | the one item-bound active ability of an equipped item (00.11.5; 08) | only while the item is equipped and its ability is **bound** | a `breather` outside conflict, or the equip action in conflict (05.2.8) |

These are the reference values of 00.17.1 Q2 (20 = 12 + 4 + 4), adopted without change. The partitions
do not lend to each other: an empty calling slot cannot hold a learned ability, and four acquired slots
are four however many callings a character has. *Why 20:* it is the one cap with a tested precedent in
this project's research (HWFWM's 4 × 5), it sits near the top of the converged "about five modifiers per
active thing" range once divided among three callings, and ch.04's ladder fills the calling partition
exactly when three callings reach tier 3 (3 × 4 picks), so the ceiling starts to bind at the moment a
character is broad enough for consolidation to be attractive [R2 §05; R3 05.1; 04.8.4; DL-05-01].

cards.title: The ceiling is closed
cards.body:
**05.2.2 The ceiling is closed.** `[D]` No effect, item, boon, rite, tier or ruling adds a slot or moves
a slot between partitions. `grant` (tool #28) refuses a write that would exceed a partition. Where the
source fiction lets rare gifts break a cap, this ruleset does not: a cap that can be raised is a menu
that grows [C:V; C:P5 "hard total-slot ceiling"; INV-13].

cards.title: What does not take a slot
cards.body:
**05.2.3 What does not take a slot.** `[D]` [DL-05-01; DL-05-31; revision: I-065] Only `ab.*` entries are held in slots. These are licenses
and take none: training licenses (`lic.training.*`, 05.9), languages, the calling capabilities
(`lic.call.*`, 04.5.3), the Focus licenses (`lic.focus.*`, 05.6), fact licenses (01.3.2), known rites
(`rit.*`, 05.8.1), the branch working a magic training license carries (05.7.11) [revision: I-009], the passive and mundane properties of items (08's item-layer budget), a calling's
Focus trigger, boon or composite (04.5.4), and conditions. Each of those is bounded by its own owner:
training by time (05.9.4), rites by material and time, item properties by 08's budget, family mechanics
by one per calling.

cards.title: How slots open
cards.body:
**05.2.4 How slots open.** `[D]` All twenty slots exist from character creation. What limits their use
is the right to fill them:
- **Calling slots** are filled only through the **pick allowance** `A` (04.8.4): cumulative 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
  picks for a deed-keyed calling at tiers 1–5; 1, 1, 2, 2, 3 for a vow or dark calling; `A` never exceeds
  12. A character with no calling has an empty calling partition.
- **Acquired slots** are open to any character, recognized or not, who completes an acquisition path
  (05.8.5–05.8.7). This is where a character without a calling, or one learning outside their calling,
  holds abilities [C:P2 baseline; C:P4: breadth of access is not day-one power, since each acquired
  ability is held at rank 1 and each costs weeks to learn].
- **Equipped slots** are open to any character who equips an item with an item-bound active ability.

cards.title: When the calling partition is full
cards.body:
**05.2.5 When the calling partition is full.** `[D]` A new pick **replaces** a held calling ability of
the player's choice (04.8.4 "at the cap"). The replaced ability is retired *from the character*
(`retire`, tool #28) and returns to the pool; it is not moved to the shelf, because the shelf belongs to
the acquired partition. An ability that names another in its `replaces` field takes that ability's slot
without using a new one (an upgrade path: the DCC fork, a replacement and never an addition)
[C:VI; R3 05.12].

cards.title: When the acquired partition is full: the shelf
cards.body:
**05.2.6 When the acquired partition is full: the shelf.** `[D]` A fifth acquired ability goes to the
**shelf**: known, not held, not usable (a beat that needs it is G3, and the redirect says "it is on your
shelf: you can bring it back after a long rest"). The shelf holds at most **4** abilities. A ninth
acquired ability (4 slotted + 4 shelved + 1) requires the player to **forget** one of the nine at once
(`retire`; it may be learned again later by its paths, at full clock). Absorbed powers use ch.04's
**library** in place of the shelf (size 4–12 by the Devourer's tier, 04.10.3); the two stores are
separate and neither can hold the other's contents [C:V; R3 04.18; DL-05-03].

cards.title: Re-slotting at a long rest
cards.body:
**05.2.7 Re-slotting at a long rest.** `[D]` [DL-05-03; revision: I-065] On every completed `rest_long` of quality `full` or
`partial` (07), handler `h.05.reslot` (phase 3) lets the player exchange any number of abilities between
the acquired slots and the shelf or library. No check, no Focus, no time beyond the rest. An
`interrupted` rest allows no exchange. Uses do not refresh by re-slotting: an ability returns with the
`uses.remaining` it had when it left, and then the rest's own recharge applies (05.4.6) [04 Interface
request 8].

cards.title: Binding equipped abilities
cards.body:
**05.2.8 Binding equipped abilities.** `[D]` [DL-05-01; DL-00A-25; revision: I-065] Equipping an item with an item-bound active ability
**binds** that ability to a free equipped slot. With all four in use, the new item's ability is
**dormant**: the item's passive and mundane properties work, its active ability does not, and the codex
says which. The player may choose which four are bound at any `breather` outside conflict. In conflict,
unequipping an item unbinds at once, and the action that equips an item binds its ability if a slot is
free (the action is ch.06's). An ability held through the equipped partition is used at the rank the
item states (08), never at a calling's rank, and its first tag earns no evidence when the item is a
relic (`feeds_evidence: false`, 00.11.5).

cards.title: One of each
cards.body:
**05.2.9 One of each.** `[D]` Three engine-enforced exclusions keep a full sheet from stacking
[R3 05.2 the one-copy rule; INV-13]:
1. **One instance per ability id** across all partitions. A second source of an ability already held
   grants nothing (a relic of a technique you know is only a spare).
2. **One held ability per `mod_group`** across the calling and acquired partitions (the pool gate of
   04.8.4 already refuses a second in the calling partition). An equipped item whose ability shares a
   `mod_group` with a held ability stays dormant.
3. **One running effect per behavioral slot** (`slot.stance`, `slot.aura`, `slot.body_form`,
   `slot.movement_mode`, `slot.strike_delivery`, `slot.spell_delivery`, `slot.defense_reaction`) by
   priority rank (05.10.3), and **one sustained working** at a time (05.4.7).

cards.title: Provisional abilities
cards.body:
**05.2.10 Provisional abilities.** `[D]` A pick is `provisional` with the tier that granted it and is
confirmed or lapses with it (04.8.2). A learned, taught, absorbed or gifted ability is `provisional`
until the first `reflection` after it has been activated (or, for a passive, has applied) in at least
**three** different scenes; at that reflection it becomes `permanent`. One that has not reached three
scenes by the second `season` boundary after it was acquired is moved to the shelf (never deleted) and
the codex says so one season earlier. A provisional ability works in full; the status is a trial of
whether the character lives with it, per Principle VI at character scale [C:VI; 00.17.1 Q12; DL-05-22].

cards.title: The ability template grammar
cards.body: ### 05.3 The ability template grammar

cards.title: The record
cards.body:
**05.3.1 The record.** `[D]` Every entry of `data/abilities.yaml` has these fields (the License schema of
00.12.1 plus the fields `data/SCHEMAS.md#abilities.yaml` requires plus this chapter's optional ones,
T-05-2). No field is prose-only mechanics: every mechanical consequence is an effect reference, a number
on a named scale, or a table reference (00.16.4).

| Field | Content | Lever (P12) |
|---|---|---|
| `id`, `name`, `kind` | `ab.*`; `ability` or `spell` | |
| `tags` | the **first** tag is a `deed` tag at level 2 or 3 (it is the ability's evidence tag, competence tag and pool-gate tag); then any `conduct`, `harm` and `trait` tags | |
| `min_tier`, `mod_group`, `slot_class` | 1–5; the exclusion family; `calling`, `acquired`, `equipped`, or `license` (the three branch workings, 05.7.11, which also carry `granted_by`, `deed_tag_rule` and `rank_rule`) | |
| `form` | one of the eight forms (05.3.2) | |
| `activation`, `timing` | `passive` or `active`; for actives `beat`, `rider`, `reaction` or `trigger` (05.3.4) | |
| `regime`, `hook`, `slot` | the combination regime (00.10.7), with its hook or behavioral slot | |
| `principle` | one sentence naming **the operation and what it operates on** (the governing principle; 05.5.1) | |
| `scope` | the positive, literal statement of what it lets the holder do (rendered from the active rank's `text`) | **scope** |
| `limitation` | the boundary of the scope, written as what it applies *to* (targets, conditions, bands, needs) | **limitation** |
| `weakness` | present only if intended: an explicit vulnerability the ability creates, as an effect reference | **weakness** |
| `cost`, `cost_text` | `{focus: 0–4}`; any price paid elsewhere (Vitality, a component, time), as effect references | **cost** |
| `limits`, `refresh_on` | `{per: <boundary>, uses: n}`; an optional hook that returns one use (05.4.6) | |
| `check` | how it is resolved: `none`, `aimed` (the holder rolls) or `resisted` (the target rolls), with verb, attribute and what it works against | |
| `effects` | effect references (00.10.1); for a ranked ability, the active rank's list | |
| `ranks` | 1–3 complete restatements `{rank, text, effects, cost, limits}` (05.3.9) | |
| `excludes` | the nearest things it does not cover, each naming what would | |
| `stretch`, `emulate`, `crude_fallback`, `acquisition_paths` | 05.5 | |
| `flares` | which of the six flares it accepts (05.6.8) | |
| `spread` | at most one spread tag it carries natively (05.10.4) | |
| `composite_key` | true on the few abilities that key a named composite (05.10.6) | |
| `dictates_choice` | true when an effect it applies dictates another being's choices (charm, compulsion, fear), for 03.2.6 | |
| `narration_may_not_imply` | a closed list | |
| `budget` | `{value, allowance, terms}` as computed by 05.11 | |
| `replaces`, `requires_conduct`, `conduct_pole`, `adversary_only`, `mirror_of` | optional | |

The four P12 fields are **separate fields**, never one sentence, because the project's one recorded
ability failure came from a limitation and an implied weakness sharing a clause ("no protection against
cold" narrated as a cold vulnerability). A `limitation` is a scope boundary, written positively
("Applies to harm tagged `harm.fire`"). A `weakness` is an effect reference with its own literal text,
and an ability with no `weakness` field **has none**: the narrator may not supply one
[C:P12; R3 05.9, #12; SG-15; R: specs/003-ability-acquisition-probe/implementation-results.md].

cards.title: The eight forms (the closed grammar)
cards.body:
**05.3.2 The eight forms (the closed grammar).** `[D]` Every ability is exactly one form. A form fixes
which regime, operations and timing an ability may use, so an ability's shape is checkable before its
numbers are [R1 M-17; C:P10; DL-05-04].

| Form | What it is | Regime · timing | Operations it may use | Fate pattern it extends |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Edge** | a number in narrow circumstances | additive · passive | `modify` (edge, harm_edge, reduction, adjust), `multiply`, `step` | action bonus |
| **Lever** | a citable fact under a stated condition | additive · passive, or rider | `lever` | action bonus |
| **Permission** | a method the basic verbs exclude, resolved by an ordinary frame | additive · beat | `grant_license`, `claim_slot` on `slot.movement_mode`, or none (the scope is the permission) | add a new action |
| **Working** | the activation *is* the beat, or rides one: it produces effects through an aimed or resisted check, or as a rider through the roll of the beat it rides | independent_trigger · beat or rider | `harm`, `apply_condition`, `remove_condition`, `resource`, `move`, `tick`, `reveal`, `create`, `trigger_check`, `set_fact`; and, as part of the activation's package, `lever`, `step`, `modify`, `restrict`, `prevent`, `multiply`, `redirect`, `claim_slot`, `grant_license` [revision: I-126] | add a new action |
| **Reaction** | fires on a hook, off the holder's own beat | independent_trigger · reaction or trigger | `prevent`, `redirect`, `harm`, `apply_condition`, `move`, `resource`, `lever` | rules exception |
| **Form** | replaces *how* something works for a duration | priority_exclusive · beat or rider | `claim_slot` (with the effects the claim carries) | rules exception |
| **Exception** | one stated exception to one stated rule in a narrow context | additive · passive, or rider | `restrict` (as an immunity), `step`, `modify` on a cap-bound quantity, `economy` (reactions only) | rules exception |
| **Reserve** | converts or returns a resource | independent_trigger · rider, reaction or trigger | `resource`, `modify` (`focus_cost`, maxima) | (fate-point economy; this game allows it inside 05.6's caps) |

A **rider Working** [revision: I-110; DL-05-42] is an active ability that adds produced effects (harm, a severity rung,
a condition, movement) to the holder's own beat of a named verb, as Aimed Shot, Hew and Cleaving Arc do on a
Strike. It has `check: none` and `hook: on_degree`: it rides that beat's roll and its effects apply on the
degrees its text names (05.3.5), resolving as an independent trigger on that hook (05.10.1) at depth 0
(05.10.5). It costs no action, so the budget's timing term is 0 against a beat Working's 2 (05.11.2), and it is
bounded by one rider per beat (05.4.3). A Lever rider gives only a lever; anything more is a Working. What separates a Working from an Edge, Lever or Exception is its regime and timing (an activated independent trigger, not a passive additive), not its operations: a beat Working may confer levers or edges on a target, and a rider Working may add a harm edge [revision: I-126].

A proposed ability that fits no form is not an ability: it is a rite (05.8), an item (08), a calling
capability (04), or out of scope. Adding a form is an amendment to this chapter.

cards.title: Passive and active
cards.worst_case: one passive wrongly applied gives its listed number once (at most +2 edge, one lever, one severity step) and appears by id in the OFFER breakdown (class i). - Passives are budgeted lower than actives by construction (05.11.2), and a passive may never contain `prevent`, a condition of the hard-control group, or harm of S3 or more (T-05-9).
cards.body:
**05.3.3 Passive and active.** `[D]` + `[J:flag]` [C:P5]
- A **passive** ability has no cost, no limits and no usage state. It applies whenever its effects'
  `applies_when` expressions hold. The engine evaluates every clause that reads tracked state (tags,
  verbs, bands, flags, conditions, harm tags). A clause that reads the fiction ("when tracking by scent",
  "when you have had an interval to study the lock") is a `[J:flag]` the DM answers when framing:
  *true only when* an established fact or the declared method makes it so; *false* when it rests on the
  player's assertion alone; uncertain → false (SG-05). A passive is verified by the narration-consistency
  check (12) and by the frame's breakdown, which lists every passive that contributed.
- An **active** ability is invoked by the player, costs Focus or a use or both, and passes through
  `use_ability` (05.4.1). Any ability with a `cost`, a `limits` entry or a duration is active.
- *Worst case (J) of a wrong fiction-clause call:* one passive wrongly applied gives its listed number once
  (at most +2 edge, one lever, one severity step) and appears by id in the OFFER breakdown (class i).
- Passives are budgeted lower than actives by construction (05.11.2), and a passive may never contain
  `prevent`, a condition of the hard-control group, or harm of S3 or more (T-05-9).

cards.title: Timing
cards.body:
**05.3.4 Timing.** `[D]` [DL-05-04; C:P5; revision: I-065] An active ability has exactly one timing:

| Timing | When it is used | Action cost | Limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `beat` | it is the declared beat (a Working, a Permission, entering a Form) | whatever ch.06 charges for the verb the ability is anchored to (`check.verb`) | one beat is one activation |
| `rider` | declared with the holder's own beat of a named verb or tag, in the same frame (a Lever, a Working, entering a Form, an Exception or a Reserve; 05.3.2) | none beyond the beat | **one rider per beat** (05.4.3) |
| `reaction` | on its hook, in response to another's act | the holder's reaction (06) | one reaction per trigger event; 06 sets reactions per round |
| `trigger` | on its hook, as a consequence of the holder's own resolved beat or of a boundary | none | fires at most once per event; subject to depth (05.10.5) |

A `trigger` ability with a Focus cost fires only on the player's yes. The engine asks at the moment the
hook fires and shows the cost; the player may set a standing answer per ability (`always`, `ask`,
`never`) in the codex. A `trigger` with no Focus cost fires automatically and may be set to `never`.

cards.title: How an ability is resolved
cards.body:
**05.3.5 How an ability is resolved.** `[D]` [DL-05-04; C:P8; revision: I-065] The `check` field decides who rolls, per 00.3.3:
- `none`: no roll. The effects apply when the activation is validated (most riders, Forms, Reserves,
  Edges and Levers).
- `aimed`: the holder rolls **one d20**. Attribute: the ability's `attribute`. Competence: the highest
  entry on the ability's **first tag** or an ancestor (00.3.6). Against: the target's defense named in
  `check.against` (a creature), or an obstacle tier (an object or the world). A harm-dealing aimed
  Working shifts its severity by `(delivered reach − 2)` like a Strike (00.3.15); other effects use
  delivered reach as the ability's text states.
- `resisted`: the holder does not roll. Each target rolls Endure or Evade (`check.resist_verb`,
  `check.resist_attribute`) against the holder's **effect DC** = `10 + attribute + competence(first tag)
  + edge` (00.3.8), read on 01.18.3's table unless the ability gives its own degree table.
A rider has `check: none` and rides the roll of the beat it attaches to: its effects apply on the
degrees its text names (default: any success).

cards.title: Literal, positive text
cards.body:
**05.3.6 Literal, positive text.** `[D]` Each rank's `text` is rendered **verbatim** into the narration
packet whenever the ability is used or applies, so the narrator works from the words on the page and
never from memory [R4 §9 05 #4]. Authoring rules, enforced by the generator script where mechanical:
(a) say what it does and to what; (b) no clause of the form "does not protect against", "offers no", or
"but leaves you"; (c) no figurative language inside a mechanical clause; (d) every number is a value on a
00 scale; (e) a "Does not:" line appears only in `excludes`, and each exclusion names the license or verb
that *would* cover the thing; (f) no behavioural hints ("may tempt you to…").

cards.title: Narration may not imply
cards.body:
**05.3.7 Narration may not imply.** `[N]` [C:P13; revision: I-065] Every ability carries a closed list. The defaults, which each
entry extends, are: a harm type, target, range band or duration other than the text's; a weakness the
record does not hold; an effect on a being or object outside the stated targets; that the ability can do
again what its uses or Focus no longer allow; any of the seven sensitive upgrades (perception, memory,
mobility, control, access, awareness, freedom; 01.3.3) beyond the scope's words.

cards.title: Tags an ability carries
cards.body:
**05.3.8 Tags an ability carries.** `[D]` [DL-05-02; DL-05-06; revision: I-065] The first tag fixes four things at once: which callings may
pick it (04.8.4), which competence its check uses (05.3.5), where `cnt.focus` evidence lands when Focus
is spent on it (03.7.4), and which training license's grade governs its stretch and flares (05.9.2).
`trait.*` tags pull in 01.17's general rules (a `trait.action.speech` working is forbidden while
`cond.choking`; a `trait.sense.loud` one ticks listening clocks). `harm.*` tags are the harm it deals.
A `conduct.*` tag with `conduct_pole` marks an oath-gated ability (05.3.10).

cards.title: Ranks: restated, never appended
cards.body:
**05.3.9 Ranks: restated, never appended.** `[D]` An ability has one to three **ranks**. Each rank is a
complete restatement: its own text, effects, cost and limits. Exactly one rank is active:

`rank = min(highest authored rank, 1 + floor((T − min_tier) ÷ 2))`

where `T` is the tier of the calling whose pick holds the ability (04.5.5), lowered by a Fraying
suspension where one applies. For a pick carried through a consolidation or a fork, `T` is the higher of
the new calling's tier and the `tier_reached` of the specialty the pick came from (04.8.5 step 3), so a
consolidation never lowers a rank. So an ability with `min_tier` 1 is at rank 2 from tier 3 and rank 3 at
tier 5; `min_tier` 2 or 3 reaches rank 2 at tiers 4 or 5; `min_tier` 4 or 5 has one rank. An ability held
in the **acquired** partition is always rank 1. One held through an **item** has the rank the item
states. The codex shows only the active rank's text. When a rank changes, the old text is gone; nothing
accumulates [R2 #3; 04 Interface request 4].

cards.title: Oath-gated abilities
cards.body:
**05.3.10 Oath-gated abilities.** `[D]` [DL-05-28; DL-05-36; revision: I-065] An ability with a `conduct.*` tag is eligible only for a calling
whose `pool_gate.conduct` lists that axis **and** whose `pole` equals the ability's `conduct_pole`
(positive: vows and oath-bearing callings; negative: dark callings). While the calling that holds it is
suspended by the Fraying (04.9.3), the ability is suspended with it: it stays in its slot, and
`use_ability` refuses it with the reason. These abilities have no `emulate` (a vow's power cannot be
copied by watching) and their `acquisition_paths` list recognition only.

cards.title: Using an ability
cards.body: ### 05.4 Using an ability

cards.title: use_ability
cards.body:
**05.4.1 `use_ability`.** `[D]` [C:I; C:P16; revision: I-065] Tool #19. Every activation, stretch and emulation runs PR-05-1. The tool
validates, in this order and with the first failure returned as a refusal that names its reason:
(1) **held**: the ability is in a slot (or the mode is `emulate` and 05.5.4 holds), bound if equipped,
not suspended; (2) **timing**: a beat, a rider on a beat of an allowed verb or tag, the holder's unused
reaction, or the hook that fired; (3) **limitation**: every limitation clause that reads state holds
(target tags, bands, flags, conditions, a free hand, speech); (4) **uses**: `uses.remaining ≥ 1`;
(5) **exclusions**: one rider per beat, one sustained working, behavioral-slot priority (the tool
*warns*, it does not refuse, when a new claim would be suppressed by a higher rank already running);
(6) **Focus**: the computed cost (05.6.3) is at most `focus.current`, or the player accepts an overdraw
(05.6.6). A refusal spends nothing: no Focus, no use, no action, no time (01.3.6).

cards.title: What an activation spends, and when
cards.body:
**05.4.2 What an activation spends, and when.** `[D]` Focus and the use are spent when the activation is
**committed**: at the OFFER's commit for a beat or rider, at the player's yes for a reaction or trigger.
They are spent whether the check then succeeds or fails. They are **not** spent when the tool refuses,
when the player withdraws at the OFFER, or when the event the ability answered is cancelled before the
ability resolves (00's edge case: a second `prevent` on an event already prevented keeps its use)
[01.7; R7 §5 Ex.7 Case B].

cards.title: One rider per beat
cards.body:
**05.4.3 One rider per beat.** `[D]` A beat carries at most one `rider` activation. A Form already
running, passives, and levers already established are not riders and are not limited by this rule. This
is the exclusivity that stops "several effects in one action" without adding an action economy of its
own (WoW's global cooldown, 5e's bonus-action patch) [R1 §05 "bonus-action riders"; R3 F-2; INV-11].

cards.title: Targets
cards.body:
**05.4.4 Targets.** `[D]` An ability names its targets over **relationship-state**, never over geometry:
"one being within `band.near`", "each being engaged with you", "one being carrying `cond.exposed`". The
engine checks bands, flags and conditions at commitment. Multi-target abilities use a **spread tag**
(05.10.4), whose selection rule and cap are data. A target that turns out to be illegal at commitment
(it moved; it is not what it seemed) is dropped; if none remain the activation is refused under 05.4.1
and spends nothing [R3 #7; 00.17.1 Q14].

cards.title: Durations
cards.body:
**05.4.5 Durations.** `[D]` [DL-00A-12; R5 §3.3; revision: I-065] Durations use `substrate.yaml#duration_forms` only (SG-28): `rounds:N`,
`intervals:N`, `hours:N`, `watches:N`, `days:N`, `scene`, `conflict`, `until_rest:<type>`, `uses:N`,
`while:<state expr>`, `permanent`. An ability's running effect is an `effect_instance` with a source and
a remaining duration, expired by `h.00.durations`. A `while:` duration ends the instant its expression
is false (a stance ends when the holder is `cond.prone` if its text says so).

cards.title: Uses and recharge
cards.body:
**05.4.6 Uses and recharge.** `[D]` + `[T]` Every active ability declares one of these seven recharge
types, each engine-counted and refreshed by a registered handler in phase 3. No recharge exists only in
prose [C:P5; 00.10.9; R3 05.8].

| Type | Data form | Refreshed by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| **At will** | `cost: {focus: 0}`, no `limits` | n/a | usable every time its timing allows |
| **Focus only** | `cost: {focus: 1–4}`, no `limits` | n/a | limited by the pool alone |
| **Per round** | `limits: {per: round, uses: n}` | `h.05.round_recharge` | reactions and counters |
| **Per conflict** | `limits: {per: conflict_end, uses: n}` | `h.05.conflict_recharge` | "once per fight" |
| **Per scene** | `limits: {per: scene_end, uses: n}` | `h.05.scene_recharge` | the usual limit outside conflict |
| **Per rest** | `limits: {per: rest_short, uses: n}` or `{per: rest_long, …}` or `{per: day, …}` | `h.05.rest_recharge`; `h.05.day_recharge` | `day` refreshes at dawn whether or not the character slept |
| **Once** | `limits: {per: never, uses: n}` | never | single-use-ever; the ability stays held and spent unless its text says it is then retired |

The **refresh ladder** is `round < conflict_end < scene_end < rest_short < rest_long`. A boundary
refreshes every use whose `per` is at or below it on the ladder, so a short rest refreshes per-scene uses
and a long rest refreshes everything but `day` and `never`. `refresh_on: {hook, when}` returns **one**
use (never above the maximum) when its hook fires; the return is an independent trigger and obeys depth.
A rest of quality `interrupted` refreshes nothing; `partial` refreshes as `full` for uses (Focus differs,
05.6.9).

cards.title: Sustained workings
cards.body:
**05.4.7 Sustained workings.** `[D]` + `[T]` [DL-05-26; revision: I-065] An effect with `trait.duration.sustained` lasts while the
holder concentrates (01.17). A character sustains **one** working at a time; beginning a second ends the
first (the player is warned). Sustaining costs no Focus per round. It ends when the holder chooses (a
free activity), becomes `cond.stunned` or `cond.unconscious`, becomes **Spent** (05.6.5), or fails the
concentration check that harm forces (01.17: Endure with Resolve against Easy for S1–S2 harm, Moderate
S3, Hard S4, Very hard S5). The aura and stance slots are separate limits and may run beside one
sustained working.

cards.title: Evidence from abilities
cards.body:
**05.4.8 Evidence from abilities.** `[D]` [DL-03-12; revision: I-065] An activation is the holder's declared deed: its frame's
primary deed tag is the ability's first tag, and judged evidence is ch.03's to compute. Counted evidence
fires from this chapter's events: `on_focus_spent` carries the ability's first tag and the Focus spent
(`cnt.focus`); a condition applied by an ability feeds `cnt.control`; harm prevented or reduced by one
feeds `cnt.ward` (03.7). Abilities used through a relic write no evidence (00.11.5). An emulation's
evidence lands on the emulated technique's first tag.

cards.title: The governing principle: stretch, emulate, and what an ability cannot do
cards.body: ### 05.5 The governing principle: stretch, emulate, and what an ability cannot do

cards.title: The principle sentence
cards.body:
**05.5.1 The principle sentence.** `[D]` Every ability's `principle` is one sentence with exactly one
**operation** (a verb) and one **object category** (what the verb acts on), written so that a new use can
be tested against it: "Push a body of air in one direction." "Set a mark on one creature that your
senses can follow." "Turn a blow aside with a shield." "Mend living flesh." The principle is the
derivation the DM reasons from when the player proposes a use the text does not list, in the way a
single physical rule lets every use of Allomantic pushing be derived instead of invented
[R2 #4; BRIEF A2 #12]. Principles are authored to a standard the script checks: at most 20 words, one
sentence, no number.

cards.title: Stretch (unstructured use)
cards.trigger: the player declares a use of a HELD ability or license that its scope text does not cover (01.3.4 finds an uncovered clause) and asks to do it with that ability
cards.license_check: the held ability itself, gate mode `stretch` (01.3.5). A license whose `stretch` is null cannot be stretched: G3 for the excess.
decisions: 1. SAME OPERATION [J:flag] "Does the new use perform the operation the principle sentence names, on something in the principle's object category, differing only in target, scale or form?" True only when both the verb and the object category still apply read literally. False when the use needs a different verb (pull where the principle pushes; create where it moves; know where it marks), a different object category (stone where it says air; a mind where it says a body), or appears on the cannot list (05.5.3). Uncertain -> false (SG-05).

2. SENSITIVE UPGRADE [J:flag] (01.3.3) "Would the stretched use give perception, memory, mobility, control, access, awareness or freedom the scope does not already grant?" True -> not a stretch: G3 or G4.
cards.computation: PR-05-2. The stretch is ALWAYS a rolled Working, even if the ability normally has check: none: verb = the ability's check.verb (default verb.handle), attribute = the ability's attribute, deed tag = its first tag. DC = the obstacle's DC (01.6.4) + stretch.dc_shift, shown as its own line. Focus = the ability's cost + stretch.cost_add. Reach capped at stretch.reach_cap. The ability's uses are spent as for a normal activation. Its listed effects apply only as far as the new use needs them, at most one severity rung, one condition, or delivered reach in ticks. Grade widens the prices (T-05-6): trained +5 DC, +1 Focus, Limited; expert +5 DC, +1 Focus, Standard; master +0 DC, +1 Focus, Standard. ch.04's Sure Hand adds a Precision lever (it counts toward the two-lever limit).
cards.stakes: framed as any beat (01.6.9); a critical failure of a stretched SPELL is a miscast (05.7.5)
state_writes: a ruling record with signature "<ability id>+stretch+<object>" (precedent, 00.15.6)
narration_may_not_imply: that the stretch is now part of the ability (the next use is a stretch again, at the same price, unless a precedent is reused)
success beyond the capped reach
cards.worst_case: decision 1 wrongly true: one beat at DC +5, one more Focus and Limited reach, which is worse than a licensed use by construction, logged with the principle sentence it relied on (class i and iv). Wrongly false: the player is redirected to the crude fallback or a basic verb and may point to the principle; the ruling ledger then holds the answer for next time (class iv).
examples: inside: ab.gust ("Push a body of air in one direction") used to blow a cloud of marsh gas off a bridge: same verb (push), same object (air), new target -> stretch (WE-05-2). inside (boundary): ab.flame_lance ("Throw a line of fire at one target") used to light a signal beacon at band.far: same verb, same object, the target is a thing and not a foe -> stretch; reach Limited = the beacon catches, slowly. outside: ab.gust used to pull a dropped letter toward the caster: the principle pushes; pulling is a different operation -> false. Redirect: push it against the far wall and go and get it. outside (boundary): ab.mend_flesh ("Close a wound in living flesh") used on a cracked wooden mast: the object category is living flesh; timber is not -> false. non-example: ab.quarrys_mark ("Fix your aim on one creature you have struck") used "to know where the creature will be tomorrow": that is foresight, a sensitive upgrade (awareness) the scope does not grant -> decision 2 true -> G3; the redirect names deed.arcane.divination and what the mark does give.

knobs.default: default obstacle + 5; allowed delta: +0 at master grade
default: the ability's own; allowed delta: object state or clock ticks when the target is a thing
default one; allowed delta: none upward

cards.title: The cannot list
cards.body:
**05.5.3 The cannot list.** `[D]` [DL-05-07; C:III; C:P9; revision: I-065] A stretch, an emulation, a flare or a ruling can never make an ability
do any of the following. Each line is a refusal by lookup, voiced with 01.3.6's redirect:
1. **Change its operation or its object category** (05.5.2 decision 1).
2. **Change the harm family it deals** (a `harm.fire` working stays fire) or add a harm type.
3. **Lift one of its own P12 fields**: act without its limitation, without its weakness, without its
   cost, or beyond its uses.
4. **Outlast its duration form** by more than the Lasting flare's one step, or become permanent.
5. **Reach past its band** by more than the Far flare's one band, or act on a target it cannot
   perceive.
6. **Grant** a license, an ability, a fact about the world's past, an item of lasting value, or a
   standing change the degree table did not deliver (INV-7).
7. **Add an action**, a second rider, or a second sustained working (INV-11; 05.4.3; 05.4.7).
8. **Supply a sensitive upgrade** its scope does not name (01.3.3).
9. **Contradict setting canon** (`canon_impossible`, the region's seed, 12.16.5): that is G4 for everyone.
10. **Affect more targets** than its spread tag's cap (05.10.4).

With lic.training.martial_blade she may emulate it and tick the clock; without it, she may ask the duelist to teach her.
