cards.title: The Ninefold Barrow: a fight that goes all the way to the menu (both keys shown)
cards.body:
### WE-07-1 The Ninefold Barrow: a fight that goes all the way to the menu (both keys shown)

*Situation.* Wren has come for the crown the Salt Guild's factor sold her a map to. In the last chamber
a **barrow-wight** rises (`adv.barrow_wight`: T3; attack +7, *grave-touch* S3 `harm.frost`; Guard 17;
Vitality 18; reduction 1; fearless; `lethal_context: true`; `defeat_disposition: kill`; `dread: S2`; its
master, `npc.barrow_king`, carries `can_bargain: true` and the recorded want "the crown returned").

**The warning (Key 1).** At `scene_start`, `h.07.lethal_scan` finds three rows true for the wight:
`advisory` (P1 against one T3 is two bands up: lethal, T-06-13), `archetype`, `disposition`. One context is
written, with the first true cause. The engine supplies the sign (the wight's tell); the DM narrates it
and appends the block:

> Frost creeps across the grave-goods toward your boots, and where it passes the gold goes dull.
> `[WARNING] THIS CAN KILL YOU — the barrow-wight. As things stand you are unlikely to win this.`
> `From your next action on, falling here can mean Dying. Fate: 1.`
> `Exits now: Yield — not accepted (it does not understand quarter) · Retreat — clean: it is slower than you; nothing to pay.`

`lethal_context {id: lc.barrow.wight, cause: advisory, shown: true, effective_from: after Wren's next
declaration}`. First sight of a `dread: S2` adversary: a dread check, Resolve +0 against Moderate (15):
d20 9 → failure → dread **1/7**.

**The fight.** The player stays for the crown and backs into a burial niche to keep the thing in front of
her. Rounds in brief (Wren's spear: +4 against Guard 17; her hits deal 3 − 1 = 2):

| Round | What happens | Wren's state |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Wren hits once (wight 16). The wight Moves to the niche's mouth: the feature has one way out and it now stands in it → `flag.cornered` (06.3.6). It Strikes: d20 14 + 7 − 2 (Fend) = 19 against Guard 14: hit; S3 frost = 5; the jack does not reduce frost. | Vitality 13 → **8** (worn) |
| 2 | Wren hits once (14). The wight: d20 12 → 17, hit, 5 → Vitality 3 (**bloodied**). Second Strike (repetition −2): d20 11 → 16, hit, 5: Vitality would be −2 → **0, Staggered; the excess 2 is discarded** (07.2.3). | Staggered; load 0/3 |

`trg.exits` → `[STATUS] STAGGERED — blows now wound you; at wound load 3 you fall to Dying. Load 0/3.
Exits: Yield — not accepted · Retreat — you are cornered: get past it first (06.5.6) · or fight on.`

| Round | What happens | Wren's state |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | Wren tries to Force past (fails), hits once (12). The wight: d20 15 → hit, 5: Staggered, so a **wound**: bucket Heavy (5–7), load +2 = **2**; family frost; site d12 = 8, body → *Frost-burned chest* (`inj.w.frost.body.s3`: −2 on Endure with Endurance, breathers restore nothing, maximum Vitality −2). Second Strike: **natural 20** → critical success → one rung heavier, S4 = 8: bucket Grievous, load +3 = **5 ≥ 3**. The context is effective and the wight's mode is lethal → **Dying 1** (brink 0). Site d12 = 2, arm → *Dead-white hand* (`inj.w.frost.arm.s4`). Prone. Dread +1. | Dying 1; dread 2/7 |

`[STATUS] DYING 1 of 3 — one action a turn; a check each turn (you need 8 or better; 65%). A blow adds a
step. Past 3 you choose from the last-chance menu. Exits: Yield — not accepted.`

| Round | What happens | Wren's state |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | Wren's one action: a last thrust from the floor (prone −2 is the worst status; +2 against 17): d20 7, miss. `turn_end`, **dying check**: d20 5 + 2 = 7 against 10: a failure by 3 → **holds**. The wight (a prone target is a lever): d20 6 + 7 + 2 = 15, hit: lethal harm → **Dying 2**; *Frostbitten foot* (leg, S3). Second Strike misses. | Dying 2 |
| 5 | Wren crawls for the back of the niche. Dying check against 15: d20 9 + 2 = 11: a failure by 4 → **Dying 3**. The wight: d20 13 → hit: the step would be 4 → **the Threshold** (07.5.1). The step is held at 3; this blow's harm is not applied; the conflict pauses; dread +2. | at the Threshold; dread 4/7 (shaken) |

**The menu (PR-07-5).** The engine evaluates the nine options against state:

| Option | Result | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Captured | not offered | the victor's disposition is kill |
| 2 Maimed | **offered**: *Lost hand* — Agility −1 (to +2), no two-handed methods; she stands at Vitality 2 | worst fresh wound: Grievous, arm; d2 between the arm maims |
| 3 Death's Bargain | **offered**: the barrow-king asks "return the crown of the Ninefold Barrow to its head" | a bargainer bound to the scene; its recorded want |
| 4 Left for Dead | not offered | kill makes sure |
| 5 Rout | not offered | cornered; no companion |
| 6 Reprieve | **offered**: fate 1 of 1 (first of her life) | `fate.current ≥ 1` |
| 7 Last Stand | **offered** | always |
| 8 Gamble | **offered**: 5% stand free · 35% live · 15% choose a price · **45% death** | Endure +2 against 15 |
| 9 The Road Ends | **offered** | always |

The DM strikes nothing: no fact rules out any survivor. Six remain; four are not death: valid.

**The two keys at this moment.** Key 1 holds: `lc.barrow.wight`, warned at the scene's start, effective
since Wren's first declaration. Key 2 does **not** hold: she is at the Threshold and has chosen nothing.
If any tool tried to write `harm_state.dead` now, the engine would refuse it. Only options 7 and 8 can
turn the second key.

**The choice.** The player takes the Bargain. Writes: stabilized (Dying ends; Staggered; Vitality 1); one
brink wound; `aff.deaths_debt` stage 1 (`cond.cursed` S1); a vow thread "Return the crown" with
`clk.deaths_debt` 0/8, +1 a week; the mark *Death's debtor* (a rime-white streak in her hair); the fact
"the wight lowers its hand and goes back to its slab"; wound load cleared; `setback.threshold`; chronicle:
"Walked out of the Ninefold Barrow owing the dead a crown." She leaves with three wounds (chest, hand,
foot), brink 1, a maximum Vitality of 7 (13 − 2 − 3 − 2 − 2 would be 4; the floor is half of 13, rounded up),
dread 4/7, and a debt that will come due.

*Boundary: the other cheap door.* Had she taken the **Reprieve**: fate 1 → 0; the last blow is undone;
Dying ends with no brink wound and no mark; Vitality 2; load 0; she stands, still cornered, facing a
wight with 12 Vitality. Her next reprieve would cost 2, and she has none.

*Other side: no Key 1.* Had no warning been shown (say the wight had been an unlisted improvisation and
no row had fired), round 3's second blow would have been `lethal: false`: load 5 → **Down**, not Dying.
A `kill` victor with no effective context can do no more (T-07-11): it leaves her for dead; she wakes a
watch later on the barrow floor with her wounds, and the engine raises the warning for any return.

*Tempting non-example.* "The natural 20: its hand closes on your heart, and you die." A critical success
is one severity rung (01.8.3). To a Staggered character it was a Grievous wound and a fall to Dying 1;
to a character at full Vitality it would have been 8 points and nothing more.

cards.title: The Tarn bridge: a hazard that nearly kills without a lethal frame, and why it cannot
cards.body:
### WE-07-2 The Tarn bridge: a hazard that nearly kills without a lethal frame, and why it cannot

*Situation.* Days earlier. Wren, at Vitality **4** after a scrap with poachers, crosses a rope bridge.
Its rot is a hidden danger (`haz.rotten_bridge`: a 40-ft fall, S4, `harm.physical.crush`; *illustrative, 10
owns*). She did not look it over, so nothing perceivable was established: the `severity` row needs the
source to be **perceived**, and it was not. No warning exists, so no context.

1. A plank goes. The hazard's resisted check: Evade, Agility +3 and the floor +1, against its listed DC,
   Hard (20): d20 9 → 13: failure → the hazard at its severity.
2. `apply_harm(S4, [harm.physical.crush], source {hazard}, lethal: true?)` — the tool tests 07.3.6: no
   effective context → **`lethal: false`**, logged `lethal_refused`. Falls take no reduction: 8.
   Vitality 4 → **0, Staggered; the excess 4 is discarded.** She is in the river.
3. The river in spate (`haz.river_spate`: S3, cadence a round, Endure against Hard; `lethal_context:
   false`) is a second source. Round 1, first exposure: Endure +2: d20 12 → 14: failure: 5, no reduction
   (the weight of water). She is Staggered: bucket Heavy, **load 2**; a first exposure makes a record:
   *Cracked ribs* (crush, body, S3).
4. Her turn: Exert to reach the bank (Might +1, the floor +1, the cracked ribs −2: +0) against Hard:
   d20 10: failure. Round 2, a continuing tick (periodic): Endure d20 4 + 2 − 2 (the ribs) = 4: a
   critical failure, one rung heavier: 8. Bucket Grievous: load 5 ≥ 3, **not lethal → Down** (07.2.9).
   No record (periodic).
5. A hazard's defeat is the `leave` row with its aftermath: she is carried down. One interval later she
   wakes on a gravel bar at the next place downstream, Staggered at Vitality 0, ribs cracked, her spear
   on the riverbed below the bridge (a recorded place: she can go back for it), the objective of the
   crossing lost, `setback.defeated` written.

**Why it could not kill her.** Three independent stops, each a `[D]` rule: (a) no lethal context was
effective for either source, so every harm event was `lethal: false` (07.3.6); (b) the fall's 8 points
could only Stagger a character with 4 Vitality (07.2.3); (c) non-lethal harm at load 3 ends at Down, and
a Down character's ladder is frozen (07.2.9). Nearly drowned is the worst the unannounced world can do.
And the world is now on notice: the gorge has been perceived, so the `severity` warning is raised and
shown; the next crossing is a fair lethal risk.

*Boundary: had she looked.* An Observe of the bridge that found the rot would have fired the warning
before she stepped out: "`[WARNING] THIS CAN KILL YOU — the bridge over the Tarn: a forty-foot drop. A
Grievous danger.`" Crossing would then be an Exert at Dire with `lethal: true`, shown in the OFFER. A
failure: 8 points, lethal: Vitality 4 → 0, Staggered, excess discarded. **Even warned, the fall alone
cannot kill.** Only a character who stepped onto that bridge already Staggered would fall to Dying 1
(a Grievous wound: load 3), and would then have dying checks, and then a menu.

*Tempting non-example.* "You fall forty feet onto rocks. Roll Endurance or die." No rule here rolls for
death. The fall is 8 Vitality through `apply_harm`.

cards.title: Blackroot: a poison runs its stages
cards.body:
### WE-07-3 Blackroot: a poison runs its stages

*Situation.* Ashford, a fortnight later; Wren is whole (Vitality 13). A Guild knife-man's blade is coated
(`aff.blackroot`: Hard; onset and cadence one interval; stage harm from stage 2; `warn_stage: 2`; six
checks and it runs its course).

| When | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the cut | The Strike hits: 3 − 1 = 2 (Vitality 11). A rider: **exposure**, Endure +2 against 20: d20 11 → 13 | failure → afflicted; onset one interval. He runs. |
| interval 1 | onset ends (`h.07.affliction_onset`) | **stage 1**: `cond.poisoned` S2 (−2 on all checks). "A numb line creeping from the cut." |
| interval 2 | stage check (no penalty from its own carrier): d20 9 → 11: a failure by 9 | **stage 2**: poisoned S3; stage harm S2 = 3, no reduction: Vitality **8**. Stage 2 is the warn stage → `[WARNING] THIS CAN KILL YOU — the blackroot in your blood. Untreated, Blackroot will put your life at risk at its next stage. Fate: 1. What stops it: a bitterwort draught; a healer; time (four more checks).` |
| interval 3 | She has walked to Maren the hedge-healer (an interval). Check: d20 15 → 17: a failure by 3 | **holds** at 2; stage harm 3: Vitality **5** (lethal now, and she is still active: it is only Vitality). |
| the same interval | Maren **Treats** the affliction: Intellect +2, medicine +3, kit lever +2 = +7 against 20: d20 16 → 23: success, reach 2 | Wren's next stage check holds a Precision lever. Maren has no bitterwort; her charcoal purge is a **general remedy**: one stage down → **stage 1**. |
| interval 4 | check with the lever: d20 12 + 2 + 2 = 16: a failure by 4 | **stage 2** again; harm 3: Vitality **2**. (One Treat a day: no second lever. One remedy a period: a second purge → stage 1.) |
| interval 5 | check: d20 18 + 2 = 20 | success → **stage 0: cured**; the carrier ends. Four checks used of six. |

She ends at Vitality 2 with no wound, owing Maren for two purges and a morning. *What a worse fourth
check would have begun:* stage 2's harm takes Vitality 2 → 0 (Staggered, excess discarded); the next
stage harm is periodic at 0 Vitality: load, no record; stage 3's 5 points are load 2; one more such
tick is load 4: Dying 1, lethal because she was warned at stage 2. From the warning to Dying is at least four
more failed checks: forty minutes of chances, each of them visible.

cards.title: Taken in the reeds: a capture that becomes a new adventure
cards.body:
### WE-07-4 Taken in the reeds: a capture that becomes a new adventure

*Situation.* (Chapter 12's WE-12-8 from this chapter's side.) Two Salt Guild riders (T2; `defeat_disposition:
capture`; `lethal_context: false`) run Wren down in the reed beds. P1 against two T2 is **hard**, and no
lethal row is true, so the framing carried the danger notice: "`[WARNING] A hard fight — you may well
lose this. Losing here means being taken alive by the Guild.`" Three rounds in she is Staggered:

> `[STATUS] STAGGERED — blows now wound you; at wound load 3 you go Down. Load 0/3.`
> `Exits: Yield — accepted: they would bind you and take you to the Guild · Retreat — they are mounted and`
> `want you: run for it (a chase), or rout: you get clear and the Guild's hold on the Salt Road tightens`
> `(Corner the Salt Road +2) · or fight on.`

**The yield.** "I throw down the spear." Accepted by lookup (capture). The allowed terms are read out; the
player chooses **keep one thing**: the Ember-Fang Charm. PR-07-7, yielded column:

1. `defeated {manner: yielded}`; `setback.yielded`; the conflict ends. No further harm; she is conscious.
2. Holding place `[J:enum]`: the engine returns the Guild's holds within reach; the nearest is the north
   warehouse in Ashford (00's fact "The Salt Guild owns the north warehouse"), two travel watches off.
   `advance_time` runs both watches and every boundary in them; she arrives at dusk and **saw the way**:
   the back lane and the river door are now facts she knows.
3. Bound (`cond.restrained`, until cleansed). Her spear, bow, rope, rations and 14 coin go to
   `cache.01 {holder: fac.salt_guild, place: the warehouse tally room}` with `clk.cache` 0/6. The charm
   stays on its thong (the term is a commitment on the victors).
4. `clk.captors_intent`, named "The factor's reckoning": 6 segments, sensed, +1 a day; the fate for this
   victor is *sale* (to the salt galleys; *illustrative, 09*). Not lethal: no warning.
5. Three openings, d8 without repeats: 6, 3, 1 → "they move prisoners down to the barge when the factor
   returns" (the clock's next tick) · "a Caravaners' agent has been asking the gate-men about a forester"
   (a rival who wants her free) · "the night guard, Tam, is young, bored and short of coin" (a named
   walk-on with a want). Each is written as a fact or an entity.
6. `thr.captivity` "Out of the Guild's hands": progress 0/6, public, racing the factor's reckoning.
7. `victory_over_pc` (the riders' sergeant is spoken of at the warehouse; 11); a reputation packet scoped
   to those who saw her brought in; chapter 12's director enters recovery.
8. Lead check: three openings, a known cache, a sensed clock. Passed.

**The next scene** is framed at the first moment she can act: a tally-room cage, a lamp, Tam on a stool
with a pair of dice. Everything a sandbox scene needs is in state: a place she has seen the way out of, a
clock with omens, people with wants, her gear forty feet away. She works on Tam (a Talk beat: ch.15): a
success at Standard reach ticks "Out of the Guild's hands" to 2/6. At the `day` boundary the reckoning
ticks to 1/6 with its omen ("the guards talk about someone who is coming"). Whether she bribes, slips
her bonds, waits for the Caravaners, or is marched to the barge and jumps, the capture has become the
adventure.

*Boundary: the same fight, fought to the end.* Staggered, then three wounds: load 3 under no lethal
context → **Down**. The defeated column: no term (the charm goes into the cache), bound, carried
unconscious (she did **not** see the way), waking in the cage with three Light wounds (a soldier's
sword through a padded jack is 2 points: the Light bucket) that her first rest will clear. Yielding
bought her the charm, the route and her senses.

*Tempting non-example.* "The sergeant takes pity and lets her go with a warning." A disposition is data;
the DM does not choose mercy. If the fiction is to free her, it does so through an opening she works.

cards.title: A broken night, and the days after the barrow
cards.body:
### WE-07-5 A broken night, and the days after the barrow

*Situation.* The night after WE-07-1. Wren: Vitality 1 of a maximum 7; wounds: chest (Heavy, 0/4), foot
(Heavy, 0/4), hand (Grievous, 0/6), brink 1 (0/4); dread 4/7; cursed at stage 1. She makes a dry camp in
a hollow with a fire: **camp**. Before she lies down the DM states the best case: no cap applies (light
armor, fed, sheltered, the curse is at stage 1), so "a full rest is possible; a watch check will run".

`advance_time(1 watch)`. Three hours in, 10's watch check interrupts: two figures at the edge of the
firelight.

- *Branch A: travelers.* They talk, share the fire, move on: no item of 07.8.3 happened. The rest was
  suspended and resumes; quality **full**. `rest_long {quality: full, site: camp, treated: false}`.
  Vitality 1 → **7**; dread stays 4 (a full rest would ease 1, but the debt's first stage says rests
  ease none); `rested_today`. Chapter 05 restores Focus to its maximum.
- *Branch B: robbers.* `conflict_start` with Wren in it: an interruption. It lasts four rounds (they run
  when she shows steel). She lies down again inside the hour and still gets her four hours: resumed,
  quality **partial**. Vitality to three quarters of 7, rounded up: **6**; dread unchanged;
  `rested_today` still set. Focus to three quarters.
- *Branch C: the same, and she chases them for an hour.* Beyond the allowance: **interrupted**: Vitality
  as a partial short rest: a quarter of 7, rounded up: +2 → 3. No `rested_today`. `watches_awake` is set
  to 2.

**The days after** (T-07-15), two ways:

| Day | On the road, no healer | In Ashford with Maren (haven; bed rest; treated daily) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | chest 1/4, foot 1/4, brink 1/4; hand 0/6 | Maren's Treat for the hand is Hard (20): +7 with her kit, needs 13. Day 1 she fails (the day's treatment is lost; the Heavy wounds still gain bed rest and rest): chest 2/4, foot 2/4, brink 2/4, hand 1/6 |
| 2 | 2/4, 2/4, 2/4; hand 0/6 | she succeeds, reach 2: everything treated: chest **4/4 healed**, foot **healed**, brink **healed**; hand 3/6. Maximum Vitality 13 − 3 = 10 |
| 3 | 3/4 … | hand 5/6 |
| 4 | chest, foot and brink **healed**; maximum 13 − 3 = 10; hand 0/6 | hand **healed**: maximum 13; a scar: *a dead-white, numb patch* (`inj.scar.frost`) |
| 7 | the hand has had no tick for 7 days: an exposure to `aff.wound_rot` (Endure +2 against Hard) | — |

On the road she is fit to fight in four days and carrying a wound that will not heal and may rot. In a
bed with a healer she is whole in four. Each of those days runs the world: the debt clock among them.

cards.title: Brack, bleeding out; and a break
cards.body:
### WE-07-6 Brack, bleeding out; and a break

*Situation.* Months on, under Grey Keep, with a hound companion, Brack (Vitality 8; 16 owns), and dread
at **5/7** (shaken) after a bad week. Ghouls (`lethal_context: true`, warned at the scene's start).

1. A ghoul's bite takes Brack from 3 to 0: a lethal event → **bleeding out**: `clk.bleeding_out` 0/4,
   public. The player sees it at once: "Brack is down and bleeding: four rounds."
2. End of round: 1/4. Wren's turn: Move to him (1 action); first aid, `verb.handle` against Moderate
   (15), Agility +3 and the floor: +4, no kit: needs 11: d20 6: nothing changes. Her third action: a
   Strike at the ghoul over him.
3. The ghoul bites Brack again: a further lethal event: +1 → 2/4. End of round: 3/4.
4. Wren's turn, first aid again (one attempt a round, PR note in Edge cases): d20 13 + 4 = 17: success →
   **stabilized**; the clock is voided. Brack will wake after a long rest with a Heavy body wound and
   cannot be sent to fight until it heals.

*The other branch.* d20 8: failure. End of round: 4/4: **Brack dies.** `setback.companion_dead`; the
ghouls' morale clock ticks −1; a dread check at S3 (Hard, 20) for Wren, Resolve +0: d20 12: failure:
dread +2 → **7/7: she breaks.** The resolve test against Hard: d20 14: not steeled. The engine draws three
haunts gated on what filled the track (the ravenous dead, a companion's death): *night terrors*, *a dread
of the ravenous dead*, *the stare*. The player picks **the stare**. Dread returns to 0; she is frightened
(S2) of the ghouls for the scene (−2 on all checks while she can see them; she cannot willingly close);
the codex shows **haunts 1 of 3**. She still chooses every action she takes.

*Boundary.* Had the resolve test shown a 20: **steeled**: dread to 3, `cond.heartened` (S2) for the scene: +2 on all checks, and the ghouls have made
a mistake.

cards.title: Three ways out of a cellar
cards.body:
### WE-07-7 Three ways out of a cellar

Wren, at Vitality 5, wants out of a fight she is losing. The same declaration, four states [revision: I-076]:

| The opposition | Pursuit test | What the DM says before she commits |
|---|---|---|
| two ghouls, slower than she is; she is engaged with one | willing (kill), not able | "**Clean.** One parting blow as you break away: its claw, a rung lighter: Light, which your jack turns (0). You leave the satchel on the far table." Certain. |
| a cinder hound, faster, hunting her; not engaged | willing and able | "**Run for it**: a chase, about three chances in five from here. Or **rout**: you get out for certain, and it follows your trail toward Ashford (Cinder Hunting Ground +2)." |
| the same hound, on the far side of the cellar door she has slammed and barred (T-06-9 row 11) | willing, not able (no way to follow) [revision: I-076] | "**Clean.** It will be through that door with a Force against Moderate; you will be up the stair by then. The satchel stays on the far table." |
| the same hound, and she is `flag.cornered` | — | "You cannot retreat with your back to the wall. Get past it first (Force or Move through, 06.5.6), or Yield (not accepted)." |

If she routs: the clock ticks 2 with its omen; `objective_lost`; `setback.retreated {severity: S3}`; she
is at the nearest place the stair reaches. *Non-example:* "I retreat, and since I got away clean nothing
is lost": the satchel's location is a fact; it is still on the table.

---

cards.title: Items: the schema, base items and quality
cards.body: ### 08.1 Items: the schema, base items and quality

cards.title: The item record
cards.body:
**08.1.1 The item record.** `[D]` Every item is an entity (00.6.1) whose record extends 00.6.2's `Item`.
The fields below are the complete shape; 00.6.2's six fields keep their names and meanings.

```yaml
Item (extends Entity; owner 08):
  base: bi.*                     # base item (data/base_items.yaml)
  quality: worn | common | fine | masterwork | wondrous | storied     # 08.1.4
  quality_index: 1..6            # the rung's index; 03's cnt.made reads it (lowest = 1)
  material: [mat.* | material.* tag]          # primary first; harvested parts keep their provenance
  signature: [Property]          # 0..1, the identity layer (00.11)
  properties: [Property]         # magnitude layer, 0..2
  worked: Property | null        # the ONE property added after making (enchanting, a crafter's addition; 08.6.10)
  flaw: Flaw | null              # from item_properties.yaml#flaws (Flawed results, cursed finds)
  sealed_properties: [prop_id]   # unidentified; sealed state (00.6.5), unsealed by 08.5.3
  bound_ability: {ability_id: ab.*, rank: 1..3} | null    # at most one (00.11.5; 05.2.8)
  relic: bool                    # derived: true when bound_ability or a license property is present
  feeds_evidence: bool           # false whenever relic is true (00.11.5; 04 request 11)
  cost_immune: bool              # true while a relic or storied item is attuned (01.13.4; 06.5.4)
  equipped: bool                 # 00.6.2
  slot: body slot id | null      # where it is worn or held (08.5.1)
  attuned: bool                  # 08.5.2
  condition: intact | damaged | broken | serviceable_until_rest_long     # 08.1.9
  uses: {current: int, max: int} | null         # kits, consumables, charges
  quantity: int | null           # stacked goods: arrows, torches, supply lots
  loaded: bool | null            # loading weapons (06.4.9)
  load: int                      # load units (08.9.1), computed from base and properties
  provenance: {domain: gen.loot | gen.craft | gen.gift | kit | bought | found,
               source_id: id | null, source_tags: [tag], circumstance: str | null, degree: str | null,
               rung: str, maker: id | null, made_at: time | null, place: place_id | null, tier_cap: int}
  facts: [fact_id]               # teaches:, kept_since:, made_by_holder:, gifted_by:, conjured:, recognizable_as:
  price: int                     # list price, computed (08.8.3)
Property: {prop_id: prop.*, tier: 1..6, effects: [effect_ref]}    # 00.6.2, unchanged
```

`provenance.maker` and `provenance.domain: gen.craft` are what 03's `cnt.made` counter reads; the quality
index is its weight (03 Interface request). Every field is written by a tool; narration restates only
what the record holds (INV-2) [R1 08 "items with states carry explicit state fields"; 00.6.2].

cards.title: Base items
cards.body:
**08.1.2 Base items.** `[D]` A base item (`bi.*`, `data/base_items.yaml`) fixes everything about an item
that does not come from its quality or properties: its `item_tags` (the most specific level-3 tag first,
per 03's request, so 03.1.6 can ground evidence in it), its `material_tags`, its kind, its **price** in
coins at quality `common`, its **load** (`weight` in the schema) in load units, its `slot_cap` (the most
properties it can hold), its body slot, its `make` (the training license, deed tag and time per tick that
crafting it uses), and the kind-specific fields of 08.1.5–08.1.8. There are **191** base items (185 plus the six prostheses of revision I-016) [verification: V2a-011] covering
every level-2 branch of `item.*`. Base items are content; adding one is a data entry with a DL line, never
a rule change [R3 00.1; 00.16.4].

cards.title: The four kinds of property
cards.body:
**08.1.3 The four kinds of property.** `[D]` Every property in `data/item_properties.yaml` declares
`kind`, and the kind fixes when it works:

| Kind | What it is | Works when | Takes an ability slot? | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **mundane** | a property of make: magnitude only (an edge, a harm edge, a reduction, carry, a snag waived, durability) | the item is **equipped** (worn, wielded or in hand); no attunement | no | Keen, Balanced, Sturdy, Quiet, Warm |
| **passive** | a magical effect: additive or triggered | the item is **equipped and attuned** (08.5.2) | no | Ember-warded, Rending, Darksight, Hunter's sense |
| **license** | lets the bearer attempt what a named license permits, with no competence | equipped and attuned | no | Lock-whisper (thievery at trained), Stone-sense |
| **item_ability** | one active ability (`ab.*`) the item holds | equipped, attuned and **bound** to an equipped slot (05.2.8) | yes: one `equipped` slot | a fang that lets the bearer Pounce |

This is the whole answer to "what does an item grant" at the level of kind; 08.4 is the rest
[00.11.5; C:P5 "passive ... or active"; R3 08.10].

cards.title: The quality ladder
cards.body:
**08.1.4 The quality ladder.** `[D]` Every item has exactly one quality rung. The rung fixes its slot
counts (00.11.3 step 3), its price multiplier, and its index for 03's `cnt.made`.

| Index | Rung | Signature slots | Magnitude slots | Price (× base) | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **worn** | 0 | 0 | ×½ (minimum 1) | below standard; **fragile**: a `cost.gear` against it is taken one severity rung heavier |
| 2 | **common** | 0 | 0 | ×1 | standard, serviceable work |
| 3 | **fine** | 0 | 1 | ×3 | better make; its one magnitude slot is **open** (empty) unless a generator or a crafter fills it; a fine garment or jewel is a citable status fact |
| 4 | **masterwork** | 1 | 1 | ×10 | a master's work or a true trophy: the identity layer opens |
| 5 | **wondrous** | 1 | 2 | ×30 | the best that hands, hoards and powers produce |
| 6 | **storied** | 1 | 2 | authored | a named, hand-authored item: a fixed property set, exempt from mod groups, never exempt from the item share (08.2) or the slot cap; never generated |

Slot counts are clamped to the base item's `slot_cap` (a garment's cap is 2, so a wondrous cloak has one
signature and one magnitude slot). Chapter 02's assumed names map exactly: `worn` < `common` < `fine` are
rungs 1–3 of this ladder; 02.8.2's "nothing above fine, nothing from a generator pool" means a kit's `fine`
item arrives with its slot **open** (02 Interface request; DL-08-03) [R3 08.9; R2 08 "rarity specializes";
00.11.3].

cards.title: Weapons
cards.body:
**08.1.5 Weapons.** `[D]` Every weapon is built on chapter 06's **T-06-6** (weight → base severity,
Strike cost, hands, bands) and **T-06-7** (at most two of twelve properties). This chapter's assumed table,
stated so the interface is checkable, is 06's exactly: unarmed S1 (1 action); light and one-handed S2 (1
action); heavy S3 (2 actions); bows S2 (1 action; longbow reaches `band.far` with no snag); light crossbow
S2 (reload 1), heavy crossbow S3 (reload 2). Base severity is raised by the wielder's **mastery** (06.4.5:
expert +1 rung, master +2), which lives at E1 outside the ±2 effect-step cap; item harm edge sits inside
the +2 harm-edge cap and inside the item share of +1 (08.2.2). The roster:

| Weight | Base items (weapon properties) |
|---|---|
| light | knife (close_quarters, concealable) · dagger (finesse, thrown) · short sword (finesse, parrying) · hand axe (thrown) · club · sap (concealable, close_quarters) · whip (reach, entangling) · darts ×5 (thrown, concealable) · throwing knives ×3 (thrown, concealable) · net, bolas (thrown, entangling) |
| one-handed | arming sword (versatile, parrying) · rapier (finesse, parrying) · battle axe (versatile) · mace (armor_breaking) · war hammer (armor_breaking, versatile) · flail (armor_breaking, close_quarters) · spear (reach, thrown) · quarterstaff (versatile, parrying) · javelin (thrown) |
| heavy | greatsword (parrying) · great axe (reach) · maul (armor_breaking) · pike (reach) · halberd (reach, armor_breaking) · lance (reach; 1 action from the saddle with `lic.training.martial_mounted`) |
| bow | shortbow · longbow · sling (one hand) |
| crossbow | light crossbow (loading) · heavy crossbow (loading, armor_breaking) |

Each weapon names its **deed tag** (the primary tag of its Strike, 00.5.6) and the **training license**
whose grade sets mastery (`lic.training.martial_<child>`). Ammunition (arrows, bolts, sling bullets) is a
quantity of 20 per lot; half of what is spent is recovered after a conflict (06.4.9). *Interface flag:* if
06 retunes T-06-6 or T-06-7, `base_items.yaml` is regenerated from the same script; no rule text here
changes [06 Interface request to 08; DL-08-04].

cards.title: Armor
cards.body:
**08.1.6 Armor.** `[D]` [DL-07-14; DL-08-07; C:P12; R5 EQ-01; revision: I-065] Worn armor reduces `harm.physical` from attacks and shaped effects by **light 1,
medium 2, heavy 3** (07.2.2; T-06-11); total reduction from all sources is capped at 4 by chapter 07, and
items' share of it is 3 (08.2.2). Armor pays for its reduction in the other pillars, each a data field:

| Armor | Kind | Price | Load worn / carried | Snags (engine-cited Precision snags) | Don | Sleeping in it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| padded jack | light | 5 | 1 / 2 | — | 1 interval | no effect |
| leather | light | 10 | 1 / 2 | — | 1 interval | no effect |
| hide coat | light | 8 | 1 / 2 | Swim | 1 interval | no effect |
| brigandine | medium | 60 | 2 / 4 | Swim | 1 interval | long rest at best partial (07.8) |
| mail hauberk | medium | 50 | 2 / 4 | Sneak, Swim | 1 interval | partial |
| scale coat | medium | 45 | 2 / 4 | Sneak, Swim | 1 interval | partial |
| splint | heavy | 200 | 3 / 6 | Sneak, Swim, Exert | 2 intervals | partial |
| plate | heavy | 400 | 3 / 6 | Sneak, Swim | 3 intervals alone, 1 with help | partial |

The snags are the armor's **intrinsic** costs, cited by the engine as the fact `armor.<item>` (outside
the two-cited count, inside the ±4 cap, like 06's repetition snags); the mundane properties *Quiet* and
*Supple* waive them (`eff.05.waive`). A helm is a garment, not armor: it carries no reduction and is the
base for head-slot properties [07 Interface request to 08; 06 "armor carries its costs in other pillars"].

cards.title: Shields
cards.body:
**08.1.7 Shields.** `[D]` [DL-06-08; DL-07-14; R5 EQ-01; revision: I-065] A shield gives **+1 edge to Guard** (T-06-7 `shield_light` / `shield_heavy`) and
**reduces nothing** (07.2.2). Four base items: **buckler** (light; load 0; does not grant Full defense's
cover; the shield hand may also hold a lit torch or a light item, not a weapon), **round shield** (light;
grants Full defense's cover), **kite shield** (heavy; usable mounted; Exert and Sneak take a snag),
**tower shield** (heavy; not usable mounted; while its bearer Defends and does not Move it is a cover
feature for one ally engaged with the bearer). A shield bash is an unarmed-weight Strike (S1) under
`deed.martial.shield.bash`. Because a shield already fills the item share of Guard edge (+1), a Guarding
property never generates on a shield or alongside a parrying weapon (08.2.4).

cards.title: The other branches
cards.body:
**08.1.8 The other branches.** `[D]` [DL-00A-13; C:II; R5 EQ-01; revision: I-065] (Every entry in `base_items.yaml`; the table is the summary.)

| Branch | Base items | What the base does on its own |
|---|---|---|
| `item.garment` | plain, working, fine and courtly clothes; winter furs; desert robes; cloak; oilskin cloak; boots; soft shoes; gloves; riding gauntlets; hood; hat; helm | clothes carry a **status** (plain / fine / noble) that is a citable fact where station matters; winter furs and desert robes carry an **intrinsic** hazard step (cold / heat one rung lower); the oilskin waives the rain snag |
| `item.jewelry` | ring, signet ring, amulet, torc, charm, circlet | nothing mundane but status; a signet is a citable seal; charms are the default trophy base (a fang, a scale, a feather on a thong) |
| `item.tool.kit` | thieves' tools, healer's kit (10 uses), climbing kit, rope, disguise kit (5), forgery kit (5) | each grants a **Precision lever** for its named beats, and its absence makes some licensed beats improvised (+5 DC) |
| `item.tool.instrument` | lute, flute, drum, horn | required for an instrumental performance |
| `item.tool.implement` | wand, casting staff (also a quarterstaff), orb, holy symbol, totem | the **sign** of 05.7.4 when it bears the keeper's mark; the **vessel** of 05.6.12 when kept a season or made by the holder (08.4.7) |
| `item.tool.trade` | smith's, woodworker's, leatherworker's, weaver's, alchemist's, cook's, mason's, tinker's, jeweler's, enchanter's tools; writing case; tools of the work; crowbar, grappling hook, shovel, manacles, spyglass, mirror, tent, fishing gear | trade tools give the Precision lever every licensed crafting beat needs (08.6.4); the others each name their lever |
| `item.tool.light` | torches ×5, lantern, candles ×10, tinderbox | light and burn time (08.9.5) |
| `item.tool.container` | backpack, belt pouch, satchel, sack, waterskin, strongbox, scroll case, bedroll and cook-pot | holds; a bedroll makes a camp a camp rest site, not rough (07.8) |
| `item.consumable` | healing draughts, clarity draught (Focus), elixirs, toxins, trail rations, scrolls, lamp oil, firepot, smoke pot, weapon oils (rime, ember, silvering, holy water), whetstone, bandages, antidotes and four specific remedies, salve | their `effects`, used up per use; oils claim `slot.strike_delivery` at rank **20** (05.10.3's 20–24 band) |
| `item.goods` | trade goods (salt, grain, cloth, ore, timber, spices, wine, furs, dyes, working stock), treasure (gems at 10 / 100 / 1,000, art objects at 50 / 500, a silver trade bar of 50), documents (letter, map, ledger, book, spellbook, manual, pattern book, charter) | value, and for documents the facts they carry (`teaches:`, title) |
| `item.conveyance` | donkey, pony, mule, riding horse, draft horse, courser, destrier; saddle and tack; light and heavy barding; handcart, cart, wagon, sledge, carriage; raft, rowboat, keelboat, river barge, sailing cog | carry capacity, pace, upkeep, crew (08.10) |

cards.title: Condition: intact, damaged, broken, destroyed
cards.body:
**08.1.9 Condition: intact, damaged, broken, destroyed.** `[D]` Chapter 01's `cost.gear` writes an item's
`condition` (01.13.4); this rule fixes what each value means (01 and 05 Interface requests):

| Condition | Written by | What still works | What stops | Mended by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **intact** | default | everything | — | — |
| **damaged** | `cost.gear` S3; `ab.sunder` rank 1; a failed crafting step on the item | the base item's weight, severity, bands and Strike; its signature, passive, license and bound ability | its **edge, harm-edge and reduction** — the mundane magnitude properties, the T-06-7 edge and harm-edge properties (versatile, parrying, shield), and **one point** of a worn armor's base reduction (heavy 3 → 2 …) | a crude repair (`verb.handle`, Easy, 1 interval: *serviceable until the next* `rest_long`, then damaged again; worn, common or fine items only [revision: I-079]) or a lasting repair (08.6.7) |
| **broken** | `cost.gear` S4; `ab.sunder` rank 2 | nothing but its value as salvage | the item does not function at all; a bound ability unbinds; a relic's license and passives are dormant | a licensed repair only (08.6.7); never by Handle |
| **destroyed** | `cost.gear` S5 | — | it is gone (`exists = destroyed`) | — |

An item that carries a **signature or a bound ability is never destroyed** by a cost: an S5 `cost.gear`
against it takes 01.13.4's other S5 form, *location sealed as unknown* (swept away, lost in the flood),
and the engine writes a rumor of where it fetched up (11), so it can be found again (07.6.4's principle).
A **worn** item takes every `cost.gear` one rung heavier (S2 → damaged); a **Sturdy** or dwarf-made item
one rung lighter (08.2.3) [01.13.4; 07.6.4; R1 08 object state].

cards.title: cost_immune
cards.body:
**08.1.10 `cost_immune`.** `[D]` An item is `cost_immune: true` while it is a **relic or a storied item
and attuned** to its bearer. `cost.gear` may not target it (01.13.4), no ability breaks it (`ab.sunder`'s
excludes), and it cannot be disarmed (06.5.4). It can still be taken from a defeated, robbed or captured
bearer (07.6.4's caches): immunity protects against attrition, not theft. *Why:* a bound relic is a
character's identity piece; losing it to a near-miss die roll is the "losing gear hurts more than the
numbers suggest" failure (R1 07), while losing it to a captor is a story with a way back [01 Interface
request; DL-08-05].

cards.title: Improvised weapons and objects
cards.trigger: a Strike, throw or block declared with an object that is not a weapon base item
cards.license_check: basic verb: verb.strike (G1); an improvised weapon is always legal
decisions: 1. RESEMBLANCE [J:enum] Which weapon does the object most resemble in how it is used? options: a base weapon of 08.1.5 (true only when the object is used the same way and is about that weapon's size: a chair leg -> club; a pitchfork -> spear; a wood-axe -> battle axe; a smith's hammer -> war hammer; a broken bottle -> knife) | none (false for every object with no weapon of similar use and size: a lantern, a book, a cooking pot) | default when uncertain: none
2. SIZE RUNG (only when resemblance is none) [J:rung] 06's improvised ladder: hand (one hand lifts and throws it) | body (about a person's weight) | heavy / massive (dropped or toppled only)
cards.computation: resembles W -> W's weight, base severity, bands and Strike cost, with NO weapon properties, NO mastery (its deed tag is deed.martial.thrown.improvised for throws, else the resembled weapon's), and the frame carries the engine-cited Precision snag "improvised" unless the wielder holds the resembled weapon's training license. none -> 06's improvised table: hand S1 (S2 if it resembles a light weapon), body S3 for two actions with one Precision snag, heavy S3 / massive S4 dropped or toppled. On a critical failure the object takes cost.gear S4 (broken) in addition to any cost.
state_writes: the object's condition on a critical failure
narration_may_not_imply: weapon properties the object does not have (reach, parrying)
harm above the computed severity
cards.worst_case: the neighboring weapon is chosen: at most one severity rung (S2 vs S3) or one action of cost; shown in the OFFER before commitment (class i)
examples: inside: a smith's hammer swung at a thief -> war hammer: S2, 1 action, snag "improvised" (no armor_breaking: properties do not carry over). inside (boundary): a pitchfork -> spear: S2 with reach? No: reach is a property and does not carry; it Strikes at band.engaged only. outside: a lantern thrown -> none, hand rung S1, plus whatever the lantern's fire does as an environment use (06.5.10). tempting non-example: "my iron frying pan is basically a mace, so it ignores armor" -> resemblance mace gives S2; armor_breaking is a property and is not inherited.
basis: 01 Interface request: "improvised weapons use the resembled weapon's stats"
cards.body:

```

Trigger [T]:        a Strike, throw or block declared with an object that is not a weapon base item
```

cards.title: Resolving item tags to base items
cards.body:
**08.1.12 Resolving item tags to base items.** `[D]` [DL-02-13; DL-00A-13; revision: I-065] Wherever a rule names an item by **tag** (02's kits,
00.17.1 Q17; 09's trophy bases; a region's stock, 12.16.9), the engine resolves it in this first-match order:
(1) a base item whose `default_for` is that tag; (2) for a level-3 tag, the first base item carrying it;
(3) for a level-2 tag with no default, the first base item carrying it or a descendant. Two tags resolve
with an extra field: `item.tool.trade` resolves to **tools of the work** (`bi.work_tools`), which carries
the fact `serves: <deed tag>` set from the livelihood's first craft, trade or work deed tag (02's kit
note), so a herder's shears serve `deed.wilds.animals` and a scribe's case serves `deed.craft.scribing`;
`item.goods.document` with a `teaches:` note resolves to `bi.spellbook` (or `bi.manual` /
`bi.pattern_book` by the taught id's prefix: `ab.*`/`rit.*`, `lic.training.*`, `prop.*`). Kit quantities
of food are **supply** (1 per day, 08.9.4); a kit's riding horse is `bi.riding_horse` at `worn`. The full
mapping for all 39 tags 02's kits use is `base_items.yaml#kit_resolution` [02 Interface request;
00.17.1 Q17].

cards.title: Every item has an id from its first mention
cards.worst_case: an inert object is recorded needlessly (harmless) or a relevant one is not (12's claim-vs-state check catches the unrecorded mention; class iv).
cards.body:
**08.1.13 Every item has an id from its first mention.** `[D]` + `[J:flag]` A found, bought, made, given
or narrated object that could later be used, sold, lost or cited is created as an item entity before the
narration that introduces it (00.6.6; INV-16). *Flag:* "Could the player cite this object later as a
weapon, a tool, a lever, a valuable or a material?" True for a sword on a rack, a coin purse, a strange
gem, a body that could be harvested; false for the clutter of a room described as clutter. Uncertain →
true. Coin is never an item: it is the `coin` quantity, and every change is `update_quantity` with a
reason; narration never states a post-transaction total the tool did not return (the gold-hallucination
failure) [R1 08 "wealth, counts and inventories are the most fragile state"; R4 §9 08 #4]. *Worst case (J):*
an inert object is recorded needlessly (harmless) or a relevant one is not (12's claim-vs-state check
catches the unrecorded mention; class iv).

cards.title: The item-layer power budget
cards.body: ### 08.2 The item-layer power budget

cards.title: What items never do
cards.body:
**08.2.1 What items never do.** `[D]` No item, property, consumable, relic or storied item: (a) changes an
attribute (00.4.3); (b) grants competence (00.3.6; a relic's license carries none, 08.4.4); (c) raises the
maximum of Vitality or Focus (those grow with power band and callings: 07, 05); (d) adds an action (INV-11)
or a reaction (06 alone grants those); (e) adds or moves an ability slot (05.2.2); (f) restores Focus
except as a consumable under 05.6.11's cap of 4 per long rest; (g) feeds a calling tier (00.11.5). These
seven are where a character's identity lives; items act only through edge, harm edge, reduction,
resistance, levers, triggered effects, licenses without competence, movement modes, hazard steps, and
`adjust`-family quantities [C:P2; C:P5; R1 08 "gear must not outclass innate abilities"; DL-08-07].

cards.title: The item share
cards.body:
**08.2.2 The item share.** `[D]` In every capped family, the contributions that come **from items** (base
item properties such as `versatile` and `shield`, mundane and passive properties, worked properties,
consumables) are summed and clamped to the **item share** before they join the family at evaluation-pass
step E4 (00.10.4). The item share is always smaller than the family's cap, so the rest of the cap belongs to
abilities, callings and composites:

| Family (00.10.6) | Family cap | **Item share** | What fills the rest |
|---|---|---|---|
| edge (per quantity: a check of a given scope, one defense, an effect DC) | +2 | **+1** | abilities, calling capabilities |
| harm_edge (per harm event) | +2 | **+1** | abilities (Cinder Stride's +1), composites |
| reduction (per harm tag, worn armor included) | 4 (07) | **3** | abilities (Thick Hide, Stone-Flesh), wards |
| multiplier (resistance ×½) | one ×½ | **one ×½, only from a signature at tier 4+** | abilities, rites |
| step (severity, reach, stakes, hazard steps) | ±2 from effects | **±1** | abilities, rites |
| circumstance (levers) | ±4, ≤ 2 levers | **at most one item-granted lever per roll** | facts of the scene, Setup, abilities |
| adjust: carry | the quantity's envelope | **+4** | — |
| adjust: supply use | — | **−1 per day** | foraging (10) |
| adjust: Focus cost | 05.6.3: −1 per activation | **−1, once per scene, only an implement's signature** | abilities |

Example: a weapon with `versatile` (+1 harm edge in two hands) gains nothing from a Keen property (the item
share of harm edge is already full), and the generator will not place Keen on it (08.2.4); a character
whose cloak is Ember-warded (reduce fire 2) and whose amulet is too (2) has an item fire reduction of 3, not
4. *Implementation:* every modifier the engine collects at E0 already knows its source entity; the sub-cap
is one sum-and-clamp per family before E4's family stacking (Interface request to 00) [R3 00.13 "a per-layer
power budget"; R3 #11; PG5's jewel-socket meta; DL-08-07].

cards.title: Per-item caps
cards.body:
**08.2.3 Per-item caps.** `[D]` [DL-08-02; DL-08-28; DL-08-27; C:V; C:P11; revision: I-065] One item holds at most its rung's slots (08.1.4), clamped to its base
`slot_cap` (weapons, armor, shields, jewelry, implements 3; garments, tools, mounts 2; consumables and
goods 0), plus its one `worked` property only if a magnitude slot is open for it (08.6.10). At most one
property per `mod_group` (00.11.3 step 6), at most one **on-hit** trigger (mod group `on_hit`), at most one
**retort** trigger, at most one **item-bound ability** (it may sit only in the signature slot), at most one
**license** property (mod group `relic_license`, also signature-only). These make every item readable in
one line of the codex.

cards.title: Saturation at generation
cards.body:
**08.2.4 Saturation at generation.** `[D]` [DL-08-07; C:P11; revision: I-065] When the generator (00.11.3 step 1) gates a pool, it drops every
entry whose family the **base item already fills to the item share**: harm-edge properties on a versatile
weapon; Guarding on a shield or beside a parrying weapon; Reinforced on heavy armor (3 of 3). At step 9 it
checks the item's whole contribution against the item share and, on a breach, drops that pick and refills
once (00.11.3 step 9). The simulation counts 10 such refills in 1,000 drops [verification: V2a-013] and **1,000 of 1,000 items
compliant** after generation (T-08-16).

cards.title: Attunement limit
cards.body:
**08.2.5 Attunement limit.** `[D]` A character may have at most **five** items attuned at once (08.5.2).
Mundane properties need no attunement; passive, license and item-ability properties do. Five sits between
D&D 5e's three attuned items and Pathfinder 2e's ten invested items, and it is the number at which the item
shares bind for about one character in five (T-08-16: with five attuned items drawn from a realistic haul,
19.2% would exceed an edge share, 8.8% the harm-edge share and 28.0% a reduction share without the
clamp; `08-loot-sim-output.txt`) [verification: V2a-013] [revision: I-036, re-run] — so the choice of *which* five is a real choice, which is the point of a budget [R2 08 Iron Man
Principle; DL-08-14].

cards.title: The math: gear never out-scales callings
cards.body:
**08.2.6 The math: gear never out-scales callings.** `[N]` The numbers below use 00.3.7's envelope, 06.4.5's
mastery and 07.2.2's armor; "items" means the item share at its maximum.

| | P1 novice | P3 elite | P5 legend |
|---|---|---|---|
| Best-domain base modifier (attribute + competence + edge) | +3 + 2 + **1 (item)** = +6 | +3 + 5 + 1 (ability) + **1 (item)** = +10 | +4 + 6 + 1 + **1** = +12 (cap) |
| Items' part of the check modifier | 1 of 6 (17%) | 1 of 10 (10%) | 1 of 12 (8%) |
| Strike harm, one-handed weapon, unarmored foe, Standard reach | S2 3 + **1** = 4 | expert S3 5 + **1** = 6 | master S4 8 + 1 (ability) + **1** = 10 |
| Items' part of harm | 1 of 4 (25%) | 1 of 6 (17%) | 1 of 10 (10%) |
| Physical reduction (armor + items / cap 4) | light 1 + **1** = 2 | medium 2 + **1** = 3 | heavy 3 + 1 (ability) = 4 |
| Growth from P1 to P5 owed to callings | — | — | check +6 of +6; harm +5 of +6; Vitality +8 of +8 |

Against a Guard-13 foe the P1's item edge moves success from 65% to 70% (T-00-6); at P5 the same +1 is the
difference between 35% and 40% against a Very hard target (25) [verification: V2a-012]. Items never stop mattering — they are the
specialization a character *chooses* — but at every band the calling owns at least 75% of the check
modifier's growth and all of the maxima. The two edge caps of 00.3.5 (+2 edge, +2 harm edge) are therefore
never filled by gear alone, which is 00.17.1 Q2's demand ("passive and mundane properties … count against
08's item-layer budget") stated as numbers [R1 08; R3 00.13; DL-08-07].

cards.title: Item density by band
cards.body:
**08.2.7 Item density by band.** `[N]` + `[D]` Encounter tuning (09) and pacing (12) may rely on this
assumption, which follows from the drop check (08.3.3), two fights per session, one site treasure about every
four sessions, principals who always drop, and 04's tier pacing (tiers at sessions ~4/9/19/34/56); the
campaign simulation holds it at every band (T-08-17) [revision: I-018; I-036]:

| Power band | Sessions in band (focused) | Property items won (typical) | Attuned (of 5) | Bound abilities (of 4 equipped slots) | Highest signature tier usual |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | 1–9 | 2–4 | 0–2 | 0 | 2 |
| P2 | 9–19 | 4–6 | 2–4 | 0–1 | 3 |
| P3 | 19–34 | 8–12 | 4–5 | 1–2 | 3–4 |
| P4 | 34–56 | 15–25 | 5 | 2–3 | 4–5 |
| P5 | 56+ | 25+ | 5 | 2–4 | 5–6 |

Items won past five are traded, salvaged into materials and recipes (08.6.8), given away or kept for
their mundane use; nothing past the attunement limit adds power. A campaign whose actual density runs more
than one row ahead of this table is the VI revisit trigger for the drop check (OEQ-08-2) [R1 08 "item
density is a balance assumption"; R2 08 HWFWM's loot system retired for over-generating].

cards.title: Loot: what a defeat or a find yields
cards.body: ### 08.3 Loot: what a defeat or a find yields

cards.title: When loot generates
cards.body:
**08.3.1 When loot generates.** `[T]` + `[D]` `generate(gen.loot, source, circumstance, degree, options)`
(tool #24) is called by PR-08-1 in exactly these cases:
1. **A side is defeated.** On `conflict_end` (or when the last member of a side is defeated, yields or
   breaks), once **per defeated side**, with source = the side's highest-band member that was defeated or
   yielded (a mob, a pack or a warband is one side, 06.10.2). Members that fled (`drive_off`) take their
   gear and purses with them.
2. **A body or a yielded creature is searched outside a conflict** (a sentry knocked out, a duel won):
   once, with that creature as source.
3. **A found thing is searched**: a cache, a corpse found dead, a chest, a lair's hoard, a site's treasure
   (source = the hoard's keeper if known, else the place, 08.3.12), with the degree of the resolved search
   beat (Observe or Handle).

Only resolved outcomes generate (00.11.2): a defeat must carry the frame id of the beat that caused it
(06.13.3's `on_defeat` payload); a narrated kill that was never resolved yields nothing. Independently of
any property item, every **body** may be harvested (08.3.10) and every carrier of coin or gear yields its
purse and gear (08.3.11) — so every resolved defeat yields *something*, which is constitution P5's "a
defeated source drops an item generated from its gated pool" [C:P5 sixth pass; R3 #8; 06.13.3].

**Once a season per creature.** `[D]` When a creature gives the party loot (it was a loot call's source, or
its purse was taken), the engine writes `loot.given_on = <date>` on it. For one season (11.11) after that date
the creature is **spent**: a later defeat or search of it calls no drop check and gives no purse; it yields
only the gear it now carries (gear the party already took is gone) and its body (08.3.10). A side whose
highest-band defeated member is spent takes its highest-band unspent defeated member as source; a side whose
defeated members are all spent calls no `gen.loot`. After a season the creature has re-armed and earned
again, and yields normally. A spar by agreement is not a defeat for loot at all (03.5.5). This closes the
daily rematch: a hired sellsword, a friendly duelist or a yielder let go and fought again gives its purse and
its chance at a drop once a season, not once a day [revision: I-041] [DL-08-34].

cards.title: The loot circumstance
cards.trigger: PR-08-1 step 2 (a generate(gen.loot) call is due)
cards.license_check: none (classification of a resolved outcome)
decisions: 1. CIRCUMSTANCE [J:enum] (gen_loot.yaml#circumstances; cites frame and fact ids) decisive - true only when the source was defeated by the PC's own resolved beat (its frame id is on on_defeat) in a conflict in which the PC was never Staggered or Dying and no frame against the PC was lethal. False for a foe finished by an ally, a companion or a hazard; a fight in which the PC was Staggered; a foe that yielded and was spared. costly - true only when the source was defeated by the PC's own resolved beat AND during that conflict the PC was Staggered or Dying, or a frame against the PC was lethal. False for a hard fight the PC came through above 0 Vitality with no lethal frame. (This is gen_absorb's narrow_survival: one classification serves both domains, 04.10.) merciful - true only when the source yielded, was subdued nonlethally, or broke and was let go, by the PC's own resolved beat, AND a mercy fact is written (it is spared alive). False for a creature bound and then killed; for a mindless creature (creature.undead.mindless, creature.construct, creature.horror.ooze), which cannot yield. scavenged - none of the above: found dead, killed by another or by a hazard, or a thing found rather than won; the degree is the SEARCH beat's. DEFAULT when uncertain.
cards.computation: fill method: decisive -> signature; costly -> biased (bias tag ward); merciful -> chosen; scavenged -> weighted (gen_loot.yaml#fill_map) quality rung: decisive, costly, merciful (success or critical success) -> masterwork; scavenged: critical success or success -> fine; failure or critical failure -> common
cards.stakes: none (no roll; the degree comes from the frame that produced the defeat or the find)
state_writes: the generated item(s) and the generation log (PR-08-1)
narration_may_not_imply: any property, tier or rung the output does not hold
that the foe "dropped" a thing it never carried (a wolf carries no coin)
cards.worst_case: decisive vs costly: the signature is the source's own instead of a ward-biased draw, same rung (class i); merciful vs decisive: the player chooses among three instead of receiving the signature, same rung (class i); scavenged vs a won circumstance: fine instead of masterwork, one rung (class i). Errs toward the default (scavenged) when uncertain, which errs low (SG-05 tie-break "does this grant something?" -> no).
examples: inside decisive: Wren shoots the spider dead with her own arrow, never below half Vitality -> decisive. boundary costly: the same fight, but the spider's bite took her to 0 and she shot it while Staggered -> costly. boundary merciful: the bandit captain yields at 2 Vitality and Wren lets him go with his life (fact mercy.bandit_captain) -> merciful; he gives up his sword. tempting non-example: "I killed it cleanly while my hound held it" -> the killing frame is Wren's, so decisive; but if the hound's bite was the defeating frame, the circumstance is scavenged (the PC's own beat did not defeat it).
cards.body:
**08.3.2 The loot circumstance.**

```
### 08.3.2  Loot circumstance: how was it won?                      [J:enum] [D]
Trigger [T]:        PR-08-1 step 2 (a generate(gen.loot) call is due)
Loads in:           situation.conflict, situation.exploration, situation.downtime
License check:      none (classification of a resolved outcome)
Decisions (J):      1. CIRCUMSTANCE [J:enum] (gen_loot.yaml#circumstances; cites frame and fact ids)
                       decisive - true only when the source was defeated by the PC's own resolved beat
                         (its frame id is on on_defeat) in a conflict in which the PC was never Staggered
                         or Dying and no frame against the PC was lethal. False for a foe finished by an
                         ally, a companion or a hazard; a fight in which the PC was Staggered; a foe that
                         yielded and was spared.
                       costly - true only when the source was defeated by the PC's own resolved beat AND
                         during that conflict the PC was Staggered or Dying, or a frame against the PC was
                         lethal. False for a hard fight the PC came through above 0 Vitality with no
                         lethal frame. (This is gen_absorb's narrow_survival: one classification serves
                         both domains, 04.10.)
                       merciful - true only when the source yielded, was subdued nonlethally, or broke and
                         was let go, by the PC's own resolved beat, AND a mercy fact is written (it is
                         spared alive). False for a creature bound and then killed; for a mindless
                         creature (creature.undead.mindless, creature.construct, creature.horror.ooze),
                         which cannot yield.
                       scavenged - none of the above: found dead, killed by another or by a hazard, or a
                         thing found rather than won; the degree is the SEARCH beat's. DEFAULT when
                         uncertain.
Computation [D]:    fill method: decisive -> signature; costly -> biased (bias tag ward);
                    merciful -> chosen; scavenged -> weighted (gen_loot.yaml#fill_map)
                    quality rung: decisive, costly, merciful (success or critical success) -> masterwork;
                    scavenged: critical success or success -> fine; failure or critical failure -> common
Stakes:             none (no roll; the degree comes from the frame that produced the defeat or the find)
State writes:       the generated item(s) and the generation log (PR-08-1)
Narration may not imply: any property, tier or rung the output does not hold; that the foe "dropped" a
                    thing it never carried (a wolf carries no coin)
Worst case (J):     decisive vs costly: the signature is the source's own instead of a ward-biased
                    draw, same rung (class i); merciful vs decisive: the player chooses among three
                    instead of receiving the signature, same rung (class i); scavenged vs a won
                    circumstance: fine instead of masterwork, one rung (class i). Errs toward the
                    default (scavenged) when uncertain, which errs low (SG-05 tie-break "does this
                    grant something?" -> no).
Examples:           inside decisive: Wren shoots the spider dead with her own arrow, never below half
                      Vitality -> decisive.
                    boundary costly: the same fight, but the spider's bite took her to 0 and she shot it
                      while Staggered -> costly.
                    boundary merciful: the bandit captain yields at 2 Vitality and Wren lets him go with
                      his life (fact mercy.bandit_captain) -> merciful; he gives up his sword.
                    tempting non-example: "I killed it cleanly while my hound held it" -> the killing
                      frame is Wren's, so decisive; but if the hound's bite was the defeating frame, the
                      circumstance is scavenged (the PC's own beat did not defeat it).
Anchor:             no
Basis:              [C:P5 "decisive vs. costly vs. merciful"] [00.11.2] [R: src/ability_pool.py
                    decisive_kill / narrow_survival / non_lethal_subdual] [04.10 gen_absorb] [DL-08-09]
```

Mercy is never worse than a kill: a spared source gives the same rung as a decisive kill and lets the
player choose. This is deliberate: the conduct axes (03) must not pay cruelty in loot [C:P5 "values-
expressive"; 03 conduct.mercy; DL-08-09].

cards.title: The drop check
cards.body:
**08.3.3 The drop check.** `[D]` Before the rung is looked up, the engine rolls d100 against the source's
**yield** (`gen_loot.yaml#drop_check`):

| Yield | Property item drops on d100 ≤ | Use for |
|---|---|---|
| `none` | never | vermin, swarms, mindless things with nothing worth keeping (they still yield materials) |
| `trophy` (default for anything with a body) | T1 **10** · T2 **15** · T3 **25** · T4 **40** · T5 **55** [revision: I-018; I-036: T3 was 30; DL-08-35] | ordinary foes |
| `hoard` | always, by the hoard table (08.3.12), **where the hoard is kept**; a hoard-keeper defeated away from its lair or vault rolls as `trophy`, and its hoard waits there [revision: I-018] | lairs, treasuries, sites |
| `always` | always, by the circumstance | principal NPCs (12.11.1), named foes, an archetype 09 marks |

A miss is not nothing: harvest, purse and gear still come (08.3.10–08.3.11). The chance rises with the
source's band and never reads the PC (no smart loot, 00.11.4): rabble rarely carry anything worth an
identity, and grinding them at P5 yields tier-1 trinkets one fight in ten. *Why a chance at all:* with one
generation per side and two fights a session, an unconditional drop would put 50–110 property items into a
campaign by P4 — the shape of HWFWM's retired over-generating loot system (R2 08). The check holds the haul
near 08.2.7's density (simulated rates 7 / 16 / 27 / 39 / 57%, T-08-16 [revision: I-036]; whole campaigns with hoards and principals,
T-08-17) [revision: I-018] [R3 A-1 (Diablo II's treasure-table
"NoDrop" weight); DL-08-08].

cards.title: The pool gate: nature and place (the contract with chapter 09)
cards.body:
**08.3.4 The pool gate: nature and place (the contract with chapter 09).** `[D]` [DL-08-13; DL-08-29; DL-00A-18; C:P5; revision: I-065] The gated pool for a loot
call is every entry of `item_properties.yaml` whose `domains` include `loot` and whose `gate_tags` match
(00.5.4c: an entry gated on G matches a source tag S when G = S or G is an ancestor of S) one of:
1. the source archetype's **`creature_tags`** (09: most specific first), **`harm_tags`**, **`evidence_tags`**
   (its `deed.*` tags) and **`org_tags`** (folk), plus any **`loot.pool_gate_tags`** 09 adds;
2. the generated base item's **`material_tags`**;
3. **`creature.folk`**, when the base item is an armament (weapon, armor or shield) taken from a folk or an
   undead source (made by hands: the folk-made mundane properties open to it);
4. the **place's terrain tags**, but only for entries flagged `place_gated: true` (a frost-shod boot can come
   from any foe killed on the high ice; a wolf in a forest never drops it).

Then entries are dropped when: an `excluded_tag` matches the source; no `base_kinds` entry is an
ancestor-or-equal of a base item tag; the base saturates its family (08.2.4); `min_tier` exceeds the tier
cap (08.3.5); the entry is `player_only`/`adversary_only` against this use. This is a hard zero-weight
exclusion (R3 08.1). The place axis is R2 #13's "gate by nature *and* place" (HWFWM's stones manifest
where their theme lives) — it widens the gate, it never adds a third fill axis.

*What 09 must give each archetype* (`gen_loot.yaml#contract_09`): `creature_tags`; `harm_tags`;
`evidence_tags`; `org_tags` for folk; `threat_band`; `loot.yield` (default `trophy`; `none` for mindless
vermin and swarms); optionally `loot.trophy_base` (an item tag or `bi.*` id), `loot.pool_gate_tags`,
`signature_property` (a `signature_eligible` entry whose gate tags match; default:
`item_properties.yaml#default_signatures`, which names a designed signature for **every one of the 45
level-2 creature tags**), `gear` (folk: the base items it carries, mundane, `worn` or `common`), `purse` (a
coin table, 08.3.11), `harvest` (a `mat.*` override). *Validation 09 must run:* for every archetype and each
base it can drop, the gated pool at tier cap 1 holds at least **3** entries; the reference set of 26
archetypes in `08-loot-sim.py` passes for all but one (an aberration's charm at tier 1, which is moot: the
aberration is T4), and 09 re-runs the same check on its own bestiary (T-08-16).

cards.title: The tier cap
cards.body:
**08.3.5 The tier cap.** `[D]` The source's threat band is its **tier cap** (T1 → 1 … T5 → 5); a place's is
its site band (10; a region's seed, 12.16.12) [revision: I-028]. Signature properties take the tier cap; magnitude properties take tier cap − 1,
minimum 1; a property at tier *t* uses its highest authored tier row ≤ *t* (values are fixed per tier, never
rolled: 00.11.3 step 8). A **Greater** result adds +1 to the signature's tier and may exceed the cap by 1
(a tier-6 signature exists only this way, and uses its tier-5 row plus 08.3.9's Greater mark). This is
Diablo II's affix-level gate with the threat band as item level: a T2 wolf can never yield a tier-4
property [R3 08.4, A-2].

cards.title: The base item
cards.body:
**08.3.6 The base item.** `[D]` First match:
1. 09's `loot.trophy_base` for the archetype (a tag resolves per 08.1.12 among bases with
   `trophy_eligible` not false; a `bi.*` id is used as is);
2. for folk and other armed sources, one item of its **gear**;
3. the trophy default for its creature branch (`gen_loot.yaml#base_selection`): beasts — charm, cloak,
   leather armor; undead — ring, amulet, weapon; spirits — charm, amulet; fiends — weapon, ring; constructs —
   shield, amulet, medium armor; elementals — charm, amulet; dragons — armor, shield, charm; horrors — charm,
   weapon. The engine draws with a d6 over the list (1–2 first, 3–4 second, 5–6 third).

**Signature-honoring:** when the fill is `signature`, the draw is made only among listed bases whose kind
the signature property accepts; if none does, the base is the default base of the signature's first base
kind (a wyvern's sting needs a weapon: a wyvern-fang dagger, not a scale shield). **Redraw:** if the drawn
base's gated pool holds fewer entries than the rung has slots, the base is redrawn once from the same list
(the simulation needed 0 redraws and 49 signature-driven overrides in 1,000 drops) [DL-08-10].

cards.title: Quality rung and slots
cards.body:
**08.3.7 Quality rung and slots.** `[D]` [DL-08-09; DL-08-02; DL-08-33; revision: I-065] From the circumstance and degree (08.3.2's table): decisive,
costly and merciful wins give **masterwork** (one signature slot, one magnitude slot); a scavenged find
gives **fine** (one magnitude slot) on a success or critical success and **common** (no property) on a
failure. Hoards give their table's rungs (08.3.12). Slots are clamped to the base's `slot_cap` (08.1.4).
Wondrous items come only from hoards of T4–T5, from bargained gifts (08.7) and from expert or master
crafting (08.6) — never from an ordinary kill, which keeps the rung legible: a masterwork trophy is what a
fair fight is worth.

cards.title: Fill, slot by slot
cards.body:
**08.3.8 Fill, slot by slot.** `[D]` [DL-08-09; DL-08-10; DL-08-24; DL-00A-18; revision: I-065] (00.11.3 steps 4 and 6; PR-08-1.)
- **Signature slot first.** `signature`: the archetype's signature property (09's, else
  `default_signatures` of its most specific creature tag) if it survived the pool gate; if it did not, a
  weighted draw among `signature_eligible` entries **excluding relics** (a decisive win never falls back to a
  relic: relics come from costly, merciful and scavenged fills, gifts, crafting and archetypes that name
  `prop.bound_power` as their signature). `biased`: a weighted draw among `signature_eligible` entries with
  weight ×3 for entries whose `bias` equals the bias tag. `chosen`: the tool shows up to three
  `signature_eligible` entries (drawn by weight without replacement) and the player picks one. `weighted`:
  a plain weighted draw among `signature_eligible` entries.
- **Magnitude slots next**, from entries not marked `signature_only`, by the same method (chosen shows three
  per slot; biased ×3).
- After each pick, every entry sharing its `mod_group` is removed (hard mutual exclusion, R3 08.5).
- **Recency:** entries produced in the last 5 draws of the loot domain (in this campaign) have their weight
  halved; to keep integers the engine doubles every weight first, so recent entries count ×1 and the rest ×2
  (00.11.3 step 7; OEQ-00-5).
- An empty pool leaves a slot empty (the item keeps its rung; its price counts only filled slots).

cards.title: Degree effects, caps and output
cards.body:
**08.3.9 Degree effects, caps and output.** `[D]` [DL-00A-18; DL-08-09; C:P8; revision: I-065]
- **Greater** (critical success): the signature, or the first magnitude property if there is no signature,
  gains +1 tier (00.11.3 step 5); the item record marks it `greater: true`.
- **Flawed** (critical failure, possible only on a scavenged search): the find's magnitude slot is removed
  (a fine find becomes common) and the item is created `damaged`.
- **Caps** (step 9): the item share and per-item caps (08.2.2–08.2.4); a breaching pick is dropped and the
  slot refilled once; if it fails again, the slot stays empty.
- **Bound power:** when `prop.bound_power` fills the signature slot, the tool calls
  `generate(gen.item_ability, …)` with the same source, circumstance and tier (08.4.3); if that pool is
  empty, the signature is redrawn once among non-ability entries.
- **Output** (step 10): the item entity with base, rung, signature, properties, sealed flags (08.5.3),
  provenance and the generation log (pool size after each gate, weights, draws). The DM names it and
  narrates only what it holds; it never adds a property (INV-2).

cards.license_check: basic verb: verb.handle (G1) for hides, bones, horn, fangs, feathers and sinew; essences (glands, hearts, blood, ichor, residue, cores) need a held license whose scope covers dissection: lic.training.wilds_foraging, lic.training.lore_bestiary or lic.training.craft_alchemy; without one, an essence is G3 with crude_fallback "cut it out anyway": dc_shift +5, reach capped Limited, and the part's harvested rarity band falls by 1

```
Each harvested part is an item with provenance {source_id, source_tags, archetype, band} and rarity band max(the material's band, the source's threat band - 1); it carries the source archetype's signature into crafting (08.6.2).
```
