cards.title: A kill becomes a drop, end to end (a giant spider)
cards.body:
### WE-08-1 A kill becomes a drop, end to end (a giant spider)

*Situation.* Under the Ashford mill, Wren fights a giant spider (`arch.giant_vermin`, `adv.giant_spider` in 09's bestiary *(numbers illustrative; 09)*:
`creature_tags [creature.beast.vermin.arachnid]`, `harm_tags [harm.venom.poison]`, T2, `yield: trophy`,
`purse: none`). Her last shot: d20 13 + 5 = 18 vs Guard 15 → success; the spider is defeated (`on_defeat`
carries frame #417). She was never below half Vitality.

1. **Trigger** (08.3.1): `conflict_end`; one defeated side (the spider) → one loot call.
2. **Circumstance** `[J:enum]`: her own resolved beat defeated it; never Staggered; no lethal frame →
   **decisive** (cites frame #417). Fill **signature**.
3. **Drop check** (08.3.3): T2 trophy → d100 = **14** ≤ 15 → a property item drops [verification: V1-005].
4. **Rung:** decisive + success → **masterwork** (1 signature + 1 magnitude). Tier cap **2**.
5. **Base** (08.3.6): no trophy base from 09; beast defaults [charm, cloak, leather armor]; the signature
   (`default_signatures[creature.beast.vermin]` = **Plague-proof**, base kinds: worn things) accepts all
   three; d6 = **2** → the charm (`bi.charm`, slot cap 3).
6. **Pool gate** (08.3.4) on `bi.charm` at cap 2 — seven entries: Venom-warded (w3), Venom-proof hazard
   (w2), Pierce-proof (w2), Darksight (w3), Tremor-sense (w1, min tier 2), Cave-eyes (w1, license,
   signature-only, min tier 2), Plague-proof (w3, signature). (No weapon entries: a charm is not a weapon;
   no Spider-grip: its min tier is 3.)
7. **Signature slot:** Plague-proof at tier **2** → `eff.harm_reduction` 2 against `harm.blight.disease`.
8. **Magnitude slot** at tier 2 − 1 = **1**: excluded are Plague-proof's group (resist_blight), Cave-eyes
   (signature-only) and Tremor-sense (min tier 2 > 1). Weights doubled; Venom-warded was produced two loot
   draws ago (by the river serpent) and is halved: Venom-warded 3, Venom-proof 4, Pierce-proof 4, Darksight
   6 → total 17. The engine rolls 1–17 = **13** (bands 1–3 / 4–7 / 8–11 / 12–17) → **Darksight** tier 1.
9. **Caps:** item contributions: reduction `harm.blight.disease` 2 (share 3), one lever (share 1 per roll).
   Pass.
10. **Output:** `item.i0211` — base `bi.charm`, **masterwork**, signature [Plague-proof T2] (apparent: "a
    spider's fang, faintly sour"), magnitude [Darksight T1] (**sealed**), provenance {arch.giant_spider,
    decisive, success, tier cap 2, loc.ashford_mill}. List price 1 × 10 + 50 + 20 = **80** (band 3).
11. **Harvest** (08.3.10): fresh `[J:flag]` true (killed this hour). Parts: chitin (band 1), bones (1), sinew
    (1), spinner's silk (2), venom sac (2, an **essence**). Wren holds no dissection license, so she leaves
    the sac (its crude fallback would cap reach at Limited: common parts only). Frame: Handle, Agility +3,
    competence floor +1 → **+4**, DC Moderate 15 (silk, band 2), stakes Safe. d20 = 14 → 18, **success**,
    delivered reach 2 → the common parts plus one special: **spinner's silk**. Items created with
    provenance; `harvest.done` set.
12. **Narration:** "Among the husks you find one fang worth keeping, still sour with its venom. The silk
    comes away in a sticky skein." The codex shows the charm: masterwork, Plague-proof (reduce disease
    harm 2), one sealed property, 80.

*Boundary pairs.* (a) **Costly:** had the bite dropped her to 0 Vitality before the shot, the fill is
biased toward ward: the signature-eligible entries are Plague-proof (w3, ward → ×3 = 9) and nothing else at
cap 2 but Cave-eyes (w1, min tier 2: eligible at 2 → weight 1) → Plague-proof 90%, Cave-eyes (a relic
license, `lic.people.cave_eyes`) 10%. (b) **Drop check miss:** d100 = 63 → no property item; the harvest
still happens. *Tempting non-example:* "It was a venomous spider, so the charm should protect me from
poison" — Venom-warded was in the pool but was not drawn; the narration may not imply it (INV-2).

cards.title: A weapon crafted from a monster's hide (a wyvern-scale whip)
cards.body:
### WE-08-2 A weapon crafted from a monster's hide (a wyvern-scale whip)

*Character.* Tamsin, a leatherworker *(illustrative)*: Agility +3; `lic.training.craft_leathercraft`
(trained), competence `deed.craft.leathercraft` +2; her own bench and tools in Ashford (facts
`tamsin.workshop`, `tamsin.tools.leatherworker`). She has two wyvern-scale parts (harvested from a T4
wyvern: band max(1, 4 − 1) = **3**, provenance `arch.wyvern`) and a wyvern venom sac (band 3).

1. **Declare:** base `bi.whip` (material tag `material.hide.leather`; scales are `material.hide.scale`:
   same level-1 branch, accepted), primary = the scales, reagent = the venom sac, target **masterwork**.
2. **Circumstance** `[J:enum]`: her license, her tools, her workplace → **crafted** (fill: chosen).
3. **Validate:** trained may target masterwork; tier cap = min(trained **2**, materials' band 3) = **2**.
   Materials: masterwork consumes ×2 the base price (3 × 2 = 6 coins' worth): two scale parts (4 each) =
   8 ≥ 6. ✓
4. **Clocks:** progress **8**, spoilage **4**. Step frame: Handle under the license, Agility +3, competence
   +2, tools lever +2 → **+7** vs Hard **20** (needs 13: success 40%, near miss 15%); a day per tick.
   - Day 1: d20 15 → 22, success, reach 2 → **2/8**.
   - Day 2: d20 9 → 16, margin −4, failure → spoilage **1/4**; cost `cost.time` S2 (a day spent recutting).
   - Day 3: d20 18 → 25, success → **4/8**.
   - Day 4: d20 11 → 18, margin −2, **near miss**: she takes success at a cost (`cost.time`, no spoilage) →
     **6/8**.
   - Day 5: d20 **20** → 27: success, natural 20 steps up → **critical success**; reach 2 + 1 = 3 → **9/8:
     complete**. Spoilage 1 (below 3) → not Flawed; the completing beat is critical → **Greater**.
5. **Generate** (`gen.craft`, PR-08-2): source tags = scales' gates + venom sac's gates + `creature.folk` +
   the wyvern's provenance tags. Pool on `bi.whip`: Keen, Balanced, Sturdy, Light make, Master's mark,
   Ember-forged, Ember-touched, Venom-forged, Venom-touched, Spell-forged, Spell-touched, Dragon-bane, Wyvern
   sting (Bound power is out: min tier 3).
6. **Signature:** the scales' provenance signature = **Wyvern sting**, at tier 2 + 1 (Greater) = **3**: on a
   hit whose d20 shows **17–20**, the creature hit is poisoned (S2) for the scene. Its mod group is
   `on_hit`, which removes every other on-hit entry (08.2.3).
7. **Magnitude** (chosen, tier 1): the tool draws three by weight — **Keen**, **Venom-forged**, **Sturdy** —
   and Tamsin picks **Keen** (+1 harm with the whip; the whip is not versatile, so the item share of harm
   edge is free).
8. **Output:** a masterwork whip, signature [Wyvern sting T3 (Greater)], magnitude [Keen T1]; maker Tamsin;
   list 3 × 10 + 125 + 20 = **175** (band 4). 03's `cnt.made` fires with weight 4 (the masterwork index).

*Boundary pairs.* (a) **Commissioned** by Wren from Tamsin: the same clocks run as engine fortune checks at
Tamsin's +7; Wren names one bias (`strike`), so the magnitude draw weights strike entries ×3 instead of
showing three; price = Wren's materials + trained wage 10 × 1 week (5 days rounds up) + 1 notch of band 4
(50) = **60 coins**, 30 up front. (b) **Improvised** in camp with a knife: no bench → improvised: +5 DC (25),
reach capped Limited, rung capped common → a serviceable scale whip with no properties at all; the
wyvern's identity is not unlocked without the craft. *Tempting non-example:* "It's wyvern hide, so the whip
should resist fire" — fire resistance is not in this whip's pool (it is a weapon; resistances are worn
things), and the signature is fixed by provenance.

cards.title: A relic lends an off-identity capability (a demon's ring of fire)
cards.body:
### WE-08-3 A relic lends an off-identity capability (a demon's ring of fire)

*Situation.* In the ash-pits east of Grey Keep, Wren beats a lesser demon (`arch.lesser_demon`
*(illustrative)*: `creature.fiend.demon.lesser`, `harm.fire.flame`, T3). At 2 Vitality it yields; Wren,
against her companion's advice, lets it go back to the pit (fact `mercy.ash_imp`).

1. **Circumstance:** merciful (it yielded, she spared it). Fill **chosen**; rung masterwork; tier cap **3**.
   Drop check: d100 = 22 ≤ 30 ✓ [verification: V1-005].
2. **Base:** fiend defaults [weapon, ring]; d6 = 4 → **ring**. Signature-eligible entries for a ring: Hellfire
   is weapon-only (excluded); the only signature-eligible entry left is the **Bound power** (min tier 3 ≤ 3).
   The tool shows it; Wren takes it.
3. **Item ability** (PR-08-4): source `creature.fiend.demon.lesser` → absorbed powers gated on fiends: Dread
   Gaze; techniques via `source_to_deed[creature.fiend]` → `deed.arcane.fire`, `deed.divine.pact`,
   `deed.influence.intimidation`: Flame Lance, Fire Shroud, Cow, Break the Will, … Chosen: the tool shows
   **Dread Gaze**, **Flame Lance**, **Cow**; Wren picks **Flame Lance** at tier 3 → **rank 1**.
4. **Magnitude** (chosen, tier 2): she picks **Ember-warded** (reduce fire harm 2).
5. **Output:** a masterwork ring, relic: bound [`ab.flame_lance` rank 1], magnitude [Ember-warded T2];
   `feeds_evidence: false`; list 5 × 10 + 250 (a tier-3 bound power ×2) + 50 = **350** (band 4) [verification: V2a-015].
6. **Attunement** at the next breather: attuned 1 of 5; Flame Lance binds to equipped slot 1 of 4;
   `cost_immune` while attuned; everything unsealed.
7. **Use, two days later**, against a bandit at `band.near`: G2 (held through the equipped partition). Cost:
   rank 1's **1** Focus **+1 relic surcharge** (Wren holds no `lic.training.arcane_fire`) = **2** (05.6.3).
   Check: Intellect 0 + competence on `deed.arcane.fire.blast` — none, so the floor **+1** — vs Guard 13:
   needs 12 (45%). Success → Moderate fire harm (3) and burning. **No evidence** toward `deed.arcane`
   (00.11.5); the shot at the bandit records nothing toward a calling.

*Boundary pairs.* (a) **Ash**, 05's hedge-taught fire sorcerer (holds `lic.training.arcane_fire`), wears the
ring: **no surcharge** (1 Focus), and her own fire competence applies — but if she already holds Flame Lance,
the ring's copy is **dormant**: a spare (05.2.9). (b) **A license relic:** a clockwork sentinel's costly
drop at T2 carries **Lock-whisper** (`lic.training.guile_thievery` at trained, no competence). At 00's Grey
Keep archive door (WE-00-3), Wren is now **G2** instead of G3: Agility +3, competence floor +1, thieves'
tools Precision +2 = **+6** vs the guild lock's Hard 20 (35%) — legal, not good, and nothing she does with
it teaches her thievery. *Tempting non-example:* "I've cast Flame Lance thirty times now, so I'm becoming a
fire sorcerer" — relic use feeds no calling; to become one, she finds a teacher (05.9).

cards.title: A merchant negotiation that touches prices (Ashford market day)
cards.body:
### WE-08-4 A merchant negotiation that touches prices (Ashford market day)

*Situation.* Ashford is a town (band ≤ 3 goods, special stock ≤ 2, market depth 150 a week).
1. **Selling materials** (trade goods to a crafter, 08.8.5): spinner's silk (list 15, band 2) is scarce in
   Ashford (the settlement fact says silk comes from the south) → **15**; three chitin plates (list 4 each,
   band 1, notch 1) are common in a fen-town → list − 1 notch = **3 each, 9**. A second sale of chitin that
   week would glut: 2 each.
2. **Buying mail.** List 50 (band 3, notch 10) → asking **60**. Wren haggles (08.8.7): ROOM true (a smith, face
   to face). Frame: Talk, Presence 0, competence on `deed.influence.trade.haggling` — only the floor → +1;
   lever: the Salt Guild armorer's quote of 55 recorded yesterday (fact `quote.salt_guild.mail`, Precision
   +2) → **+3** vs the smith's Wits defense 10 + 1 + 2 = **13** (needs 10: 55%). Stakes Risky (a closed door
   for the day). d20 = 14 → 17, success, reach Standard **2** → list − 1 notch = **40**. `update_quantity(coin,
   −40)`. Her load: mail worn 2 (her leather goes in the pack: carried 2): she checks capacity (08.9.1).
3. **Selling the spider charm** (WE-08-1, list 80): a property item → `clk.find_buyer` (6, public). Ashford
   ticks 1 a week; Wren spends a week in town and makes one Talk (trade) beat: reach 2 → **3/6** after week 1;
   week 2: +1 + reach 1 → 5/6; week 3: complete → a buyer pays half of list, **40** (inside the 150 depth).
4. **Lifestyle:** three weeks comfortable = 42 coins through `h.08.upkeep`.

*Boundary pairs.* (a) Failure on the haggle (d20 = 6 → 9): the smith holds firm at **60** and will not haggle
again today (cost.closed_door S2); a critical failure would close his door for the week. (b) A **toll** at
the Grey Keep bridge: ROOM false — a fixed fee is paid or not. *Tempting non-example:* "I tell him mail
like that is worth thirty" — an assertion is not a lever (SG-06); only the recorded quote is.

cards.title: Damage, the item share, and repair
cards.body:
### WE-08-5 Damage, the item share, and repair

Wren's arming sword (versatile, parrying) in two hands has harm edge +1 from `versatile` — the item share of
harm edge is full. She hones it with a whetstone (+1 harm edge for 3 Strikes): it adds **nothing** (08.2.2),
and the codex says so before the interval is spent. A guard's critical counter imposes `cost.gear` **S3** on
the sword: **damaged** → `versatile` and `parrying` stop (no harm edge, no Guard edge); severity S2 and
bands remain. At the next breather she makes a crude repair (Handle, Easy 10, Agility +3 + floor 1 = +4:
needs 6, 75%): success → serviceable until the next `rest_long`. In Ashford a smith's lasting repair costs
`svc.repair` 1 notch of band 2 (the sword's list 10) = **2 coins**. *Boundary:* an S4 cost would have broken
it: only a licensed smith (a 4-segment project or `svc.repair` 2 notches = 4 coins) could mend it.

cards.title: Identifying before attuning (graduated reveal)
cards.body:
### WE-08-6 Identifying before attuning (graduated reveal)

Wren holds a masterwork amulet from a barrow (place-gated hoard, T2): signature apparent ("Whispering:
grave-cold, it murmurs near old stones"), one sealed magnitude property. She has five items attuned and does
not want to drop one blind. **Study:** Observe, Wits +2, competence on `deed.lore.arcana`: floor +1 → +3; DC
by the highest sealed tier (tier 1 → Moderate 15): needs 12 (45%); stakes Safe; the player ranks "what does
it do" first. d20 = 15 → 18: success, reach 2 → up to two sealed properties revealed → the one: **Tomb-ward
T1** (reduce blight harm 1). Had she failed, she could not study it again until her next long rest; the
sage in Ashford (`svc.identify`, 10 coins) would tell her everything, flaw included.

cards.title: Encumbrance after the barrow
cards.body:
### WE-08-7 Encumbrance after the barrow

Wren (capacity 12) carries: shortbow 1, arrows 1, spear 1, leather worn 1, rope 1, bedroll 1, 6 supply (3),
the charm 0, the amulet 0, and now a looted mail hauberk *carried* (4) and a strongbox of coins (3, plus
240 coins = 2). Load = 1+1+1+1+1+1+3+4+3+2 = **18** > 12 → **burdened** (snag on Evade, Sneak, Exert; one
step slower). Over 24 she could not travel. She abandons the strongbox, pockets the coins (2) → 15, still
burdened; she wears the mail and stows the leather (worn mail 2, carried leather 2: 1+1+1+2+1+1+3+2+2 = 14)
— still over by 2 until she eats into the supply or buys a mule (carry 30).

cards.title: An earned gift from the Wardens
cards.body:
### WE-08-8 An earned gift from the Wardens

The Wardens of the Marches (a faction, tier 2 *(illustrative; 11)*) promised "a blade from our armory" for
clearing the barrow (thread fact `thr.barrow.reward`). The thread completes; 11 writes `gift_due.wardens`.
1. **Circumstance** `[J:enum]`: a reward owed and its terms met → **earned**: masterwork, chosen; tier cap 2.
2. **Base:** the Wardens' customary gift, an arming sword (`bi.sword`; versatile, so every harm-edge entry
   is saturated and drops out).
3. **Pool** (gift domain; giver tags `org.order.knightly`, its patron deeds `deed.martial`,
   `deed.divine.oaths`, plus the folk hand): Balanced, Sturdy, Light make, Dawn-forged, Dawn-touched — and,
   always eligible for its giver's gifts, the order's **boon signature** (`boon_signature:
   prop.sig_well_made` *(illustrative; 13)*).
4. **Signature** (chosen): Well-made is the only signature-eligible candidate at cap 2 → **Well-made T2**
   (+1 to beats that use the sword). Its mod group (strike_edge) removes Balanced.
5. **Magnitude** (chosen, tier 1): the tool shows **Sturdy**, **Dawn-forged**, **Dawn-touched**; Wren takes
   **Dawn-touched** (on a hit whose d20 shows 20, the creature hit is blinded for 2 rounds).
6. **Output:** fully unsealed (the giver says what it is); fact `gifted_by: fac.wardens`; list 10 × 10 + 50
   + 20 = **170**.

*Boundary:* had the captain merely liked her (standing +2, nothing owed), the gift is **favored**: the same
rung, but Well-made is *placed* (signature fill) and the magnitude slot is a weighted draw — no choice.
Goodwill gives the giver's identity; a debt paid lets the recipient choose. *Non-example:* "they owe me for
saving the miller" when no thread or bargain recorded a reward → no gift is due; whether anyone gives is
11's or 15's.

cards.title: Salvage and a recipe
cards.body:
### WE-08-9 Salvage and a recipe

Wren has three wolf charms with Hunter's sense. She asks Tamsin (leathercraft, trained) to salvage two:
Handle under the license, DC Moderate, 1 hour each. Successes yield no stock (a charm is load 0, 08.6.8 (a)) [verification: V2c-004] and
one **residuum** (gates = Hunter's sense's gate, `creature.beast.predator`; band tier − 1 = 1). On the
second, delivered reach 3 → Tamsin writes `knows_recipe: prop.sig_hunters_sense`. From now on, any project
of hers whose gated pool contains Hunter's sense (any predator part, or the residuum) may *name* it for the
signature slot (recipe fill) and cite the recipe as an Amplifying lever on the steps.

cards.title: Enchanting a fine cloak
cards.body:
### WE-08-10 Enchanting a fine cloak

Ash (05's sorcerer; `lic.training.arcane_fire` trained) has learned `lic.training.craft_enchanting`
(trained) and knows `rit.imbue`. Wren's kit cloak is `common` (no slot); her **fine** boots have an open
slot. Ash uses a fire gland (reagent, band 2: gates fire) to imbue **Ember-warded** — a fire property, so
Ash's fire school license qualifies. *For a season:* the rite (6 segments, Hard, an hour a step, 2 Focus)
seats it until the next `season` boundary. *Lasting:* an 8-segment project at Hard under
`deed.craft.enchanting.imbuing`, a day a tick, whose last step is the rite; tier = min(gland band 2, trained
cap 2) = **2** (reduce fire 2). The boots' `worked` property is now spent: no further enchantment can ever
be added. *Non-example:* imbuing Wren's common cloak — no open slot (common has none); first a crafter must
remake it as fine.

cards.title: The item share at E4 (two fire wards)
cards.body:
### WE-08-11 The item share at E4 (two fire wards)

Wren wears the demon's ring (Ember-warded T2: fire −2) and a cloak that also carries Ember-warded at T1
(−1); one item cannot hold two entries of the same mod group, but two items each may. A fire bolt deals S3
(5). Receiver side, E4: item reductions against `harm.fire` are 2 + 1 = 3, inside the item share of 3 → 3;
her leather armor reduces only `harm.physical` (0 here). 5 − 3 = **2** taken. If she also held an absorbed
power reducing fire by 1, the family would reach 4 (07's cap): 1 taken. *Non-example:* a third fire-warded
item adds nothing — the item share is full, and the codex shows the clamped line ("items: −3 of 3").

---

cards.title: What an adversary is
cards.body: ### 09.1 What an adversary is

cards.title: The adversary record
cards.body:
**09.1.1 The adversary record.** `[D]` An adversary is an entity of kind `adversary` (00.6.1) whose record
extends 00.6.2's `Adversary` shape with the fields of T-09-14. Every field is computed by PR-09-1 from four
inputs — **archetype** (09.2), **threat band** (09.3), **role** (09.4.2) and **variant** (09.4.6) — plus at
most a handful of named overrides an entry may carry (a level-3 creature tag, a size, which of the
archetype's attacks it uses, powers added or dropped, pool abilities, gear). The record is stored in
`data/adversaries.yaml` for the bestiary and in state (`create_entity(kind: adversary, template_id)`) for
each instance met in play; a mob is one entity with a `members` count (06.10.2). An instance keeps its
template id, so the codex, chapter 03's evidence, chapter 08's generator and chapter 04's Taking all read the
same nature [R3 §09.1; 00.6.2].

cards.title: Sealed state
cards.body:
**09.1.2 Sealed state.** `[S]` An adversary's stat block (attributes, competence, defenses, Vitality, attacks,
powers, Focus, effect DCs, reaction kinds, morale nerve, weak spot, behavior list, disposition switches,
calibration) is **sealed** (00.6.3, 00.6.5). The narrator's permitted slice is, and is only: its name as
perceived; its size; its **tells** (09.10.1: presence, the band tell, wounded, breaking, windup); the shown
descriptors `bloodied` and `down` (06.7.6); its visible conditions; a Windup in progress (06.9.5); its
side's morale omens (06.11.4); the number the PC needs on the die, inside an OFFER (01.7.1); and whatever the
PC has learned (09.10.2), which becomes `available` in the codex item by item. A secret in the narrator's
context leaks [R4 §5.1]; a stat block never enters it.
*Narration may not imply:* any number of the stat block; a resistance, weakness or power the PC has not
perceived or learned; that the creature is weaker or stronger than its tells say.

cards.title: Deliberate asymmetries
cards.body:
**09.1.3 Deliberate asymmetries.** `[D]` The opposition is cheaper to run than the PC, by design [R1 §09
(Lancer: NPCs cannot Brace or Overcharge); 07.2.10]:
- **Two actions a turn at every band**, a reaction by band (06.1.1, 06.6.5; 09.3.9). No variant, power or
  ruling adds an action (INV-11; 06.1.2).
- **No push, no fate, no last-chance menu.** An adversary's Focus buys only its listed powers and pool
  abilities (09.5.3); it never pushes a roll (05.6.7 is the PC's). It has no fate (01.16). It uses chapter
  07's short ladder: at 0 Vitality it is defeated (07.2.10).
- **No mastery rung** (06.4.5): its attack severities are listed in its record, which is the same idea as
  data.
- **Its rolls are fortune checks** (01.6.7): the engine frames and rolls them with `offer.choice: auto`.

cards.title: Nothing changes mid-fight
cards.body:
**09.1.4 Nothing changes mid-fight.** `[D]` Restating 06.9.7 for this chapter's fields: once
`conflict_start` has run, an adversary's record changes only by harm, conditions, positions, the morale
clock, its own powers' declared effects (a solo's phase, 09.7.7; a Shrug, 09.5.1), and reinforcements on a
clock whose omens were rendered. The DM may not re-band, re-role or re-variant a creature, add or remove a
foe, alter Vitality, or have a creature "hold back". A creature met again in a later scene keeps its record
(and its wounds, until chapter 07's recovery for NPCs says otherwise) unless chapter 11 or 09.9.3 has
written a change [R1 §4 T-5; R4 §6.3].

cards.title: Archetypes: the manufacturers
cards.body: ### 09.2 Archetypes: the manufacturers

cards.title: One tag set drives four things
cards.body:
**09.2.1 One tag set drives four things.** `[D]` An **archetype** (`arch.*`, `data/archetypes.yaml`) is a kind
of creature: wolves and hounds, brigands, barrow-wights, golems, great dragons. Its tag set is read, without
restatement, by four consumers [R3 §6 #14; C:P5]:

| Consumer | Reads | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Evidence (03) | `creature_tags` (opponent kind), the adversary's threat band (through the advisory word and for conduct-only events, 03.4.3), its `lethal_context` [verification: V2b-002] | 09.11.2 |
| Loot (08) | `creature_tags` (most specific first), `harm_tags`, `evidence_tags`, `org_tags`, `loot.*`, `gear`, `purse` | 08.3.4; 09.11.1 |
| Absorption (04) | `absorbable.pool_gate_tags`, `absorbable.cannot_absorb`, `absorbable.signature` | 04.10; 09.11.3 |
| Behavior (this chapter, 06) | `behaviors`, `morale`, `default_behavior_role`, `mind` | 09.7 |

`evidence_tags` are the deed tags the creature **practices** (a brigand: `deed.martial.blade`,
`deed.guile.ambush`; a lich: `deed.arcane.necromancy`, `deed.lore.arcana`). They are its competence keys
(09.3.2), they open folk-made and practice-themed loot (08.3.4 item 1), and they tell chapter 03 what a fight
with it was *about* when 03 records secondary context. They are never evidence for the PC by themselves:
evidence comes from the PC's own method (00.5.6).

cards.title: The archetype record
cards.body:
**09.2.2 The archetype record.** `[D]` [DL-09-01; C:P12; revision: I-065] Every archetype carries the fields of T-09-1, all data, none prose-only
(00.16.4): identity (`creature_tags` most specific first, `harm_tags`, `evidence_tags`, `org_tags`, `mind`,
`speaks` and `tongue`, `size`, `bands` (the lowest and highest band it is fielded at), `roles`); its body
(seven `attribute_rungs`, `trained_defenses`, `armor`, natural `attacks` with severity offsets, `powers`,
`traits` as effect references); its limits (`cannot`); its conduct (`behaviors`, `default_behavior_role`,
`morale {nerve, break_then}`, `reaction`, `reaction_roll`, `pace`); its stakes (`lethal_context`,
`defeat_disposition`, `kill_when`, `captive_fate`, `can_bargain`, `dread`); its voice (`tells`, `weak_spot`);
its outputs (`loot`, `gear`, `purse`, `harvest`, `absorbable`); its knowledge (`lore {deed_tag, rarity}`); and
its place in the world (`encounter {terrain, group, objective_default}`). T-09-2's band tables turn the rungs
into numbers (09.3).

cards.title: The library covers every creature branch
cards.body:
**09.2.3 The library covers every creature branch.** `[D]` [DL-09-01; C:VI; R3 §09.6; revision: I-065] Sixty-three archetypes span all nine branches of
the creature facet (00.5.1) and every level-2 tag under them except where one archetype honestly covers two
(T-09-12): beasts 10, folk 14 (human brigands, soldiers, knights, cultists and mages; elves; dwarves; orcs;
goblins; gnolls; lizardfolk; ogres; trolls; true giants), undead 9, spirits 6, fiends 6, constructs 4,
elementals 5, dragons 4, horrors 5. The count is deliberately high: archetypes are *instances* of the nine
low-cardinality families, which are what key hybrid and absorption tables (R3 §09.6). A new archetype is a
data entry in 09's file (or a pre-made setting's owner-block for adversaries, 13), never a new rule.

cards.title: Classifying an unlisted creature
cards.trigger: a creature is introduced (write-on-mention, 00.6.6) that matches no bestiary entry and no region entry (12.16.12; a pre-made setting's), or a player asks what kind of thing it is (G0)
cards.license_check: none (classification)
decisions: 1. BRANCH [J:enum] the creature facet's nine branches, by data/tags.yaml's definitions (beast: no speech or culture; folk: speech and culture of a living people; undead: the dead made to move or linger; spirit: native spirit, not dead, not fiend; fiend: infernal or abyssal; construct: a made thing given motion; elemental: of a raw element; dragon: dragon or dragon-kin; horror: unnatural, fits no other branch). Tie-break: the branch of what the creature IS, not what it does (a wolf ridden by a goblin is two creatures; a wolf-shaped fire is elemental). Default: horror only when nothing else fits.
2. ARCHETYPE [J:enum] among that branch's archetypes (T-09-12), by `summary` and creature tags. Default: the archetype whose creature_tags include the most specific matching tag.
cards.computation: the archetype id; PR-09-2 builds the rest.
state_writes: entity.creature_tags (the archetype's, plus a level-3 tag if one matches exactly)
narration_may_not_imply: a power, weakness or immunity of an archetype not chosen
cards.worst_case: a neighboring archetype of the same branch: the loot pool, absorbable pool and behavior list differ, the band and numbers do not (bands are 09.3.1's). The id is in state; a later contradiction is corrected by 12.3.4 before the creature acts again (class iv). A wrong branch is two rungs of error and is the reason decision 1 comes first with the facet's own definitions.
examples: inside: "a hulking thing of stitched corpses" -> horror -> arch.abomination. boundary: "a wolf of living flame" -> elemental (what it is), not beast -> arch.fire_elemental with the presence tell of a wolf. non-example: "the bandit leader is basically a demon" -> a figure of speech; he is folk (arch.brigand), and the player's words create no fact (SG-06).

knobs.default: one creature; each creature of a mixed group is classified alone

cards.body:
**09.2.4 Classifying an unlisted creature.** `[J:enum]`
```

```

cards.title: What it categorically cannot be or do
cards.body:
**09.2.5 What it categorically cannot be or do.** `[D]` An archetype's `cannot` list states, positively and
literally (SG-15), what is impossible for every creature of that kind: a ghost "cannot leave the place it
haunts"; a golem "cannot disobey its command"; a vampire "cannot cross running water by its own power"; a
plant "cannot pursue". Each entry is backed by state wherever it has mechanics: a restriction effect
(`eff.restrict`), a condition immunity (`eff.condition_immunity`), a fact the behavior predicates read, or a
rule of another chapter it cites (06.10.5 for swarms). Three uses:
1. **Gate G4** (00.12.3): a beat whose intent needs the creature to do what it cannot ("I lure the
   ghost out to the road") is impossible for that intent, and the redirect names what *is* possible
   ("it cannot leave the mill; you can leave it").
2. **Behavior.** No behavior row may produce an act on the `cannot` list; the engine refuses the row and
   takes the next (09.7.1).
3. **Recognizable provenance and crisp legality** [R3 §6 #14]: loot and absorbed powers carry the source's
   identity, and a power that would make the source do the impossible is never in its pools.
Immunities that follow from the body (`pow.mindless`, `pow.deathless`, `pow.unliving`, `pow.amorphous`,
`pow.incorporeal`) are written as powers so that they compose through the substrate (00.10) and are listed
once.

cards.title: Flags that keep effects on the right side
cards.body:
**09.2.6 Flags that keep effects on the right side.** `[D]` Three flags, all chapter 00's and 08's, are honored
by every adversary entry [R3 §09.3 (Risk of Rain 2's AIBlacklist and CannotCopy)]:
- `adversary_only` — every `pow.*` power is adversary-only: it never enters a pick, a learning clock, a loot
  pool or a gift. A Devourer takes *abilities* from 04's pool (`ab.abs_*`), never a `pow.*` entry.
- `player_only` — an effect so flagged is never given to an adversary; specifically, no adversary holds any
  effect that would bypass the two keys (07.3.1): there is no "kills outright", "dies at once" or "no
  saving the target" effect in this chapter's data, and chapter 07's edge case reads any such text as S5
  harm against PCs.
- `cannot_absorb` — named per archetype in `absorbable.cannot_absorb`: the pool entries a Devourer may not
  take from it even though the gate matches (a celestial's sight is its god's, not its own).

cards.title: Mind
cards.body:
**09.2.7 Mind.** `[D]` [DL-09-18; revision: I-065] Every archetype has one `mind` from a closed list; it decides which social and mental
rules apply, with no further judgment:

| Mind | Means | Effects bearing `trait.nature.mental` | Talk (parley, intimidate, demand) | Yields when broken (06.11.5) | Reaction roll (12.11.2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mindless` | no will of its own (skeletons, zombies, golems, oozes) | no effect (`pow.mindless`) | G4: there is no one to talk to | never: fearless | no: its behavior list decides |
| `animal` | a beast's mind | yes | Talk is G4 except calming and intimidating by manner (Handle, Presence) | no: it flees or cowers | no: `tbl.09.beast_mood` (09.8.7) |
| `cunning` | sly, hungry, little culture (ogres, ghouls, lesser demons) | yes | yes; its standing starts Hostile in a fight | if it `speaks` | only if `reaction_roll: true` |
| `sapient` | a person or a power with a will | yes | yes | yes | if `reaction_roll: true` |
| `alien` | a mind, but not one like ours (spirits of place, elementals, aberrations) | yes | Talk's reach is capped Limited unless the PC holds a license or fact that bridges it | per its `break_then` | if `reaction_roll: true` |

*Basis:* 06.11.5's state table; 12.11.2 step 4; the `trait.nature.mental` definition in `data/tags.yaml`
("mindless beings are unaffected").

cards.title: Threat bands (no character levels)
cards.body: ### 09.3 Threat bands (no character levels)

cards.title: Assigning a threat band
cards.trigger: PR-09-2 builds an unlisted adversary; 13 or 11 adds an entry
cards.license_check: none
decisions: 1. BAND [J:rung] by the creature's NATURE, anchored by who it threatens (T-09-11): T1 rabble — untrained folk, vermin, the walking dead: a trained person handles one easily; numbers make them dangerous. (village thugs; a lone wolf / a goblin skulk) T2 trained — soldiers, hunting beasts, ghouls: an even match for a seasoned fighter, dangerous to a novice in pairs. (a man-at-arms; a dire wolf / a giant spider) T3 elite — knights, ogres, wights, sorcerers: a veteran's match; a novice's death. (an owlbear; a barrow-wight / a sabre-tooth in its den) T4 champion — heroes, trolls, young dragons, demons of name: they end careers. (a troll; a champion of the realm / a hill giant) T5 legend — ancient dragons, liches, demon lords: regions arrange themselves around avoiding them. (an elder dragon; a lich / a frost-giant jarl) NEVER from title, location, hostility or dramatic importance alone: a "bandit king" is the band of what he can do; a frightening scene is not a stronger monster. Tie-break: the lower rung (a wrong high band manufactures a lethal warning; a wrong low band is caught by the advisory, which reads the real numbers). The archetype's `bands` [min, max] bound the choice.
cards.computation: T-09-2 and T-09-3 give every number for that band (PR-09-1).
state_writes: entity.threat_band (and every number PR-09-1 derives from it)
narration_may_not_imply: a band other than the stored one (tells are by the stored band)
cards.worst_case: one rung: every number shifts by one row of T-09-2/T-09-3, loot tier cap by 1, evidence challenge band by 1. The advisory (09.6) is computed from the resulting numbers and shown before the fight, so the player sees the consequence before committing (class ii); the band is in state and can be corrected between scenes (12.3.4, class iv).
examples: inside: an old soldier turned highwayman -> T2 (trained), whatever his reputation. boundary: a goblin chieftain with a magic sword: the sword is an item (08), the goblin is T2 at most (arch.goblin bands 1-2); his elite variant (09.4.6) is the "chieftain". non-example: "it's the final boss, make it T5" -> drama is not nature; build what it IS, and let 09.6 report how hard it is.
basis: R4 §6.3 (Story-Engine: "never use boss from title, location, hostility, or dramatic importance alone")

cards.title: Band competence and attribute rungs
cards.body:
**09.3.2 Band competence and attribute rungs.** `[D]` [DL-09-07; revision: I-065] An adversary's numbers are top-down: its band fixes a
**band competence** `c_b` and the value of five **attribute rungs**; its archetype names a rung for each of
the seven attributes (`attribute_rungs`) and which defenses it is trained in (`trained_defenses`).

cards.title: Band tables
cards.body:
**T-09-2 Band tables** (`data/archetypes.yaml#band_tables`).

| Band | `c_b` | apex | high | mid | low | feeble | none (mindless mental) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | +1 | +3 | +1 | 0 | −1 | −3 | −5 |
| T2 | +2 | +5 | +3 | +1 | −1 | −3 | −5 |
| T3 | +3 | +6 | +4 | +2 | 0 | −2 | −5 |
| T4 | +4 | +8 | +6 | +3 | +1 | −2 | −5 |
| T5 | +5 | +9 | +7 | +4 | +1 | −2 | −5 |

Every value sits inside 00.3.5 and 00.4.3: attributes −5…+10; competence 0…+6; base modifier (apex + `c_b`)
at most +14, reached only at T5 (INV-18). Competence entries are written on the adversary as
`{tag, value: c_b}` for each of its `evidence_tags` and for `deed.martial.unarmed` (its natural weapons), so
00.3.6's lookup works on it like on anyone.
*Why these numbers.* With rung `high` and `c_b`, an attack is +2 / +5 / +7 / +10 / +12 and a Guard 12 / 15 /
17 / 20 / 22 — exactly chapter 06's reference lines (T-06-12), which sit inside 00.3.7's typical
attack/defense modifiers (+0…+2, +3…+5, +6…+8, +9…+11, +12…+14). With rung `mid` and no training, tempo is
10 / 11 / 12 / 13 / 14 — 06.2.2's reference by band. The rungs are the same for every archetype, so an ogre
and an elf at T3 differ only in *which* attributes are high, never in the scale
[R: https://2e.aonprd.com/Rules.aspx?ID=2874 (benchmarks by tier: extreme, high, moderate, low)].

cards.title: The standard line
cards.body:
**09.3.3 The standard line.** `[D]` [DL-09-04; revision: I-065] The **standard** of a band is the line an average adversary of that band
fights with. It is chapter 06's reference line with the two changes the full rules require (DL-09-04):

cards.title: The standard line by band
cards.body:
**T-09-3 The standard line by band** (`data/archetypes.yaml#band_tables.standard`).

| Band | Attack | Guard | Vitality | Harm (standard) | Heavy blow | Reduction | Nerve (clock) | Tempo DC | Reaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | +2 | 12 | 5 | S2 | S3 | 0 | skittish (4) | 10 | none |
| T2 | +5 | 15 | 12 | S2 | S3 | 0 | steady (6) | 11 | Opportunity Strike |
| T3 | +7 | 17 | 18 | S3 | S4 | 1 | steady (6) | 12 | OS + Fend |
| T4 | +10 | 20 | **24** | S3 | S4 | 2 | resolute (8) | 13 | OS + Fend |
| T5 | +12 | 22 | **36** | S4 | S5 | 2 | resolute (8) | 14 | OS + Fend |

The two changes from T-06-12: (1) adversaries of T3 and above **Fend** the PC's first attack each round,
which 06.6.5 states but 06's script did not model; (2) with Fend in, T4 and T5 Vitality are lowered from 26
and 40 to **24** and **36** so that 06.10.6's target still holds: one foe of the PC's own band is beaten 80%
or more of the time with no Focus. Simulated, extended model with Fend, 8,000 fights a row (section A of the
output):

| One foe of the PC's band | win% / Staggered% | Word |
|---|---|---|
| P1 vs T1 | 100 / 0.1 | trivial |
| P2 vs T2 | 99.9 / 0.7 | trivial |
| P3 vs T3 | 99.4 / 4.7 | easy |
| P4 vs T4 (Vitality 24) | 87.8 / 42.8 | fair (26 would give 81.6 / 53.5: hard) |
| P5 vs T5 (Vitality 36) | 80.2 / 58.2 | hard (40 would give 73.6 / 65.4) |

Both values are inside 00.3.7's envelope (T4 20–32, T5 32–60). Harm severity values are 00.3.11's
(1 / 3 / 5 / 8 / 12) and are never changed by this chapter.

cards.title: Defenses
cards.body:
**09.3.4 Defenses.** `[D]` [DL-09-07; DL-09-04; DL-06-08; revision: I-065] Every adversary stores Guard and all seven attribute defenses (06.4.1; 01's
request):
- `Guard = 10 + Agility + c_b + edge` (edge +1 for a carried shield; 06.4.1's guard tag is its natural
  weapons or its weapon, at `c_b`);
- `defense[attr] = 10 + attribute + (c_b if attr is in trained_defenses else 0)`;
- `tempo = 10 + Wits` (06.2.2; adversaries are not trained in `deed.martial.tactics.reading` unless their
  entry says so, which none in the bestiary does: alert creatures have a high Wits rung instead).
Defenses are stored numbers (`defenses` in T-09-14), read sealed by `frame_check`; status from conditions
applies on top (00.3.5).

cards.title: Attacks and severity
Reduction
cards.body:
**09.3.6 Reduction.** `[D]` [DL-09-04; DL-07-14; DL-06-10; revision: I-065] From the archetype's `armor` (T-09-5b), capped at 4 (07.2.2):

| Armor | T1 | T2 | T3 | T4 | T5 | `no_gaps` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| natural: none | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | — |
| natural: hide (thick skin, scale, chitin, bark) | 0 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 2 | yes |
| natural: plate (stone, iron, carapace) | 1 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 3 | yes |
| worn: from its gear (padded, leather or hide 1; mail, scale or brigandine 2; plate 3) | by gear | | | | | no |

Natural armor is `no_gaps`: 06.4.10's called shot at the gap does not bypass it. Worn armor has gaps.
Reduction applies to `harm.physical` only (06's T-06-11); elemental harm goes around it.

cards.title: Size and pace
cards.body:
**09.3.7 Size and pace.** `[D]` [DL-06-30; DL-06-07; revision: I-065] Size is from the archetype or the entry (06.3.10's six rungs: tiny, small,
medium, large, huge, colossal); it sets reach, engagement capacity and grapple scale (06's table). Pace is
06.3.3's `speed`: 1 by default; 2 for runners and fliers (wolves, cats, raptors, fire elementals, hellbeasts);
0 for things that cannot move (a rooted creeper: Move is G4 for it); a creature with `pow.flight`,
`pow.swimmer`, `pow.climber` or `pow.burrower` moves in that mode (`slot.movement_mode`).

cards.title: Focus and effect DCs
cards.body:
**09.3.8 Focus and effect DCs.** `[D]` [DL-09-17; DL-09-07; DL-00A-09; revision: I-065] An adversary's **Focus** is its special budget, spent only on its
powers and pool abilities (09.5.3): base by band 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4, +1 elite, +2 solo, +1 for the `caster`
role, 0 for minions. Focus does not recover during a conflict; an adversary met again in a later scene has
its full Focus. Its **effect DC** for each attribute its powers name (`effect_dc_source`) is
`10 + attribute + c_b` (00.3.8), stored per attribute in `effect_dc` (05's request d).

cards.title: Reactions
cards.body:
**09.3.9 Reactions.** `[D]` [DL-09-04; DL-09-08; DL-06-01; revision: I-065] By the adversary's **effective band** (its band, +1 for an elite), following
06.6.5: T1 none; T2 one reaction, Opportunity Strike only; T3 and above one reaction, Opportunity Strike or
Fend (Fend spent on the first attack against it each round from the attacker with the highest modifier it
has seen, 06.6.5). A **solo** has Opportunity Strike and Fend at any band; a **minion** and every **mob**
have none (06.10.2). An archetype may set `reaction: false`. Reaction *abilities* an adversary holds by id
(05) compete for the same one reaction.

cards.title: Building a stat block
cards.body: ### 09.4 Building a stat block

cards.title: Archetype + band + role + variant → stat block
cards.body:
**09.4.1 Archetype + band + role + variant → stat block.** `[D]` [DL-09-06; C:I; revision: I-065] PR-09-1 is the only way an adversary's
numbers come to exist, for the bestiary and for every creature improvised in play (PR-09-2). The DM supplies
four classifications and the engine does the rest. The data generator runs the same procedure, so every
bestiary entry is reproducible from its four inputs plus its listed overrides.

cards.title: Roles
cards.body:
**09.4.2 Roles.** `[J:enum]` + `[D]` A **role** is how a creature fights: it picks the primary attack, the
default behavior list where the archetype names several, and chapter 06's default-behavior family when no
list applies. Roles do not change the band's scale; numbers stay budget-neutral through the Vitality solve
(09.4.4) [R: https://2e.aonprd.com/Rules.aspx?ID=2874 (roadmaps); R1 §06 (Lancer's NPC templates);
R3 §09.4 (GW2: no encounter requires a role of the PC)].

cards.title: Roles
cards.worst_case: a neighboring role: a different primary attack and default list; the numbers are re-solved to the same band budget, so the fight is no harder or easier than the band says, only different in shape (class i).
cards.body:
**T-09-4 Roles.**

| Role | Fights by | Primary attack | 06's default family | True only when… / false for… |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `soldier` | holding a line, steady blows | its primary melee attack | melee | its strength is trained, even fighting; not when it relies on one huge blow (brute) or on range (archer) |
| `brute` | heavy blows behind a Windup, absorbing harm | its primary attack; its heavy attack is the threat | melee / beast | it is big and hits like a falling tree; Guard tends low, Vitality high |
| `skirmisher` | speed, hit-and-withdraw, flanking | its primary attack | melee / beast | it moves more than it stands; pace 2 is common |
| `archer` | range and cover | its first ranged attack | ranged | it would rather shoot than close |
| `caster` | workings from range | its attack working | ranged | its threat is magic; it carries pool abilities and +1 Focus |
| `controller` | conditions, holds, terrain | its primary attack (often a Grapple) | melee / beast | its threat is what it does to your options, not your Vitality |
| `leader` | making its side better | its primary attack | melee | it rallies, commands and is its side's morale anchor (06.11.2) |
| `lurker` | ambush from hiding | its primary attack | beast | it strikes from concealment and leaves fair fights |
| `swarm` | many tiny bodies (06.10.5) | its primary attack, one roll per engaged Guard | mob | it is a swarm or a mob of tiny things |

*Decision* `[J:enum]` (improvised creatures only): the role whose "true only when" fits the creature's
fiction; tie-break: the archetype's first listed role. *Worst case (J):* a neighboring role: a different primary
attack and default list; the numbers are re-solved to the same band budget, so the fight is no harder or
easier than the band says, only different in shape (class i).

cards.title: Powers and the power premium
cards.body:
**09.4.3 Powers and the power premium.** `[D]` [DL-09-05; revision: I-065] An adversary's **powers** are its archetype's plus any its
entry adds (09.5). A power that adds threat beyond the attack line carries a **premium** (T-09-6): 0.06 for
each rider, offensive action or aura, except a **lingering-harm rider** (burning or bleeding: `pow.bleed`,
`pow.burning_touch`), 0.15, its measured worth (`09-lingering-rider.py`: the band's standard line with the
rider raises the PC's harm ratio by 0.09–0.19, mean 0.15, the PC ending it at once) [revision: I-090]
[DL-09-28]; 0.03 for each lesser power (pack tactics, shield wall, frenzy, ambush,
blink, glamour, mend, rally, call, drag, Shrug, second wind); 0.10 for a summoning; 0.04 for each pool ability
held; total capped at 0.40. Movement modes, senses and bodily immunities carry none: their worth is
situational and they are the creature's identity, not its weight. Resistances and regeneration carry none
either, because they are handled as counters (09.4.4).

cards.title: The Vitality solve: every adversary of a band is worth the band
cards.body:
**09.4.4 The Vitality solve: every adversary of a band is worth the band.** `[D]` Vitality is not chosen.
The engine computes the **harm ratio** that one standard adversary of the band inflicts on the reference PC
of the same band (PR-09-4, the advisory's estimator: expected harm taken before the foe falls or breaks,
over the PC's Vitality), divides it by `1 + premium`, and takes the Vitality, inside the band's envelope
(00.3.7: T1 2–5, T2 6–12, T3 12–20, T4 20–32, T5 32–60), whose harm ratio is nearest that target
(log-distance; ties to the lower). So a dodgy skirmisher with Guard 17 at T2 has less Vitality than a
lumbering brute with Guard 13, and both are worth one T2 standard; a creature with three riders has less
Vitality than a plain one. Resistance and regeneration are **not** counted in the solve: Vitality is solved
as if the PC holds the **counter** (silver, a magical property, fire, acid, a blunt weapon), and the advisory
(09.6.4) reports how much harder the creature is when the PC does not. Resistances are puzzles with a named
answer, not weight [R2 #12; DL-09-05].

cards.title: Severity compensation
cards.body:
**09.4.5 Severity compensation.** `[D]` [DL-09-20; revision: I-065] If the solve lands at the envelope's floor and the creature is still
stronger than the band by more than half again (fidelity > 1.5; at T1 > 2.0), its primary attack and its
non-shaped heavy attack drop one severity rung and the solve runs again; if it lands at the ceiling and is
weaker by more than a third (fidelity < 0.67; at T1 < 0.5), they rise one rung. At most two steps. The
record keeps `calibration {premium, solved_vitality, fidelity, severity_compensation, line}`. Across the
123-entry bestiary, 11 entries took one compensation step (nine up, two down) and every entry's
final fidelity lies within
0.67–1.5 (T1: 0.5–2.0) (`09-gen_data09-output.txt`).

cards.title: Variants
Variants
cards.body:
**T-09-5 Variants.**

| Variant | Vitality | Reaction | Nerve | Focus | Gains | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `minion` | ½ of the solved Vitality (min 1) | none | one rung lower (steady → skittish, resolute → steady) | 0 | — | the body of a mob (06.10.2), an escort, a crowd; fielded alone, a weakened one of its kind (below) |
| `standard` | the solved Vitality | by band (09.3.9) | the archetype's | by band | — | most foes |
| `elite` | × 2 at T1–T3, × 1.25 at T4–T5 | as one band higher | one rung higher (skittish → steady → resolute) | +1 | usually one added power; a leader is usually elite | a sergeant, a pack alpha, a chieftain |
| `solo` | × 4 at T1, × 3 at T2–T3, × 1.75 at T4, × 1.5 at T5 | Opportunity Strike and Fend at any band | one rung higher | +2 | `pow.shrug`, `pow.second_wind`, a heavy blow (its primary at the band's heavy severity, wound up) if it had none; `beh.09.solo_overlay` before its list | a creature built to be fought alone: the troll under the bridge, the dragon in the hill |

**A lone minion.** `[D]` + `[N]` An encounter row may field one to three `minion`s of an archetype without a
mob (09.8.2's top ring, 10.10.1): each is a **weakened single foe** — spent, wounded, young, starving or a
straggler of its kind. It is the minion line exactly (half Vitality, no reaction, a nerve one rung lower,
Focus 0), so it can pay for no power or pool ability that costs Focus: a lone minion lich is a lich whose
phylactery is cracked and whose spells are gone, fighting with what its body has left; its free powers
(costing no Focus) and its attacks stand. The narration must show the weakness at first sight (one tell of it
beside the band tells, 09.10.1) and may not imply the full creature's powers. The advisory (09.6) prices it as
fielded. The bestiary ships no lone minions (09.12.1); the tables field them [revision: I-066].

*Why the multipliers fall at the top.* At P1–P3 the lone PC's three actions against two dominate (06.1.1);
at P4–P5 armor and Vitality outgrow unaided output (T-06-13: "the curve steepens at the top"). One multiplier
for every band would make an elite T2 trivial and an elite T5 lethal. The multipliers were fitted so that,
against a PC of its own band with no Focus, an **elite** is one or two words harsher than a standard of its
band and never lethal, and a **solo** is **hard** from T3 up and at the edge of hard at T2 (simulated,
section C of the output, 3,000 fights a row; win% / Staggered%):

| Against P(b), no Focus | T1 | T2 | T3 | T4 | T5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| standard | trivial 100/0 | trivial 100/1 | easy 99/5 | fair 88/43 | hard 80/58 |
| elite | trivial 100/1 | fair 97/15 | fair 90/36 | hard 74/63 | hard 63/75 |
| solo | easy 99/9 | fair 86/46 | hard 68/68 | hard 43/86 | hard 46/86 |
| solo, with a Focus push each turn | 100/5 | 93/29 | 83/51 | 70/67 | 66/69 |
| elite vs P(b+1) | trivial | trivial | easy 98/14 | trivial 100/1 | — |
| solo vs P(b+1) | trivial | trivial | fair 92/38 | easy 99/4 | — |

(A T1 solo cannot be made harder inside bounded accuracy: a novice's three actions against a band-1
creature's two are decisive. A T1 "boss" is a leader with a mob, 09.8.1.) The 00.3.7 Vitality envelope
applies to `standard` (and to `minion` from below); elite, solo and mob pools exceed it the way a mob's
pooled Vitality already does (06.10.2). This is filed as an amendment to 00.3.7 (Interface requests).

cards.title: Mobs and swarms
cards.body:
**09.4.7 Mobs and swarms.** `[D]` [DL-06-20; revision: I-065] Chapter 06 owns mobs and swarms (06.10). This chapter's part: a mob entry
is a `minion` (or `standard`) template with `members` 3 or more; its Vitality is pooled (`members ×
per_member`), it has two actions, no reaction, one Guard and one morale clock; its numbers step is 06.10.3's.
A swarm entry carries `swarm: true` and a tiny size; 06.10.5's three differences apply (it engages everyone
in a group to four targets, unshaped attacks harm it one rung lighter, it cannot be grappled, shoved,
flanked or knocked prone). A leader, a champion or anything named is never folded into a mob (06.10.2); the
archetype's `encounter.group` names its usual leader.
