cards.title: Building an adversary: the dire wolf, and its alpha
cards.body:
### WE-09-1 Building an adversary: the dire wolf, and its alpha

*Inputs.* `arch.wolf` (attribute rungs M H H H L L M for might, agility, endurance, wits, intellect, presence,
resolve; trained in Agility and Wits; natural armor none; bite: Might, offset 0, rider `pow.knockdown`;
powers pack tactics, keen scent, night eyes; nerve skittish, break flee; disposition drive off), band **T2**,
role **soldier**, variant **standard**; entry overrides: creature tags `creature.beast.predator.canine`,
`creature.beast.monstrous.dire`, size large.

1. **Attributes** (T-09-2, T2): might +1, agility +3, endurance +3, wits +3, intellect −1, presence −1, resolve
   +1. `c_b` = +2.
2. **Defenses**: Guard 10 + 3 + 2 = **15**; agility 15 and wits 15 (trained); might 11; endurance 13;
   intellect 9; presence 9; resolve 11. **Tempo** 10 + 3 = **13** (it often acts before a novice).
3. **Bite**: Might +1 + 2 = **+3**; T2 standard harm S2, offset 0 → S2; rider knockdown with effect DC
   10 + 1 + 2 = **13** (Evade or prone).
4. **Premium**: knockdown rider 0.06 + pack tactics 0.03 = **0.09** (scent and night eyes carry none).
5. **Solve**: the T2 standard's harm ratio against P2, ÷ 1.09, is the target. With the bite at S2, even the
   envelope's ceiling (12) leaves the wolf too weak (fidelity under 0.67): a +3 bite at Moderate harm does too
   little against Guard 16 and armor 1. **Compensation** (09.4.5): the bite rises one rung to **S3**, and the
   solve lands at **Vitality 9**, fidelity 0.95.
6. **Variant** standard: × 1. **Reaction** (T2): Opportunity Strike. **Nerve** skittish (4). **Focus** 1.
   **Pace** 2 (from the archetype). **Lethal context** false; **disposition** drive off.
7. **Advisory alone**: P1 easy, P2 trivial, P3–P5 trivial.

*The alpha (boundary pair).* `adv.warg_alpha`: the same archetype at **T3**, **elite**, with `pow.howl` and
`pow.call_kin` added. T3 rungs give might +2, agility +4 …; bite +2 + 3 = **+5**, standard harm S3; Guard 10 +
4 + 3 = **17**; premium 0.18 (two more actions); solved Vitality 20, **× 2 = 40**; reaction as T4: Opportunity
Strike and **Fend**; nerve skittish → **steady (6)**; Focus 2 + 1 = **3**. Advisory alone: P2 lethal, **P3
fair**, P4 trivial. It is the pack's leader (`leader: true`): its defeat ticks the pack's morale +2.
*Tempting non-example.* "It leads the pack, so make it T4." Leading is the elite variant and the leader flag;
the band is what it *is* (09.3.1). A T4 wolf would drop tier-4 loot and count as a band-4 deed for a wolf.

cards.title: The advisory for a mixed encounter
cards.body:
### WE-09-2 The advisory for a mixed encounter

*Situation.* A P3 character (the reference line) meets an orc warchief (`adv.orc_warchief`: T3 elite leader;
axe +7, S3; Guard 16; reduction 1; Vitality 36; Fend; nerve resolute) and his warband (`adv.orc_warband`: a mob
of five T2 minions; axe +5, S2; Guard 14; reduction 1; 6 Vitality each, pool 30; nerve skittish).

1. **Rates** (exact d20 enumeration). The PC deals the warband 10.2 a round (three Strikes at +9, +7, +5 vs
   Guard 14; S3 = 5 − 1 reduction, a critical 8 − 1) and the warchief 7.55 (his Fend makes the first −2). The
   warchief deals 3.0 a round, the warband 2.4 (numbers step +1 at three to five members) and 0.9 at one or two.
   The PC's Fend goes to the higher rate: the warchief's 3.0 becomes **2.7**.
2. **Timeline.** Lowest total Vitality first: the warband (30) falls member by member every 6 ÷ 10.2 = 0.59
   rounds, the last at **2.94**; then the warchief, 36 ÷ 7.55 = 4.77 rounds, to **7.71**.
3. **Morale.** The side's nerve is the leader's: resolute, **8**. Ticks: five members defeated (+5 by 2.94);
   strength first at half (33 of 66) when the warchief has taken 3, at 2.94 + 4.77 × 3/36 = **3.34** (+2 → 7);
   the warchief first bloodied at 2.94 + 2.39 = **5.32** (+1 → 8): **the side breaks at 5.32 rounds.**
4. **Harm.** Warchief 2.7 × 5.32 = 14.36; warband 2.4 × 1.76 + 0.9 × 1.18 = 5.28; tempo edges (the warchief
   acts first 35% of the time, the warband 30%) −0.89. **H = 18.8** against Vitality 16: ratio 1.17.
5. **Outcome.** σ = 7.8; mean landed blow h̄ = 2.27. Staggered = 1 − Φ((16 − 1 − 18.8)/7.8) = **69%**;
   win = Φ((16 + 1.75 × 2.27 − 0.5 − 18.8)/7.8) = **54%**.
6. **Word**: win ≥ 40 → **hard**. The Monte Carlo (10,000 fights) gives 46% / 66%: also hard.
7. **What the player sees.** Chapter 07's danger notice: "`[WARNING] A hard fight — you may well lose this.
   Losing here means they take you for labor.`" (the orcs capture; captive fate labor). In fiction: drums, a
   burned farmstead, the band tell "the others give it room".
*Boundary pair.* The same encounter for a P4 character is **fair** (90 / 28). With an able hireling at the P3
character's side it **stays hard**, shown as "hard, with your companions beside you": its no-ally win, 54, is below
75 (09.6.3's hard exception) [verification: V2b-004]. If the orcs ambush a P3 character who did not notice them
(`cond.surprised`), **lethal** (one word harsher), and chapter 07's lethal warning fires — but takes effect only
after the player's first declaration (07.3.5), so the ambush's opening blows can at worst put the character
Down.
*Tempting non-example.* "The warchief is T3 and so is the PC, and the warband is weaker: call it fair." Band
alone is the challenge-rating failure (R2 #11): five extra bodies are most of this fight's danger.

cards.title: Running an adversary's turn from its list
cards.body:
### WE-09-3 Running an adversary's turn from its list

*Situation.* A barrow-wight (`adv.barrow_wight`: T3; blade +7 S3, draining touch +7 S3 with grave chill and
life drink; Guard 15; Vitality 15; Focus 2; `pow.summon_dead`; list `beh.09.grave_lord`) at `band.near` from a
P3 character who has just broken its barrow's seal. Rows (09.7.1):

| # | when | do |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | broken | fighting_withdrawal |
| 2 | can_pay & reinforcements_possible & not_engaged | use pow.summon_dead |
| 3 | windup_held & target_in_reach | heavy |
| 4 | heavy_ready | windup |
| 5 | can_pay & engaged_target | use pow.dread_gaze |
| 6 | not_engaged | move_engage |
| 7 | always | strike (primary) |

- **Round 1, action 1.** Row 1 false. Row 2: it can pay (2 Focus), the summon is unused, nobody is engaged
  with it → **use `pow.summon_dead`** (two actions, 2 Focus): a mob of three `adv.skeleton_rabble` claws up at
  `band.far`. The tell is narrated ("it chants; the ground at the edge of the light begins to move"); the
  engine writes `witnessed.pc.pow.summon_dead.<wight>`; the advisory is recomputed and re-shown (09.6.5 b).
  Both actions are spent.
- **Round 2, action 1.** Row 2: Focus 0 → false. Row 3: no windup. Row 4: `heavy_ready` false (no heavy attack
  on its record). Row 5: it holds no `pow.dread_gaze` → the row's act is illegal → skipped. Row 6: not engaged →
  **Move** near → close (1 action). **Action 2**: evaluated again: still not engaged → Move close → engaged.
- **Round 3.** Row 7 → **strike** with its primary (the blade), twice; target by attention: the enemy engaged
  with it. First Strike +7 against Guard 18, the PC Fends (−2): needs 13 (40%); second at −2: needs 13 (40%).
  On a hit, 5 − 2 (armor) = 3 harm.
*Boundary.* Had the PC rushed it in round 1 (engaged before its turn), row 2 is false (`not_engaged` fails) and
it strikes at once: whether the dead rise depends on what the PC does first. *Non-example.* "It's a dramatic
moment, it should use its draining touch." The list says `strike (primary)`; the primary is the blade. Drama
does not choose rows (06.9.1).

cards.title: A morale break, and prisoners
cards.body:
### WE-09-4 A morale break, and prisoners

*Situation.* A P1 character fights a bandit captain (`adv.bandit_captain`: T2 elite leader; +3, S2; Guard 13;
Vitality 24; nerve steady, break yield) and four brigands (`adv.brigand_band`: a T1 minion mob of 4, 2 each,
pool 8). The advisory: **hard** (79 / 49: one point short of fair), so 07's danger notice is shown ("losing here
means they rob you"). The side reads the leader's nerve: **steady (6)**.
1. The PC's first turn drops two brigands (each hit: 3 − 1 armor = 2, one member's whole Vitality): +1, +1 →
   **2**. Omen (stirring): "one of them glances back at the road".
2. Second turn: the last two brigands fall (+2 → **4**). The captain, alone, rallies (`pow.rally_cry`,
   a fortune check against Moderate: success, reach Standard → −2 → **2**).
3. Third turn: two Strikes put the captain at 12 of 24: first bloodied (+1 → **3**) and the side's strength
   (32 at the start) is past half — 8 + 12 = 20 removed — (+2 → **5**, building: "he gives ground a step at
   a time"). The PC's third action is a Talk to demand surrender — "Drop it and walk, and you keep your life"
   — against the captain's Resolve defense **11**: success, reach Standard → **+2 → 7 ≥ 6: the side breaks.**
4. The break row: the archetype's `break_then` is **yield** (09.7.5): the captain drops his sword and asks
   quarter. He is `defeated` with manner `yielded` (06.11.7) and is the PC's prisoner (07.6.5); sparing or
   killing him is chapter 03's `conduct.mercy` evidence. Loot: one generation for the side (08.3.1),
   circumstance **merciful** if he is spared (the chosen fill).
*Boundary.* Had the captain been defeated first, his defeat ticks +2 (leader) and the brigands, now leaderless,
read the most numerous template's nerve, skittish (4), for their remaining clock. *Non-example.* "They're
bandits, they'd run." They would — if the clock completed. Until it does, they fight (06.11.1).

cards.title: A defeat disposition fires, and a switch to kill
cards.body:
### WE-09-5 A defeat disposition fires, and a switch to kill

*Situation A (drag to lair).* A P2 character is beaten by gnolls (`arch.gnoll`: disposition **drag_to_lair**,
captive fate **the larder**, `lethal_context` false). No lethal context was recorded (no row of 07.3.3 true:
the advisory was fair, the gnolls' disposition is not kill, no S4 attack), so the falling blow puts the
character **Down**, not Dying (07.2.9). The disposition runs its *defeated* column (T-07-11): the PC wakes in
the gnolls' den (a place created with one recorded exit), its weapon lying where it fell, `clk.larder`
created (countdown 4, +1 a watch; at imminent its completion is lethal, so 07's warning fires then), three
openings written, `setback.captured`. A rescue, an escape, or a bargain is the next scene.
*Situation B (the switch).* Brigands (`arch.brigand`: disposition rob; `kill_when`: "the PC killed one of
theirs and they outnumber the PC 3 to 1"). In the fight the PC kills a brigand outright while four remain.
`[J:flag]` *"Is a kill_when fact now true?"* — a brigand is recorded dead by the PC's lethal Strike, and four
against one is 4 : 1 → **true**. The engine writes `side.defeat_disposition_toward_pc = kill`; 07's `disposition`
warning fires ("It means to kill"), effective from the player's next declaration. Yield is now refused (07.4.1:
kill does not accept); the exits card shows Retreat. *Boundary:* had the brigand been dropped with a nonlethal
blow, no one is dead: the flag is false and the brigands still only rob.

cards.title: Learning what a troll is (P17)
cards.body:
### WE-09-6 Learning what a troll is (P17)

*Situation.* A P3 forester sees a troll (`adv.troll`: T4; advisory alone vs P3 **hard**; without the counter
**lethal**; counter "fire or acid"). The player asks what the character knows about trolls.
- **Gate.** `lore` is `deed.lore.bestiary`, rarity common; the troll's terrain (highland, deepwood,
  underground, road, wetland, frozen [verification: V2b-005]) touches the forester's origin (forest): **common knowledge true** → G1 Recall (Intellect).
- **DC.** Common at T4 → **Hard (20)**. The forester's Intellect 0 + floor 1 = +1: success on 19+ (10%),
  natural 20 a critical. The player ranks: (1) kind and threat, (3) resistance and counter, (5) weak spot.
- **Roll** 19 → success; delivered items by 01's `deliver_count(3 ranked, Standard)`: about half → the
  first two of the ranked list: "a troll, and a big one"; "it heals from anything but fire or acid". Both are
  written as knowledge and become `available` in the codex.
- **What changes.** The advisory is re-read against the PC's actual attack: with a torch's fire as the
  attack's harm (06.5.10), regeneration does not apply → **hard**; with the spear alone → **lethal**, and 07's
  warning fires. The player was given a plan, not a number.
*Boundary.* A city-born character has no common knowledge here: without `lic.training.lore_bestiary` the
Recall is G3, redirected to Observe it in action (06.9.6) or to asking the old hunter. *Non-example.* "Everyone
knows trolls hate fire" is an assertion (SG-06) until a Recall or a source delivers it.

cards.title: The victor remembers
cards.body:
### WE-09-7 The victor remembers

*Situation.* The orc warchief of WE-09-2 breaks at 5.32 rounds (his `break_then` is flee), is not cornered,
and gets away. Trigger (09.9.3): an adversary escaped a conflict with the PC alive. The engine promotes him to
`recurring`, names him (12's tables: "Gorbrak Vey"), and rolls `tbl.09.nemesis`: **4, Grudge** — his disposition toward the PC becomes
**kill**. It writes `knows_pc` (face, the PC's spear-work). Three weeks later the warband is rolled on the hill
road's table: when the PC perceives him, 07's `disposition` warning fires at first sight, the narrator voices
"he knows you, and he has not come for captives", and the advisory is computed for a T3 elite leader and his
new warband (a second roll, months later, gave **6, Retinue**). Chapter 04 may stage V8: he calls the PC by the
name the hill-clans now use.
*Non-example.* "He'd hold a grudge, so he's stronger now." A grudge changes what he wants, not his numbers; only
result 5 changes a variant (he is already elite, so a 5 would be rerolled), and nothing changes his band.

cards.title: Out of band: the barrow at P1
cards.body:
### WE-09-8 Out of band: the barrow at P1

*Situation.* A P1 character pries open a barrow. Inside stands a barrow-wight: T3, **two bands above**. At
first perception (09.6.6) the advisory is lethal (P1 vs the wight: 3% / 99%), so 07's lethal warning fires in
the same turn, its sign the band tell ("it reads your stance before you move") and the wight's presence tell
("frost on the grave-goods; a handprint on the inside of the seal"). The `[WARNING]` block lists the exits: Yield
— not accepted (it drags to its lair; T-07-11); Retreat — the barrow door, a chase. The wight's list has a
parley row ("when the PC returns what was taken from its barrow"): if the character drops the grave-gold and
backs out, the parley is legal. *Boundary:* a P2 character gets the same warning (14% / 96%); a P3 character
meets a **trivial** wight (99.99% / 1.4%), with no warning and no band tell. *Non-example:* "The PC is only P1;
make the wight T1 so it's fair." Encounters belong to places; 09.3.1 forbids banding by the scene's needs and
06.9.7 forbids tuning.

cards.title: A structural weakness: the swarm
cards.body:
### WE-09-9 A structural weakness: the swarm

*Situation.* A P1 martial character (sword S2) meets a rat swarm (`adv.rat_swarm`: T1 minion swarm, members 6,
2 each, pool 12). Advisory: easy. Every unshaped sword Strike harms it one rung lighter (S1: 1 Vitality), so
the PC's three Strikes a turn chip it; the swarm engages the PC and makes one roll against its Guard each turn
(06.10.5). The player asks what else might work. *Boundary pair:* a torch swept through it (06.5.10's
environment use, a `burst`-shaped fire through a feature) applies full harm several times over and the swarm's
fire vulnerability doubles it; a lantern smashed on the floor is a hazard feature it must cross. *The lesson the
data encodes:* the single-target fighter's weakness against swarms (R2 #12, Jason vs swarms) is real, and the
answer is a different kind of action, not a bigger number.

---

cards.title: The place graph
cards.body: ### 10.1 The place graph

cards.title: The world is a graph of places
cards.body:
**10.1.1 The world is a graph of places.** `[D]` [DL-10-01; C:IV; R5 EX-07; revision: I-065] Every location the character can be in is a **place**
(entity kind `place`, 00.6.2) and every way between two places is a **route link** on the place it
leaves from. The graph is canonical; descriptions follow it. A place's **place kind** (`place_kind`,
closed list, T-10-1) fixes what rules load there:

| `place_kind` | True only when it is… | Holds | Mode on entry (T-12-3) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `region` | a named stretch of country with one home band and one danger rating (the Marches, the Fenmoor) | areas | — |
| `area` | a stretch of country one can cross in about a day or less, with one terrain (a hex, a valley, a wood) | routes, landmarks, sites, settlements | `travel` while moving |
| `settlement` | a place where people live (village, town, hold, camp) | buildings, districts | `free` |
| `site` | a place explored area by area: a ruin, a cave, a barrow, a lair (10.13) | site areas | `site` |
| `site_area` | one area inside a site, made when explored (10.13.6) | features, exits | `site` |
| `landmark` | a fixed, visible thing in an area used to find the way (a standing stone, a peak, a ford) | — | — |
| `building` | a building or district within a settlement | rooms | `free`, or `site` for a room-by-room search |

`parent` (00.6.2) nests them: region → area → site → site_area, and settlement → building. A place
belongs to exactly one parent; an area's region gives it its home band and danger rating unless the area
overrides them.

cards.title: The place record
cards.body:
**10.1.2 The place record.** `[D]` [DL-10-01; DL-00A-22; C:P3; revision: I-065] Chapter 10 extends 00.6.2's `Place` with these fields (all data; the world seed
writes them for the starting region, 12.16.8, and a pre-made setting such as 13 authors its own; generated
places get them from the generator that made them) [revision: I-028]:

```yaml
Place (extends 00.6.2 Place):
  place_kind: enum            # 10.1.1
  band: int|null              # home band 1..5 (region, area, site); tier cap for place-gated loot (08.3.5)
  danger: enum|null           # safe | settled | wild | perilous | deadly   (10.9.2)
  safe: bool                  # true = a haven: ventures end here; no time-tick check (10.2.3)
  rest_site: enum|null        # haven | camp | rough   (07.8.2 reads it; null = ask 07.8.2's rung)
  terrain: [tag]              # terrain.* tags (00.6.2); first is primary
  climate: enum|null          # temperate | northern | highland | arid | coastal  (weather zone, 10.11.2)
  nav_tier: enum|null         # easy | moderate | hard | very_hard  (10.4.3; areas)
  forage_tier: enum|null      # by terrain and season unless set (T-10-12)
  game_tier: enum|null        # hunting (T-10-12)
  openness: enum              # open | broken | closed   (encounter distance, landmark visibility, T-10-15)
  landmarks: [place_id]       # visible landmarks (10.4.4)
  water_source: bool|null     # a spring, river or well a traveler can drink from (10.6.2)
  grazing: bool|null          # mounts may graze here in season (10.8.3)
  encounter_table: tbl_id     # the region's table (12.16.13), else the generic terrain table (10.10.1)
  hazards: [{hazard_id, where, active_when}]   # standing hazards of the place (10.12)
  resonance: [tag]            # deed keys, branches or conduct axes (04 V11; 05.6.9)
  settlement_scope: place_id|null   # the nearest settlement ancestor or patron settlement (03.10 scope)
  known: bool                 # the PC has heard of it (rumor, map, story)
  discovered: bool            # the PC has been there or perceived it (00.6.2); 10.1.5
  site: SiteRecord|null       # 10.13.3
  state_log: [{at, change}]   # persistent changes made by play (10.13.12)
```

Facts a place may carry, read by other chapters: `desecrated`, `consecrated`, `dead_ground` (05.7.2; dead
ground is the fact that makes primal workings G4 there), `haunted` (a dread source, 07.11.2),
`weather.today` and `weather.tomorrow` (10.11; 05.7.3 reads the first), `light` (10.7.2), `roused` (a
site, 10.13.9), and a pre-made setting's own facts (chapter 13's Thallen Vale adds `hushed` and `true_bell`, 13.2, read only
through that region's hazards and the Waking rule) [integration: IR ch.13; revision: I-028]. Each is written with `set_fact` and never
implied by narration alone.

cards.title: The route link
cards.body:
**10.1.3 The route link.** `[D]` [DL-10-01; DL-10-02; revision: I-065] A link (00.6.2: `{to, route, travel_watches}`) carries:

```yaml
RouteLink:
  to: place_id
  route: str                  # route id, shared by both directions ("rt.salt_road.3")
  route_kind: enum            # road | track | river | water | trackless | underway | secret | passage
  travel_watches: int         # watches at NORMAL walking pace, fair weather, unburdened (10.3.2)
  terrain: [tag]              # what it crosses (may differ from both ends)
  current: enum|null          # downstream | upstream | none   (water routes)
  known: bool                 # the PC knows this way exists
  danger: enum|null           # overrides the area's rating along it (a patrolled road)
  hazards: [{hazard_id, where}]   # fixed hazards on the way (a ford, a scree slope)
  vehicle_ok: [str]           # bi.* conveyances that can use it (08.10.3)
```

The route kinds mean: **road** (kept, never lost on it, vehicles); **track** (a trail; never lost in fair
visibility); **river** and **water** (by boat, or followed on foot along a bank: never lost); **trackless**
(across country toward a known destination: navigation, 10.4); **underway** (a known underground
passage: never lost with light; navigation without it); **secret** (exists sealed until found by a search
or a clue; `known: false` until then); **passage** (within a site or building; 1 interval to cross).

cards.title: Write-on-mention for places
cards.trigger: narration (or a table result) introduces a way, a place, a landmark, an exit, a feature of terrain or a sign in a place
cards.license_check: none (state discipline)
decisions: 1. ADDRESSABLE [J:flag] (00.6.6): "Could the player cite this later as a route, a destination, a landmark, an obstacle, a hazard, cover, a place to rest or a clue?" True only when it is concrete and locatable ("a deer track down to the stream", "a cairn on the ridge", "a door on the left"); false for pure atmosphere ("mist in the hollows", "the smell of pine"). Uncertain -> true.
cards.computation: true -> create_entity(place | object) or a route link with the fields the narration implies; every unimplied field stays undetermined and is settled by the Oracle or the place's tables when first needed (00.6.6). An exit named in a site area is a link with route_kind passage. A "way down to the river" is a route link with route_kind track and travel_watches from T-10-3 if the narration gave no length.
narration_may_not_imply: a route, exit or place that has no record after this turn
a length, a danger or a destination the record does not hold
cards.worst_case: an atmospheric detail is recorded needlessly (harmless); a usable one is not, and the claim check (12.3) catches it at the scene end (class iv)
examples: inside: "a fallen oak spans the gully" -> landmark + a track link across the gully. inside: "the corridor runs on into the dark" -> a passage link to an undetermined site area. outside: "the wind smells of snow" -> atmosphere; but the weather record already holds snow tomorrow, so nothing new is written. non-example: the player says "there must be a pass through these hills" -> an assertion; it is an Oracle question (Likely in hills) before any link exists.

cards.title: Known, discovered, and the discovery fact
cards.body:
**10.1.5 Known, discovered, and the discovery fact.** `[D]` [DL-10-01; C:P3; R5 EX-13; revision: I-065] A place is **known** when the PC has a fact
about it (a rumor, a map, a story, an NPC's directions) and **discovered** when the PC has been there or
perceived it directly. Discovery is written `set_fact(loc.<id>, discovered, true)` with:
- `frame_id` = the frame whose delivered result found it (a navigation reach 4, a scout's beat, a search,
  an Explore onward, a vantage Observe), when a frame found it — this is the event 03's `cnt.discovery`
  counts (03.9: "written as the delivered result of the actor's frame");
- `frame_id: null` when the PC simply arrived by a known route or by a table result (the discovery face,
  10.9.4), which records the place but is not evidence: wandering into a place is not finding it.
An undiscovered place is sealed (00.6.4) with the gate "the PC arrives, or perceives it". Rumored
places (`known: true, discovered: false`) appear in the codex's Journal view (T-14-3), on request, by name only [editor: E2-002], with the truth of
the rumor still sealed (11).

cards.title: The settlement scope
cards.body:
**10.1.6 The settlement scope.** `[D]` [DL-10-31; DL-03-09; DL-11-15; revision: I-065] Every area and site carries `settlement_scope`: the place id of the
settlement whose people would hear of what is done there (the nearest settlement by route watches, or the
one the region's seed or setting names as the area's market). Chapter 03's witness scopes (03.10) and chapter 11's reputation read
it. A settlement's own scope is itself. Areas with no settlement within 8 travel watches carry `null`:
deeds done there carry only to witnesses' own scopes.

cards.title: Places of power
cards.body:
**10.1.7 Places of power.** `[D]` [DL-05-14; C:P13; revision: I-065] `resonance: [tag]` on a place names the deed keys, branches or conduct
axes it answers (04's V11 *The Place Answers*; 05.6.9's resonant rest: +1 Focus on a breather or short
rest when a held calling or ability matches). Resonance is data (the region's seed, 12.16.9, 12.16.12) or a written result of a rite
(`rit.consecrate_ground`, 05). `consecrated`, `desecrated` and `dead_ground` are facts with sources;
T-10-24 (`data/hazards.yaml#zones`) lists the magical-zone hazards that go with them (a desecrated
place's dread, dead ground's silence of primal workings).

cards.title: Generated places
cards.body:
**10.1.8 Generated places.** `[D]` [DL-10-01; DL-12-23; C:I; revision: I-065] When play reaches a place no data holds (the player strikes out across
country the region's seed did not author [verification: V2b-006]; a site's new area), the place is generated, never imagined: an area takes its
region's band, danger and climate, a terrain from the region's terrain list by `roll_table`, and its
`nav_tier`, `forage_tier`, `openness` from that terrain's defaults (T-10-12); a site takes a theme and a
domain from the region's site tables (10.13.2); a site area takes its feature from the domain table
(10.13.6). Every generated place is written before it is narrated (PR-10-1 step 2). The DM chooses names
and words, never fields.

cards.title: Time, modes, ventures and safety
cards.body: ### 10.2 Time, modes, ventures and safety

cards.title: The modes of this chapter
cards.body:
**10.2.1 The modes of this chapter.** `[D]` [DL-00A-12; R5 TM-01; revision: I-065] Three of 00.7.3's time modes are this chapter's to run:
- **`travel`**: each **travel activity is one watch** (00.7.3). The PC spends every watch of a journey day
  on one activity (T-10-6: travel, camp, sleep, forage, hunt, scout, rest, keep watch, map, other).
- **`site`**: each **significant beat is one interval** (00.7.3; `h.10.site_time`, 10.13.5); a beat is
  significant when it resolves a check or performs an activity listed in T-10-20 with a duration; looking
  around casually, talking and free activities take no interval.
- **`free`**, outside settlements, for scenes at one spot in the wild (a parley at a ford, a camp
  conversation): activities take their listed durations (T-10-20).
Transitions follow 12's T-12-3: departing along a route link → `travel`; entering a place whose
`place_kind` is `site` or `site_area`, or beginning a room-by-room search of a building → `site`;
arriving at a settlement → `free`; `conflict_start` → `conflict` and back at `conflict_end`.

cards.title: Venture start and end
cards.body:
**10.2.2 Venture start and end.** `[T]` + `[D]` [DL-10-24; revision: I-065] A **venture** (00.18) runs from leaving safety to returning.
- `venture_start` is marked when the PC moves from a place with `safe: true` onto a route link whose
  destination is not safe, or begins a travel watch outside any safe place.
- `venture_end` is marked when the PC enters a place with `safe: true`, or when chapter 07 records the PC
  captured and carried to a captor's place (the venture ends in captivity; the next is begun from there).
- Handler `h.10.venture` (`venture_start`/`venture_end`, phase 9) writes the **venture record**
  `{id, started_at, from, route_plan, supply_at_start, light_at_start, places_discovered: [ids],
  sites_entered: [ids], encounters: [ids], hazards_met: [ids], ended_at, to, days}` (the start fields at
  start; the rest appended through play; closed at end). Chapter 11's `h.11.reckoning` and 12's
  `h.12.venture_bookkeeping` read it on `venture_end` (00.7.6 runs `venture_end` after rests and
  reflection).
- While a venture is open, the fact `pc.on_venture = true` holds: 08's lifestyle charge is replaced by
  supply (`economy.yaml#lifestyle_rules`), and 07's rest site is never `haven` unless the place is one.

cards.title: Safety
cards.body:
**10.2.3 Safety.** `[D]` [DL-10-24; DL-07-11; revision: I-065] A place with `safe: true` is a **haven** for this chapter: no time-tick check
runs there (07's request: "no encounter check in a haven"), its `rest_site` is `haven`, and ventures end
there. Safety is a property of the place, written by data (the region's seed, 12.16.9, or a pre-made setting: the base
town, a friendly hold, a guarded shrine) [verification: V2b-006] or by play (11: a holding the PC owns and garrisons; a village that grants the PC
hospitality writes `safe: true` while standing is Friendly or better). A safe place loses safety only by
a written world change (a faction takes it; a situation's default timeline burns it, 11), never by
narration. Danger may still enter a haven through chapter 11 (a World Turn event, a bang), chapter 12's
pushes, or a clock — never through this chapter's die.

cards.title: The West Marches shape
cards.body:
**10.2.4 The West Marches shape.** `[N]` [R6 B-15; C:P2; DL-10-07; revision: I-065] A starting region (the world seed's, 12.16.8, or a pre-made one) is laid
out as a haven at the center and
**concentric danger rings** (R6 B-15, B-R7): the farther from the base, the higher an area's home band and
danger rating, so distance is the difficulty dial in a game with no character levels (C:P2). This chapter
gives the dial its meaning: band (how strong what lives there is, 09.8.2) and danger rating (how often it
comes, 10.9.2) are separate fields, and both are shown to the player before a journey (10.3.4) as words,
never numbers. T-10-2 is the reference ring layout a region starts from (12.16.8) [verification: V2b-006].

cards.title: Reference danger rings
cards.body:
**T-10-2 Reference danger rings** (`data/travel.yaml#rings`; the world seed uses them as given, 12.16.8; a pre-made setting may alter a ring with a DL entry).

| Ring | Typical distance from the haven | Home band | Danger rating | In words to the player |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | the haven and its fields | — | safe | "safe under the walls" |
| 1 | up to 1 day | 1 | settled | "farm country; trouble is rare and small" |
| 2 | 1–3 days | 1–2 | wild | "the borderland: wild, but folk pass through" |
| 3 | 3–6 days | 2–3 | wild or perilous | "the deep wilds: dangerous things live here" |
| 4 | 6–10 days | 3–4 | perilous | "the old lands: only the strong travel here" |
| 5 | beyond | 4–5 | deadly | "the far reaches: legends live here, and so do the things that killed them" |

cards.title: What runs while time passes here
cards.body:
**10.2.5 What runs while time passes here.** `[D]` [DL-10-20; DL-00A-12; C:I; revision: I-065] This chapter's handlers (T-10-23) run on these
boundaries and never anywhere else (00.7.4): `h.10.site_time` (`beat_end`, 9), `h.10.light`
(`interval`, 4), `h.10.site_exposure` (`interval`, 2), `h.10.site_check` (`interval`, 7),
`h.10.travel_progress` (`watch`, 4), `h.10.wayfinding` (`watch`, 4, after travel progress by id order),
`h.10.watch_exposure` (`watch`, 2), `h.10.watch_check` (`watch`, 7), `h.10.supply` (`day`, 4),
`h.10.weather` (`day`, 7), `h.10.site_recovery` (`day`, 6), `h.10.day_reset` (`day`, 9), `h.10.site_regrowth` (`week`, 6),
`h.10.weather_regime` (`season`, 6), `h.10.scene_frame` (`scene_start` and `mode_change`, 7), `h.10.venture`
(`venture_start`, `venture_end`, 9). Skipping time runs every one of them for every boundary crossed
(00.7.7): a three-day journey "skipped" is twelve watch checks, three supply days and three weather rolls,
and its narration comes only from the returned list (12.4.6).

cards.title: Leaving a haven into its own area
cards.body:
**10.2.6 Leaving a haven into its own area.** `[D]` [DL-10-29; revision: I-065] A settlement's `parent` is usually the area it stands in,
and its route link to that area (a road of a watch or two, 12.16.9) is the walk from its gate out into the
land. That leg is the **area's first leg**: the haven stops being a haven when the PC passes its gate (the
venture starts, 10.2.2), every watch of the leg ends outside a haven and is checked at the area's danger
rating with the area's tables (10.9.1), and "arriving in the area" means standing in it at the leg's end,
from where its trackless legs and its other links start (10.3.1, 10.4). The way back is the same leg; the
venture ends at the gate (10.2.2) [revision: I-055].

cards.title: A settlement's day
cards.worst_case: a crime called where it was not (or missed) moves one clock by 1–3 ticks of 8, which decay 1 a week; the call cites the act and the value.
cards.body:
**10.2.7 A settlement's day.** `[D]` + `[J:flag]` A settlement keeps hours, a watch and a law; each is a fact
or a clock, never the narrator's mood [R5 EX-12; revision: I-051]:
1. **Hours.** Its gate stands open in the morning and afternoon watches and shuts at the evening watch's
   start. A town or a city (`settlement.tier`, 15.13.8) also keeps a **curfew**: from the evening watch to
   dawn its streets belong to the watch. A hamlet or a village shuts its doors and keeps no curfew. The place's
   `curfew` fact (`none | gate | streets`) overrides the default when the region's seed or play writes it.
   These are ordinary rules of a place, facts and not refusals (15.2.4).
2. **The watch.** The settlement's ruler (the faction whose seat or hold it is, 11.3; the region's seed names
   one for the haven, 12.16.9) keeps a watch of its own folk: `arch.soldier` at the settlement's home band,
   fielded by 09.8.3 when it comes to blows. Passing the shut gate or walking the streets under curfew is
   done with leave (a Talk beat with the watch's officer, an ordinary request, 15.3), unseen (a Sneak against
   the watch's Wits defense, 00.3.8 (2), stored for the night on the place), or by force (a conflict with
   the watch, 06).
3. **The law.** `[J:flag]` Is the act a crime here? Yes for theft, violence, killing, breaking a curfew or a
   shut gate, and trespass in a hold, and for any act the ruler's faction despises by its values (11.3.1).
   A crime the watch sees, or a witness in the settlement's scope reports (10.1.6, 03.10), is a
   `public_deed` the ruler despises: its attention clock ticks 1 (violence 2, a killing 3; 11.3.12), and a
   watch that catches the PC in the act demands an answer then and there — the PC talks (15.3, at the PC's
   standing with the ruler), pays, flees (06.12) or fights. The law's long memory is that clock: its
   completion is the ruler's entanglement (11.3.12), and status moves only by 11.3.11's rows.
4. **The haven holds.** None of this is a time-tick check: a settlement stays a haven (10.2.3), and trouble
   reaches the PC inside its walls only through these facts, chapter 11's clocks and chapter 12's pushes.
*Worst case (J):* a crime called where it was not (or missed) moves one clock by 1–3 ticks of 8, which decay
1 a week; the call cites the act and the value.

cards.title: Journeys: routes, pace, and the travel watch
cards.body: ### 10.3 Journeys: routes, pace, and the travel watch

cards.title: A journey is a plan over the graph
cards.body:
**10.3.1 A journey is a plan over the graph.** `[D]` [DL-10-02; R5 EX-01; revision: I-065] A **journey** is an ordered list of **legs**, each one
route link from one place to the next, ending at a destination the player names (a place id, or "the
standing stones the hermit spoke of" — a known place). The engine finds the legs (the path through
known links with the fewest watches; the player may name a different path); a destination with no known
path is reached by a **trackless** leg across the area toward it (10.4). The plan is a record
`{journey_id, legs, pace, schedule, roles, started_at, progress_points}` written at departure.

cards.title: Length and pace
cards.body:
**10.3.2 Length and pace.** `[D]` [DL-10-02; DL-10-03; revision: I-065] A route's length is its `travel_watches` (W): watches at **normal**
walking pace in fair weather, unburdened, with terrain already folded in by the author (a region writes "3" for
a day and a half over the moor). The engine converts it to **progress points**: a leg needs **6 × W**
points, and each travel watch earns points by the party's **effective pace** on the pace ladder
(`travel.yaml#pace`):

| Pace rung | Points per travel watch | Who moves at it |
|---|---|---|
| crawl | 2 | wading deep snow; groping in the dark; the floor of every slowed party |
| slow | 4 | walkers going carefully, quietly or mapping |
| normal | 6 | walkers; walk-pace mounts (donkey, pony, mule, draft horse); carts and wagons on roads |
| fast | 8 | walkers hurrying |
| ride | 9 | riders on ride-pace mounts (riding horse, courser, destrier); a carriage on a road |
| hard_ride | 12 | riders pressing their mounts |

**The party's base pace** is the slowest member's: a rider escorting a walker walks. **Chosen pace**: the
player picks slow, normal or fast; for a party all on ride-pace mounts (or in a carriage) these mean
normal, ride and hard_ride. **Steps** then move the rung down (never up), clamped at crawl:
1. **burdened** (08.9.2: load above capacity) — one step (a mount's own load against its carry capacity
   counts for the mount); **overloaded** — no travel at all (08.9.2);
2. **weather** off roads (`weather.yaml#states[].pace_steps`: rain 0, storm 1, snow 1, blizzard 2; deep
   snow lying on the ground 1 more) — roads and rivers ignore rain and storm, never snow;
3. **night** (the evening and night watches) without a road, a light or a clear sky — one step;
4. **a hazard on the leg** that slows (`hazards.yaml#…pace_steps`: scree, mire, a flooded ford).
Each step is engine-cited from a fact; none is chosen. Example: Wren (walker, normal) in a storm across
the moor → normal → slow (storm, off-road) → 4 points a watch.

cards.title: The travel watch
cards.body:
**10.3.3 The travel watch.** `[D]` [DL-10-02; R5 EX-01; revision: I-065] Each watch of a journey day is given **one activity** (T-10-6) for the PC
and one for each companion (16). The **default day** is: morning *travel*, afternoon *travel*, evening
*camp*, night *sleep* (a `rest_long`, 07.8.1). The player may change any watch's activity before it
starts. A *travel* watch earns its points at `h.10.travel_progress` (`watch`, phase 4); arrival happens
inside the watch when the points needed run out (arrival hour = the hour at which the cumulative points
reach the leg's need, rounded up), and leftover points carry into the next leg if the journey goes on.
Then `h.10.watch_check` (phase 7) rolls the time-tick die (10.9) for the watch, whatever the activity —
an encounter can find a sleeping camp.

cards.title: The journey OFFER
cards.body:
**10.3.4 The journey OFFER.** `[D]` + `[N]` Before the first travel watch the engine shows the plan out of
fiction, and the player commits, changes it, or stays. No die is rolled; nothing is hidden that the PC
knows:

```
[JOURNEY] To <destination> by <legs in words>. At <pace>: about <days and watches> (<n> travel watches).
          Country: <region words per T-10-2> · Weather: today <state>; tomorrow <state | unknown>.
          Supply: <carried> for <consumers> = <days> days; needed about <days needed> (+ <margin>).
          Light: <sources and intervals> (needed only at night or underground).
          Way-finding: <none needed | <n> trackless days, <navigator | "no navigator: you would go by
          <landmark | the long way | blind>">>. Known hazards: <list | none known>.
```

A journey into a region whose home band exceeds the PC's power band adds one fixed line: "`[WARNING]
Things there are stronger than you.`" at one band above, or "`[WARNING] Things there are far stronger than
you: what lives there can kill you.`" at two or more. It writes no lethal context (07.3.3's rows fire when
a creature there is first perceived, 09.6.6); it is the earlier, regional notice, the West Marches
promise that distance is danger and that the player is told so [R6 B-15; R5 P-32].

cards.title: The march allowance and forced marches
cards.body:
**10.3.5 The march allowance and forced marches.** `[D]` + `[T]` [DL-10-18; R5 HR-07; revision: I-065] A body can march so much a day.
- **Walkers**: an allowance of **2 march units** a day (reset at the `day` boundary, dawn). A travel watch
  at slow or normal pace costs 1 unit; at fast, 2.
- **Mounts**: each mount has its own allowance of **2 units** (ride pace, or normal for walk-pace
  mounts: 1 unit a watch; hard_ride: 2; a mount loaded past half its carry capacity: +1 per watch).
- **A forced march** is any travel watch that takes a walker or mount past its allowance. For each unit
  over, the walker receives **one stack of `cond.exhausted`** (07.8.10), applied at that watch's end by
  `h.10.travel_progress`; the player may first declare 07.8.10's **push-on** Endure beat (Endurance,
  against Moderate; Hard with one stack held; Very hard with two) to defer the stack by as many watches
  as the delivered reach. A mount's stacks are its own (16/07): at three stacks it cannot be ridden or
  loaded until it has had a long rest.
- So a third travel watch at normal pace in a day is one forced unit, a fourth two. `cond.exhausted` is
  removed by long rests per T-07-14 (−1 stack a night), so a walker who marches a third watch at normal pace
  each day wakes clear each morning; one who makes that third watch fast (2 units over) holds two stacks on the
  first evening, one the next morning and three on the second evening, without pushing on: every army story's
  forced march, priced in the same condition 07 uses for sleeplessness and want [verification: V2b-007].

cards.title: Changing the plan, turning back, and stopping
cards.body:
**10.3.6 Changing the plan, turning back, and stopping.** `[D]` [DL-10-02; R5 EX-01; revision: I-065] The player may change destination, pace,
schedule or roles at any watch boundary, or after any interrupt; the journey record keeps the points
earned on the current leg. Turning back on a leg reverses it: the points already earned are the points
needed to return. Stopping in the open turns the next watches into *camp* or *rest*; an interrupted
journey is resumed with its remainder (00.7.8).

cards.title: Travel by water
cards.body:
**10.3.7 Travel by water.** `[D]` [DL-10-03; R5 EQ-10; revision: I-065] A water leg (`route_kind: river | water`) is travelled by vessel (08.10.4)
or by passage (08.8.8). Paces (`travel.yaml#vessel_pace`, points per watch):

| Vessel | Calm water | Downstream | Upstream | Sea | Watches a day |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| raft | — | 8 | cannot | cannot | 2 (moored at night) |
| rowboat | 6 | 8 | 4 | coast only, 4 in calm weather | 2 |
| keelboat | 6 | 9 | 6 | cannot | 3 (crew rows in shifts) |
| river barge | 6 | 8 | 4 | cannot | 3 |
| cog | — | — | — | 16 | 4 (crew in watches; passengers rest) |

A crewed vessel travelling through the night does not tire its passengers: they may sleep aboard
(`rest_site: camp` under cover, `rough` on an open deck). A vessel's **hull clock** (08.10.4) takes
`cost.gear` against the vessel; when it completes the vessel **founders**: everyone aboard is in the water
(`haz.swift_water` on a river, `haz.open_water` at sea, 10.12) and the cargo is lost unless saved by
beats. A water route's hazards (rapids, a weir, reefs) are fixed on its link and met in order; a storm
at sea is the weather's `haz.storm_at_sea`.

cards.title: Travel underground
cards.body:
**10.3.8 Travel underground.** `[D]` [DL-10-23; DL-10-04; R5 EX-01; revision: I-065] An underground leg (`route_kind: underway`, or trackless through
`terrain.underground`) is travelled as overland, with three differences: it is always dark (10.7.2: a
light is needed, or the party moves at crawl with sight-reliant beats under `cond.blinded`); its
way-finding uses `deed.wilds.navigation.underways`; and weather does not apply (only the place's own
hazards: bad air, flooding, collapse). Watches, supply and the time-tick check run as above.

cards.title: Navigation and getting lost
cards.body: ### 10.4 Navigation and getting lost

cards.title: When the way must be found
cards.trigger: a travel watch on a leg begins (h.10.travel_progress, before points)
cards.license_check: none for the question
decisions: 1. NEEDED [J:flag] "Is the party leaving every road, river and track, or is the way hidden from them?" True only when (a) the leg's route_kind is trackless, or underway without light, or (b) the leg is a track and the visibility facts say fog, blizzard, or night without light; false on a road or river, on a track in fair visibility, and on a known site passage. Uncertain -> true.
cards.computation: true -> one way-finding beat is due for this leg today (10.4.2), at the first such watch of the day; it rides (01.4.2) for the rest of the day unless a snag-bearing condition appears that was not on the frame (fog rolls in, night falls, the party is driven off its line by a chase), which makes a new beat due.
narration_may_not_imply: that a road-follower might be lost
that a trackless traveler cannot be
cards.worst_case: a needed beat skipped -> the party cannot become lost that day (one day's chance, errs lenient, class i); a needless one -> a roll the player sees at a road's Easy tier (class ii)
examples: inside: crossing the Fenmoor from the causeway to the drowned chapel (trackless). inside: the drovers' track in fog (track + fog). outside: the Salt Road at night with a lantern (road). outside: a deer track the party has already followed in daylight today (it rode). non-example: "we follow the stream, so we can't get lost" on a trackless leg -> the stream is a landmark that makes the crude fallback usable (10.4.4); the beat is still due.

cards.title: The way-finding beat
cards.trigger: journey.wayfinding_due (10.4.1), or the player asks "where are we?" while lost
cards.license_check: lic.training.wilds_navigation (G2; scope "keep a course without road or landmark, by stars or underground"; grade caps trained Hard, expert Very hard, master Legendary). Without it: G3, redirected to the license's crude_fallback (verb.observe, "follow a road, a river or a visible landmark", dc_shift +5, reach capped Limited) when 10.4.4 finds a usable landmark; else 10.4.5's paths.
decisions: 1. TIER [J:rung], only when the area holds no stored nav_tier (data and generated areas hold one; T-10-12 gives the default by terrain): EASY - open country with long sightlines: grassland, farmland, hills, moor; managed woodland with paths. typical: the downs. boundary: downs under low cloud (still easy: weather is a snag, never a tier). MODERATE - country that hides the sky or bends the line: deepwood, marsh, badlands, tundra, coast cliffs. typical: an old wood with clearings. boundary: the trackless Tangle (hard). HARD - country that misleads: swamp, jungle, desert dunes, snowfield, mountains off the passes, ancient deepwood, caves with light. typical: the mire. boundary: a desert with a known well-line (hard) / open sand (v. hard). VERY HARD - featureless or folding country: glacier, open sand sea, open sea out of sight of land under cloud, deep warrens, fey-touched woods. Uncertain between two -> the harder (the tier word is shown in the OFFER).

2. LEVERS and SNAGS [J:flag each], citing facts (00.3.9; at most two of each): Precision levers - a map of this area (an item with the fact maps: <area>); the area mapped by the PC (fact area.mapped_by_pc); slow pace (journey fact); stars visible at night (weather clear or fair); a guide's Help (01.14.8). Precision snags (engine-cited) - night without stars; fog, storm, snow or blizzard (weather.today); fast pace.
cards.computation: verb.observe; attribute Wits (Intellect when the method is reading a map or the stars); primary tag deed.wilds.navigation.wayfinding (underways underground; stars by stars); DC = the area's stored nav_tier (+5 for the crude fallback); SECRET frame (01.4.7): the character cannot know whether the line is true; threatened cost cost.time (the detour), alternate cost.drain (supply spent on the long way). Reach Standard (Limited for the fallback). Delivered reach -> 0: OFF COURSE (10.4.6: the veer, sealed); 1: on course, the day's pace one step slower (the long way round); 2: on course; 3: on course, +2 points on each travel watch of this leg today (a better line); 4: as 3, and one undiscovered place in the area is discovered (with this frame's id, 10.1.5). Take the time (01.4.4) is allowed at Easy, Moderate and Hard: no roll, reach Standard, and each travel watch of the day earns half its points.
cards.stakes: RISKY; DIRE only when the area's standing hazards include one of S3+ that a wrong line walks into (a crevasse field, a sucking bog), cited as the source
narration_may_not_imply: that the character knows the line is wrong
a landmark not in state
cards.worst_case: TIER one rung off: DC 5 off; the tier word is shown even though the odds are not (class i). A wrongly allowed lever: +2 (class i).
examples: inside: Wren (no license) crossing the Fenmoor (moderate) toward the drowned chapel, whose tower stands clear on a fair day -> fallback usable: Observe +3 vs 20, Limited. boundary: the same in fog -> the tower is not visible: 10.4.5. inside: a trained navigator (+4) on the downs (easy, 10) with the PC's own map (Precision +2) -> +6 vs 10: off course 5%, a better line 35%. non-example: "I've got a good sense of direction" -> an assertion, not a lever.
basis: R5 EX-02, P-31 (lead the way), P-33 (Map the Area)
