   names them or what they hold, their kin, master, secret or standing, or a recorded refusal or want of theirs), or
   the practice is fight and they are within its reach [revision: R2-H; DL-12-93]. Every other present NPC does
   nothing new and says nothing: no reaction line, no interjection, whichever way they face. An NPC who responds
   takes the first that applies: (a) a resolved frame's delivered outcome; (b) a
   recorded refusal or want that matches the event (12.2.9 (b)), matched by **tags** [revision: R2-G; DL-12-87;
   I-176]: code tags the event from the beat's verb, facets, target, topic, terms and pressure mark, and from the
   request's one `asks` tag (the Framer's `[J:enum]` on a Talk request), all from the closed list
   `social.yaml#event_tags`; each refusal kind and want object carries its tags there. A matching refusal is spoken
   (step 4); a want the event serves (`offers_payment`, `offers_help`) takes row 9 for a request, else row 8; a want it
   defeats (`harms`, `threatens`, `against_kin`, `asks_against_master`) takes row 2, row 1 at Hostile; a want it only
   engages takes row 6. The World call runs only as the fallback, when no tag matches and the event is ambiguous (two
   or more motives with opposite rows); (c) `tbl.npc_action` by standing (12.11.5), where a rolled row the practice
   does not allow moves to the nearest row it does (toward row 5 on a tie). **For a question or plain speech the source
   gives willingness only** (12.10.8; PR-12-10 step 2) [revision: R2-H; DL-12-90]: the rows' talk wordings ("asks the
   PC something", "wants something first", "misdirects") no longer script what is said; rows 1–3 read `unwilling`, 4–6
   `guarded`, 7–10 `willing`. For an act asked of them, or an event that concerns them, the row is the deed. The
   response writes the NPC's manner by T-12-18's response rows, and their activity only when the body does something
   else (squares up, turns away, takes cover); talk alone never changes the activity (a practice row replaces the
   generic row whole; an empty entry keeps the activity) [revision: R2-F].
4. **An addressed NPC always answers.** An NPC the PC addressed this turn responds in words, never with silence:
   within the willingness code gave, in words the narrator chooses from the speaker card (12.10.8), or, when the
   source refuses (a recorded refusal, a failed frame, an `unwilling` row), with a **refusal spoken in their own
   voice**: the reason (their recorded refusal, else the row) said through their voice register and habit (12.11.3),
   never a stock formula. A walk-on who answers for the first time has their voice rolled then (12.11.1's tables). A
   deed still needs its source [I-140].
5. **Acceptance is code.** Whether an NPC agrees to what the PC asks is decided by the source in step 3 (a frame's
   outcome, a refusal honored by 12.11.4, a want the request serves, the row), never by the narrator.
6. **Standing changes tone and willingness, never truth.** Standing (12.11.6) moves the row (12.11.5) and colours the
   words. It never changes what is true or what the NPC knows (12.10.6); whether they lie is 15.6.2's alone.

An addressed NPC's answer and each response deed are must-name record lines (12.14.12, 12.3.1a); an activity, a manner
and a non-addressed NPC's reaction are optional material [revision: R2-H; DL-12-92]. LLM-voiced characters drift
toward engagement and agreement; willingness and deeds decided before the prose are the remedy (12.11.4), and the
words stay the character's. *Evidence:* ROUND3-ANALYSIS S2: idle activity lines every turn in all four runs, officers
beating rugs in a hall, and NPCs interjecting with their backs turned.

cards.title: The ruling ledger in use
cards.body: ### 12.12 The ruling ledger in use

cards.title: When the DM consults precedent
cards.body:
**12.12.1 When the DM consults precedent.** `[D]` [DL-12-19; C:III; R5 DM-05; revision: I-065] `find_rulings(anchor_id, deltas, tags)` is called
(INV-19; 01.5.2) before: any anchor adaptation with deltas; any Oracle question (the DM's or the
player's) — so the same kind of question in the same kind of place gets the same odds; any Good Idea; any
G3 or G4 decision; and, added here, any **scene-logic answer** (Certain or Impossible by scene type) to a
player's G0 question, because "a smithy has a quench trough" is a ruling the next smithy should share.

cards.title: Reuse and departure
cards.worst_case: a reuse where a fact differed — the player can cite the fact and a new ruling supersedes (class iv).
cards.body:
**12.12.2 Reuse and departure.** `[D]` + `[J:flag]` [DL-12-19; C:III; R5 DM-05; revision: I-065] A matching precedent's numbers are reused (01.5.2). The DM
departs only when an established fact present now and absent then (or the reverse) changes the tier, the
stakes, the reach, or the odds rung, and it names that fact's id in `precedent.differing_fact`. "This time
feels different" is not a fact. A difference that is a lever or snag is applied as a lever or snag on the
reused frame, not as a departure (WE-00-9). *Worst case (J):* a reuse where a fact differed — the player can
cite the fact and a new ruling supersedes (class iv).

cards.title: Two precedents disagree
cards.body:
**12.12.3 Two precedents disagree.** `[D]` [DL-12-19; R5 DM-05; revision: I-065] The later record wins (00.1.4: latest write), unless the later one
departed citing a fact that is absent now — then the earlier one applies. Either way the conflict is
logged with `review_flag: true`.

cards.title: Review flags and Principle III's revisit trigger
cards.body:
**12.12.4 Review flags and Principle III's revisit trigger.** `[D]` `review_flag` is set by 01.5.4's
conditions and also on: every correction (12.3.4); every turn that needed a rendered line, the plain fallback included (12.3.3) [revision: R2-B]; every upheld dispute
(12.3.6); every breach of 12.1.3 detected by a sweep; two seasons in a row outside 12.7.7's sessions-per-season
band (`pacing.yaml#world_time.review`) [revision: I-085]. At `session_end`, `h.12.session_close` compiles the
session's flagged records into the **review list**. When **three or more** flagged records in which the
DM's own judgment was overturned (a correction, an upheld dispute, or a ruling-error correction) share an
error class — the same anchor id, the same claim class, or the same 12.1.3 breach — across **two or more
sessions** (`pacing.yaml#review.iii_candidate`), the class is reported as a **Principle III candidate**:
the "recorded, concrete failure case" the constitution requires before an exception-gating mechanism may
be considered [C:III]. The report is evidence for the project's maintainers; it changes nothing in play.
The review list also carries the session's new **promotion candidates** (00.16.3's test, read from the ruling
ledger): the campaign's own entries are promoted at once; shipped entries are reported [revision: I-043].

cards.title: The player may see the ledger
cards.body:
**12.12.5 The player may see the ledger.** `[D]` Rulings are `available` (00.6.3). "How was this ruled
before?" is answered with the matching record in format 12.15.8. Seeing that the same case gets the same
answer is part of what makes rulings legible as the game rather than the DM's whim [R4 §7.3].

cards.title: Precedents that recur become rule proposals
cards.body:
**12.12.6 Precedents that recur become rule proposals.** `[D]` A ruling reused **three or more** times
without departure is listed in the review list as a **rule candidate**: a recurring adaptation that may
deserve to become a written anchor card or sub-rule (entering as `provisional` under VI). The DM keeps
applying the precedent meanwhile [C:VI; R7 §4.8].

cards.title: Improvising from the substrate
cards.body: ### 12.13 Improvising from the substrate

cards.title: Hook first, then primitives
cards.worst_case: a near-but-wrong anchor is picked; the two-change limit bounds the adaptation, and the logged signature lets a later beat depart from it by naming the differing fact (00.15.3, 00.15.6; class iv). [integration: 00.2.3 audit]
cards.body:
**12.13.1 Hook first, then primitives.** `[J:enum]` When a player does something no rule names, the DM
(i) restates the beat neutrally — method, target, intended change (01.2.6); (ii) retrieves anchors for it
(12.13.2); (iii) picks one (01.5.1); (iv) checks precedent (12.12.1); (v) adapts at most two knobs
(01.5.3); (vi) frames and offers. The same order serves improvised *content* (12.13.4): start from what the
thing is for in the fiction, then express it only through existing primitives — Sanderson's "begin from
the hook, then formalize into the grid" [R2 ch.12; C:P3]. *Worst case (J):* a near-but-wrong anchor is picked;
the two-change limit bounds the adaptation, and the logged signature lets a later beat depart from it by
naming the differing fact (00.15.3, 00.15.6; class iv). [integration: 00.2.3 audit]

cards.title: Retrieval from the anchor index
cards.body:
**12.13.2 Retrieval from the anchor index.** `[D]` [DL-12-16; R5 DM-04; revision: I-065] `load_cards(anchors for verb, deed tags, situation)`
queries `data/anchors.yaml` and returns at most **eight** candidates (00.15.3), scored: **+3** per intent
verb matching the beat's restated method or intended change; **+2** when an anchor's deed tag equals the
beat's primary deed tag or is its ancestor; **+1** per matching situation tag; the gated basic verb's own
card (or the G2 license's own rule) is always included regardless of score; ties broken by specificity
(a chapter sub-rule over a license rule over a verb card) then rule id. *Runtime capability:* RC-RETRIEVE,
RC-QUERY.

cards.title: The two-change limit, the third change, and splitting
cards.worst_case: a split that could have been one adapted beat — two rolls instead of one, each shown at OFFER (class ii) [R7 §3.4; 01.5.3].
cards.body:
**12.13.3 The two-change limit, the third change, and splitting.** `[D]` + `[J:enum]` An adapted ruling
moves at most two knobs (00.2.7). When a third change is needed, `[J:enum]`:
- **Re-anchor** — true when another candidate needs two or fewer changes for this beat; use it.
- **Split** — true when the beat holds more than one of: a distinct **method** (swing *and* kick), a
  distinct **target** (the rope *and* the archer), a distinct **intended change** (get across *and* knock
  him down), or a **sequence** (one must happen before the other can). Split into sequential beats
  (01.14.1), each anchored separately; their order is the fiction's order.
- Default when both seem possible: split (each part becomes simpler and is logged on its own).
Knobs are counted by T-00-20's entries, not by the words that change [revision: I-062]: a created feature's
length and its growth are one knob (`duration`), and where it sits is the beat's target, not a knob. *Example inside the
limit:* an improvised fire barrier in a doorway (lamp oil, lit, "nothing follows us"). Retrieval finds
`anc.06_t9_31` ("set the thatch alight": fire S2 and smoke growing one group a round), but that card lists
only `reach_unit`, so it cannot carry a stationary burn: re-anchor to `anc.10_12_9` (a hazard no one
listed; 07.10.2): severity S2 (lamp oil, a campfire's flames) is the default; `duration` (stays put, no
spread, a lamp's worth of oil: three intervals) is one knob, though it changes both length and growth; the
doorway is the beat's target, not a knob. One adapted ruling, no split. *Outside:* the same barrier made to
burn fiercer than lamp oil can (S3, `harm_severity`) **and** to spread along the corridor (`duration`) and
to cost no action (`action_cost`): three knobs, so re-anchor or split.
*Worst case (J):* a split that could have been one adapted beat — two rolls instead of one, each shown at
OFFER (class ii) [R7 §3.4; 01.5.3].

cards.title: Improvised content uses existing primitives only
cards.worst_case: a less apt primitive — its stated numbers apply, inside the substrate's caps (class i/iv).
cards.body:
**12.13.4 Improvised content uses existing primitives only.** `[D]` + `[J:enum]` [DL-12-16; C:V; C:III; R5 DM-04; revision: I-065] A new hazard, an NPC's
unusual ability, a location's strange property, a trap, an improvised item's effect: each is built from
the substrate — effect ids from `data/effects.yaml` with parameters, conditions from `data/conditions.yaml`,
a clock, a license, a hazard or trap entry, a generator output — never as a prose-only mechanic
(00.16.4). The DM picks `[J:enum]` the nearest existing entry and moves at most two parameters (the
two-change limit applied to content). If nothing fits within two changes, the DM uses the nearest entry
unchanged, logs a `rule_conflict` ruling with `review_flag`, and the review list carries an extension
proposal (PR-00-8). **Tier** [revision: R2-D] [DL-12-64]: what the DM improvises in play is T1 at most (12.14.13), and
only by a procedure: a seed or region table, the default NPC layer (12.11.9), or the settlement of testimony (PR-12-12) [revision: R2-H]. A T2
element (a hazard, a trap, an adversary, a valuable item, a person with a want, a clue) is never improvised: it comes
from its generator (ch.10's tables, 12.11.1, 00.11, PR-15-6), and this rule then builds it from primitives.
*Worst case (J):* a less apt primitive — its stated numbers apply, inside the
substrate's caps (class i/iv).

cards.title: Every improvisation is logged
cards.body:
**12.13.5 Every improvisation is logged.** `[D]` [DL-12-19; R5 DM-05; revision: I-065] A beat or content improvisation writes a `RulingRecord`
(00.15.5) with its signature, cited facts and result; the ledger is what makes the next identical case
come out the same (12.12).

cards.title: The anchor index: compilation spec for data/anchors.yaml
cards.body:
**12.13.6 The anchor index: compilation spec for `data/anchors.yaml`.** `[D]` [DL-12-16; DL-12-26; revision: I-065] Ch.12 compiles the index
from every chapter's anchor cards; no chapter edits it by hand.
1. **Sources**: (a) the `anchor:` fields of `data/basic_verbs.yaml` (the fifteen verb cards, 01.18); (b)
   every rule in chapters 01–16 whose template says `Anchor: yes` (00.2.6), from the chapter's rule card
   (00.15.2 `anchor` block); (c) data entries that declare an `anchor` block (a hazard, an activity, a
   ritual) in their own files.
2. **Entry** (SCHEMAS `anchors.yaml` plus the common envelope): `id` (`anc.` + the rule id with dots as
   underscores, e.g. `anc.01_18_4`; the `anc.` prefix is 00.16.2's [editor: E2-038]), `name`, `rule_id`,
   `source` (file and key), `intent_verbs`, `deed_tags`, `situation_tags`, `knobs` (from T-00-20 only, each
   with `default` and `allowed_deltas`), `degree_table` (a reference, never a copy), `specificity`
   (`verb_card` | `license_rule` | `chapter_rule`), `tags`, `lifecycle` (the source's), `basis`.
3. **Validation** (the compile fails on any): the rule id exists; every knob is in T-00-20; at least one
   intent verb; every deed and situation tag exists in `data/tags.yaml` (or is listed as pending in an
   Interface request); the degree table reference resolves; no two entries share an id.
4. **Derived fields**: `deed_tags` and `situation_tags` for verb cards are taken from the compile map in
   `anchors.yaml#compile.verb_tag_map` (the deed branches and situations where each verb is the usual
   method); a chapter rule's are taken from its card's `deed_tags` and `loads_in`.
5. **Recompile** whenever any source changes; the index is versioned (`schema_version`, `compiled_from`
   with each source file's revision) so old ruling records still resolve their `rule_id`.
6. **Lifecycle**: an anchor whose source is retired is kept with `lifecycle: retired` and `superseded_by`
   (00.16.3); retrieval skips retired entries.
The shipped index is compiled by `_process/simulation/12-compile_anchors.py` from the fifteen verb cards,
every chapter rule its template marks as an anchor (00.2.6), ch.06's T-06-9 ready rulings and ch.07's shape anchors (counts under
`anchors.yaml#compile.counts`) [editor: E2-039].

cards.title: The narration standard
cards.body: ### 12.14 The narration standard

cards.title: Voice and point of view
cards.body:
**12.14.1 Voice and point of view.** `[N]` [DL-12-17; C:IV; R5 DM-06; revision: I-065] Narration is **second person, present tense**, addressed to the
character ("You step onto the landing"), limited to what the character perceives and knows (12.10.1).
The player is addressed only in OOF blocks (12.15). Classic-fantasy register: concrete nouns, physical
detail, no modern idiom, no meta-commentary ("in this scene", "your turn") inside the fiction.

cards.title: No unestablished details
cards.worst_case: an addressable detail treated as atmosphere — caught by the claim check as `new_element`, and written or cut (class iv). *Example inside:* "A coil of rope hangs by the door" → addressable (it could be taken, used as a lever) → `create_entity(obj.rope_…)`. *Outside:* "Rain needles the river" → atmosphere, unless the scene's weather is not yet written (then the weather is state, ch.10, and is read, not invented). *Non-example:* "The guard — a big man — blocks the stair": "man" is identity; if the guard's gender is not in the store, the walk-on roll comes first (12.11.1).
cards.body:
**12.14.2 No unestablished details.** `[J:flag]` + `[D]` [DL-12-05; DL-12-03; R5 DM-06; revision: I-065; revision: R2-G] Every detail in narration is either **established**
(in the store, or written this turn by a legitimate source) or **generic atmosphere** — not addressable,
not citable later (the smell of rain, the color of the dusk sky, the general murmur of a market). The test
for each concrete detail: *"Could the player cite this later as a fact — a lever, an obstacle, a target, a
clue, a person, a thing to take?"* (00.6.6). True → it must be in the store before the narration is
delivered (write-on-mention), with only the properties the narration implies; properties it needs that are
unsettled go to the Oracle or a table first. The categories where invention slips in most often; each blocks only
as 12.3.1b lists it (counts, harm states, what an item does, a relevant possession, an unknown name in the
narrator's voice), and the rest is written by its tier or logged [revision: R2-G; DL-12-80]:
- **identity** — names, gender and pronouns, ages, kinship ("her brother"), titles, professions, species
  (the probe's unearned pronoun, constitution P13);
- **counts** — of coins, arrows, guards, doors, days;
- **states** — locked, lit, broken, poisoned, asleep, alone;
- **properties of things** — what an item does, what a material resists, what a creature fears (the
  probe's invented cold vulnerability, BRIEF §7; SG-15);
- **motives and knowledge** — why an NPC does something, what they know (12.10.6); what an NPC *says* is
  testimony, never checked (12.3.1b) [revision: R2-G].
A detail of an addressable element stated in delivered narration is **established** (00.6.6a): it is stored in
its slot and binds later turns. Atmosphere is not [revision: R2-E; DL-12-70].
*Worst case (J):* an addressable detail treated as atmosphere — caught by the claim check as
`new_element`, and written or cut (class iv). *Example inside:* "A coil of rope hangs by the door" →
addressable (it could be taken, used as a lever) → `create_entity(obj.rope_…)`. *Outside:* "Rain needles
the river" → atmosphere, unless the scene's weather is not yet written (then the weather is state, ch.10,
and is read, not invented). *Non-example:* "The guard — a big man — blocks the stair": "man" is identity;
if the guard's gender is not in the store, the walk-on roll comes first (12.11.1).

cards.title: The player owns the character
cards.worst_case: one sentence of imposed interiority — cut by the claim check, or disputed and corrected (class iv) [R1 #3 (input fidelity); R4 §7.3 (locus of control)].
cards.body:
**12.14.3 The player owns the character.** `[D]` + `[J:flag]` The narration never gives the PC words,
decisions, feelings, beliefs or actions the player did not state. It may describe: what the PC perceives;
the physical results of resolved outcomes ("your foot slides on the wet stone" — a footing cost's form);
sensations that a resolved effect licenses (a `cond.frightened` instance: "your heart hammers and every
step toward the beast is lead" — describing the condition, while what the PC *does* stays the player's).
`[J:flag]` *"Did the player state this, or does a resolved effect produce it?"* False → cut it (claim
verdict `pc_agency`). Quoted PC speech is only the player's own words, lightly tidied for punctuation,
never extended. *Worst case (J):* one sentence of imposed interiority — cut by the claim check, or disputed
and corrected (class iv) [R1 #3 (input fidelity); R4 §7.3 (locus of control)].

cards.title: No mechanics in the fiction
cards.body:
**12.14.4 No mechanics in the fiction.** `[D]` [DL-12-01; C:P7; R5 DM-06; revision: I-065] No number from the rules (Vitality, Focus, fate, DCs, totals,
degrees, standing values, ticks, bands, tiers, odds) and no rules term (T-00-22) appears in narration or in
any in-world voice. **Physical counts** of things the character can see or count — "your last two arrows",
"three riders" — are fiction, not mechanics, and are allowed when they match the store. Every mechanical
number belongs in an OOF block (12.15). The vocabulary of T-12-10 gives the in-fiction words for the PC's
condition, an adversary's state and an NPC's standing.

cards.title: Recognition without an announcer
cards.body:
**12.14.5 Recognition without an announcer.** `[D]` Growth is voiced by the world, never by an in-world
announcer of mechanics (BRIEF §4; 00.1.7). Forbidden in narration (closed list): "you gain …", "you have
unlocked …", "your skill increases", "level", "experience", "class", "achievement", stat names spoken by
anyone in the world, bracketed or boxed text inside the fiction, any disembodied voice announcing a
change. Recognition is staged through ch.04's vehicles — a mentor's acknowledgement, a title others start
using, an oath sworn, an order that seeks the PC out, a power that wakes in a crisis — and its
accept / decline / defer choice is put to the player in an OOF CHOICE block (12.15.6) [R6 §A.4–A.5;
R2 #14 ("narrate milestones; the codex holds the crunch")].

cards.title: Describing positions in text
cards.body:
**12.14.6 Describing positions in text.** `[D]` + `[N]` [DL-12-17; R5 EX-14; revision: I-065] Text has no map, so position must be said (R5 EX-14):
1. **Scene openings** name what the PC can see that matters for movement and danger: exits, cover,
   elevation, hazards, and anything within reach (each written on mention).
2. **In conflict**, at `conflict_start` and in every narration in which any range band or positional flag
   involving the PC changed (01.12.2 obliges naming every change), each participant's band to the PC is
   stated in the fixed words of T-12-11, and any flag on the PC.
3. **Distances** are given as bands, not feet, unless an established fact states a measure (a 20-ft
   wall).
*Narration may not imply:* a band or flag the store does not hold (claim class `position`).

cards.title: Tells, omens and moods
cards.body:
**12.14.7 Tells, omens and moods.** `[N]` + `[D]` [DL-12-17; DL-11-10; R5 DM-06; revision: I-065]
- **Omens** (INV-14): each tick of a sensed or hidden clock renders, in that turn's narration, the omen
  entry the engine selected — as a perceivable trace the PC could notice (a sound, a sign, a changed
  behavior, a rumor) — in the DM's words, never explained ("a dog barks twice somewhere below", not "the
  alarm is spreading"), never more than one per tick, and never one without a tick.
- **Tells** voice adversaries and NPCs instead of numbers (12.10.7).
- **Tension and intensity** are never named; they may color the world's mood (weather already rolled,
  crowds, the quality of silence) only through elements already in the store.
- **Standing** is voiced as behavior, by rung (T-12-10): Hostile — open enmity, refuses dealings; Unfriendly
  — curt, suspicious, unhelpful; Wary — guarded, measured, gives little; Neutral — businesslike; Warm —
  friendly tone, small courtesies; Friendly — goes out of their way; Devoted — would take risks for the PC.

cards.title: Failure is the world's answer
cards.body:
**12.14.8 Failure is the world's answer.** `[N]` A failure is narrated as the world responding — the guard
turns at the wrong moment, the hasp holds, the current is stronger than it looked — and the chosen cost's
form is named plainly (01.12.2). A success is narrated as the character's doing. Neither is softened nor
sharpened beyond the frame: the degree, the delivered reach and the cost are exactly as resolved (01.7.2)
[R5 P-16; R2 ch.12 ("failure moves the plot forward")].

cards.title: The open prompt
cards.body:
**12.14.9 The open prompt.** `[D]` [DL-12-20; C:P16; revision: I-065] Every DM response that is not a pause point ends by handing the moment
back to the player: a direct question to the character ("What do you do?" or a situation-specific one:
"The ferryman holds out his hand. Do you pay?") or an unresolved image that plainly awaits a response.
Never a numbered list of options; examples only under 12.8.6. Pause points end with their own OOF block
instead (12.15).

cards.title: Length
cards.body:
**12.14.10 Length.** `[D]` Narration word limits (`pacing.yaml#narration`), excluding OOF blocks: a beat's
narration ≤ **200** words; a conflict turn ≤ **150**; a scene opening ≤ **200**; a recap ≤ **120**; a time
skip ≤ **150**. Longer only when the player asks ("describe it in detail"). Short narration is also a
consistency measure: every sentence is a claim to check [R1 12.A (narration quality decays through
repetition); R4 W11].

cards.title: Freshness
cards.worst_case: a repeated phrase — harmless (class i) [R4 W10; R1 12.A (RPGBench's interestingness decay from repetitive narration)].
cards.body:
**12.14.11 Freshness.** `[J:flag]` + `[D]` [DL-12-76; revision: R2-E] The engine keeps the opening clause of the
last three scene openings and, per entity, stored **usage marks**: each established detail (00.6.6a), each part
of an object's written words and each NPC's speech opener carries `last_used`, the turn a delivered sentence
last stated it, read from the declarations (PR-12-1 T12), not by re-scanning prose. The DM does
not reuse an opening pattern from the last three scenes (`[J:flag]` *"Does this opening start the same way
— same time-of-day or weather lead, same sentence shape?"*) and does not restate a detail, an object's written words or a
speech opener for the same entity within ten turns of its `last_used` mark (it reaches for another detail, or
says nothing of the look), except a deliberate callback (an NPC's recorded habit; a recurring omen;
the player's own phrase) or the player's own request (reading the notice again). A scan of the last ten
deliveries for repeated opening clauses and speech openers stays as a cheap backstop. **Said lines** [revision: R2-H; DL-12-90]: an NPC never repeats a line it already said.
Each `said` record (12.3.1b) is a usage mark on its speaker, and a speech span whose content words overlap one of
the speaker's `said` records by more than `narration.freshness.said_overlap` is redrafted (a code scan), unless the
player asked them to say it again. **Setting once** [revision: R2-I; DL-12-99]: a place's stored look, furniture and
exits (12.16.9) reach the narrator on arrival or at scene framing (12.4.3) and are then marked described; on later
turns of the scene they are optional material only (12.14.12), not restated unless the PC looks again or asks.
(ROUND4-ANALYSIS R6: the seeded look line was in every narrator packet, and five turns in one place repeated it.)
*Worst case (J):* a repeated phrase — harmless (class i) [R4 W10; R1 12.A
(RPGBench's interestingness decay from repetitive narration)].

cards.title: What every narration must name: the must-name diet
cards.body:
**12.14.12 What every narration must name: the must-name diet.** `[D]` [DL-12-17; DL-12-01; DL-12-92; R5 DM-06;
revision: I-065; revision: R2-H] (from 01.12.2, restated so this card stands alone)
**Must-name** (closed list): (1) the **outcome of each beat**: its degree and delivered reach, the typed intended
change it applied (01.2.7), and the form of every cost paid; (2) **what changed**: harm, conditions and quantities,
a possession or a coarse position (every visible condition applied; every changed range band or positional flag
involving the PC; one omen per sensed or hidden clock tick), including a change an NPC's response deed made; (3) the
**answer to a direct question**, in the asked character's voice (PR-12-10: the willingness line or the case's
delivery) or in the narrator's (a FICTION_QUESTION, 01.3.8) [revision: R2-B]; (4) a **clue delivered** or a lead
injected; (5) a **pause** (its one block, 12.14.9). Each is an adjudication-record line with a handle; coverage checks
every turn that some sentence cites it (12.3.1a), and 12.3.3 states an uncited one by its rendered line. Missing any
of these is also a claim-check failure of the sweep (12.4.8).
**Optional material** is everything else code supplies: NPCs' activities, postures and manners, detail slots, other
present NPCs' reactions, the crowd's mood, scene texture, and a place's look and furniture after the turn they were first given (12.14.11,
setting once) [revision: R2-I]. The view lists it as material the narrator may use, never as
a line it must cite; no check requires it, and leaving it out is never a coverage failure. A sentence that does use it
is checked like any other (12.3.1b). *Evidence:* ROUND3-ANALYSIS S2: with every code line mandatory, idle activity
lines appeared every turn in all four runs and NPCs spoke out of turn.

cards.title: What narration may create: the content tiers
cards.worst_case: an ordinary-seeming element that turns out useful is written — it is an established fact the player may cite as a lever, worth at most +2, one stakes rung or one reach rung (00.3.9; class i). *Example inside (furniture):* "a coil of rope hangs by the boathouse door" at a ferry landing. *Outside (a clue):* "the ferryman's boots lie by the hut, laces cut" when the ferryman's fate is a sealed thread — cut it. *Non-example:* "a gleaming sword hangs over the hearth" in a poor fisher's hut — an item of value; if the DM wants to know what hangs there, it rolls the region's furnishings or the loot gen
cards.body:
**12.14.13 What narration may create: the content tiers.** `[J:flag]` + `[D]` [DL-12-05; DL-12-40; C:VII; revision: I-065; revision: R2-B]
Who decides that something is true depends on its tier. Each element a sentence introduces is declared with an
`element_kind` from a closed list (`furniture`, `feature`, `person`, `item`, `document`, `knowledge`, `clue`,
`hazard`, `adversary`), and the kind fixes the tier (`pacing.yaml#claim_check.element_tiers`) [I-129]:

| Tier | Contents | `element_kind` | Who decides it is true | Stored | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **T0 Atmosphere** | light, smell, sound, weather words, mood, an unnamed crowd's murmur; fine placement within a place ("by the hearth", "at the window") [revision: R2-F; DL-12-77] | none (the sentence's atmosphere flag) | the narrator, freely | never | only against the hour, season, weather and climate the store holds, and the lines and veils (12.3.1) |
| **T1a Incidental detail** | the things any such place has, with ordinary properties (a rope by a door, benches in a hall, a puddle, a woodpile); an ordinary walk-on (a fishwife at the market, 12.11.1); an item or document of common value; an incidental property of a thing in view (the smith's scarred hands, a notice's lettering) | `furniture`, `feature`, `person`, `item`, `document` | the narrator, **as written**: written on mention with the properties the sentence states (00.6.6) | yes; it binds later turns | later prose must not contradict it; a clash is logged, not blocked (12.3.1b) [revision: R2-G] |
| **T1b Ordinary knowledge** | what someone in a role would know of the world beyond the view: roads, prices, local news, trade facts | `knowledge` | **in speech: testimony** — the character says it freely; a `said` record, settled lazily only when it matters (PR-12-12: the case if consequential, else accepted, or the Oracle at Likely beyond the ordinary) [revision: R2-H; DL-12-40; DL-12-91]; **in the narrator's voice**: settled by the Oracle at 12.10.6(d)'s odds before it is narrated (12.6.1, 01.3.8) | speech: as a `said` record, a fact once settled; narrator's voice: as a fact and a knowledge record, "does not know" too | speech: never checked for truth (12.3.1b); narrator's voice: the sentence must match the settled answer |
| **T1c Scene state** | each present person's activity, posture, hold and manner, and a range band to the PC (T-12-18; 12.11.9) [revision: R2-F] | none: prose never introduces it | **code**, from the resolved beats and the default NPC layer | yes, for the scene; expires at scene end | the sentence must match the record line |
| **T2 Consequential** | a **clue** toward a sealed fact or an open thread; an **item of more than common value** or any property beyond the mundane; a **hazard** or **trap**; an **adversary**; a **person with a want, a secret or knowledge of a thread**; the identity of a story role | `clue`, `hazard`, `adversary`; and a `person`, `item` or `document` the question below finds true | **generators only**: clue graphs and their placements (ch.15/11), the item generator and the region's data (00.11), ch.10 tables, encounter tables, clocks and behavior lists, NPC generation and the clue graph (12.11.1) | at generation, sealed until revealed | in the narrator's voice: in this turn's record, as delivered or unsealed, or the sentence is cut; in speech: testimony, never checked or written (12.3.1b) [revision: R2-G] |

A narrated detail (00.6.6a) is ordinary T1a: it may be cited as a lever under the cap below and never creates value [revision: R2-E].
An **unnamed description** of people or things present ("the refugees", "the other carters", "the queue") is T1a: a
beat may target it, a typed change on it is a scene fact about the description (01.2.7), and the narrator voices
whoever answers for it as an ordinary walk-on. It becomes an individual only when it is consequential (it holds a
clue or a story role); then the case's placement or casting picks the person (15.9.5; 00.11 `cast`), never the
narrator [revision: R2-I; DL-12-97]. Something **ordinary looked for** that is not in the scene (a well, an inn, a
carter for hire) is found and written as established, T1a (01.18.5) [revision: R2-I; DL-12-98].
The narrator assigns the kind (`[J:enum]`, part of 12.3.1's declaration). Whether a `person`, `item` or `document`
is T1a or T2 is one question, `[J:flag]` *"Would this element, as described, help or hinder the PC beyond what any
such place ordinarily offers, or point toward something hidden?"* True → T2: it must come from its owning
procedure or be cut. Uncertain → false: the element is T1a, written and logged, and an **uncertain kind is T1a**
[revision: R2-G; DL-12-80]; only a declared `clue`, `hazard` or `adversary`, or an element the question clearly finds
true, is T2. *Worst case (J):* an ordinary-seeming element that turns out useful is written — it is an
established fact the player may cite as a lever, worth at most +2, one stakes rung or one reach rung
(00.3.9; class i). *Example inside (furniture):* "a coil of rope hangs by the boathouse door" at a ferry
landing. *Outside (a clue):* "the ferryman's boots lie by the hut, laces cut" when the ferryman's fate is a
sealed thread — cut it. *Non-example:* "a gleaming sword hangs over the hearth" in a poor fisher's hut — an
item of value; if the DM wants to know what hangs there, it rolls the region's furnishings or the loot
generator.

cards.title: Out-of-fiction message formats
cards.body:
### 12.15 Out-of-fiction message formats

Every number, odds, choice and rules matter goes in an **OOF block**: a line or short block that begins
with a bracketed label, set apart from the fiction, never written in a character's voice. Ch.14 owns how
blocks are rendered for the player (14.6.5) [editor: E2-040]; these are the contents and the default
text form. Order within one DM response: (1) SAFETY and SESSION acknowledgements; (2) CORRECTION blocks;
(3) the fiction; (4) RESULT blocks in beat order; (5) REDIRECT blocks; (6) one pause block last (OFFER,
NEAR MISS, CHOICE, CLARIFY, FLAG, CUT?) because it awaits the player.

cards.title: General rules
cards.body:
**12.15.1 General rules.** `[D]` [DL-12-18; C:P7; R5 DM-09; revision: I-065] OOF blocks are terse, use ids and canonical names, show only `shown` and
`available` state (never background or sealed values: a hidden clock appears as nothing, a sensed clock
by name only), and never contradict the store. A block's fields appear in the order given below; empty
fields are omitted.

cards.title: OFFER
cards.body:
**12.15.2 OFFER** [DL-12-18; DL-12-51; R5 OB-05; revision: I-065; revision: R2-C] (renders 01.7.1 items 1–7 as a
template over the frame's typed fields; no rule id, DC code, severity code or mode name appears in the player's
text, and the log keeps them all). One line of fiction first ("The press thickens toward the gate; a gap opens
and closes."), then:

```
[OFFER] Slip through the crowd toward the gate.
  Chance: better than even — 55%   (Agility +1, practised +1, packed bodies −2)
  If it works:  you reach the gate.            Very well (5%): and no one marks you.
  If it fails:  you're stuck and jostled — a setback.   Badly (5%): something's lost in the press — serious.
  Close call (15%): get there anyway and be marked, or fail.
  Takes: a minute · noisy
  [Enter] Do it   [b] Go big   [s] Play it safe   [c] Another way   [w] Back off   [?] Explain
  Another way:  shove through (45%) · wait for it to thin (no roll, takes an hour)
```

**Lines, from frame fields [D].** *Title*: the beat restated (01.2.6). *Chance*: the band word, a dash, the
success-or-better percentage, then the modifier in words (attribute, competence by its tag's name, each lever
and snag by its fact's short name; edge and status when not 0). *If it works / Very well*: what the framed
reach delivers on success and on a critical success (01.6.10, in the anchor's reach unit). *If it fails /
Badly*: the threatened cost's form as one clause, with its severity word, on a failure and on a critical
failure (01.6.11, 01.9.2). *Close call*: the near-miss percentage and the alternate cost (01.9.3); omitted when
0 and on a hidden roll. *Takes*: action, time, every method consequence (loud → noisy), whether it rides on
an earlier result, and fate. *Another way*: up to three approaches the engine computes with no model call
(the verb's alternative attributes and sibling anchors whose DC is stored, opposed or the same obstacle class),
each with its chance or "no roll".

**Fixed word maps (the glossary, 14.2.7).**
- Chance: 95 *almost certain* · 75–90 *likely* · 55–70 *better than even* · 45–50 *even* · 25–40 *unlikely* ·
  10–20 *long shot* · 5 *only by luck* · 0 *impossible as framed*. Both the number and the word are shown
  (D6: owner confirmed 2026-10-09; may revisit odds display and menus; DL-12-51) [revision: R2-G].
- Severity: S1 *a nuisance* · S2 *a setback* · S3 *serious* · S4 *grave* · S5 *ruinous*; lethal adds, under If
  it fails, `THIS CAN KILL YOU — <source> (warned <when>)`. A Dire frame's If-it-fails line starts `Danger:`.
- Reach: Limited *partly* · Standard *what you wanted* · Great *more than you asked*.

**The trades, one line each** (01.7.3; I-138): `Go big: if it works you get more; if it fails it costs more;
same chance.` · `Play it safe: if it works you get less; if it fails it costs less; same chance.` A trade not
allowed on this frame (01.7.3) is not printed. When one is taken, a NOTE line says what changed.

**Variants.**
- **Mode** (stretch, emulate, fallback; I-134): one line in words, never the mode name, e.g. `You're improvising
  without training: harder (+5), and at best a partial result.` or `You're stretching what you know: harder
  (+2).`
- **Secret frame** (01.4.7; I-143): the If lines stay; the Chance line reads `Chance: you can't judge how hard
  this is.` and there is no Close call line. The OFFER keeps 01.7.1's promise: odds, or the reason they are
  hidden.
- **Long shot** (01.6.13): `Chance: long shot — 10% (failing badly is likelier: 35%)`, and the Another way
  line lists the best computed alternative first.
- **Only a natural 20**: `Chance: only by luck — 5%, and at best what you wanted`.
- **Bundled** beat: `Rank your questions:` with the deduplicated items.
- **Ability activation**: the Takes line names its prices, `Focus 2 (flared hard) · uses 1 of 2 left`, and,
  when the Focus is short, `overdraw: <its price>` (05.6.6; never automatic); a power used **through a relic**
  adds `Relic: +1 Focus (no training license)` (08.4.4) [revision: I-030].
- **Auto-commit** (01.7.4): the same block, labelled `[OFFER — auto]`, immediately above its RESULT.

**One menu convention for every pause point** (12.2.6: OFFER, clarifying question, redirect, near miss,
ranking, last chance, recognition, generator pick, rewind). **Enter** is the labelled default and is always
printed as `[Enter] <label>`; alternatives take **letters**; `?` explains any word from the glossary (14.2.7),
never a rule card. Enter never withdraws or backs off (P-044). On an OFFER, Enter is `Do it`, except on a
Dire, lethal or long-shot frame, where it is `Show this again` and committing takes the letter `[d] Do it`.
An unanswered pause still persists as 12.2.6 says. *Worst case:* none (template; a word map error shows a
wrong word beside the right number).

cards.title: RESULT
cards.body:
**12.15.3 RESULT.** [DL-12-18; C:P7; revision: I-065]
```
[RESULT] d20 9 → 13 vs 15 · failure (near miss)
```
A beat that needed no roll shows its necessity reason (01.4.1) in place of the die, and whether it can
yield evidence, so the player sees that a free yes earns nothing toward recognition [revision: I-054]:
```
[RESULT] no roll (certain: Neutral, R1) · granted · no evidence
[RESULT] no roll (take the time) · success · evidence as a no-roll success
```
`no evidence` is printed for every `trivial` or riding no-roll beat (03.2.6); the no-roll successes of
03.3.2 D1 (good idea, take the time, certain with cost) print `evidence as a no-roll success`. Either is
followed, after the player's choice or when no choice exists, by the changes to shown state:
```
[RESULT] Changed: Vitality 13 → 10 · bleeding (S1) · arrows 6 → 5 · Focus 4 → 3 · fate 1 → 2
```
A drop is one line of fiction (08.3.13); its `Changed:` entry names the item only, and its rung, known
properties and price are in the codex [revision: I-030]. A secret frame: `[RESULT] hidden check made.` Hidden and sensed clocks never appear; an Oracle answer
never appears (the oracle log is background, 00.6.3); a delivered bundled count appears as `Answered 2
of 4: <items>`.

```
[CHOICE] <what is being chosen> — (a) … · (b) … · (c) …
         If you move on without choosing: <the rule's default>
```
Two CHOICE blocks carry **no default line** and wait for an answer: the last-chance menu (07.5; T-07-7) and the
Bent's offer (02.6.6) [integration: IR ch.07 to 12, IR ch.02].

cards.title: CORRECTION
cards.body:
**12.15.9 CORRECTION** [DL-12-18; DL-12-04; revision: I-065] (12.3.4).
```
[CORRECTION] Earlier I said the purse held twenty coins; it holds 12 (your record is right).
             You spent nothing because of it. Logged.
```
With reliance: `You climbed the wall believing the gate was barred; it was open. Keep that, accept it as it
stands, or rewind to before the climb?` (a CHOICE follows).
The answers to a report (12.3.6, PR-12-11) [revision: R2-G]:
```
[CORRECTION] You're right: Maren's coat was grey (turn 14: "a grey coat, patched at the elbow"). Fixed; it stays.
[CORRECTION] Taken back: the climb (turn 31) is undone and its roll is void. Declare again.
[FIX] As recorded: turn 22, "She turns away without answering." Her name was never given. Logged.
[FIX] That frame stands: 01.6.5, class "barred door" (Moderate, DC 15), no nudge; cited: fact.88. Logged.
[FIX] You're saying the lift succeeded but you never got the purse. Here's why: it succeeded at reach 1, so your
      hand is on the purse but she still has the strings (01.2.7). Another beat takes it.
[FIX] I can't find a turn where Nero answered for the officer. Did you mean turn 14, "'Move along,' Nero says"?
```
Every answer restates the report in plain words and ends in a correction, an explanation or a "did you mean";
never "logged" alone [revision: R2-H; DL-12-94].
