cards.title: Labels added by other chapters
cards.body:
**12.15.15 Labels added by other chapters** [DL-12-18; DL-12-25; revision: I-065] [integration: IR ch.02, 04, 07, 10, 11 to 12]. Each follows
12.15.1 and the order rule above; its contents are its owner's format.

| Label | Owner and format | Where it goes |
|---|---|---|
| `[WARNING]` | 07.3.4 (T-07-7): THIS CAN KILL YOU — source, cause line, exits | before the fiction's pause block; never omitted, never softened |
| `[CONFLICT]` | 06 (06.9.5–06.9.6, 06.11.4): the PC's status line in conflict — each foe's band to the PC and shown descriptors (bloodied, down, visible conditions), the PC's flags, every held windup ("winding up: the maul"), and each side's morale clock by name only when sensed (never a count) | after the RESULT blocks of every conflict turn [revision: I-030] |
| `[STATUS]` | 07.3.7 (T-07-7): STAGGERED or DYING n of 3, with what follows and the odds | when `trg.exits` fires (on becoming Staggered, and on entering Dying) |
| `[RECOGNITION]` | 04.7 (`vehicles.yaml#markers`): one line before a crisis offer's CHOICE block | immediately before the CHOICE |
| `[CREATE n/N]` | 02 (PR-02-7): a creation step's pause block, a CHOICE with a step count | the pause block during creation |
| `[SHEET]` | 02 (PR-02-6): the character summary | on request and at creation's end |
| `[JOURNEY]` | 10.3.4: the journey plan, points, supply against need, way-finding | with the RESULT blocks at a journey's planning and each day |
| `[SEASON]` | 11.11.2: the season herald, one week before the Season Turn | after the fiction |
| `[RETIRE]` | 11.13.1: the retirement offer listing the endings available (04.7's protocol: accept, decline, defer) | as the pause block |
| `[SEED n/14]` | 12.16.3: a world-seed step's summary (what was answered or rolled, and what it wrote, sealed parts withheld) | the pause block during session zero [revision: I-028] |

cards.title: The world seed: starting from nothing
cards.body:
### 12.16 The world seed: starting from nothing

The rules generate places, people, factions and sites on demand, but a game also needs the handful of things
a setting supplies before the first scene: what is impossible, how magic and faith work, who lives here and
what they speak, a safe place to start from, powers already in motion, and somewhere dangerous to go. The
**world seed** writes those, from session-zero questions and oracle tables, so the game runs with no pre-made
setting. Chapter 13's Thallen Vale is one optional pre-made seed; nothing in the rules depends on it
[revision: I-028] [R5 P-22..P-36 (solo sandbox generation: Ironsworn's truths, Starforged's sector
creation, the Alexandrian's hexcrawl and West Marches); R: https://www.ironswornrpg.com/ (setting truths);
R6 B-12, B-20; DL-12-21].

cards.title: What a seed is and when it is made
cards.body:
**12.16.1 What a seed is and when it is made.** `[D]` [DL-12-21; DL-12-22; DL-12-23; DL-12-24; revision: I-065] A **world seed** is a region record of the shape of
`region_*.yaml` (SCHEMAS.md#region_yaml): the region, its canon, keepers, peoples, tongues, names, places,
cast, factions, clocks, situations, encounter and rumor tables, calendar, opening and pregens. It is made
once, at session zero (12.5.1), after chapter 14's preferences and before character creation (chapter 02
reads its peoples, tongues, keepers, names, org-tie map and bond placement), by PR-12-9 from
`data/world_seed.yaml`. Every entity it writes is `lifecycle: provisional` (00.16.3) and from then on is
established canon: state, never narration. A campaign that loads a pre-made seed instead (chapter 13's
`region_thallen.yaml`, or any region file) runs only the seed check (12.16.17) on it. *Reads:*
`world_seed.yaml`, and through it `archetypes.yaml`, `origins.yaml`, `factions.yaml`, `world_turn.yaml`,
`sites.yaml`, `travel.yaml`, `oracles.yaml`, `companions.yaml`, `rituals.yaml`, `licenses.yaml`,
`calendar.yaml`, `weather.yaml`. *Writes:* the region record (`create_entity`, `set_fact`, `set_clock`).

cards.title: Who answers a question
cards.trigger: the player answers a seed question in their own words, not by an option
cards.worst_case: a neighbouring option (a "feared" magic law where "licensed" was meant): one fact one rung off, shown to the player in the step's summary before the next step, and changed at their word (class i: corrected the same turn).
basis: R4 §3.2 S1: closed-set classification is the AI's reliable form
cards.body:
**12.16.2 Who answers a question.** `[D]` + `[J:enum]` Each of the seed's questions (T-12-15) has a closed
list of options and an oracle roll. In **guided** mode the player answers every question; in **oracle** mode
the engine rolls every one and the player may veto one answer per step, which is rolled again once; in
**mixed** mode (the default) the player answers the ones they care about and the engine rolls the rest.
The DM's only judgment is classifying a player's answer that is not one of the listed options:

```
### 12.16.2  Classify a custom seed answer                         [J:enum] [D]
Trigger [T]:        the player answers a seed question in their own words, not by an option
Decision [J:enum]:  which listed option of that question the answer is nearest to; "none fits"
                    is not an option. True only for the option whose listed effects (what the
                    step writes from it) the player's words state or plainly imply.
Effect [D]:         the step writes that option's effects; the player's own words are kept as
                    the entity's description (`desc`, a keeper's `what`, the region's `pitch`),
                    never as a mechanic.
Worst case (J):     a neighbouring option (a "feared" magic law where "licensed" was meant):
                    one fact one rung off, shown to the player in the step's summary before the
                    next step, and changed at their word (class i: corrected the same turn).
Anchor:             no (session zero only)
Basis:              [12.16.1] [R4 §3.2 S1: closed-set classification is the AI's reliable form]
```

The player may also supply content the tables would roll — a keeper's name, a faction, a town — which is
written as given and then completed by the step's rules (a supplied faction still takes a template, a tier,
a goal clock and sealed linchpins, PR-11-8).

cards.title: The steps
cards.body:
**12.16.3 The steps.** `[D]` [DL-12-21; DL-12-22; revision: I-065] PR-12-9 runs fourteen steps in order (T-12-15); each step reads only what
earlier steps wrote, so a step re-run (a veto) re-runs every later step that read it. A step's summary is
shown to the player out of fiction (12.15.1 `[SEED n/14]`) before the next step, except what is sealed
(faction goals, linchpin fates, rumor truths, site objectives, secrets): the player sees what a character
raised there would know.

cards.title: Premise: what went wrong here
cards.body:
**12.16.4 Premise: what went wrong here.** `[D]` [DL-12-33; DL-12-22; DL-12-21; revision: I-065] One wound (`tbl.12.seed.wound`, d12: a fallen realm, a
plague, an invasion, a curse, a sundering, a silent keeper, a long winter, the restless dead, a frontier, a
schism, a tyrant, an awakening) and a climate (one of 10.11.2's five). The wound writes the region's
`pitch` and three `truths` (Ironsworn's "truths") and fixes the **age of the wound**: one roll in its row's
`era_years` (a fallen realm 40–60 years; a plague or an invasion 20–30; a schism 15–25; a silent keeper or a long
winter 8–15; a frontier 5–12; a waking 2–5; any other wound 11–30). That number is the opening year of the era
(12.16.15), and the pitch says it in words ("twenty-three winters ago"), so the premise and the calendar are one
fact [revision: I-069]. The wound is read by later steps: the creature tags its
encounter pools weight × 3 (12.16.13), the situation template of its trouble and the org kind, goal and
temperament of the faction behind it (12.16.10, 12.16.12), the site themes it favours, the keeper forms it
favours, and the calendar's era. The region's name is drawn from `tbl.12.seed.place_names`.

cards.title: Canon: what is impossible, and how magic works
cards.body:
**12.16.5 Canon: what is impossible, and how magic works.** `[D]` [DL-12-22; DL-12-24; DL-12-21; revision: I-065] The seed writes `canon_impossible` and
`canon` (read by 01.3.7's G4 test 2, 05.7.10 and every chapter that defers to canon):
1. **Impossible for anyone** (`canon`'s `impossible` list, ids `ci.*`): always 05.7.10 item 1's five (true
   resurrection, time travel, making a soul, reading an absent mind, destroying a keeper) and 08's
   transmutation; plus none, one or two from `tbl.12.seed.extra_impossible`.
2. **Facts the Oracle treats as settled** (`canon`'s `facts`): the wound; how common magic is (rare,
   uncommon, common); whether open magic is lawful, licensed or feared where the game begins (05.7.10 item
   6; a visible working where it is not lawful is a method consequence, 01.11.2); who answers at the door
   of death (07.5.5; 12.16.6); whether any rite regrows a limb (07.7.6; default no); who may learn arcane
   magic (05.7.10 item 2).
3. **Magic** (`canon`'s `magic`, 05.7.10 items 1–8 in order): the impossibilities; the three sources; the
   keepers; the places of power (every place the seed gives `resonance`, `consecrated` or `desecrated`);
   spirit frequency for the Oracle's odds; lawfulness; components (`stock.components`, 08) and where texts
   and teachers are (`places[].settlement`); a closed school, if the player or the d12 names one.
4. Whether relics count as magic to those who refuse it (15's `magic` refusal), and whether chapter 04's
   four empty hybrid pairs stay empty (they do; a seed never authors a hybrid, 04.4's audit does).

cards.title: Faith: the keepers
cards.body:
**12.16.6 Faith: the keepers.** `[D]` [DL-12-22; DL-05-35; DL-12-21; revision: I-065] Two to four keepers (05.7.4), each from a form of
`tbl.12.seed.keeper_form` (d12, the wound's favoured forms weighted × 3, no form twice): its kind, its
**nature** (`sacred`, or `profane` for a pact-power; what Rebuke and every "sacred or profane keeper" effect
reads, 05.7.4) [revision: I-052], what it keeps, three divine schools (the only schools its priests and
acolytes can hold, 05.7.4), the conduct axes it cares for and despises (04.9.2), its sign, and its faith's
org kind; its name from the name tables and a title. The first keeper whose nature is not profane is the
**main keeper**: its faith is a full faction seated in the haven (12.16.10); every other keeper's faith is a
petty faction (11.3.16). Who bargains at the door of death (07.5.5) is answered here: the keeper of death and
crossing if there is one, a fey lord (`arch.fey_noble`), a tempter (`arch.tempter`), or no one.

cards.title: Peoples and tongues
cards.body:
**12.16.7 Peoples and tongues.** `[D]` [DL-12-22; DL-12-21; revision: I-065] Each of chapter 02's eight peoples is `common`, `uncommon`, `rare` or
`absent` (`tbl.12.seed.presence`, d6 each; a people the wound's creature gates name moves one step more
present). Humans are at least uncommon and at least one non-human people is present. Each present people
gets a name table (d20 given names, d12 family names or epithets, built from `tbl.12.seed.names` without
repeats; a common human people gets two styles, the land's folk and incomers), which replaces
`tbl.name_given` / `tbl.name_family` for that people (12.11.1); the people behind the wound's threat gets one
too, as outsiders. Tongues: the Common tongue, renamed for the region; each present people's native tongue;
the Cant; and a **second tongue** (02.2.2's creation default): the native tongue of the most present
non-human people, or the Old Tongue as the speech of what went before. Absent peoples are listed
(`absent_origins`); C2 (PR-02-1) offers only present ones.

cards.title: The land: rings, areas and routes
cards.body:
**12.16.8 The land: rings, areas and routes.** `[D]` [DL-12-35; DL-12-32; DL-12-21; R5 LW-06; revision: I-065] The region is laid out as T-10-2's rings (10.2.4):
ring 0 the haven; rings 1–5 with three, three, three, two and two **areas** (10.1.1), each with a terrain
(ring 1 from the climate's farm country; rings 2–5 from `tbl.12.seed.terrain_by_climate`, d12), a home band
in its ring's range (T-10-2: 1 · 1–2 · 2–3 · 3–4 · 4–5; if both ring-5 areas would roll 4, the second is 5, so
every region has a home-5 table and lair for a party at band 5 [revision: I-084]) and a danger rating (settled · wild · wild or perilous
· perilous · deadly), a name (`tbl.12.seed.place_names`) and every 10.1.2 field (nav tier and openness from
`travel.yaml#terrain_defaults`, 10.1.8). Routes (10.1.3): the haven to every ring-1 area by road (1–2
watches); each area to the next in its ring (2–3 watches) and to one area of the ring inside it (3–4 watches);
roads and tracks in rings 1–2, trackless beyond. Rings 1–3 are `known`; rings 4–5 are rumor.

cards.title: The haven
cards.body:
**12.16.9 The haven.** `[D]` [DL-12-22; DL-12-21; revision: I-065] One settlement in ring 0 (10.2.3: `safe: true`, `rest_site: haven`), a village
or a town, standing where `tbl.12.seed.haven_site` says (a ford, a bridge, a harbour, an old fort…), with its
buildings (a temple or shrine of the main keeper, consecrated and with `resonance`; an inn; a smithy; the
rulers' hall; its gate; in a town a market and a healer) and a graveyard tended by the main keeper's faith.
Its settlement record: tier (15, 16.3.2); market (common and scarce goods by terrain, 08.8.4; depth 30 or
150); crafters by tier (08.6); teachers drawn from the cast (12.16.11); texts; the rites the keepers' and the
place of acceptance's schools know (05.8); hire roles and the band limit (16.3.2); sentry post floors (15).
A **place of acceptance** for primal workers (02.5.5; `tbl.12.seed.acceptance`) is written as a landmark in
ring 1 or 2 with a spirit, three primal schools, what it asks, and a contact. The haven's fight locations
(06.3.8) come from its site; the region's rare metal and rite components from `world_seed.yaml#defaults`.
**Seed packs for places** [revision: R2-D] [DL-12-61; I-130]: every place (the region record aside) gets a one-line
**look** (`tbl.12.seed.place_look`, by place type), **2–4 furniture items** (`tbl.12.seed.furniture`; a haven building
of a region with its own `tbl.<region>.furnishings` takes its last item from it) and its **exits** (its routes; for a
building, its settlement and two neighbours). They are rolled after step 13, each on a stream keyed by the seed and the
place's id, so a pack never moves another draw of the seed. The look is atmosphere and incidental detail (T0/T1a,
12.14.13); each furniture item is T1a furniture, a lever worth at most +2.

cards.title: Factions with running clocks
cards.body:
**12.16.10 Factions with running clocks.** `[D]` [DL-12-34; DL-11-05; DL-12-21; R5 LW-01; revision: I-065] At least three full factions (11.3.2), each by PR-11-8 from
its template (11.3.18): the haven's **rulers** (`tbl.12.seed.rulers` by haven tier; tier 2 in a town, 1 in a
village); the **main keeper's faith** (the same tier); the **threat** behind the wound (its org kind, goal and
temperament from the wound; tier 2 or 3; seated at a ring-3 site, 12.16.12); and a **fourth** from
`tbl.11.faction_seed` (any kind not already present; tier by `tbl.11.faction_tier`), plus the minor keepers'
faiths as petty factions (tier 0; their goal a `factions.yaml#petty_goals` kind, local, on its 6-segment clock,
by PR-11-8's petty branch, so the World Turn's petty d6 runs them as written, 11.3.16) [revision: I-070]. Each
goal clock is **running**: it starts with d(segments ÷ 3) ticks filled, so the
world is already moving when the PC arrives; each linchpin's four fates are written and sealed (11.3.10).
Relations: the threat stands at −2 to the rulers and the faith, −1 or 0 to the rest; other pairs d6 (1: −1,
6: +1, else 0). The seed also writes the **org-tie map** chapter 02's faction ties read (02.9.5: every org
kind the origins name maps to the faction of that kind, else to one of its branch that is not the threat,
else to `none`), the **institutions** by deed branch (11.8.1; V3, V9), and the region's **values** (the
rulers', 11.7.6). Faction names come from `tbl.12.seed.faction_names`.

cards.title: The cast
cards.body:
**12.16.11 The cast.** `[D]` [DL-12-29; DL-12-32; DL-12-13; DL-12-21; revision: I-065] By 12.11.1 (role, gender, age, detail, demeanor, want, fear, refusal, secret,
voice; the name from the seed's tables; the people weighted by presence, common 6 · uncommon 3 · rare 1,
the threat's people for the threat's members): each faction's head (its linchpin) and, for a full faction,
an officer, each with one of the faction's duties; and the haven's smith, innkeeper, gate captain, healer
(or herb-wife), the place of acceptance's wise one, a sellsword, and in a town a scribe; a hedge-mage where
magic is common enough to be taught there (`ws.q.magic_level`). The captain and the sellsword can be
recruited (16.3.4). **Teachers** (15.13; `downtime.yaml#teacher_odds`) are the cast's trades: the main
keeper's priest its three schools; the captain polearm and shield; the smith smithing; the healer foraging;
the wise one the place's primal schools; the scribe letters and history; the hedge-mage two arcane schools.
**Competence and licenses** [revision: I-059]: every cast NPC is written with `competence` (each role tag at
its band's `c_b`, T-09-2: band 1 +1 … band 5 +5; `world_seed.yaml#defaults.npc_competence`) and `licenses`
(each level-2 role tag's domain training license at `trained`; a divine one only in a school of a keeper
whose faith the NPC belongs to, 05.7.4). A teacher's record holds what it teaches: the target license at
`expert`, a tongue or letters held (15.11.1's MENTOR test), so "can the healer teach foraging?" is read
from the record, never guessed. The seed check (12.16.17) fails a teacher whose record does not hold its
target.
**The powers of the far rings** [revision: I-083]: one principal NPC in each ring-4 area at **band 4** and in each
ring-5 area at **band 5** (`tbl.12.seed.powers`, d8, a used row stepping down; the people by presence), at
its area, with no faction (until an outgrown faction wins a band-5 one to its cause as its patron, 11.3.3: the
seed's threat, tier 2 or 3, fields a champion of band 3 or 4 at most, so this is how the campaign's wound keeps
pace with a band-5 party [revision: I-084]). Each **keeps a truth** (`keeps`, sealed: the keeper of a lore contest, 15.9.20)
and holds a position a social contest can move (its want and refusal, 15.3.11). These are the band-4 and
band-5 opposition that tiers 4 and 5 of a social or lore calling need (04.3.4: six great deeds at band ≥ 4,
four at band 5, at most two from one opposition): without them a seeded region's parties top out at band 4
(a tier-3 threat's head) and its factions at tier 3, and an envoy or scholar never reaches tier 5
(`04-recog-parity.py`, I-083 section: never in 90 sessions; with them 49, beside the archer's 52). They are
"the old lands: only the strong travel here" of T-10-2, so a P1 who walks to one meets band `power_band` + 2
at most (03.4.3).
**Bond placement** (02.9.2): where each of the eight bond kinds is placed — anchors in the haven, a rival in
the fourth faction, a creditor in the market, an enemy in the threat's seat, a lost one at a ring-2 site —
always as a new NPC when the bond is filled (02.9.8), never one already in the cast.
**Knowledge packs and stances** [revision: R2-D] [DL-12-61; I-130]: every cast NPC gets 2–4 knowledge facts
(`tbl.12.seed.knowledge_pack`), each a knowledge record (`how: seed`) with its topic: one of their trade (a topic of
their role, `social.yaml#common_knowledge.by_role`), one local or public (news or folk), one tie to another cast
member (both hold it), and on a d6 of 4–6 a rumor of 12.16.14 they hold (its truth stays sealed). A pack fact is T1
ordinary knowledge: it never names a secret, a clue or a case's solution. Each cast NPC also gets a **stance** toward
the opening incident: helps when they hold a placement of its case, hinders when of the threat faction, else the
table's d6 (helps, wary, indifferent, hinders). The narrator sees the pack's ordinary facts on the asked NPC's speaker card (PR-12-10 step 3) [revision: R2-H].

cards.title: Sites, lairs and threats
cards.body:
**12.16.12 Sites, lairs and threats.** `[D]` [DL-12-23; DL-12-21; R5 LW-07; revision: I-065] One site per area in rings 1–3 and one **lair** in each of rings
4 and 5, each by PR-10-6 (theme d8 with the wound's themes × 3; a domain whose terrain fits the area; band the
area's, −1 on a d6 of 1; lairs one band above their area, telegraphed by rumor, 09.8.2), named from the
domain, its objective sealed from the theme's climax, and its denizen table built by PR-10-10. The first
ring-3 site takes the wound's first theme and is the **threat's seat**; its objective is the faction's head.
Two **situations** (11.4.1) begin with their first step already done: the wound's (its template, its roles
bound to the threat, the rulers and the faith) in a ring-2 area, and one from `tbl.11.hook` (the first row
with a template) in a ring-1 area. The region's **bestiary** is every archetype its tables and sites name
and its factions field (09.11.2; PR-09-1 builds any entry the bestiary lacks).

cards.title: Encounter tables
cards.body:
**12.16.13 Encounter tables.** `[D]` [DL-12-35; DL-12-21; revision: I-065] Every area gets a regional table in 10.10.1's two-sub-table shape: its
threat sub-table built by **PR-10-10** at the area's home band from a pool of every archetype whose
`encounter.terrain` fits the area's terrain (× 3 for the wound's creature gates, × 2 for archetypes a seed
faction fields; elf wardens and dwarf holdguards only where their people are present), with the terrain
branch's archetypes as the fallback pool; its non-threat sub-table is the generic table of its terrain
(T-10-16). Each table is audited by PR-10-8 and the audit is stored (`encounter_table_audit`); a table that
fails is rebuilt with the next RNG draw, and the generic table stands in only if three builds fail (none
has: 12.16.17).

cards.title: Rumors
cards.body:
**12.16.14 Rumors.** `[D]` [DL-11-11; DL-12-21; R5 SO-06; revision: I-065] One rumor table (11.6.1; d12, or d20 when there are more than twelve): each full
faction's goal (true; points to its goal clock), each situation's first trace (true), each site (truth by
`tbl.11.rumor_truth`: hearsay in rings 1–2, legend beyond; a false site rumor says it is empty), and one
about a keeper; faces beyond the list repeat a rumor as hearsay, one step less true. Every rumor's truth is
sealed and its `points_to` is a real record (11.6.4).

cards.title: The calendar
cards.body:
**12.16.15 The calendar.** `[D]` [DL-12-33; DL-11-21; DL-12-21; revision: I-065] 11.10's calendar with the seed's names: twelve month names from
`tbl.12.seed.calendar_names` (three per season, no repeats) or the counted defaults; seven day names; the
era named by the wound ("years since the Burning"); the four quarter-day festivals named for the main keeper
(spring), a fair (summer), the harvest (autumn) and a remembrance of the wound (winter); the opening date,
the spring quarter day of the era's year that 12.16.4 rolled (the wound's age) [revision: I-069]. Lifespans are `calendar.yaml#lifespans`.

cards.title: The opening and the pregens
cards.body:
**12.16.16 The opening and the pregens.** `[D]` [DL-12-22; DL-12-21; revision: I-065] The inciting incident (`tbl.12.seed.inciting`, d8) is framed in
the haven at a moment of decision (12.5.2 step 5; 12.4.3) and pairs with the PC's long vow (02.9.1). The
opening writes the start (date, dawn, the incident's place, the first day's weather rolled by
`h.10.weather`, the new moon, the spring festival) and **three leads** to three different records — the
incident's target, the other situation or the wound's, and the fourth faction's goal — so the first session
cannot dead-end (12.8.1). **Pregens** (02.2.5): four, by 02's creation defaults (the livelihood's priority and
the Peaked shape, the Typical rule unless 02.3.5's exception applies), covering a fighter (Soldier), a sneak
(Thief, of the most present non-human people), a talker (Merchant, Scholar or Courtier) and a worker of magic
(an Acolyte of the main keeper, trained in one of its schools: healing if it keeps healing, else its first
school, with the livelihood's suggested technique of that school [revision: I-052]; or a Hedge-taught of the
place of acceptance when the main keeper is a pact-power); each with a drive, an aspiration and an anchor bond to a cast NPC; birth drawn live when picked.
**The incident's case** [revision: R2-D] [DL-12-62; DL-15-38; I-145; I-148]: at seed time the inciting incident runs
PR-15-6 in its reduced profile (15.9.4; `investigation.yaml#reduced_case`). Its subject is the story role the incident
names (who is missing, who the message was for, who makes the offer, who the challenger is; for an alarm, a theft or an
omen, the thing itself), cast from the cast where the role fits (00.11 `cast`), else generated by 12.11.1 (a missing
child, elder or priest, by d6). Two necessary nodes (the subject; the way on, toward the first lead's target), three
placements and one reserve each, and the first node's core placement held at the opening place (by a reporter there:
a cast NPC whose home it is, else a walk-on). All sealed. **Documents**: the hire lead's notice and one more notice (a
warning, a charter or a bounty) are written from `tbl.12.seed.document`, each a `document` entity with a `text` fact,
delivered first when read (12.10.5). When a lead points to a document, its text names where the lead goes: who to ask,
and where.

cards.title: The seed check
cards.body:
**12.16.17 The seed check.** `[D]` [DL-12-24; DL-12-36; revision: I-065] A seed is complete when every requirement of **T-12-16**
(`world_seed.yaml#requirements`) holds: 64 checks, one for everything the other chapters read from a region
(built from every chapter's requests of chapter 13 and every rule that names region data). A requirement a
seed leaves to a generic table or an on-demand rule names it (`seed.uses_generic`: local events, hooks,
season events, NPC tables, omens, chase ground, hire quirks, cases by PR-15-6, storied items, regional
afflictions, setting origins). A failed check re-runs the step that writes the key; the seed is not used
until every check holds. *Evidence:* `_process/simulation/12-world-seed.py` runs PR-12-9 from data and the
check: seed 1 (oracle) and a guided run pass 64 of 64; 200 further oracle seeds pass every check, with 2,600
regional tables built by PR-10-10, every one passing PR-10-8, whose home-1 tables are audited against both
reference PCs (PR-10-8 step 2; `travel.yaml#encounter_audit_reference`) (word mix trivial 35.4 / easy 26.4 /
fair 34.7 / hard 3.5 / lethal 0 %) [revision: I-096]. Seed 1 is committed as `_process/simulation/12-world-seed-example.yaml`.
**Seed-pack checks** [revision: R2-D] [DL-12-61; I-130]: seven more rows (`world_seed.yaml#pack_requirements`, the last
rows of T-12-16) hold for every place's look, furniture and exits, every cast NPC's knowledge pack and stance, every
document's text, and the incident's reduced case. Seed 1, the guided run and the 200 oracle seeds pass all 71.

cards.title: After the seed
cards.body:
**12.16.18 After the seed.** `[D]` [DL-12-23; DL-12-31; DL-12-35; revision: I-065] The seed writes the world at the depth play starts with; everything
deeper is written on demand by its owner's rule and never invented in narration: a place on mention (10.1.4),
a person (12.11.1), a faction (11.3.18), a site's areas (PR-10-7), a case (PR-15-6), a storied item (08.4.8). A
**new region** (the PC travels past ring 5, or 11's World Turn opens one) runs steps 5, 9, 10 and 11 again
for it, with home bands that start where the old region's ring 5 ended: its ring 1 at home band 4 and rings 2–5
at 4–5 (rolled as 12.16.8, a ring-5 area at 5), because the ladder has no band above 5 [revision: I-084]; its own
factions by
11.3.18's new-region rule, and its own powers by 12.16.11, every one at band 5 [revision: I-083]. A **pre-made seed** (chapter 13's Thallen Vale, or any `region_*.yaml`) replaces
PR-12-9 entirely and must pass the same seed check; a key it lacks is written by the step that owns it, with
the seed's other content as input. Chapter 13's region, run through the same script, holds 54 of the 64
requirements; its gaps (among them unlinked areas, encounter tables that fail PR-10-8, situations without
`trace`, a rumor that points at prose, no powers of the far rings, and petty factions without petty goals
[revision: I-070]) are listed in `12-world-seed-output.txt`
and left as they are, because chapter 13 is no longer maintained (I-035) [revision: I-083].

---

cards.title: The turn loop
cards.body:
**PR-12-1 The turn loop.** `[D]` + `[J]` as marked in each rule. Runs once per player message. Steps T1–T6
are the **adjudication pass** (state, no prose); T7–T10 the **narration pass**; T11–T12 delivery and
record. A pause point (12.2.6) jumps to T7 with what has been resolved so far, then T10–T12.

| Step | Name | What the DM does | Tools | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **T1** | RECEIVE | Store the player's message verbatim in the turn log. Read it in full; never paraphrase it into state. | `log_turn` (35) [editor: E2-041] | 12.2.5 |
| **T2** | CLASSIFY | Split the message into parts; classify each (SAFETY, SESSION, DISPUTE, PENDING_ANSWER, OOF_QUESTION, FICTION_QUESTION, DECLARATION, SPEECH); order them. SAFETY first: act on it before anything else. | — | 12.2.2, 12.5 |
| **T3** | LOAD | `get_active_triggers()`; `get_state(scene, narrator)`; `load_cards(situation tags, mode, triggers)` within the packet cap. The core checklist is always present. | 30, 8, 31 | 12.2.3, 12.2.4 |
| **T4** | ADJUDICATE | For each SESSION / DISPUTE / OOF part: answer it (12.5, 12.3.6). For each PENDING_ANSWER: resume the paused pipeline. For each FICTION_QUESTION: 01.3.8 (state → canon → Oracle, PR-01-4). For each DECLARATION: PR-01-1 (PARSE … CONSEQUENCE) per beat, up to three, `find_rulings` before any adaptation. Stop at the first pause point reached. | 1–6, 29 | 01.1–01.15 |
| **T5** | WORLD | World responses in fixed order: adversaries (conflict), NPCs present by the default NPC layer (activity, practice, frame → want/refusal → `tbl.npc_action`; the addressed NPC always answers) [revision: R2-B], clocks and omens, fired triggers (lead injection, pacing push, offers), time and boundaries (`advance_time` / `mark_boundary`). Each from its closed source only. | 7, 21–23 | 12.2.9, 12.11.9, 01.11.3 |
| **T6** | WRITE | All state writes not already made: RECORD of every beat (01.12.1), evidence by **PR-03-1** for every resolved beat, rulings, NPC memories, knowledge records, `beat_end` marks; a cut scene is always marked `scene_end`, since ch.03's settlement hangs on it [integration: IR ch.03 to 12]. Then re-read the narrator view. | 9–18, 25, 29 | 12.2.8, 12.2.10 |
| **T7** | DRAFT | Draft the narration as declared sentences (12.3.1) [revision: R2-B] from the adjudication record and the fresh narrator view only: fiction first, then OOF blocks (12.15). Name everything 12.14.12 requires. Respect length (12.14.10). | — | 12.14 |
| **T8** | MENTION | Write each declared new element by its tier (12.14.13) [revision: R2-B]: T1a on mention (`create_entity` / `set_fact`; NPCs via 12.11.1), T1b in the narrator's voice once the Oracle settles it (in speech, a `said` record; PR-12-12) [revision: R2-H], T2 only if this turn's record holds it. Ask the Oracle or roll the table for a consequential property the draft needs that is unsettled; an incidental one is written as drafted. For an existing entity, diff each stated property against its profile (PR-00-7 step 2) [revision: R2-E]. Redraft a sentence if an answer changes it. | 6, 7, 9, 10 | 00.6.6, 00.6.6a, PR-00-7 |
| **T9** | CHECK | Resolve declarations into claims and compute coverage (12.3.1, 12.3.1a) [revision: R2-B]; `check_claims` on narrator-voice claims with a certain subject; fix each blocking failure by its rule and log the rest (12.3.1b, 12.3.2) [revision: R2-G]; re-check only the redrafted sentences; at most two redrafts, then cut and render (12.3.3). | 32 | 12.3 |
| **T10** | SCREEN | Input fidelity ×3 (12.2.7); next step exists (01.11.4); safety screen against lines, veils and flags (12.5.6); PC agency (12.14.3); no mechanics in fiction (12.14.4); open prompt or one pause block last (12.14.9). Any failure → back to T7. | — | 12.2.7, 12.5.6, 12.14 |
| **T11** | DELIVER | Send the response. | — | 12.15 |
| **T12** | RECORD | Store the delivered response verbatim; set `last_used` on each detail, written word and speech opener its sentences stated (12.14.11) [revision: R2-E]; update turn counters (dead air, 12.4.2); if a scene cut was reached, `mark_boundary(scene_end)` then frame the next scene (PR-12-7) in the *next* response unless the cut was the player's own request in this message. | 35, 22 | 12.2.5, 12.4 |

cards.title: The claim check
cards.body:
**PR-12-2 The claim check.** `[D]` + `[J:enum]` (inside T9) [revision: R2-G; DL-12-80]
1. Resolve each sentence's declarations into claims (12.3.1) and split speech from the narrator's voice by the
   `speaker` declarations (12.3.1b item 1); scan every narrator-voice sentence for numerals, names and aliases,
   outcome words and sealed strings (and the OOF blocks' state values); compute coverage (12.3.1a)
   [revision: R2-B; DL-12-41].
2. Speech: check that the speaker is present and is not the PC, and that no words are put in the PC's mouth;
   record each speech part as a `said` record on its speaker. Nothing else in speech is judged.
3. Keep for judging each narrator-voice claim with a certain subject (12.3.1b item 4); log the rest.
   `check_claims(claims)` → a verdict per claim (12.3.2): support against the packet and the record,
   contradiction against the whole store.
4. For each `new_element`: write it by its tier (12.14.13): T1a on mention (only the stated properties); T2 not
   in this turn's record → cut the sentence.
5. For each `undetermined`: incidental → write it as drafted; consequential → ask the Oracle or roll the settling
   table, write the answer, and redraft that sentence to it.
6. For each blocking `contradicted` or `overreach` (12.3.1b item 2): redraft that sentence to the store's value or
   the literal scope. For each blocking `unsourced_change`, each `leak` or `pc_agency`, and each scan-flagged
   sentence citing no must-name item: cut the sentence (and replace a leak with its permitted slice if the
   narration needs one). Every other verdict: log it in the claim log and keep the sentence.
7. Re-run steps 1–3 on the redrafted sentences only. After the second redraft, cut each sentence still failing
   and render each uncited must-name item (12.3.3); log a `rule_conflict` ruling with `review_flag: true` if any
   line was rendered.
8. On a sampled turn (1 in 10; `pacing.yaml#claim_check.audit`), after delivery, run the audit (12.3.1) and log
   what it finds; it never changes the delivered turn.

cards.title: Lead injection
cards.body:
**PR-12-3 Lead injection.** `[D]` + `[J:flag]` (when `trg.lead_injection` fires; 12.8.2)
1. Walk the source ladder (12.8.2 step 1) and take the first eligible source; ties at a rung go to the
   higher list weight, then to the stalest rotation axis (12.9.2), then `roll_table` on the tied set.
2. `roll_table(tbl.lead_injection, {phase})` for the form (threat-tagged forms excluded in RELAX and
   PEAK). Fit test `[J:flag]`; re-roll once; then the fallback form.
3. Apply the three lead tests (concrete, actionable now, connected) and the three prohibitions (does not
   solve the thread, costs nothing, is not a threat during PEAK or RELAX [verification: V2b-016]). A failing lead → the next source.
4. Write: unseal the clue through its gate, or write the NPC's approach, or the rumor heard;
   `record_knowledge(pc, …)`; set the inconclusive counter to 0.
5. Narrate it in this turn's world responses (T5 → T7). Log the injection in the scene log
   (`lead_injection: {source_rung, source_id, form_roll, facts}`); it is not a ruling, because nothing
   was adjudicated.

cards.title: Correcting an error the player has seen
cards.body:
**PR-12-4 Correcting an error the player has seen.** `[D]` + `[J]` (12.3.4)
1. State the mismatch: the delivered claim (turn id), the store's value.
2. Narration error or record error? Name the resolved source if any (`[J:flag]`). Record error → corrective
   write citing the source (`source: correction`, pinned, 12.3.6) [revision: R2-G].
3. Reliance test (`[J:flag]`): list the committed beats since the error that cited, targeted or premised
   the claim.
4. If none: choose the form (in-fiction reconciliation only if it adds no new fact; else the OOF note);
   deliver it; go to step 7.
5. If some, within the current scene: CHOICE (pause point 9) — keep (only if each frame stays valid
   without the false element), accept forward, or rewind (`revert_writes` to before the first relying
   beat; void its rolls in the log; the player re-declares). Under 12.5.8's take-back limit the same choice is
   offered for a beat before the scene's start [revision: R2-G].
6. If some, before the current scene: correct forward; refund every quantity spent because of the
   falsehood (corrective writes); nothing else.
7. Log the correction record and a ruling with `review_flag: true`, and the dispute record when a report started
   it (12.3.6 item 6) [revision: R2-G]; check the review list's Principle III candidate rule (12.12.4).

cards.title: Generating an NPC and the first meeting
cards.body:
**PR-12-5 Generating an NPC and the first meeting.** `[D]` + `[J:enum]` (12.11)
1. Check the region roster and the cast list for an existing NPC who fits (`[J:flag]`); if one does, use
   them and stop.
2. Walk-on: role (from the narration, else `tbl.npc_role` with the place's tags) → name (region table,
   else `tbl.name_given` + `tbl.name_family`) → gender and pronouns → age band → distinctive detail →
   demeanor. `create_entity(kind npc, …)`; add to the cast list at weight 1.
3. At first interaction: the reaction roll (12.11.2) → `set_relationship`.
4. On a recurring trigger: want, fear, voice register and habit, refusal, knowledge scope.
5. On a principal trigger: the Oracle for a secret (sealed with a gate), two more wants (ranked), ties.
6. Every field is written before the narration that uses it; nothing is chosen.

cards.title: A random event
cards.body:
**PR-12-6 A random event.** `[D]` + `[J:open]` (12.6.5)
1. `roll_table(tbl.event_focus, {phase})` → focus (threat foci read as *omen* in PEAK and RELAX).
2. Target from the weighted list if the focus names one; empty list → the stated substitute focus.
3. `roll_table(tbl.meaning, {kind: action})` → verb + subject.
4. Interpret in one sentence under the four conditions of 12.6.5 step 4; `find_rulings` for the same focus
   and target kind if the event is of a recurring kind.
5. Write (`create_entity` / `set_fact` / NPC action / one clock tick from a listed `random_event` source);
   check the bounds (no harm, no cost, no license, no sealed fact, no protected thread resolved).
6. Narrate now (in scene) or schedule as news (remote).

cards.title: Scene start and scene end
cards.body:
**PR-12-7 Scene start and scene end.** `[D]` + `[J]`
*At scene_start:* (1) write the scene record: agenda, the PC's hoped answer (12.6.3), mode (12.4.5),
pillar and challenge type (12.9.1), cast present; (2) `mark_boundary(scene_start)` → `h.12.scene_test`
(unless untested) and `h.12.pacing_push` if raised; (3) apply an altered or interrupted result; (4) frame
the scene (12.4.3); (5) if a flagged topic is present, the FLAG pause first (12.5.6).
*At scene_end:* `mark_boundary(scene_end)` runs every registered handler (00.7.5 phases), including
`h.12.bookkeeping`'s eight steps (12.4.8), in this order of ch.12's own handlers: phase 7
`h.12.lead_audit`; phase 9 `h.12.tension_update`, `h.12.intensity_scene`, `h.12.rotation_update`,
`h.12.npc_memory`, `h.12.bookkeeping`.

cards.title: Session open and close
cards.body:
**PR-12-8 Session open and close.** `[D]` (12.5.2, 12.5.4)
*Open:* `mark_boundary(session_start)` → `h.12.session_open`: preferences re-read → recap from state →
SITUATION block → pending pauses re-shown → strong start (vignette if nothing presses) → check-in if due.
*Close:* finish the beat only if past ROLL → `mark_boundary(session_end)` → `h.12.session_close` (review
list compiled, 12.12.4) and the mirrored `h.12.bookkeeping` → optional next-time question → one line of
where the PC stands. No time passes at either.

cards.title: The world seed
cards.body:
**PR-12-9 The world seed.** `[D]` + `[J:enum]` (12.16; reference code `_process/simulation/12-world-seed.py`;
data `data/world_seed.yaml`) [revision: I-028]
1. **Mode.** Ask once: guided, oracle or mixed (12.16.2; default mixed). In mixed mode, list the questions
   (T-12-15) and let the player name the ones they want to answer.
2. **Run steps 1–13 in order** (T-12-15). For each question: the player's option, or the player's own words
   classified by 12.16.2, or the oracle roll; log `{question, answer, source}`. Each step writes its keys by
   its rule (12.16.4–12.16.16), reading only earlier steps' writes. Then run the **seed-pack pass** (12.16.9, 12.16.11,
   12.16.16) [revision: R2-D].
3. **Show each step's summary** as `[SEED n/14]` (shown parts only; sealed parts withheld). A veto re-rolls
   that step's oracle answers once and re-runs every later step that read them.
4. **Seed check** (step 14; 12.16.17): run every T-12-16 requirement; a failure re-runs the step that writes
   its key. The seed is used only when every check holds.
5. **Hand over** to chapter 02's creation (its C2 shows the seed's present peoples; its defaults read the
   seed's second tongue, keepers and name tables; a pregen may be picked) and then to the opening
   (12.16.16): `mark_boundary(session_start)`, strong start at the incident.

cards.title: Answering a question
cards.worst_case: an answer that is wrong about the world — it is testimony, settled only if the player relies on it (PR-12-12), and then by the case, by acceptance or by the Oracle (class iv).
cards.body:
**PR-12-10 Answering a question.** `[D]` + `[J:enum]` as marked (12.10.8; `pacing.yaml#answer_ladder`) [revision: R2-H]
[DL-12-90; DL-12-60]. Trigger: an NPC is asked a question, a part whose PARSE carries `question_kind` and `topic`
(12.2.2). Runs at RECORD for each delivered item (01.10.4; a Talk's items by T-15-5's questions rule), before the draft.
R2-D's rungs (the store, the knowledge pack, propose-and-ratify, the pointer) are retired as sources of speech.
1. **Route** `[D]`. A topic given as an entity resolves to topics by `social.yaml#common_knowledge.entity_topics`.
   - **consequential** (a story role such as who is missing, who did it or who sent them; a case's solution; a sealed
     fact; a thread's knowledge) goes to the case graph only. An NPC holding a placement on it delivers it (15.9.5–
     15.9.7); one who holds none says so and points to the holder of the node's core placement, else of a live one. A
     story-role question with no case behind it builds PR-15-6's reduced case now and is answered from it. The answer
     is a record line the narration must name (12.14.12);
   - **who is <role>** (not a story role) goes to casting (00.11 `cast`; `social.yaml#cast`); its answer, a person or
     "no one you know", is a fact;
   - everything else (ordinary knowledge, what the NPC wants or thinks, who would know) is the NPC's to answer in
     words: steps 2–5.
2. **Willingness** `[D]` (12.11.9 step 3), first that applies: a recorded refusal whose tags match the question
   (`social.yaml#event_tags`) → `unwilling`, the refusal its reason; a Talk frame → its delivered items (failure:
   `unwilling`); a SPEECH question that 15.3.10's certainty test would pass (a Neutral or warmer listener, an R1
   request, no hesitation) → `willing`; else `roll_table(tbl.npc_action, {standing})` read as a willingness band only
   (`answer_ladder.willingness_by_row`: rows 1–3 `unwilling`, 4–6 `guarded`, 7–10 `willing`). Great or better reach
   adds one volunteered extra from the NPC's record (a want, a fear, a tie or a lead; T-15-5 row 3).
3. **Speaker card** `[D]`: the narrator view shows, for the asked NPC, the question and the willingness line, then
   what the NPC knows — their knowledge records and the ordinary facts of their pack on the topic first, their role's
   common-knowledge topics, public news in their scope — and their recent `said` records
   (`answer_ladder.said_shown`, and every one on this topic). Never anything sealed, an undelivered placement or a
   motive (INV-10).
4. **Voice** `[J]` (the narrator): the answer in character, within the willingness, from the card first. Beyond the
   card the NPC still answers **plainly and with ordinary confidence** about ordinary things, as people do. Every
   ordinary claim is testimony settled lazily (PR-12-12) whatever its tone, so a hedge protects nothing: a hedge ("I
   only hear it", "folk say", "I could not say") is a characterisation choice for a cautious or gossipy NPC, not the
   default [revision: R2-I; DL-12-96]. Speech never opens by reciting the speaker's own name or title unless asked:
   the card is what the narrator knows, not what the NPC says [revision: R2-I; DL-12-100]. "I don't know" is the
   character's choice: rare, in voice, with a natural redirect. (`12-answer_ladder_sim.py` part A: the card holds
   nothing on the topic for 48% of first asks when half the asks are on the NPC's trade, so most answers come from
   beyond the card, plain testimony settled only if relied on.)
5. **Write** `[D]` the spoken words as a `said` record `{speaker, turn, words, about, question}` (12.3.1b); the index
   entry `(npc, question_kind, topic) → said id`; a name heard that equals the stored name, a PC knowledge record
   `how: heard` (12.10.2). No world fact is written: the PC learns *that the NPC said it* (12.10.5).
*Worst case (J):* an answer that is wrong about the world — it is testimony, settled only if the player relies on it
(PR-12-12), and then by the case, by acceptance or by the Oracle (class iv).

cards.title: Checking a player's report: understand first, then verify
cards.worst_case: the understanding call misreads the complaint — the restatement shows the player what was understood, so they correct it at once (class ii); a wrong passage is quoted, and `/turn N` shows the right one (class ii).
cards.body:
**PR-12-11 Checking a player's report: understand first, then verify.** `[D]` + `[J:enum]` as marked (12.3.6;
`pacing.yaml#feedback`; `engine/dm/dispute.py`) [revision: R2-G; revision: R2-H] [DL-12-84; DL-12-85; DL-12-86;
DL-12-94]. Trigger: a DISPUTE part, or `/fix`.
1. **Understand** `[J:enum]`. One model call reads the player's report **with the whole transcript** (past
   `feedback.understand_call.transcript_budget_tokens`: the scene cards plus the turns that search hits for the
   report's words) and returns `{believes, happened, category, turn, quote}`: what the player believes, what the
   transcript shows happened, the category (12.3.6 item 2, including `ruling_question`), and the turn and words
   concerned. Code does not pin the report first by a number or a name in it.
2. **Restate** `[D]`: the answer opens with the complaint in plain words, from `believes` ("You're saying the lift
   succeeded but you never got the purse.").
3. **Verify** `[D]`: gather the passage and every other turn that mentions the same subject; the store's current value
   with its provenance (source event, source kind, turn); the frame of any beat in the passage with its cited facts,
   rule ids, typed intended change (01.2.7) and inputs; the claim log's entries for those turns (12.3.1b).
4. **Decide** `[D]`, first row that fits:

   | Evidence | Outcome |
   |---|---|
   | no passage fits what the player believes | not found: "I can't find that; did you mean …?" with the nearest passage |
   | `rule_wrong` or `ruling_question`: the recomputed frame differs, or an established fact that changes it was omitted | ruling error: 12.3.4 with reliance true (keep, accept forward or take back) |
   | `rule_wrong` or `ruling_question`: the recomputed frame matches | explain in plain words why the ruling came out so: the frame, its typed change and reach, its rule ids and cited facts |
   | `misread`: the beat resolved on a reading the player never saw (12.5.8 item 2), and the player's words support their reading | take back and redo the beat |
   | a resolved source in the log requires the player's value | record error: a pinned corrective write (12.3.4 step 1) |
   | the narration said one thing and the store holds another | narration error: 12.3.4 (the store wins; OOF note; reliance) |
   | the store holds what the player says, and the narration said otherwise or never said it | narration error or omission (12.3.4): state the store's value |
   | the transcript shows the player is mistaken (the quote says otherwise, or it never happened) | explain with the quote; nothing written |
   | incidental fiction (T0, T1a), the evidence uncertain (no stored value, or only logged clashes) | act on it: the player's reading wins, a pinned correction, `source: correction` (00.6.7) |
   | mechanics or consequential content, the evidence uncertain | explain what the record holds and why; logged for review; nothing written (INV-9) |

5. **Deliver** the restatement and the outcome as a `[CORRECTION]` or `[FIX]` block (12.15.9), with a CHOICE when
   reliance applies. Every report gets a plain answer: corrected, explained, or not found with a "did you mean";
   never "logged" alone.
6. **Log** the dispute record and its review-log entry (12.3.6 item 6); a correction also logs 12.3.4 step 4's
   record and a ruling with `review_flag: true`.
*Worst case (J):* the understanding call misreads the complaint — the restatement shows the player what was
understood, so they correct it at once (class ii); a wrong passage is quoted, and `/turn N` shows the right one
(class ii).

cards.title: Settling testimony when it matters
cards.worst_case: a claim stated a little off at step 2 — the settled fact is ordinary or at Likely odds by construction, worth at most +2, a stakes rung or a reach rung (12.14.13; class i); a consequential claim can only be found true where the case already holds it (class iv).
cards.body:
**PR-12-12 Settling testimony when it matters.** `[D]` + `[J:enum]` as marked (12.10.8, 12.3.1b; `pacing.yaml#testimony`)
[revision: R2-H] [DL-12-91]. What a character says is a `said` record, never a world fact (12.3.1b). It is settled —
made world truth or found false — only at the moment it matters, once.
1. **Triggers** `[D]` (closed list; code finds each from the beat and the `said` records in scope):
   (a) **acted on**: a beat's target, topic or method rests on it (the Reader's `rests_on` names a `said` id, 12.2.2,
   or the target is known to the PC only from a `said` record);
   (b) **cited**: a lever, snag or term cites it (01.6.8, 15.3.5);
   (c) **travel**: the PC sets out for a place, or a person at a place, that a `said` record names and the store does
   not hold as the PC knows it;
   (d) **mechanics**: it would change a mechanical outcome if true: a gate, tier, DC, stakes, reach, cost, an NPC's
   response source or a clock.
   Nothing else settles testimony: hearing it, repeating it, asking about it, or another character contradicting it.
2. **State the claim** `[J:enum]`: one call reads the said words and returns `{subject, predicate, value}`, the subject
   an id in scope or a new name, in the typed form of a fact (00.6). It judges nothing else.
3. **Route by tier** `[D]`, first that applies:
   - **consequential** (its subject or predicate touches a case node, a sealed fact, a story role, a thread's knowledge
     or a clue): **the case settles it** — true when the case holds it, otherwise false. It never delivers a clue: a
     clue comes only by its placement (15.9), and a true claim only points the PC to where the case already is;
   - **beyond the ordinary** (12.14.13's question is true: it would help or hinder the PC beyond what any such place
     ordinarily offers): the Oracle at **Likely** (00.12.7), odds fixed before the roll; yes, true; no, false;
   - **ordinary** (everything else): **accepted**, true as stated.
4. **Write** `[D]`: a true claim is a fact `{source: testimony | oracle, said_by, said_turn}`, citable from this beat on
   (the words were said before the declaration, 01.6.8); a false one is written as the speaker's error
   (`npc.<id>.wrong_about: <claim>`, or a lie when 15.6.2 recorded one) and followed in the same breath by what *is*
   there (P16: the mill is there; Marta is not). The `said` record is marked `settled: true | false` with the fact id
   and is never settled again.
5. **The speaker stays themself**: a false settlement changes the world, not the past words; the NPC owns the error
   only when confronted (12.10.8).
*Worst case (J):* a claim stated a little off at step 2 — the settled fact is ordinary or at Likely odds by
construction, worth at most +2, a stakes rung or a reach rung (12.14.13; class i); a consequential claim can only be
found true where the case already holds it (class iv).

---

cards.title: The always-loaded checklist
cards.body:
**T-12-1 The always-loaded checklist** (this is the card that travels with every turn; about 250 words;
`pacing.yaml#packet.core_checklist` holds the same text).

> **Every turn.** T1 Store the message verbatim. T2 Classify its parts; safety first. T3 Load triggers,
> the narrator view and the cards for this scene; handle every fired trigger this turn. T4 Adjudicate
> before writing prose: questions from state, canon or the Oracle; declarations through the pipeline
> (PARSE, GATE, NECESSITY, ANCHOR, FRAME, OFFER, ROLL, READ, DELIVER, CONSEQUENCE, RECORD); check
> precedent before any adaptation, Oracle call, Good Idea, G3 or G4; stop at a pause point. T5 Let the
> world respond only from its sources: adversaries' behavior, NPCs' frames, wants, refusals or the
> action table, clocks and omens, triggers, time. T6 Write all state, then re-read it. T7 Draft from
> the record and the fresh view. T8 Write on mention every new addressable thing; roll what is unsettled.
> T9 Check every claim against the store; fix or cut; never write a change to match prose. T10 Intent
> acknowledged, not substituted, not reset; a next step exists; no line crossed; no words or feelings
> given to the character; no numbers or rules words in the fiction; end on an open prompt or one pause
> block. T11 Deliver. T12 Log it; count dead air; cut the scene if its question is answered.
> **Never**: choose a number; pick at random; decide what is true; change a committed frame; add a
> complication from nowhere; narrate a sealed fact; speak for the character; voice a mechanic.
> **If unsure**: roll (a check, the Oracle, a table) rather than decide; grant less rather than more.

cards.body:

defaults).

| State | Words the fiction may use |
|---|---|
| PC Vitality above half | steady, scraped, breathing hard |
| PC bloodied (at or below half) | bleeding, battered, every movement costs |
| PC Staggered (0) | reeling, on your knees, the world narrowing |
| PC Dying | ch.07's dying narration (the brink) |
| PC Focus low (0–1) | drained, the well run dry, nothing left to draw on |
| Adversary unhurt | fresh, untouched, easy in its stance |
| Adversary bloodied | bleeding freely, guard dropping, favoring a side |
| Adversary down | falls, does not rise, out of the fight |
| Standing (12.14.7) | Hostile: open enmity · Unfriendly: curt, suspicious · Wary: guarded · Neutral: businesslike · Warm: small courtesies · Friendly: goes out of their way · Devoted: would take risks for you |

cards.title: Scene state from a resolved beat and an NPC's response
cards.body:
**T-12-18 Scene state from a resolved beat and an NPC's response** (`pacing.yaml#details.scene_writes`; 00.6.6a
item 4, 12.11.9) [revision: R2-F]. It is the scene-state face of the typed intended change (01.2.7: `restrain`, `move_to`,
`harm`), one case of it [revision: R2-H; DL-01-34]. Code writes these scene slots (T1c, 12.14.13) for the PC and every present person or
creature; the narrator cites them and never improvises them. Degree: *success* covers critical success, success at
cost and a no-roll beat (which counts reach 2). Every row whose `reach_min` is met (the delivered reach,
00.3.15) applies in order, a later value overwriting an earlier one for the same slot. `{actor}` and `{target}` are names as the PC knows them ("you" for
the PC). "—" writes nothing: the beat line carries it. A band is not a slot; it is scene state all the same and
clears at scene end (12.4.8 step 8).

| Verb | Degree | Position (band) | Actor's slots | Target's slots |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Move | any | in a conflict (ch.06): one band toward or away from the target (PR-06-4); outside one, an approach to someone or something present ends beside it (`band.engaged`) in one beat (01.4.1) [revision: R2-I; DL-12-98] | — | — |
| Observe, Recall, Exert, Evade, Sneak, Handle, Endure, Setup | any | — | — | — |
| Talk | any | — | — | — (the target's response writes: below) |
| Strike | any | melee: engaged on the attempt (06.3.5) | — | manner: on guard against {actor} |
| Grapple | success, reach 1–2 | engaged on the attempt (06.3.5, 06.5.2) | held: {target} in a grip | posture: held fast by {actor}; manner: straining against {actor} |
| Grapple | success, reach 3 | engaged on the attempt | held: {target} restrained | posture: restrained by {actor}; manner: straining against {actor} |
| Grapple | success, reach 4 | engaged on the attempt | held: {target} pinned | posture: pinned by {actor}; manner: straining against {actor} |
| Grapple | failure, critical failure | engaged on the attempt | — | manner: on guard against {actor} |
| Force | success | engaged on the attempt (06.3.5); then reach 2 one band away, reach 3+ two bands, unless knocked down (06.5.3) | — | manner: on guard against {actor}; at reach 2+ with a knock-down in the beat's words (trip, sweep, floor, prone), posture: down on the ground |
| Force | failure, critical failure | engaged on the attempt (06.3.5) | — | manner: on guard against {actor} |
| Help | success | — | activity: helping {target} | — |
| Ready | success | — | posture: braced and ready | — |
| Help, Ready | failure, critical failure | — | — | — |

A posture is the visible face of a beat's outcome and never a ch.07 condition; when a condition is applied
(06.5.2's `grabbed`, 06.5.3's `prone`) it governs the mechanics (00.6.6a item 1).

**Responses** (12.11.9 step 3: an engaged or addressed NPC's response writes their manner, and their activity
only when the body does something else: squares up, turns away, takes cover; talk alone never changes the
activity. "—" keeps that slot).

| Source | Activity | Manner |
|---|---|---|
| Talk frame, success | — | willing |
| Talk frame, failure | — | unmoved |
| Recorded refusal | — | unwilling |
| Recorded want | — | — |
| `tbl.npc_action` row 1 | squaring up to you | hostile |
| `tbl.npc_action` row 2 | turning away from you | closed off |
| `tbl.npc_action` row 3 | — | guarded |
| `tbl.npc_action` row 4 | — | calculating |
| `tbl.npc_action` rows 5–6 | — | — |
| `tbl.npc_action` row 7 | — | curious |
| `tbl.npc_action` row 8 | — | helpful |
| `tbl.npc_action` row 9 | — | friendly |
| `tbl.npc_action` row 10 | — | warm |

**Practice rows** (`tbl.npc_practice`): under the scene's practice, a listed row replaces the generic row whole.

| Practice | Rows it replaces (row: activity; manner) |
|---|---|
| fight | 2: taking cover; frightened · 3: getting in the way; guarded · 5: keeping clear and watching; wary · 6: looking to their own; wary · 8: shouting a warning; alarmed · 9: helping you; willing |
| trade | 2: —; unwilling · 3: —; hard-nosed · 4: —; calculating · 5: —; busy · 8: —; grudging · 9: —; businesslike · 10: —; generous |
| greeting | 2: —; curt · 3: —; wary · 5: —; polite · 6: —; preoccupied |
| conversation | 3: —; evasive · 5: —; distracted · 6: —; insistent |
| crowd | 1: calling for the watch; alarmed · 2: backing away; uneasy · 3: blocking the way; guarded · 5: —; watchful · 7: —; curious · 8: stepping up to help; helpful |
| work | 2: moving off; — · 3: —; pointedly ignoring you |
