cards.title: Full turn-loop trace 1: a simple action (with a secret frame and a pause)
cards.body:
### WE-12-1 Full turn-loop trace 1: a simple action (with a secret frame and a pause)

*DM turn 1. Player:* "I walk down to the landing and look it over. Is the ferry still there? Anything odd?"

| Step | What happens | State / tools |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | Message stored verbatim. | turn log #118 |
| T2 | Parts: "walk down to the landing" — DECLARATION (Move, Trivial: no roll, a scene change); "Is the ferry still there?" — FICTION_QUESTION; "look it over … anything odd?" — DECLARATION (Observe). No SAFETY, SESSION or DISPUTE. | classes logged |
| T3 | `get_active_triggers()` → none. Place change → `scene_end` (market) then `scene_start` (landing). Scene record: agenda "What happened at the landing?"; hoped answer: Wren hopes to find a sign (yes); mode `free` → `site`? No: one place, no room-by-room search → `free`; pillar `investigation`; challenge type `mystery`. `h.12.scene_test`: expected scene "the landing at dusk, deserted"; d10 = **8** > T − 3 = 2 → **expected**. Cards loaded: `situation.investigation.search`, `situation.exploration`, the Observe anchor. | `mark_boundary` ×2; scene `scn.0231` |
| T4a | FICTION_QUESTION: is the ferry here? No fact; canon silent; scene logic? A ferry landing *usually* has its ferry, but the ferryman is missing (fact) — open. `find_rulings(oracle)` → no precedent. Odds `[J:rung]` **Even** (could have gone with him or been left); eventful tag `none` (static availability). Tension 5 → no shift. `oracle(…)` d100 = **63** → yes (63 ≥ 51; not in 51–55; not doubles). | `set_fact(loc.ashford_landing.ferry_present = true, source: oracle)`; `create_entity(obj.ferry_flatboat)` |
| T4b | DECLARATION Observe. PARSE: method "look over the landing for anything out of place", target `loc.ashford_landing`. GATE G1 `verb.observe`. NECESSITY: the landing holds a sealed clue placement → uncertain; costly? the riders' search runs and time matters → roll (`[J:flag]` ×3; tie → roll). Secret frame `[J:flag]`: the target's content is sealed → **true** (01.4.7). ANCHOR: `verb.observe` card, no deltas (no `find_rulings` needed: no adaptation). FRAME: Wits +2; primary tag `deed.lore.investigation` → floor +1; no levers or snags; obstacle `clu.scorched_rope`, stored DC 15 (hidden); stakes **Safe** (no one near, the night young: failure only means nothing found); threatened cost `cost.time` (used only on a critical failure, S1); reach Standard (one question). Total +3. | frame #771 |
| — | **Pause point 1**: auto-commit does not apply to a secret frame (01.7.4). The turn jumps to T7 with what is resolved. | — |
| T5 | World: no NPC present; no clock ticked; `advance_time`: the walk down is unlisted free movement in town (0 time, 00.7.3 `free`). | — |
| T6 | Writes done (fact, boat); narrator view re-read. | — |
| T7 | Draft: "Dusk has gone blue over the river. The flatboat rides at its mooring, nosing the reeds; a coil of rope hangs by the boathouse door, and the ferryman's hut sits dark above the steps. Someone has left a pair of boots by the hut door." | — |
| T8 | Elements: flatboat (written), rope coil (ordinary furniture → `create_entity(obj.rope_coil_02)`), hut (`create_entity(loc.ashford_landing.hut)`, implied: dark), **boots** — `[J:flag]` 12.14.13: a pair of boots left by a missing man's door *points toward something hidden* → true → not furniture; cut. | 2 entities |
| T9 | Claims: `existence` boat ✓, rope ✓, hut ✓; `location_time` dusk ✓ (watch: evening); `identity` "the ferryman's hut" — ✓ (`loc…hut.owner = npc.hob_coldwell`, written with the thread). No other verdicts after the cut. | `check_claims` → all supported |
| T10 | Fidelity: three parts acknowledged ✓ (walked, ferry answered, search offered); nothing substituted ✓; nothing reset ✓. Next step exists ✓. Safety ✓. No numbers in fiction ✓. Ends on the OFFER block (pause). | — |
| T11 | Delivered (below). | — |
| T12 | Logged. Dead-air counter 0 (a declaration). | — |

*Delivered:*
> Dusk has gone blue over the river. The flatboat rides at its mooring, nosing the reeds; a coil of rope
> hangs by the boathouse door, and the ferryman's hut sits dark above the steps. You start along the
> landing, looking for anything out of place.
>
> `[OFFER] Search the landing for anything out of place — verb.observe (Observe), anchor 01.18.5`
> `Roll: Wits +2 · competence +1 (deed) = +3   ·   Against: hidden   ·   the roll is hidden; you'll see only what you perceive`
> `Stakes: Safe — failure: nothing found · critical failure: Time (S1)   ·   Reach: Standard — one answer`
> `Costs: 1 interval · fate 1   → commit · change · withdraw`

*DM turn 2. Player:* "Commit." — PENDING_ANSWER. T4: `roll_check(#771)`: d20 = **14** → total 17 vs 15 →
**success**; delivered reach 2 → the one question is answered (`deliver_count`). `unseal(clu.scorched_rope)`;
`record_knowledge(pc.wren, clu.scorched_rope, how: observed)`; evidence (ch.03); `mark_boundary(beat_end)` →
`h.12.inconclusive_streak`: a new fact learned → counter **0**; `h.10.site_time` not applicable (free mode).
T5: `advance_time(1 interval)` — no boundary handler fires. T7–T10: the draft names the delivered item; the
claim check passes; the next step is evident (the hut; who burned the rope?).
> You find it at the mooring post: the old rope end is black and stiff, the fibers fused. Not cut —
> burned through, close to the knot, as if someone held a flame to it until it parted. The hut above the
> steps is still dark. What do you do?
>
> `[RESULT] hidden check made.`

*Boundary pair.* Had the clue's existence been undetermined (no thread placed anything here), T4b would
first ask the **sealed** Oracle (01.15.6) — "is anything hidden here?", Unlikely — and the search would be
just as secret. *Non-example:* resolving "Anything odd?" by narrating the scorched rope at once, with no
roll, "because the scene needs a clue" — the clue is sealed behind its gate (a successful Observe); the DM
may not unseal it by mention (12.10.3).

cards.title: Full turn-loop trace 2: a wild creative action, an anchor, a precedent, a split, and a catch
cards.body:
### WE-12-2 Full turn-loop trace 2: a wild creative action, an anchor, a precedent, a split, and a catch

*Situation.* Two days later, in the toll-house on the Grey Keep bridge *(illustrative stat lines; ch.06/09
own)*. Conflict mode. Established at the scene's opening (written on mention): `obj.lantern_chain` (an iron
chain hanging from the rafters by the stair, a cartwheel lantern at its end); `loc.toll_hall.gallery` with
`f.gallery_height = 12 ft`; the archer `adv.toll_archer_02` (T2: Might +2, Agility +3, competence
`deed.martial` +2; Vitality 8) on the gallery at `band.near` with `flag.elevated`; after his last shot,
`adv.toll_archer_02.loaded = false` (he is spanning his crossbow; ch.06 reload). Wren stands at the foot of
the stair.

*DM turn 1. Player:* "I run up the stair, grab the lantern chain, swing across onto the gallery and kick
that archer off the rail before he can reload!"

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| T2 | One DECLARATION. |
| T3 | Triggers: none. Cards: `situation.conflict.*`; anchors retrieved below. |
| T4 PARSE | Three methods in sequence (run to the chain; swing; kick) → three beats, `sequential` (01.2.2; 12.13.3 split — distinct methods, distinct targets, and an order). ≤ 3 beats, inside ch.06's action budget *(illustrative)*. Neutral restatements: B1 "Wren moves up the stair to the chain"; B2 "Wren swings on the lantern chain to the gallery"; B3 "Wren kicks the archer to topple him off the gallery rail". |
| B1 | GATE G1 Move; NECESSITY: passable stair, no one blocks → **Trivial**, no roll. Position written: Wren at the chain. |
| B2 ANCHOR | `load_cards` → candidates scored (12.13.2): `verb.exert` (deed `athletics` +2, situation `conflict` +1; no intent verb "swing" → 3), `verb.move` (3), `verb.evade` (3). Pick `[J:enum]` **verb.exert** — the intended change is crossing a gap through the air (Exert's "jump"), not repositioning on passable ground (Move vs Exert test). The plain card is wrong for the obstacle (a chain changes a Beyond-tier jump into a swing), so `find_rulings(verb.exert, [dc:tier_rederived, stakes])` → **r.0412** (WE-00-9: the gatehouse chain swing; Hard; Dire for a 20-ft fall). Same signature, same kind of case (a hanging chain or rope replacing an unjumpable crossing) → match. Differing fact `[J:flag]`: is there an established fact that changes tier, stakes or reach? **Yes** — `f.gallery_height = 12 ft`: a 12-ft fall is not ch.10's Heavy (S3) fall source (falls of 20 ft and more are) → stakes **Risky**, not Dire. Tier reused: **Hard**. Departure logged with `differing_fact: f.gallery_height`. Deltas used: `dc` (tier re-derived) and `stakes` (source: the 12-ft fall) — two knobs, at the limit. |
| B2 FRAME | Attribute `[J:enum]`: the swing's success is in timing and an exact landing → **Agility** +3 (Exert's listed alternative for "a precise leap"; not a knob change). Tag `deed.martial.athletics` → floor +1. Levers/snags: none cited. Obstacle `obs.toll_hall_swing`, tier Hard → DC **20**, written as its stored DC (key: obstacle + anchor signature). Threatened cost `cost.harm` (the fall, S2); alternate `cost.footing`. Reach Standard: onto the gallery, engaged with the archer. `frame_check` → +4 vs 20: need 16 · success-or-better **25%** (crit success 5, success 20, failure 45, crit failure 30; near miss 15). |
| — | Pause point 1: 25% < 50% → no auto-commit. B3 is queued: its frame is built after B2's RECORD (01.14.1). |

> You take the stair two at a time; the lantern chain is cold and gritty in your fists, the gallery rail a
> long swing away above the boards, and up there the archer is cranking his crossbow back, eyes on you.
>
> `[OFFER] Swing on the lantern chain to the gallery — verb.exert (Exert), anchor 01.18.11, ruling r.0412 (departed: f.gallery_height 12 ft)`
> `Roll: Agility +3 · competence +1 (deed) = +4   ·   Against: DC 20 — Hard (precedent r.0412)`
> `Need: 16+ · 25% · crit success 5% · crit failure 30% · near miss 15%`
> `Stakes: Risky — failure: Harm (S2), the fall · crit failure: Harm (S3) · near miss: succeed and pay Harm or Footing (S2), or fail`
> `Reach: Standard — success: you land on the gallery, at his reach`
> `Costs: 1 action · rides: no · fate 1   ·   Then (queued): kick the archer off the rail`
> `→ commit · change · withdraw   (one trade: go big / play it safe)`

*DM turn 2. Player:* "Play it safe — I just want to get to the rail. Commit." The trade (01.7.3): stakes
Risky → **Safe** (failure: you swing back to the stair; critical failure: an S1 cost), reach Standard →
**Limited** (partway: hanging at the rail). `roll_check`: d20 = **16** → total 20 vs 20 → **success**;
delivered reach 1. RECORD: `set_position(pc.wren, {band_to: {adv.toll_archer_02: band.engaged}})`; fact
`pc.wren.hanging_from_gallery_rail = true` (the Limited reach's "partway"); ruling **r.0533** logged
(signature `verb.exert+dc:tier_rederived+stakes`, `precedent: {status: departed, from: r.0412,
differing_fact: f.gallery_height}`, `review_flag: true` per 01.5.4 because it departed). Sequential feed:
success → B3 gains what B2 was for — Wren is at the archer's reach.

B3 FRAME (built now, so B2's facts are established before it): GATE G1 `verb.force` (topple); ANCHOR
`verb.force`, no deltas; against the archer's higher defense — Agility: 10 + 3 + 2 = **15**. Attribute Might
+1 (Force allows only Might); `deed.martial.athletics` → floor +1. **Lever** (Precision): `adv.toll_archer_02.loaded
= false` — he is busy spanning the crossbow, a distracted target (the player cited it: "before he can
reload") → +2. **Lever** (Amplifying): `f.gallery_height` with the rail at his back — a drop that makes
success go further → reach +1. **Snag** (Precision): `pc.wren.hanging_from_gallery_rail` — kicking while
hanging is done worse → −2. Total +1 +1 +2 −2 = **+2**; reach Standard +1 = **Great**; stakes Risky:
threatened `cost.footing` (you lose your grip and drop), alternate `cost.harm` (S2). Need 13 · **40%**
(crit success 5, success 35, failure 45, crit failure 15; near miss 15). Pause point 1 again (40% < 50%).

*DM turn 3. Player:* "Commit." d20 = **12** → total 14 vs 15 → **failure, near miss** (margin −1). Pause
point 4:
> `[NEAR MISS] 14 vs 15. Succeed and pay one — (a) Footing (S2): you lose your grip and drop · (b) Harm (S2): your shoulder wrenches as you kick — or (c) let it fail (Footing S2 applies).`

*DM turn 4. Player:* "(b) — I'll take the shoulder." READ: success at a cost, delivered reach Great (3) →
pushed two bands, or prone and off-balance (01.18.10): over the rail and down. `apply_costs(cost.harm, S2,
form: "wrenched shoulder")` → Wren Vitality 13 → **10**. Archer: `set_position` (floor, `band.near` from Wren),
`cond.prone`; the fall is a ch.10 hazard resolved by the engine for him *(illustrative: S2, 3 harm → 8 → 5)*.
T5: the other foe (the toll-keeper's mate, at `band.far`) acts on his turn from his behavior list (ch.09) —
he runs for the bell; ch.06 orders it after Wren's turn.

T7 draft (first version): "You lash out with both heels; the archer pitches over the rail and his crossbow
clatters to the boards. You haul yourself up onto the gallery, your shoulder screaming, as the toll-keeper's
mate bolts for the bell rope." T9 claim check:
- "pitches over the rail" — `outcome`/`position` ✓ (delivered Great; position written).
- "his crossbow clatters to the boards" — `possession`: no write moved the crossbow → **unsourced_change**
  → cut (the archer is prone on the floor with his weapon).
- "You haul yourself up onto the gallery" — `position`: Wren's position is *hanging at the rail* (Limited
  delivered on B2; nothing since moved her) → **unsourced_change** → cut. Hauling herself up is a new beat
  the player has not declared (and `pc_agency`).
- "your shoulder screaming" — `harm_condition` ✓ (the chosen cost's form).
- "bolts for the bell rope" — ✓ (the mate's behavior result this round).
Redraft 1 passes. T10 ✓ (intent acknowledged, nothing substituted: the kick happened as declared; open
prompt). Delivered:
> You lash out with both heels from the rail. Something in your shoulder tears hot as the kick lands —
> and the archer pitches backward over the rail and hits the boards below, sprawled beside his crossbow.
> You hang from the gallery rail by one good arm, at the height of a man and a half over the floor. Across
> the hall the toll-keeper's mate is running for the bell rope. What do you do?
>
> `[RESULT] d20 12 → 14 vs 15 · near miss → success at a cost: Harm (S2), wrenched shoulder · reach Great`
> `[RESULT] Changed: Vitality 13 → 10`

*What the trace shows.* The wild idea was never refused and never waved through: it was split into the
beats it really contained, the novel beat reached for the nearest anchor and the ledger, the precedent's
numbers were reused except where an established fact differed (and that departure is logged and flagged),
the player saw the odds and traded ambition for safety, and the claim check caught two of the most common
narration errors in the project's own logs — a possession change and a position change that no tool wrote
(R4 W9). *Non-example:* ruling the whole sentence as one Exert at DC 15 "because it's cool" and narrating
the archer off the rail on a success — three methods compressed into one roll (01.2.3), a lenient tier
chosen for drama (SG-01), and a precedent ignored (INV-19).

cards.title: Full turn-loop trace 3: a soft-lock broken by lead injection
cards.body:
### WE-12-3 Full turn-loop trace 3: a soft-lock broken by lead injection

*Situation.* Back in Ashford the next morning. The player chases the burned rope but makes no headway.
Counter at 0.

| Beat | Declaration and resolution | Inconclusive? | Counter |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "I search the ferryman's hut." Observe, Safe, Standard; DC 15 *(stored: the hut holds no clue placement; a sealed Oracle at creation said nothing is hidden)*. Secret frame. d20 = 9 → 12: failure → one vague impression: "someone left in a hurry" — but the hut's state was already narrated (dark, door shut) and the impression adds no fact the PC can act on. | yes: no new fact, no clock, no position, no reach | 1 |
| 2 | "Do I know anyone in town who'd want Hob gone?" Recall (common knowledge of Ashford). Safe. d20 = 6 → total 6 vs Easy 10: failure — nothing comes to mind. | yes | 2 |
| 3 | "I look for tracks along the riverbank." Observe with tracking: Wits +2, `deed.wilds.tracking` +2 = +4 vs Moderate 15 *(three nights of rain; stored tier)*; Safe. d20 = 7 → 11: failure, Safe → nothing. | yes | **3 → `trg.lead_injection` raised** |

*DM turn after beat 3.* T3 returns `trg.lead_injection`; it must be handled this turn (12.2.3). PR-12-3:
1. **Source ladder.** Rung 1: unfound clue placements of the scene's thread (`thr.missing_ferryman`):
   `clu.toll_ledger` (Grey Keep; reachable — a half-day's travel) and `clu.daughter_purse` (Maren, in
   Ashford; reachable now). Both eligible → tie. List weights: neither placement's holder is on the cast
   list (Maren not met; the toll-keeper met once, weight 1). Rotation ledger: `social` pillar at 7 scenes
   (overdue, threshold 6) vs `travel` at 3 → **Maren** (the stalest axis wins the tie).
2. **Form.** `roll_table(tbl.lead_injection, {phase: build})` d12 = **11**: "A plea for help from someone
   caught up in it." Fit `[J:flag]`: can Maren plausibly come asking for help finding her father? **Yes.**
3. **Tests.** Concrete (Maren, a named person) ✓; actionable now (she is here) ✓; connected (holder of
   `clu.daughter_purse`) ✓. Does not solve the thread (her purse clue stays sealed until a Talk unseals
   it) ✓; costs nothing ✓; not a threat ✓.
4. **Write.** Maren steps from walk-on to recurring (12.11.1) — she already exists with the thread's
   generated fields (name, gender, age) and now gains want "find — the truth about the past" (d20 = 2 /
   10), fear "being found out" (d12 = 6), voice register nervous (d8 = 6), habit "apologizes constantly"
   (d20 = 14), refusal "will not speak of their past" (d12 = 5); first interaction → reaction roll: she is
   unaffiliated; modifier +1 (Wren arrives as someone she hopes will help — `[J:flag]` citing the fact
   that she sought Wren out); 2d6 = 7 + 1 = **8 → Neutral (0)**. Fact `npc.maren_coldwell.approaches
   pc.wren`; `record_knowledge(pc.wren, "Maren is Hob's daughter", how: told)`. Counter → **0**.
5. **Narrate** it in this turn's world responses.
> The bank gives you nothing but rain-flattened reeds. As you straighten, a young woman is picking her way
> down the steps toward you, a shawl over her head, ink on her fingers. "Sorry — I'm sorry, you're the one
> who was asking after the ferryman? He's my father. Hob. Nobody will tell me anything." She glances back
> up the steps, then at you. "Please. I think he took money from someone, the day before."
> What do you do?

Her last sentence is the *offer* of a lead, not the clue: what she knows (the Guild silver) is still behind
`clu.daughter_purse`'s gate — a Talk to win her trust over her refusal to speak of the past (ch.15). *Boundary
pair.* After beat 2 the counter stood at 2: no injection — the DM's per-beat next-step check (12.8.3) was
satisfied by the visible riverbank and toll-house options. Had beat 3 succeeded (tracks found), the counter
would have reset and no injection would fire. *Non-examples:* (a) having a fishwife blurt "the Salt Guild
took him!" — that solves the thread (forbidden) and invents knowledge she lacks (12.10.6); (b) inventing a
fourth clue ("a Guild badge in the mud") — narration may not create clues (12.14.13); (c) waiting for the
player to ask for help — P16 says the DM must act at three.

cards.title: Error correction: one caught before delivery, one after
cards.body:
### WE-12-4 Error correction: one caught before delivery, one after

**(a) Caught before the player saw it: the pronoun slip.** At the toll-house a week later, the draft
reads: "The toll-keeper looks up from her ledger." T9: `identity` claim "her" for `npc.toll_keeper_01` —
the store has no gender for this walk-on → verdict **undetermined** → `roll_table(tbl.npc_gender)` d10 = **7** → man, he/him, written →
redraft: "The toll-keeper looks up from his ledger." The player never sees the slip. (An earlier turn's T8 wrote the toll-keeper without the gender roll — itself an error the sweep would have
caught at scene end.) This is the exact
failure the project's first probe recorded and its self-assessment missed [C:P13]; the claim check catches
it because identity is a checked class, not because the DM "noticed".

**(b) Caught after delivery.** Turn 41: Wren's Observe in the toll-house archive succeeded and delivered an
item — an iron key on a hook (`obj.key_cellar` unsealed, `location: archive hook`). The delivered narration
said: "…an iron key hangs on a nail by the door. **You pocket it.**" The claim check that turn missed the
`pc_agency` + `possession` claim (no possession write; the player never said to take it). Turn 42 the player
talked with the toll-keeper about the tolls; turn 43 left the archive for the cellar stair. Turn 44: "I
unlock the cellar door with the key I took."
1. **T4 GATE** finds `obj.key_cellar` not in Wren's possessions → mismatch with the turn-41 narration →
   PR-12-4.
2. **Truth.** Is there a resolved source requiring possession (`[J:flag]`)? The frame delivered the key's
   *existence*; no beat took it → **narration error**; the store stands (the key is on the hook).
3. **Reliance.** Committed beats since turn 41 that cited, targeted or premised the key: turn 42's Talk did
   not mention it; turn 44's beat has not been committed (it is at GATE) → **no reliance**.
4. **Form.** An in-fiction reconciliation would need a new fact (that she dropped it, or never took it in
   some invented way) → not allowed → **OOF note**. Spent quantities because of it: none.
5. **Log**: correction record `{turn_of_error: 41, found: 44, by: gate, claim: "pc holds obj.key_cellar",
   store: "obj.key_cellar on the archive hook", kind: narration_error, form: oof_note, reliance: false}`;
   ruling `review_flag: true` (12.12.4: a correction).
Then the turn proceeds: the unlock beat is redirected by lookup — the cellar door is locked
(`door_cellar.locked = true`), the key exists and is reachable, so the nearest path is to fetch it
(picking it up is a free activity, 00.12.6; walking back up the stair is Trivial, 1 action):
> `[CORRECTION] On turn 41 I narrated you pocketing the iron key; you never took it — it is still on the nail by the archive door. Nothing you did relied on it. Logged.`
>
> The cellar door is solid oak, banded, locked. The key you saw is upstairs on its nail in the archive,
> a short climb back. What do you do?

*Variant with reliance.* Had turn 42 been "I show the toll-keeper the key and ask what it opens" (a Talk,
committed and rolled, premised on holding the key), reliance would be **true**, the beat in the current
scene: CHOICE — **keep** is not available (the frame's premise rested on the false possession); **accept
forward** (the conversation happened as resolved; Wren simply was not holding the key — the toll-keeper
answered a description) or **rewind** to before turn 42 (`revert_writes`; the Talk's roll logged void; the
player re-declares). *Non-example:* writing the key into Wren's possessions "since the narration already
said so" — a change written to match prose (INV-1; 12.3.2's asymmetry). The narration was wrong; the world
was not.

cards.title: An NPC from first mention to memory
cards.body:
### WE-12-5 An NPC from first mention to memory

Wren walks into the Drowned Lantern. Draft T8 mentions "the man behind the bar" → a person, addressable →
cast list check: no barkeeper generated yet → **walk-on** (PR-12-5): role "innkeeper or tavern-keeper" (the
narration implies it; no roll); name `tbl.name_given` d100 = 29 → **Osric**, `tbl.name_family` d100 = 30
→ **Pike**; gender d10 = 9 → man, he/him; age d6 = 5 → middle-aged; detail d100 = 85 → "a ledger always
under one arm"; demeanor d12 = 11 → sly. Written before the narration; the narration calls him "the
barkeeper with the ledger under his arm" — not "Osric": Wren has not learned his name (12.10.2).

First interaction ("I ask the barkeeper if Hob Coldwell drinks here"): reaction roll — Osric is
unaffiliated as far as the store knows *(his Salt Guild tie is undetermined; it is settled only if he
becomes principal)*; modifiers: Wren arrives as a customer (+1); no others → 2d6 = **4** + 1 = 5 → **Wary
(−1)**. The question is SPEECH plus a FICTION_QUESTION about Osric's knowledge: does he know Hob drinks
here? Role knowledge (a barkeeper knows his regulars) → (d) common knowledge of the role → yes, and
whether he *tells* is his decision: no frame (Wren did not try to persuade), no want or refusal yet →
`tbl.npc_action` d10 = 5 + standing −1 = **4** → "wants something first: names a price". Voice: not yet
recorded (walk-on) — the DM voices him plainly; after this second-scene interaction trigger he will gain
want, fear, voice and refusal.
> The barkeeper doesn't look up from his ledger. "Hob? Might do. Might not." He turns a page. "Memory's a
> thirsty thing, friend."

Memory (12.11.7): written at RECORD — `{npc: npc.osric_pike, deed: "Wren asked after Hob Coldwell",
valence: none of the twelve fits a mere question → no memory}`; *boundary pair:* had Wren paid him (a
`helped` exchange, salience 1) or threatened him (`threatened`, salience 3 with a standing change), a
memory would be written, and the next time Wren walks in, `[J:flag]` "does a memory bear on this
exchange?" → the threatened memory (salience 3) leads his first line ("You. Back again — keep your hands on
the bar where I can see them.").

cards.title: Scene framing, the scene test, and the tension update
cards.body:
### WE-12-6 Scene framing, the scene test, and the tension update

*Tension update after WE-12-2's toll-house scene.* Chaos points: an opposition clock completed? No.
Cost S3+? No (S2). Staggered? No. Twist? No. Interrupt? No. The agenda ("Does Wren take the toll-house
before the bell is rung?") — answered at scene end: the mate reached the bell and rang it (ch.09 behavior;
the alarm clock completed) → **against** the hope (+1 chaos) and **opposition clock completed** (+1 chaos).
Control points: the PC overcame part of the opposition paying no cost heavier than S2 — the archer was
dropped, but the scene's opposition was not overcome (the mate rang the bell) → 0. Chaos 2 > control 0 →
**tension 5 → 6**. Intensity: conflict 2 + failed frames 0 (a near miss taken as success at a cost is not a failed frame) +
cost S2 paid 1 + opposition clock completed 2 = **5** → intensity max(5, 0 − 3) = 5 < 7 → still
BUILD.

*Next scene.* The player: "I ride back to Ashford and go to the Drowned Lantern to find someone who drinks
with Hob." Scene start: agenda "Who drinks with Hob, and what do they know?"; hope: yes. Expected scene:
"Wren finds Hob's drinking companion at the Lantern." `h.12.scene_test`: d10 = **3** ≤ 6 − 3 = 3 → deviates;
odd → **altered**. `tbl.scene_adjustment` d10 = **10** → "someone is already here for the same reason" →
walk-on (role from the adjustment: a stranger asking after Hob; gender d10 = **3** → woman; detail and
demeanor rolled; written). Is she with the Salt Guild? The DM's own question: Oracle **Even** (the Guild is
active in the thread, but nothing ties her to it yet), eventful `none`; d100 = **58** → yes → fact, and her
Guild sash is now an established visible detail. The drinking companion the player expects: his existence
is the player's premise — Oracle **Likely** (a regular has drinking friends), d100 = **47** → yes → walk-on.
Framing `[J:enum]`: **at the threshold** (new place, social). Impetus (a): the alteration.
> The Lantern is low-beamed and loud with fishermen; smoke hangs under the rafters. At the corner table
> by the hearth, a woman in a Salt Guild sash is leaning over a frightened-looking old man, speaking low —
> and you hear Hob's name. The door to the yard stands open behind them. What do you do?
*Boundary pair.* At tension 5, the same d10 = 3 would be > 2 → expected: Wren finds the old drinker alone.
*Non-example:* adding the Guild woman because the scene "needs tension" — no roll put her there.

cards.title: A random event from Oracle doubles
cards.body:
### WE-12-7 A random event from Oracle doubles

The DM needs to know (for the narration of the Lantern) whether the keeper is behind the bar — its own
question: "Is the barkeeper at the bar?" Odds **Likely** (an inn at evening); eventful `none`. d100 = **33**
→ doubles; digit 3 ≤ tension 6 → **random event**, and the answer is extreme: **yes, and** (01.15.3).
- The "and": `tbl.meaning` (action) → verb d100 = **99** "warn" + subject d100 = **60** "a messenger" →
  interpretation, written as a fact: "and a messenger has just warned him to say nothing about the ferry"
  (`source: generation`) — a fact the player may uncover; it does not reveal any sealed clue.
- The event: `tbl.event_focus` d100 = **37** → **faction move**; faction list (weights: Salt Guild 2,
  Ash Wardens 1) roll → **Salt Guild**; meaning: verb d100 = **88** "seize" + subject d100 = **52** "a tax"
  → "Guild men are nailing up a notice: from today the Guild collects the ferry toll." Writes: `set_fact`
  (the notice; the Guild's claim on the toll); one tick on `clk.corner_the_salt_road` *(illustrative; it
  lists `random_event` as a tick source, as ch.11's goal clocks do)* [editor: E2-043].
- Bounds checked: no harm, no cost, no license, no sealed fact, no thread resolved.
> Behind the bar, the keeper is pouring, his jaw tight; a boy in a Guild-blue cap is just slipping out past
> you. Through the window, two men are hammering a notice to the ferry-post across the lane.

cards.title: Pacing: a setback, a recovery window, and a push
cards.body:
### WE-12-8 Pacing: a setback, a recovery window, and a push

Three scenes later Wren loses a fight in the reeds to Guild riders and **yields** (ch.07) — a setback
(12.7.5). Intensity: conflict 2 + Dire failure 2 + cost S3 2 + Staggered 3 = 9 (capped 10) → **9** ≥ 7 →
PEAK; the scene ends → `standard` profile: **recovery for 3 scenes** (RELAX regardless of intensity).
During recovery: the scene test's *interrupted* reads as *altered*; an Oracle-doubles random event that
rolls *PC complication* (67–74) reads as *omen*; no pacing push. The World Turn still runs, and the riders'
clock still ticks from its own sources — the director suppresses only its own pushes. Lead injection would
still fire, without threat forms.

When recovery ends, `trg.pacing_push` is raised for the next `scene_start`. Candidates: (a) ch.11 bangs —
"the riders return to the landing" (threat, delta 3), "Maren is followed" (keyed to an NPC the PC dealt
with, delta 3), "a Guild clerk offers Wren work" (keyed to this PC's deed — the toll-house — delta 1);
(b) `tbl.vignette`; (c) the overdue rotation opportunity (`downtime` at 9 scenes). Phase target after
recovery: delta ≤ 1 and advisory ≤ fair → (a1) and (a2) are out; the clerk's offer (delta 1, keyed to this
PC and their deed — the most specific rung) wins over the vignette and the generic downtime opportunity.
*Non-example:* softening the riders' Vitality in the reeds fight once Wren was losing (12.7.6) — the
adaptation comes *after* the setback, as a choice of what comes next, never as a hidden edit.

cards.title: Rotation, check-in weights, and the tie-break
cards.body:
### WE-12-9 Rotation, check-in weights, and the tie-break

At session 4's start the check-in (12.5.9) records: fights **less**, investigating **more**, others same.
Pillar thresholds become: conflict 12, investigation 3, others 6. Ledger after the next scene: investigation
4 (overdue: 4 ≥ 3), exploration 5, conflict 2, social 0. Facets: `deed.martial.archery` (specialty) 9 scenes
— **overdue** (8); `ab.quarrys_mark` *(illustrative; 05)* untested, acquired 6 scenes ago — **overdue** (4) [verification: V2b-019].
Framing the next scene, the impetus list reaches (f): the stalest axis relative to threshold is the untested
ability (6/4 = 1.5, ahead of investigation's 4/3 ≈ 1.33 and archery's 9/8) → an opportunity where marking a quarry would matter is put in front of Wren — drawn from
state: the Guild woman from WE-12-6 is seen leaving town on the north road at dusk (a quarry to follow and
mark). Nothing forces Wren to use the ability; the opportunity is simply there.

cards.title: Session open, a flag, and an adjust
cards.body:
### WE-12-10 Session open, a flag, and an adjust

*Session open.* `h.12.session_open`: preferences re-read (a flag "harm to children" set at session zero);
recap from state (120 words max, from the chronicle and the threads); then:
> `[SITUATION] Where: Ashford, Maren's cottage, morning · Pressing: The riders' search (sensed) · Threads: The missing ferryman; Corner the Salt Road · Open offers: the Guild clerk's work · Last time you said: "find out where they took Hob"`
The last session ended at rest with nothing pressing that scene → `tbl.vignette` d12 = **2** "someone you
know is in trouble" (threat-tagged; phase BUILD, allowed) → rooted in an existing NPC: Maren's younger
brother has not come home. The brother is a child → the content carries the flag's tag → FLAG pause before
narrating it:
> `[FLAG] This touches harm to children. Continue, veil it, or steer away?`
The player: "Steer away." → **adjust** (12.5.7), *replace*: the troubled person becomes Maren's elderly
neighbor (same mechanical weight: a known NPC in trouble, the same vignette row), written as a superseding
fact; logged in the safety ledger, not as a correction.

*Session close.* The player: "Let's stop." Wren is mid-conversation (no frame past ROLL) → nothing to
finish; `mark_boundary(session_end)`; the review list compiles one flagged record this session (r.0533's
departure); no Principle III candidate (one record, one session);
> `[SESSION] Ending here — anything to focus on next time? (optional)`
> You leave Maren at her door with the morning still grey; the north road waits.

cards.title: A world from nothing: the High Fells (the world seed, oracle mode)
cards.body:
### WE-12-11 A world from nothing: the High Fells (the world seed, oracle mode)

The player opens a new game with no setting. Session zero's preferences are recorded (12.5.1); the DM asks
the mode, and the player says "surprise me": oracle mode (12.16.2). Every number below is
`_process/simulation/12-world-seed.py`'s seed 1, committed as `12-world-seed-example.yaml` [revision: I-028].

| Step | Rolled (oracle) | What it wrote |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Premise | wound **invasion**; climate **highland** | the High Fells: *"The horde came down from the passes twenty-three winters ago and burned the High Fells to the river. It was driven back. The watchfires on the passes were lit again this spring."* Three truths (the horde gathers again; some veterans took its gold; the pass forts are under-held). The wound's age: 23, rolled in the invasion's 20–30 [revision: I-069]. |
| 2 Canon | magic **rare**; open magic **feared**; spirits rare; arcane: anyone literate; one extra impossibility; no regrowth; no school closed | `canon_impossible`: the six defaults plus "No working makes gold, silver or gems". A visible working in Merestead's market is a method consequence (01.11.2). |
| 3 Faith | three keepers: war, knowledge, sky; bargainer: a tempter | **Oswen, Lord of the Line** (smiting, oaths, warding; courage +, loyalty +) is the main keeper; Halda, the Keeper of Keys, and Ala, the High One, have petty faiths. `canon.default_bargainer = arch.tempter`. |
| 4 Peoples | halflings common; humans, orc-kin and beastfolk uncommon; dwarves, goblin-kin and giant-kin rare; elves absent | seven name tables (humans uncommon: one style; the orc-kin's also serves the horde); second tongue: the Old Tongue, "the speech of the time before the Burning". |
| 5 Land | ring 1 farmland and hills; rings 2–5 mostly mountains and hills, a ruin, a moor, a wood | 13 areas (3, 3, 3, 2, 2) with T-10-2's bands and ratings (both ring-5 areas rolled 4, so the Tangled Ridge is home 5 [revision: I-084]), 35 places in all, every one reachable from the haven. |
| 6 Haven | a **town** at a **harbour** | **Merestead**: temple of Oswen (consecrated, resonance divine), the Golden Hound inn, smithy, hall, quay, market square, healer's house, graveyard; market depth 150; hire up to band 2. Place of acceptance: Shepwell Spring and its lady (weather, growth, elements). |
| 7 Factions | rulers **a noble house**; fourth **a town council** | the lords of Hawkgate (tier 2, goal 4/12: *humble the rival house*); the faithful of Oswen (tier 2, 3/12); **the Horde of the Millwick** (tier 3, aggressive, 4/12: *break the watch on the passes and burn the lowlands again*; −2 to both); the council of Merestead (tier 0, 1/8); two petty faiths on 6-segment `petty_goals` clocks (1/6 each): Halda's would *win more of Merestead to it, and a hold of its own*, Ala's would *settle its quarrel with the faithful of Oswen* (a feud) [revision: I-070]. Every linchpin's four fates sealed. |
| 8 Cast | 12.11.1's tables | 17 NPCs: heads and officers (Tible of the Wet Warren, the goblin-kin lord; Milby Greenfoot, Oswen's halfling priest; Brugnak Three-Scar of the horde), the smith, innkeeper, gate captain Loran Millbrook and the sellsword Zzirik Swift (both recruitable), Shepwell's wise-woman, a scribe, a healer. 12 teachings (`12-world-seed-output.txt`, `ws.req.15_teachers`) [verification: V2b-020]. The powers of the far rings (4 more, 21 in all) [revision: I-083]: Magwen Thistlefoot, a hermit-judge whom the old lands still obey (the Still Heath, band 4), and Selda Thornwell, an archmage in a tower that should have fallen (the Lonely Ridge, band 4); Sketaa of the Reed Clan, an exiled heir and her court (the Broken Greenwood, band 5), and Ymmulf of the Long Winter, master of a lost guild's last hall (the Tangled Ridge, band 5); each keeps a sealed truth. |
| 9 Sites | 9 sites and 2 lairs | e.g. Whitfield's Temple (haunted temple, band 1: *the dead rising tonight*, sealed); **Wolfcrag's Delving** (fortified mine, band 3: the horde's seat); lairs Whitmouth's Undercroft (band 5) and the Delving of Ashhollow (band 5). Situations: *War comes* in the Hungry Pikes (step 1 done: the levy called) and *The hunting ground* in the Sunken Fells (a savaged ewe). |
| 10 Tables | PR-10-10 at each area's band | 13 regional tables, all passing PR-10-8. The Drowned Ridge (home 2): 4–6 raptor minions and two orcs at band 1; a dwarf holdguard elite, a monstrous beast elite (complication), two frost elementals, two ancestor spirits at band 2; a bear minion and a wyvern minion at band 3. Words: 6 trivial, 3 easy, 11 fair. |
| 11 Rumors | `tbl.11.rumor_truth` per site | 20 rumors (8 true, 7 partial, 5 false) [verification: V2b-020]: "Word is that the Horde of the Millwick will try to break the watch on the passes…" (true); "Whitfield's Temple is empty now" (false). |
| 12 Calendar | months **named** | the Month of Thaw, Plough, Lambing-month…; Oswen's Day (spring), the Midsummer Fair, Harvest Home, the Night of Remembrance; the era "years since the Burning". |
| 13 Opening | incident **alarm** | the spring quarter day, 23 years since the Burning (the pitch's twenty-three winters) [revision: I-069], dawn, Merestead's gate: the haven's alarm sounds, and something from the wound is at the gate. Leads: the war situation (the incident), *The hunting ground* ("a savaged ewe; folk say it is only the beginning"), the council's goal (it is hiring). Pregens: Tamred Stoneby (Soldier), Magly Mughill (halfling Thief), Tamric Ashsmith (Courtier), Evo Elderward (Acolyte of Oswen). |
| 14 Check | T-12-16 | 64 of 64 requirements hold. |

*Boundary pair — guided.* A second player answers fourteen questions themselves (a long winter, northern,
rare magic, two keepers of hearth and death, the death keeper bargains, a hill village ruled by a family, a
refugee opening, named months, no teleporting, the Old Tongue, and who may learn arcane magic) and leaves the
rest to the oracle (`12-world-seed.py`'s guided run): the result also passes 64 of 64. Their custom answer "magic is something only the old families do" is not
an option of `ws.q.arcane_source`; 12.16.2 classifies it as `order_only` (an admitting order: the old
families) and keeps their words as the canon fact's text — shown in `[SEED 2/14]`, where the player could
have corrected it.

*Boundary pair — a veto.* Had the player vetoed step 7's rulers (`[SEED 7/14]`), the d6 is rolled again
once, and steps 8–14 re-run, because the cast, sites, rumors and opening all read the factions.

*Tempting non-example.* Mid-session the player asks "who rules the next valley?" and the DM, remembering
nothing in the seed, answers "a cruel baroness". Wrong: a faction is never invented in narration (11.3.18).
The question is a FICTION_QUESTION (T4): the next valley is a new region past ring 5, so 12.16.18 runs steps
5, 9, 10 and 11 for it and 11.3.18's new-region rule writes its factions before a word is said.

cards.title: What this game is
cards.body: ### 14.1 What this game is

cards.title: The premise, as told to a new player
cards.body:
**14.1.1 The premise, as told to a new player.** `[N]` [C:P7; DL-00-02; DL-14-01] *You play one person in
a dangerous, living fantasy world. You say what they do, in your own words, anything you can imagine, and
the game tells you what happens. There are no classes to pick and no levels to grind: the world watches
what you actually do, and in time recognizes you for it as a ranger, a smith, a healer, a liar, a lord. The
world keeps moving without you. Death is real, but it never comes unannounced: when something can kill
you, the game says so before you commit.* The DM reads this aloud at session zero (PR-14-1 step 1), in
these words or close to them.

cards.title: What a roleplaying game is (for someone who has never played)
cards.body:
**14.1.2 What a roleplaying game is (for someone who has never played).** `[N]` [R5 OB-01; DL-14-01] It is
a conversation.
- The game describes a situation, and you say what your character does.
- When the outcome is uncertain and something is at stake, the game shows you the odds and what could go
  wrong (an OFFER, 01.7). You decide whether to go ahead.
- A die is rolled and the game tells you the result. The world changes, and the conversation continues.

There is no winning or losing. There is a story about one person, and how far they get.

cards.title: The three promises the game makes
cards.body:
**14.1.3 The three promises the game makes.** `[D]` [C:VII; DL-07-01; DL-14-01] These are stated at
session zero (PR-14-1 step 2) and are binding:
1. **You will see the odds before every risky roll**, and nothing you are shown will turn out false
   (01.7.2, 00.6.4).
2. **Death is telegraphed.** No harm can kill your character unless the lethal warning was delivered first
   for that source (07.3.3) and the frame was shown as lethal (07.3.6). Lethal frames never roll without
   your explicit commit (01.7.4).
3. **Your safety settings override everything** (00.1.5; 12.5.6). Lines never appear. Veiled
   content happens off-screen. Any content can be adjusted at any time without explanation (12.5.7).

cards.title: How to play
cards.body: ### 14.2 How to play

cards.title: Say what you do, not which rule to use
cards.body:
**14.2.1 Say what you do, not which rule to use.** `[N]` [R5 OB-06; R7; DL-14-02] Describe intent and
method ("I climb the chimney to come down behind them"). The DM finds the governing rule (00.15) and frames
it. You never need to know a rule's name. You may still ask for one at any time (12.5.10).

cards.title: Anything can be tried
cards.body:
**14.2.2 Anything can be tried.** `[N]` [C:II; 01.3; DL-14-02] If an action is physically or magically
impossible for your character, the game says why and offers what *is* possible (a REDIRECT, 12.15.5). It
never says no without a path. Unusual ideas are expected. Using the environment, talking instead of
fighting, retreating, bargaining, and preparing are all real options with real rules behind them.

cards.title: Read the OFFER, then choose
Offers of recognition
cards.body:
**14.2.4 Offers of recognition.** `[N]` [04.7.1; 04.7.2; DL-14-02] Sometimes the game offers your character
a calling, a tier or an oath, in an OUT-OF-FICTION block marked `[RECOGNITION]`. You can always accept,
decline or defer. Declining costs nothing and the offer can return (04.7.7). An accepted grant that is still provisional
can be set aside at any rest, at no cost (04.8.2) [editor: E2-051].

cards.title: When things go wrong for you
cards.body:
**14.2.5 When things go wrong for you.** `[N]` [12.3.6; 12.5.7; DL-14-02]
- **The game made a mistake.** Type `/fix` and say what, or just say so ("that's wrong"). It checks the whole
  record, then corrects the error, takes back a beat it got wrong, or shows you the line it went by. On small
  details the record can't settle, your reading wins (12.3.6) [revision: R2-G].
- **Content isn't working for you.** Say "adjust", "skip this", or "X". The DM reframes at once and never
  asks why (12.5.7).
- **You don't know what to do.** Say "I'm stuck". You will get concrete options from the current situation
  (12.8.5).

cards.title: The codex
cards.body:
**14.2.6 The codex.** `[N]` [C:P7; DL-14-03] Ask for your codex at any time ("show my codex", "what do I
know about X", "what are my abilities"). It is your character sheet, journal and rulebook in one. It shows
only what your character could know (14.6).

cards.title: The OFFER's words
cards.body:
**14.2.7 The OFFER's words.** `[N]` [revision: R2-C] [12.15.2; DL-12-51] The glossary `?` explains from. The words are fixed, so the same
word always means the same odds or the same price.

| Word | Means |
|---|---|
| almost certain · likely · better than even · even | 95% · 75–90% · 55–70% · 45–50% to succeed |
| unlikely · long shot · only by luck | 25–40% · 10–20% · 5% |
| a long shot (as a label) | failing badly is likelier than succeeding; the OFFER shows a better way first |
| a nuisance · a setback · serious · grave | how bad a failure's price is, from mildest to worst |
| THIS CAN KILL YOU | this roll can leave you dying; you were warned before, and may back off |
| Danger | a failure here costs something serious, even before a bad roll |
| partly · what you wanted · more than you asked | how much a success gets you |
| very well · badly | a critical success, a critical failure |
| close call | you just missed: take what you wanted and pay the price shown, or fail |
| Go big | if it works you get more; if it fails it costs more; same chance |
| Play it safe | if it works you get less; if it fails it costs less; same chance |
| Another way | other approaches the game worked out for you, each with its chance |
| you can't judge how hard this is | the roll is hidden; you see only what your character perceives |
| improvising without training | harder, and at best a partial result (you lack the training) |
| auto | a safe, likely roll made without asking you (you can turn this off) |

At every pause, **Enter** does the labelled default (printed as `[Enter] …`), letters pick the others, and `?`
explains a word. Enter never backs you out of anything.

**Something wrong?** Type `/fix` and say what: a fact or name remembered wrong, a rule applied wrong, a
contradiction, or an action read wrong. The game checks the record and fixes it (12.3.6) [revision: R2-G].

cards.title: Session zero
cards.body: ### 14.3 Session zero

cards.title: Session zero comes first, and is short
cards.body:
**14.3.1 Session zero comes first, and is short.** `[D]` [12.5.1; R5 SC-03; DL-14-04] The first session
opens with session zero (PR-14-1). Then come the world seed (12.16, PR-12-9), character creation (02), and
the seed's opening scene (12.16.16). Every question in it is optional, and a skipped answer takes its
default (T-14-1). The whole of session zero is designed to take under ten exchanges. A player who says
"just start" receives the defaults and the premise, and play begins.

cards.title: What session zero records
Lethality consent is not optional
cards.body:
**14.3.3 Lethality consent is not optional.** `[D]` [C:VII; 07.3; DL-14-05] The player must acknowledge
the lethality promise (14.1.3 item 2) before character creation. This is the only answer session zero
requires. A player who wants no permanent death is offered the `death.mode: retire` preference (T-14-1).
Under it, a death result becomes The Road Ends (07.5.11, 07.5.14): the character leaves play alive, and
retirement, legacy and succession (11.13) still apply. Nothing about danger, warnings or odds changes. The fiction remains lethal in every
other respect.

cards.title: Progressive disclosure
cards.body: ### 14.4 Progressive disclosure

cards.title: Mechanics are taught when they first matter
cards.body:
**14.4.1 Mechanics are taught when they first matter.** `[D]` [R5 OB-05; 12.5.2; DL-14-06] When
`player.new_to_this` is `yes`, or was skipped (02.10.1), the DM appends one first-use note the first time
each item in T-14-2 appears. Notes are one OOF line each, after the fiction and before the OFFER, and each
is shown once per campaign. Experienced players see none. Any player may ask for any note again
("explain").

cards.title: The first-session teaching arc
The preference record
cards.body: ### 14.5 The preference record

cards.title: Shape and storage
cards.body:
**14.5.1 Shape and storage.** `[D]` [00.6.3; 00.14.2; DL-14-07] Preferences are facts on the subject
`player`, written with `set_fact(subject: player, predicate: pref.<key>, value, source: session_zero |
checkin | request, visibility: shown)` and read with `get_state(scope: codex, view: codex)` (00.14.2 #8) [editor: E2-053] or by the owning chapter's
handler. No separate preference tool exists: the preference record is the set of `pref.*` facts. A later
value supersedes the earlier one (00.14.2 #10), so the history is kept in the log. T-14-1 is the closed
list of keys, with their defaults and readers.

cards.title: Changing a preference
cards.body:
**14.5.2 Changing a preference.** `[D]` [12.5.9; DL-14-07] The player may change any preference at any
time by asking ("add a line: …", "turn on auto-commit"). The change takes effect from the next frame. A new
line also triggers 12.5.6's screen on anything already drafted. Preferences never change a difficulty
number, odds or cost (12.5.9). `death.mode` may be changed only between sessions, so that no one switches
it mid-danger.

cards.title: Lines, veils and flags are topics, not lists of words
cards.worst_case: a mapping that is too narrow lets adjacent content through. The safety screen at PR-12-1 step T10 (12.5.6) [editor: E2-054] and adjust (12.5.7) catch it, and the corrected mapping is recorded at the player's word.
cards.body:
**14.5.3 Lines, veils and flags are topics, not lists of words.** `[J:flag]` [12.5.6; R5 P-10; DL-14-08]
Each entry is recorded as a short topic in the player's own words, plus the tags the DM maps it to
(`safety.topic`, `tags: [...]`). The mapping is shown back to the player for confirmation ("I'll treat
'spiders' as spider creatures and webs as a threat; right?"). 12.5.6 screens content against the tags and
the topic text.
*Worst case (J):* a mapping that is too narrow lets adjacent content through. The safety screen at
PR-12-1 step T10 (12.5.6) [editor: E2-054] and adjust (12.5.7) catch it, and the corrected mapping is recorded at the player's word.

cards.title: The codex
cards.body: ### 14.6 The codex

cards.title: What the codex is
cards.body:
**14.6.1 What the codex is.** `[D]` [C:P7; 00.6.4; 00.14.2; DL-14-03] The codex is the `codex` tool's
render (00.14.2 #34) of the PC's state through `get_state(scope: codex, view: codex)`. It shows every `shown` item by
default and every `available` item on request. It **never** shows `background` or `sealed` state, in any
form: no number, no band, no "you sense…". Nothing the codex shows may be contradicted by narration
(00.6.4). If they disagree, it is a claim-check error (12.3), and the store wins.

cards.title: The views
cards.body:
**14.6.2 The views.** `[D]` [00.6.3; DL-14-03] The codex is organized as views (T-14-3). Each view's
contents are exactly the 00.6.3 families listed for it, at that family's visibility. A view reads state; it
never computes a value the owning chapter does not define. Computed sheet values come from 02.7.4 through
`evaluate` (00.14.2 #20).

cards.title: Asking the codex
cards.body:
**14.6.3 Asking the codex.** `[D]` [12.5.10; DL-14-09] The player may ask in natural language. The DM maps
the request to a view and an optional subject ("what do I know about the Ash Court" → Journal, filtered by
the subject's id) and returns the render. Questions about sealed or background things are answered with
"Your character doesn't know that", plus what the codex shows (12.5.10). The answer never includes a
hint.

cards.title: Rules entries
cards.body:
**14.6.4 Rules entries.** `[D]` [C:P7; 00.15; DL-14-09] The **Rules** view answers "how does X work?" for
any rule the PC has met, using the rule card's own text or a faithful one-line paraphrase with its id
(12.5.10). Rules the PC has not met are still answered on request. The codex shows rules, not the world's
hidden state.

cards.title: Format
cards.body:
**14.6.5 Format.** `[D]` [12.15.1; DL-14-09] Codex renders are OOF blocks in 12.15's general format,
labelled `CODEX: <view>`. They are plain text, readable without any interface. A graphical client may
render the same data richer, but may not show more.

cards.title: Quick reference
cards.body: ### 14.7 Quick reference

cards.title: The player's quick sheet
cards.body:
**14.7.1 The player's quick sheet.** `[N]` [R5 FN-10; DL-14-10] T-14-4 is the one-page player reference.
The codex's Rules view returns it for "quick reference" or "help".

cards.title: Credits and attribution
cards.body: ### 14.8 Credits and attribution

cards.title: Attribution
cards.body:
**14.8.1 Attribution.** `[D]` [R5 FN-12; DL-14-11] The ruleset is original text. Designs it learned from
are cited at the rule (`[R: …]`) and listed in `appendix/credits.md`. No third-party rules text is
reproduced verbatim. Should that ever change, the credits file carries the licence notice.

cards.title: An example of play
cards.body: ### 14.9 An example of play

cards.title: A short exchange
cards.body:
**14.9.1 A short exchange.** `[N]` [R5 OB-04; DL-14-12] This shows the shape of play. The DM's
out-of-fiction blocks follow 12.15.

> **DM:** The ferry rope groans. Halfway across, the raft lurches: the far post is pulling free of the mud.
> Two figures on the far bank watch, and do not help.
>
> **Player:** I grab the rope and haul us the rest of the way before it goes.
>
> **DM:** *OFFER: haul the raft in (Might, `deed.martial.athletics`). Risky. Success 55% (critical 10%) → you land
> before the post fails. Failure → the post fails mid-haul: you're in the river, and your pack's lighter
> items wash away. Not lethal. Commit, change approach, or walk away?*
>
> **Player:** Can I loop the rope round the raft's cleat first, so it holds even if the post goes?
>
> **DM:** *That's a Setup (01.14.9). It takes the moment you have, and the OFFER becomes: Risky. Success 70%;
> a failure strands you at the cleat with the raft adrift, but still on it. Commit?*
>
> **Player:** Commit.

The example shows each element of play: the fiction first, then a freeform action, then the OFFER with its
odds and costs, then the player improving the approach, and finally an explicit commit. A full-length
example of play is in `_process/reports/verification-playtest.md` (three playtests).

cards.title: Session zero
cards.body:
**PR-14-1 Session zero.** `[D]` [12.5.1; DL-14-04] At `session_start` of the first session, before 12.16:
1. Read the premise (14.1.1). If `player.new_to_this` is unknown, ask it now: "Have you played a game like
   this before?"
2. State the three promises (14.1.3). Ask for the lethality acknowledgement (14.3.3), and offer
   `death.mode` (T-14-1).
3. Ask for lines, veils and flags (14.5.3). Confirm each mapping. (There is no tone question: the register
   is fixed classic fantasy, BRIEF §4 and 12.14.1 [revision: I-121].)
4. Ask for the pacing profile (12.7.3) and auto-commit (01.7.4), in one question each, with defaults
   stated.
5. Run the first preference check-in (12.5.9 (a) only: the pillar interest).
6. Write every answer given as a `pref.*` fact (14.5.1). A skipped question writes nothing; an absent key
   reads as its T-14-1 default [revision: I-124]. Then hand off
   to PR-12-9 (world seed).

cards.title: Render the codex
cards.body:
**PR-14-2 Render the codex.** `[D]` [14.6; DL-14-03]
1. Map the request to a view and an optional subject (14.6.3).
2. Call `codex(view)`. It reads `get_state(scope: codex, view: codex)`, which already withholds sealed and
   background fields (00.14.2 #8).
3. For computed values, call `evaluate` (02.7.4).
4. Emit one `CODEX: <view>` block (14.6.5) and log it with the turn (`log_turn`).

cards.title: First-use notes
cards.body:
**PR-14-3 First-use notes.** `[D]` [14.4.1; DL-14-06] On each turn where `player.new_to_this` is not `no`:
for each T-14-2 item first appearing this turn and not in the record `pref.shown_notes`, append its note
line and add its id to `pref.shown_notes`. Creation's closing `[RULES]` notes (PR-02-7) count as shown: when
PR-02-7 delivers them, `fn.offer` and `fn.lethal` are added to `pref.shown_notes` [revision: I-123].

cards.title: The preference record (closed list of pref. keys)
cards.body:
**T-14-1 The preference record (closed list of `pref.*` keys).**

| Key | Asked at | Values | Default | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lethality.acknowledged` | session zero (required) | true | — | 02 (creation may not start without it) |
| `death.mode` | session zero; between sessions | die, retire | die | 07.5.14 (a death result under `retire` becomes The Road Ends, 07.5.11) |
| `safety.lines` | session zero; any time | topics and mapped tags (14.5.3) | none | 12.5.6 |
| `safety.veils` | session zero; any time | topics and mapped tags | none | 12.5.6 |
| `safety.flags` | session zero; any time | topics and mapped tags | none | 12.5.6 |
| `pacing.profile` | session zero; check-in | standard, gentle, relentless | standard | 12.7.3 |
| `auto_commit` | creation; any time | on (Safe frames only), off | on [revision: R2-C] | 01.7.4 |
| `pillars` | check-in (12.5.9) | more, same or less per pillar | same | 12.9.3 |
| `player.new_to_this` | session zero / creation C0 | yes, no | no answer → treated as yes | 14.4, 12 |
| `creation.path` | creation C0 | fast, full, ready_made | fast | 02 |
| `shown_notes` | engine | ids from T-14-2 | none | PR-14-3 |

cards.title: First-use notes (shown once, for new players)
cards.body:
**T-14-2 First-use notes (shown once, for new players).**

| Id | When it first appears | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `fn.offer` | the first OFFER | "This is an OFFER: the odds and stakes before you roll. Nothing happens until you commit; you can change your approach first." |
| `fn.lethal` | the first lethal warning | "This can kill your character. You'll always get this warning first, and you'll always have to commit by hand." |
| `fn.focus` | the first Focus spend shown | "Focus is your stamina for special efforts and abilities; rest restores it." |
| `fn.recognition` | the first recognition offer | "The world has noticed what you've been doing. Accept, decline or defer; declining costs nothing." |
| `fn.harm` | the first harm result | "Harm is tracked in words, not just numbers. Your codex shows your current state." |
| `fn.codex` | the first session's teaching arc (14.4.2) | "Ask for your codex any time: sheet, journal, abilities and rules." |
| `fn.adjust` | the first scene with a flagged or intense element | "If anything isn't working for you, say 'adjust' and the scene changes, no reason needed." |
| `fn.oracle` | the first Oracle answer | "When the story needs a fact nobody decided yet, the game asks the dice and tells you the answer." |

cards.title: Codex views
cards.body:
**T-14-3 Codex views.** Each family's visibility comes from 00.6.3; the view shows a family only at that
visibility. Every 00.6.3 family that is `shown` or `available` appears in exactly one view; a view holding
`shown` families is a default view, and `available` contents appear on request (14.6.1) [editor: E2-055].

| View | Contents (00.6.3 families) | Default or on request |
|---|---|---|
| **Sheet** | attributes; computed values (02.7.4); Vitality, harm state, dying step, wounds, marks; Focus; Fate; conditions on the PC; callings, tiers and provisional status once recognized; time, calendar position and time mode; the PC's location. In a scene, also: the current frame or OFFER; relationship-state in conflict (bands, flags); conditions on others marked `visible`; adversaries' "bloodied" and "down"; clocks at their own visibility (a sensed clock by name only, 12.15.1) | default |
| **Abilities** | licenses held, slots and abilities, with each rule card's text; standing offers; commitments, oaths and vows | default |
| **Gear** | possessions, coin, item properties (an unidentified property is sealed and shows only as "unidentified"); supply, light | default |
| **Journal** | threads; clues found and PC knowledge; rumors heard (text only; truth sealed); world facts known to the PC; NPCs met (identity, appearance); places discovered and their route links, with places known only by rumor listed by name on request (10.1.5) | default |
| **Leanings** | 04.6.5's up to three rows (tag plain name and band word); never a calling name or number | on request |
| **Competence** | the competence map, each entry with its source | on request |
| **Deeds** | the evidence ledger per 03.11.1 (deed text, tags and signs, no weights) | on request |
| **Reputation and factions** | reputation content and scope (never the score); known factions and their status to the PC; NPC standing toward the PC (rung name only) | on request |
| **Allies** | companions and allies per 16.1.3's classification: its `shown` fields by default, its `available` fields on request | default when any exist |
| **Rulings** | the ruling ledger (12.12.5), the chronicle (11), the turn log (12.2.5), the corrections ledger (12.3.4), and the session's `next_time` notes (12.5.4) [revision: I-122] | on request |
| **Rules** | rule cards on request (14.6.4); T-14-4 | on request |
| **Settings** | the preference record (T-14-1): safety settings, preferences, auto-commit | default |

cards.title: The player's quick sheet
cards.body:
**T-14-4 The player's quick sheet.**

| You want to… | Say | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| do something | what you do and how, in your own words | the DM frames it; an OFFER appears if it is risky |
| see the odds first | "what are my odds?" / "what would it take?" | an OFFER, nothing spent (12.5.10) |
| improve your chances | change the approach, prepare, use the scene, get help | a better OFFER (levers, Setup, 01) |
| roll | "commit" | the die is rolled; RESULT |
| back out | "walk away" or another action | nothing spent |
| see your character | "codex", "sheet", "abilities", "journal" | a CODEX block |
| understand a rule | "how does X work?" | the rule card or its paraphrase |
| fix a mistake | "I think that's wrong" | the DM checks the record (12.3.6) |
| change content | "adjust" / "skip this" / "X" | reframed at once, no reason asked (12.5.7) |
| add a line or veil | "add a line: …" | recorded; screened from then on |
| get unstuck | "I'm stuck" | concrete options (12.8.5) |
| rest, travel, craft, train | say so | the matching procedure (07, 10, 08, 15) |

cards.title: Session zero, defaults and one line
cards.body:
**WE-14-1 Session zero, defaults and one line.** The player answers "no" to "played before?". They give one line, "harm to
children", mapped to a `safety.lines` entry (topic "harm to children", mapped to the tags for child victims and any harm) and
confirmed. They skip pacing and auto-commit, so the defaults apply (`standard`, `off`). They say "yes, I
understand" to the lethality promise, and choose `death.mode: die`. Four `pref.*` facts are written (`player.new_to_this: yes`, `safety.lines`, `lethality.acknowledged`,
`death.mode: die`); the skipped questions write nothing and read as their defaults [revision: I-124]. Then
PR-12-9 runs. Later, the seed's rumor table rolls "the miller's boy is missing". The 12.5.6 screen matches
the mapped tags, re-rolls once, and logs the substitution.

cards.title: A sealed question
cards.body:
**WE-14-2 A sealed question.** The player asks: "How close am I to becoming a ranger?" The codex's
Leanings view shows "tracking — becoming" and "the bow — leaning". The DM adds nothing: no calling name,
no number. Then the player asks: "Is the innkeeper lying to me?" The innkeeper's want and knowledge are
sealed (00.6.3), so the DM answers "Your character doesn't know that" and offers what the PC could do to
find out: a read, 15.

cards.title: Standing: what it means, where it starts, how it moves
cards.body: ### 15.1 Standing: what it means, where it starts, how it moves

cards.title: Standing
cards.body:
**15.1.1 Standing.** `[D]` **Standing** is the signed relationship scale of 00.3.16 — **−3 Hostile, −2
Unfriendly, −1 Wary, 0 Neutral, +1 Warm, +2 Friendly, +3 Devoted** — held as a `relationship` (00.6.1) from
one entity toward another (`set_relationship(npc, pc, kind: standing, …)`). It is directional: the miller's
standing toward Wren is not Wren's toward the miller (the PC's feelings are the player's, and are never
tracked). Every NPC who has interacted with the PC holds exactly one standing toward the PC
(`NPC.standing_to_pc`, 00.6.2); NPCs may also hold standing toward companions (16) and toward one another
where a rule needs it (15.1.8). **Visibility** (00.6.3): the rung *name* is `available` to the player
through the codex; the number never appears in fiction. Standing is never picked freely: it changes only
by the `[D]` steps of 15.1.5 (SG-02) [00.3.16; R6 §B.3 B-R2; R: https://bladesinthedark.com/the-faction-game].

cards.title: The behavior contract
cards.body:
**15.1.2 The behavior contract.** `[D]` Each rung is a contract the NPC keeps whatever the narrator's mood,
in the style of Blades in the Dark's faction status, where every status rung is "an explicit behavioral contract
an AI can follow literally" [R6 B-02]. T-15-1 (canonical: `data/social.yaml#standing_effects`) fixes, per
rung: the **social DC modifier** (15.3.3), the **ceiling** — the largest request Talk can obtain without
terms (15.3.4), the NPC's **patience** per scene (15.2.6), its **price shift** as a trader (15.7.4), what it
does **unasked**, what it **shares**, and how it is **voiced** (12.14.7).

cards.title: The standing contract
cards.body:
**T-15-1 The standing contract.**

| Rung | DC mod | Ceiling | Patience | Price shift | Unasked, they… | They share… | Voiced as (12.14.7) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| −3 Hostile | +5 | none (only with terms; 15.3.4) | 0 (parley and terms only) | will not trade | act against the PC when it costs them little: report, obstruct, attack if able and their behavior list allows | nothing; lie when it suits them | open enmity, refuses dealings |
| −2 Unfriendly | +3 | R1 | 1 | asking +1 notch | hinder quietly when safe; never help | only what costs nothing and hurts the PC | curt, suspicious, unhelpful |
| −1 Wary | +1 | R1 | 2 | asking +0 | carry on with their own business | public knowledge only | guarded, measured, gives little |
| 0 Neutral | 0 | R2 | 3 | asking +0 | carry on; answer civil questions | what anyone in their role would say (R1 information) | businesslike |
| +1 Warm | −1 | R3 | 3 | asking +0 | small courtesies; warn of an obvious danger | private but harmless things (R2 information) | friendly tone, small courtesies |
| +2 Friendly | −3 | R4 | 4 | asking −1 notch | go out of their way: pass on news that touches the PC, shelter them for a night | confidences that do not betray others (R3 information) | goes out of their way |
| +3 Devoted | −5 | R5 | unlimited (never walks away from the PC) | at cost (list −1 notch, never below the 08.8.7 floor) | take risks for the PC; seek them out with anything that matters to them | anything they know that their refusals allow | would take risks for the PC |

*Why these numbers.* The DC modifiers make the ceiling request about equally hard at every rung (T-15-3):
a commoner (defense 10) asked for exactly their ceiling faces DC 11–15 from Wary upward, and a request one
rung above the ceiling is not a harder roll but a different kind of problem (terms, or a campaign). The
asymmetry (Hostile +5 but Wary only +1) reflects that strangers in a classic-fantasy world are a little
guarded (12.11.2's reaction mean is −0.25) and that ill will costs more to overcome than goodwill buys
[DL-15-01]. *Simulation:* `scratchpad/social15.py`, exhaustive d20 under 01.8.1.

cards.title: Faction members: personal offset
cards.body:
**15.1.3 Faction members: personal offset.** `[D]` Q13 (00.17.1) puts individuals and factions on one
scale: a faction member's default standing toward the PC is the faction's **status** toward the PC (11),
and 12.11.2's member roll shifts it by at most one. This chapter keeps the two in step by storing, for each
member, a **personal offset**:
- `offset = standing − status`, set when the member's standing is first written (the member roll's −1/0/+1)
  and **recomputed whenever a personal step (15.1.5 sources 1–6) changes the member's standing**.
- When 11 changes the faction's status, every member's standing is recomputed as
  `clamp(status + offset, −3, +3)` and logged with reason `faction_status`. That recomputation is not a
  personal step: it does not change the offset. When the offset is positive, the recomputed standing may
  not exceed the higher of the faction's status and the highest **source cap** (15.1.7) among the member's
  own positive steps — so a member whose regard was built from small kindnesses tops out at Friendly
  however the faction's mood swings (WE-15-6).
So a member the PC has never dealt with simply follows the faction; a guard the PC once spared (offset
+2) stays two rungs warmer than her captain's grudge; a guildmaster's daughter who has become Devoted to
the PC while the guild is at war (offset +6) stays Devoted. Individuals and factions diverge exactly as far
as personal history has pushed them, and no further — Mount & Blade's per-lord beside per-kingdom relations, made
deterministic [R6 B-09; 00.17.1 Q13; DL-15-02]. The recomputation runs in `h.15.member_standing`
(`week`, phase 6, after `h.11.world_turn`) and immediately on any status write 11 makes outside the turn.

cards.title: Starting standing
cards.body:
**15.1.4 Starting standing.** `[D]` Standing toward the PC is written once, at the NPC's **first
interaction** with the PC, and never chosen:
1. A **bond** NPC (02.9.2): the set value of the bond kind (anchor kin/friend/ward +2, mentor +1 [verification: V2b-021]; thorn rival
   −1, creditor 0, enemy −2), reason `bond` [02.9.2].
2. A **faction member** (00.17.1 Q13): the faction's status plus the member roll (12.11.2 step 1).
3. **Anyone else**: the reaction roll, 2d6 plus at most ±2 in cited modifiers (12.11.2 step 2): ≤2 Hostile,
   3–4 Unfriendly, 5–6 Wary, 7–8 Neutral, 9–10 Warm, 11+ Friendly; **never Devoted** as a first impression.
4. **Adversaries** met outside a fight: only if their archetype has `reaction_roll: true` (09.2.7); a
   `cunning` mind met in a fight starts Hostile; a `mindless` one has no standing at all.
The NPC's standing exists in state from that write onward; the claim check (12.3) flags any narration of
attitude before it exists (claim class `attitude`). Starting standing is a first impression, never a
verdict: everything in 15.1.5 moves it [12.11.2; 02.9.2; 09.2.7; R5 AV-07].

cards.title: How standing moves: the closed list of sources
cards.body:
**15.1.5 How standing moves: the closed list of sources.** `[D]` [DL-15-03; DL-15-04; C:I; R5 NP-03; revision: I-065] Standing changes only through these
sources, each writing `set_relationship(npc, pc, steps, reason, source_ref)` and a memory (12.11.7):
1. **A Talk frame's delivered reach** on a win-over (15.4.2) — +1 step, never above Warm.
2. **A cost**: `cost.closed_door` at S3 (−1) and S4–S5 (−2) (01.13.9).
3. **A deed** the NPC did, witnessed, or was told of, through its memory valence (15.1.6).
4. **A gift** given with nothing asked in return (15.1.7): +1, never above Friendly.
5. **A kept or broken commitment** involving the NPC (a promise, a debt, a deal; 15.7.6), through
   15.1.6's `promised`, `owed` and `betrayed` rows.
6. **Intimidation that succeeds, or leverage used** (15.4.3, 15.3.5): −1 at `scene_end` (fear is not regard).
7. **The faction's status** for a member (15.1.3), by recomputation, not by step.
8. **An ally's regard or grievance clock completing** (16.5.3): +1 or −1 for that ally
   [integration: IR ch.16 to 15 (a)].
Nothing else moves standing. In particular: the passage of time does not warm or cool anyone; a long,
pleasant conversation with no frame does not; the DM's sense that the NPC "would come round by now" does
not (12.11.6) [00.3.16; SG-02].

cards.title: Memory valences to steps
cards.body:
**15.1.6 Memory valences to steps.** `[D]` + `[J:flag]` [DL-15-03; C:III; revision: I-065] Chapter 12 writes an NPC memory for every beat that
touches them (12.11.7), with one **valence** from a closed list. This table (T-15-2, canonical
`data/social.yaml#memory_steps`) is the one mapping from memories to standing steps; it applies at RECORD
of the beat that wrote the memory (the NPC's attitude changes in the scene, not later), except
`threatened`, which applies at `scene_end` (the NPC complies now and resents afterward).

cards.title: Memory valence → standing step
cards.trigger: 12.11.7 writes a memory with a valence whose row in T-15-2 has a magnitude condition
decisions: 1. MAGNITUDE [J:flag] "Does this memory's deed meet the row's condition?" True only with a cited state fact: the frame's cost severity (harmed), the request rung of the help as 15.3.2 classifies it (helped), the recorded relationship to the victim (kin, ally, member), or a want record (impressed). False when the condition rests on the narration's tone. Uncertain -> the smaller step.
cards.computation: set_relationship(npc, pc, step, reason: memory, source_ref: memory id), clamped -3..+3 and to the row's cap and 15.1.7's caps; offset recomputed (15.1.3)
narration_may_not_imply: a change of attitude larger or smaller than the step
cards.worst_case: one step too many or too few for one NPC (class i), auditable from the memory's cited frame; the uncertain tie-break errs toward the smaller change.
examples: inside: Wren carries the miller's wounded son two miles to the healer (S3 harm prevented, a day's work) -> helped, R3 -> +1 (cap Friendly). boundary: she pulls him out of the millrace as he drowns (death prevented) -> rescue +2 (cap Devoted). inside: a shove that spilled a merchant's wares (S1 cost) -> harmed -1. outside: the same shove spilled nothing (no cost) -> insulted at most. non-example: "She'd be moved by how I nursed him, surely +2" -> the step follows the cited cost and request rung, never the description of the nursing.
cards.body:
**T-15-2 Memory valence → standing step.**

| Valence (12.11.7) | Step | Condition / magnitude rule | Cap from this source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `helped` | +1 | the help was worth at least an R2 favor to them (15.3.2: it cost the PC a day, a Unit of coin, or a real risk) | Friendly; Devoted only when the help was R4+ (saved a livelihood, a life, a kinsman) |
| `helped` (rescue) | +2 | the PC saved them or their kin from S4+ harm, death, captivity or ruin | Devoted |
| `harmed` | −1 / −2 / −3 | the harm or cost to them, their kin or property was S1–S2 / S3 / S4+, or killed kin | none |
| `lied_to` | 0 | they do not yet know (15.5.3) | — |
| `caught_lying` | −2 | they learned the PC deceived them (15.5.5) | none |
| `impressed` | +1 | they witnessed a resolved deed that serves one of their recorded wants or matches their role's values (a knight sees mercy; a smith sees fine work); at most once per NPC per season | Friendly |
| `insulted` | −1 | the PC's words or act were recorded as an affront (a taunt that landed, a refusal of hospitality, mocking their faith); at most once per NPC per scene | none |
| `owed` (the PC owes them) | 0 | the debt is leverage *for them*; repaid on time → `helped` +1 | — |
| `owes` (they owe the PC) | 0 | a term the PC may call (15.3.5 Leverage); calling it in clears it without a step | — |
| `promised` | 0 | kept → +1 (as `helped`, cap Friendly; a kept R4+ promise may reach Devoted); broken → `betrayed` | — |
| `betrayed` | −3 | a promise, oath, deal or trust they relied on was broken by the PC | none |
| `spared` | +2 | the PC held their life or freedom and gave it back (a yielded foe let go, a thief not handed over) | Devoted |
| `threatened` | −1 | at `scene_end` after a successful intimidation or a leverage term against them | none |

*Heard of, not witnessed.* An NPC who learns of a deed only by report (12.10.6 c, `how: told`) takes at
most **±1** from it, and only when the deed touched their kin, allies, faction or wants.
